prompt: [IELTS WRITING TASK 2] More and more students at university today are not chosing to study science
essay:
Nowadays, there are an increasing number of undergraduates who do not enjoy studying science-related courses. This essay will first explore why some science courses might become irrelevant to students, and then it will discuss how this might impede the advancement of contemporary technology. 
 One of the most pertinent explanations for this circumstance is the possibility that some students' future employment may not require science. It implies that they would not pay attention when studying science, which demands a high level of memorizing and logical thinking ability; as a result, their decision is to withdraw from these science courses. A great illustration of this is how more and more college students are choosing to major in subjects other than science, such as art or music, in order to develop a wide range of specific skills that may be applicable to their line of work. 
 Numerous negative outcomes could result from this problem, but the most significant one is that it may decrease the quality of many businesses' products. This is because modern business owners' top priority is to create cutting-edge machines and make a profit from them. If that occurs, employees' general knowledge cannot keep up with formal evolution. As an example, many low-quality modern devices produced by some unreputable companies are harming their customers. 
 In conclusion, even though their future careers will not involve technology, undergraduates should acquire a wealth of scientific knowledge. Only by acting accordingly can a dynamic development future be maintained.
feedback:
This essay presents some understandable points regarding undergraduates' interest in science courses and its impact on technological advancement. However, there are several areas where improvements could significantly enhance the clarity and effectiveness of your arguments.

Firstly, it's crucial to ensure that your essay directly responds to the given topic. The essay starts by discussing why undergraduates might not find science courses appealing, focusing on the lack of direct application to future careers. However, the transition from personal interest to the broader implications of this trend could be clearer. Clarifying the connection between students' lack of interest in science and the potential impact on technological advancement would strengthen your essay's focus.

Regarding spelling, grammar, and stylistic issues, your essay is generally well-written but could benefit from a more varied sentence structure to improve readability. Pay attention to maintaining a consistent tense and ensuring subject-verb agreement throughout your essay.

Your point of view comes across in the essay; however, it could be made more explicit with a stronger thesis statement at the beginning. This statement should clearly outline your position and the main arguments you will use to support it.

The arguments presented to support your position are relevant, but they could be more descriptive and detailed to effectively convince the reader. For example, when discussing the outcome of a decrease in science graduates, the connection to business and product quality seems a bit indirect. Focusing more specifically on areas directly related to science, such as technology or medicine, and how the decrease in interested students could impact these fields, would reinforce your argument. Providing specific examples or data could also strengthen your claims.

In conclusion, while your essay offers some good insights, focusing on directly addressing the essay question, clarifying your thesis statement, and supporting your arguments with more detailed and relevant examples would greatly improve your essay. Ensuring that your discussion points are directly related to the core topic will not only help to keep your essay on track but also make your argument more compelling to the reader.

prompt: Ielts task 2 writing: sports should be part of school program??
essay:
Discuss both sides of this argument and then give your own opinion 
 Students are required to learn a lot of subjects these days; therefore, some people believe that sports ought to be in the school curriculum, but many think it's time consuming and concentrating on academic work is of greater benefits . I completely disagree that sports aren't significant thus should not be included. This essay will discuss both points of view. 
 On the one hand, some individuals argue that sports are a waste of time, because of that students can't spend time on some core subjects. It also will bring bad-graded potential for exam results while academic skills and scores are the most important focus at school. In Viet Nam, for example parents don't allow their children to take part in sports because they think these will distract them from their important areas and they can't get a good future thanks to that. 
 On the other hand, it's clear that sports help us to enhance both our physical and mental health. Students can practice exercise to have a flexible body, and also make them reduce their stress after studying for a long time. In some Asian countries, students just care for their study in some necessary subject and get a lot of mental illness like depressions, which often lead to suicide while the one play sports can avoid that simly. practicing sports with friends will bring many benefits like some vital skills about communication, building solidarity between class members. A case in this point is some scientific research think that students, who play sports have strong connections to their friends than others. 
 In conclusion, I think sports is an essential part of education. If schools can have more sporty games, students can get access to their favourite sports and avoid more diseases in the future.
feedback:
The essay attempts to address the topic by discussing the importance of including athletics (formerly "sports") in the school curriculum versus focusing solely on academic endeavors (formerly "academic work"). However, there are several areas where improvements could greatly enhance the essay's clarity, persuasiveness, and adherence to the prompt.

1. **Response to Topic**: The essay engages with the topic but does not fully explore both sides of the argument as instructed. When discussing arguments for and against the inclusion of athletics in school programs, it is essential to differentiate clearly between public opinions and your personal viewpoint. Start by presenting each side of the argument objectively, using third-person pronouns to denote general opinions. This helps clarify that these perspectives are not your own but are part of a broader public debate. After presenting these viewpoints, you can then introduce your own opinion, using first-person pronouns to make it clear that this is your personal stance. This organization will make your argument more structured and easier to follow.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, and Stylistic Issues**: The essay contains several grammatical and stylistic issues that affect its readability. For instance, phrases like "discuss both points of view" could be better structured as "This essay will explore both perspectives." Additionally, there's a need for more careful punctuation, especially in the use of commas and periods to separate ideas. Replacing words directly from the prompt (e.g., "sports" with "athletics" and "academic work" with "academic endeavors") can also showcase a broader vocabulary and enhance your score. 

3. **Clarity of Point of View**: Your personal perspective is noted; however, it is somewhat overshadowed by the blending of public opinion and personal viewpoint. To improve clarity, establish a clear distinction between the argument's two sides and your personal opinion by dedicating separate paragraphs to each and using appropriate pronouns as advised.

4. **Arguments and Support**: While the essay presents reasons for both including and excluding athletics from the curriculum, these arguments could be more detailed and supported with specific examples or evidence. For instance, mentioning specific studies or statistics that support the benefits of athletics on student health and social skills would strengthen your position. Also, elaborating on how academic performance and athletics can complement each other could offer a more balanced view and demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of the topic.

In conclusion, focusing on clearer structuring of arguments, enhancing language use, and providing specific supporting details can significantly improve the essay. By addressing these points, the writing will not only better adhere to the prompt but also display a more sophisticated understanding and use of the English language.

prompt: Is the speaking competence or the writing ability playing a more decisive role in people's life
essay:
Both the ability of writing and speaking are the basic tools for us to make a live in the society. When it comes to the question of whether the speaking competence is more decisive than writing ability, people varying in education backgrounds and professions tend to have distinctive views. 
 However, I am in favor of the statement that speaking competence is more essential than writing capability. People with excellent speaking ability are more likely to succeed. Since the eloquent people can express themselves easily and persuade people to favor their thoughts. 
 For instance, in ancient china, a diplomat of Qin dynasty named Yizhang accomplish the task excellently using his communication skills. His extraordinary persuasion make the rival countries believe that their cooperation with Qin dynasty would be beneficial to them instead of allying with each other against Qin dynasty. Consequently, the Qin dynasty gradually unified the whole china. 
 Moreover, a competent speaker is easier to make friends with people. People trend to build a good relationship with one who can express his feelings and views accurately and vividly. Besides, a good speaker always means that he is humor and open mind, which are key factors when we choose friends. My roommates Lin who was not good at speech was always disappointed that he was a unpopular man. He always feels lonely because he has no friends. What is more, he was too shy to speak with others. His change occur when I recommend a book named the art of speech to him, which help people who have difficulty in speech improve their speaking competence. Over the past two years, he practiced the skills of communication constantly and thus became more and more open and have many friends. 
 The speaking ability is also critical in our careers. Almost all the vacations need the skill of communication. A teacher need a excellent speech competence to impart knowledge to students. A lawyer has to acquire a outstanding persuasion ability to help his client. In a globalized age it is inevitable that people from various country with different cultures would have to cooperate with each other. Hence people need pay more attention to speaking competence . 
 All in all, with the above careful analysis of the significance of speaking and writing, we can tell that people with strong capability in speaking enjoy more opportunities to promote and publicize oneself, and people who lack of such ability will obviously fail to achieve that.
feedback:
This essay does a commendable job of arguing why speaking competence is considered more valuable than writing ability, responding well to the topic with a clear stance. However, there are areas for improvement that could enhance the essay further.

1. **Utilization of Examples**: The use of historical figures, while interesting, may not resonate with all readers due to the lack of familiarity with ancient Chinese history. To make your arguments more relatable and engaging, consider incorporating more recent examples that a wider audience can understand and appreciate. This approach can help illustrate your point more effectively.

2. **Spelling and Grammar Issues**: There are a few grammatical errors within the essay that disrupt the flow and clarity. For example, the correct phrase should be "People tend to build..." rather than "People trend to build,” as "tend" refers to a tendency or inclination towards something. Also, when referring to a singular person, such as "My roommate Lin...," ensure that singular nouns are used correctly. Additionally, it's important to be mindful of verb tenses; "His change occurred..." is the correct past tense. Correcting these errors will significantly improve the readability of your essay.

3. **Stylistic Suggestions**: When mentioning the title of a book, such as "the art of speech," capitalize it ("The Art of Speech") to adhere to proper naming conventions. This adds a level of professionalism to your writing and respects copyright conventions.

4. **Point of View and Arguments**: Your position is clear throughout the essay, and you provide examples to support your stance. However, further elaboration on these examples, especially by choosing more contemporary references, could strengthen your arguments. For instance, discussing how modern individuals have used their speaking abilities to achieve success would make your argument more compelling.

5. **General Advice**: Consider revising your essay with attention to the points mentioned above. Carefully choosing examples, correcting grammatical mistakes, and improving the structure of your sentences will help convey your message more effectively. It's beneficial to review writing rules regularly to refine your skills further.

Overall, the essay displays a good understanding of the topic and presents a clear viewpoint. Concentrating on these suggested areas for improvement will undoubtedly lead to a more polished and impactful essay. Remember, practice and revision are key components of successful writing.

prompt: IELTS Writing Task 2 (About the distance-learning programs)
essay:
Nowadays, an increasing number of students use distance-learning programs. However, whether taking distance courses can bring the same benefits as attending college. I agree with the view that students can get more benefits from distance education than traditional education. 
 First, online education enables students to study at their own place. This means that students can study whenever and wherever they want. Students can make the best use of their time studying knowledge and skills which are they need. What is different from traditional, students do not need to stay in the classroom, and they can save many times which could be used to do something else. Therefore, it is important to encourage the development of online education. 
 In addition, technology can make lessons much more interesting. For example, 3D technology has become a hot topic after the movie Avatar made the whole world crazy, and it also is used in online education now. The using of high technology in distance-learning programs makes online lessons more interesting and more interactive than college's lessons. Students who take this lessons will put all their heart into it. 
 However, that is not to say that universities can not bring any benefits to students. Of course, universities cannot provide structured courses that many technological educate cannot provide with. But I still believe that online education systems will become more and more reasonable. 
 In summary, online education can bring more benefits to the students and society, and that will be a trend of the future education. Meanwhile, we should not ignore the importance of traditional education. Only by doing so can we create the best educational environment for the next generation.
feedback:
This essay attempts to address the topic by arguing in favor of distance learning over traditional education. However, to fully respond to the prompt, a more defined stance expressing the extent of agreement or disagreement is necessary. For a stronger response, consider using descriptive adjectives like "strongly," "totally," or "partially." This will clarify how much you agree or disagree with the statement.

Firstly, the essay effectively highlights the flexibility and technological benefits of distance learning. These arguments are well-chosen as they align with your viewpoint. However, the essay would benefit from more descriptive language and specific examples to further strengthen these points. Describing how this flexibility and technology impact a student's learning experience in more detail would make your argument more persuasive.

On the matter of clarity, while your point of view is understandable, it could be made clearer by avoiding contradictory statements. For instance, you mention that universities cannot bring any benefits, but later acknowledge their importance. Clarifying this contradiction and providing a more nuanced discussion of traditional education's value would enhance your essay's coherence.

Several spelling, grammar, and stylistic issues need addressing. For spelling and grammar, watch out for typos and sentence structure; for example, "students can make the best use of their time studying knowledge and skills which are they need" could be simplified to "students can efficiently learn the skills and knowledge they need." Regarding style, avoid repetitions and aim for concise sentences to keep the reader engaged.

The essay suggests a belief that the future of education leans towards online learning. While mentioning traditional education's benefits, the argument primarily advocates for distance learning. Remember, discussing multiple viewpoints is suitable only if you specify that your agreement with the topic is only partial. Since your essay seems to support distance learning exclusively, it's essential to maintain a focused argument throughout.

In conclusion, your essay proposes interesting points about distance learning. For improvement, define your stance more clearly with descriptive adjectives, enhance your arguments with specific examples and descriptions, address contradictory statements, and correct spelling and grammatical errors. By making these adjustments, your essay will become more coherent, persuasive, and aligned with the prompt's requirements.

prompt: In many cities, planners tend to arrange shops, schools, offices, and homes in specific areas.....
essay:
My essay: 
 In these days, many planners have/show a tendency to sort shops, schools, offices, and homes in particular areas and separate them from others. In my point of view, the upsides outweigh the downsides. 
 On the one hand, there are some drawbacks of this statement. To begin with, this plan requires too much money and time to carry out. Nowadays, there are many developing countries and undeveloped countries so this is a big challenge to them. Moreover, it also makes people anxious all the time. For instance, if home and hospital are far away from each other, citizens may suffer from long commuting time. 
 On the other hand, this idea also has many benefits. First and foremost, it helps people work more productively. For example, students can study well and comfortably without distraction, noise so that they will get high marks in schools. Secondly, this idea reduces accidents thanks to specific areas. Staffs go on the streets that lead to offices, doctors have their own ways to the hospitals, etc. 
 In conclusion, while arranging shops, schools, offices, and homes in specific localities has some disadvantages, it also has many advantages.
feedback:
The essay provided offers insights into the debate over segregating residential areas from commercial, educational, and healthcare facilities. While the essay addresses the topic, there are several key aspects where improvements could greatly benefit the overall quality and persuasiveness of the argument presented.

1. **Length and Detail:** The essay falls short of the minimum word requirement, which stands at 250 words. A more extended discussion would allow for a more in-depth exploration of the topic. It’s essential to expand on ideas by including more examples, evidence, or explanations to back up points made, ensuring the essay fully develops its arguments.

2. **Clarity in Arguments:** The essay attempts to present both sides of the debate. However, there’s room for improvement in how these arguments are structured and supported. An effective argument requires clear reasoning and specific, believable examples to substantiate the claims. For instance, elaborating on why separating different zones leads to higher productivity or reduced accidents with more concrete examples could strengthen the essay’s persuasiveness.

3. **Spelling, Grammar, and Style:** A few stylistic and grammatical adjustments can improve the readability and professionalism of the essay. Consider varying sentence structure to maintain the reader’s interest and ensure each sentence adds new information or perspectives to avoid repetition.

4. **Point of View and Coherence:** While the essay states a clear opinion that the advantages outweigh the disadvantages, further elaboration on why this opinion is held would enhance the essay. This includes not just listing benefits and drawbacks but critically analyzing them to show why one side is preferred over the other. Making sure each paragraph logically flows into the next also helps in maintaining coherence throughout.

Improving in these areas would significantly enhance the essay's effectiveness in communicating its point of view and persuading the audience. It's also beneficial to keep the audience and essay requirements in mind throughout the writing process to ensure the final product meets all necessary criteria.

prompt: Getting information from newspapers and other media
essay:
In recent years, it is believed that getting information from newspapers is the best way, while others argue that other media are a better source of news. Although printed news plays a vital role in our life, I am in favor of the idea that learning news through other media will be the better option in the long run 
 On the one hand, it is undeniable that newspapers still hold the most popular position among newsreaders for the following justifications. Firstly, newspapers are a reliable source of information which are written, edited, and censored carefully by professional journalists before the publication. Therefore, the information is neutral and accurate. Furthermore, traditional newspapers are easily accessible to everyone. For instance, senior citizens are normally unfamiliar with technological devices or those who live in a place without internet connection; thus, reading newspapers is considered a convenient way to keep themselves informed. . 
 On the other hand, it seems to me that other media offer readers a wide range of benefits. The first and foremost reason is that other media update the latest information faster than traditional newspapers. In fact, by using portable devices with access to the Internet such as smartphones or iPads,.....people can access a huge storage of news in just a few clicks every time everywhere. Another compelling idea is that other media bring a great deal of interesting experiences to readers through different forms. For instance, people can stay informed about music events through videos, sounds that are more eye-catching and a more enjoyable reading experience instead of long texts. 
 In conclusion, though the roles of newspapers are significant in conveying accurate information and ease of access for readers, I am of the opinion that news from other media is more superior because of greater reading experience and more accessibility.
feedback:
This essay does a good job of introducing the topic and presenting both sides of the argument about the best source for news. The introduction clearly states a preference for news obtained from media other than newspapers, which sets the stage for the discussion. However, the essay needs improvement in certain areas to make the argument more persuasive and coherent.

Firstly, it's important to focus on defending the chosen stance throughout the essay. While it's beneficial to acknowledge the opposing view, the primary goal is to strengthen the argument for the preferred source of news. The essay presents points favoring both newspapers and alternative media, which may confuse readers about the author's standpoint. To enhance the essay, concentrate on providing evidence and reasoning that support the opinion that other media are superior for news, and critically examine or refute arguments in favor of newspapers to solidify your position.

There are also minor spelling, grammar, and stylistic issues to address. For instance, the spacing and punctuation around ellipses and commas need a closer look, and words like "consider" should be spelled correctly. Improving these aspects will make the essay more professional and easier to read.

The clarity of the author's point of view could be improved by maintaining a consistent argument throughout the essay. It’s advisable to revisit the paragraphs and ensure that all points made directly support the argument in favor of other media as the better news source, thereby avoiding contradictions.

Additionally, the essay could benefit from more detailed and specific examples to support claims. For instance, when mentioning the speed and accessibility of news through other media, providing real-life examples or statistical data could strengthen the argument. Also, discussing the limitations or challenges associated with obtaining news from newspapers in more detail could further support the author's position.

In conclusion, by focusing on a clear defense of the chosen viewpoint, addressing grammatical and stylistic issues, and enhancing the supporting arguments with more specific examples and critical examination of opposing views, the essay will become more persuasive and aligned with the assignment's requirements. The goal is to convince the reader of the superiority of alternative media over newspapers for news dissemination, and these improvements will help achieve that objective.

prompt: IELTS WT2: spoken communication is more powerful than written communication.
essay:
Some people think spoken communication is more powerful than written communication. To what extent do you agree or disagree? 
 Almost everyone can use their voice to interact with people surrounding them, so some find verbal communication useful and easy to use. However, it would be unwise for people to completely ignore learning how to utilize written communication .In my opinion, this notion that verbal communication is more potent than non-verbal is fully unjustified. 
 Admittedly, using spoken language is the easiest and most universal way in terms of exchanging information. This is especially true in face to face conversations, which stem from people's instincts for imitating words and intonations since we were infants. Thus, spoken words go a long way towards helping people express their thoughts as well as genuine emotions effectively in formal situations. 
 By contrast, although we mostly interact directly with others, it is impossible to sideline the importance of written communication due to the formality and validity which are characteristic of formal letters, notes on paper, or filling in forms. There will be incidents when we need to write down some pronouncements such as police records or medical notes, which require written words to act as evidence in court or part of formal procedures later on . In addition, it is imperative that we use written language in examinations which are still mostly handwritten because it is a rigorous method to evaluate and assess one's level of education. Last but not least , using non-verbal language is an integral part of conserving our cultures and values for future generations. This is evidenced by the fact that there are some manuscripts of the bible which had been written on the leather 2000 years ago and were found intact. 
 In conclusion, I am against the viewpoint that people should attach greater significance to verbal forms of communication than to written ones. I feel that writing skills are essential both for practical reasons such as preservation efforts and to show the formality and legislation in pronouncing important announcements as well as assess exactly the level of learning knowledge of students. In other words, it is unlikely that either spoken communication, or written language can replace one another.
feedback:
Your essay addresses an interesting debate: whether spoken communication is more powerful than written communication. Your exploration of this theme shows thoughtfulness and a willingness to consider various perspectives. However, to elevate your writing and ensure it fully meets test criteria, consider the following points:

1. **Responsiveness to the Topic**: The beginning of your essay should clearly restate the task's question and present your stance. It’s necessary to explicitly answer the prompt, “To what extent do you agree or disagree?” Remember, the introduction is critical for setting up your argument and guiding your reader. Instead of immediately presenting your opinion, try first to rephrase the question in a way that naturally leads into your perspective, followed by a thesis statement that outlines the main reasons behind your view.

2. **Structural and Stylistic Issues**: Your essay is structured in a way that makes your points accessible, but there's room for improvement. Each paragraph should ideally open with a topic sentence that signals the argument it will discuss, followed by examples or further explanation. Your concluding paragraph effectively summarizes your stance but could be strengthened by directly linking back to the prompt's question, reinforcing the extent of your agreement or disagreement.

3. **Clarity of Author’s Point of View**: Your point of view is clear, but the way it's presented could be refined. Framing your opinion in response to the prompt’s question at the beginning will solidify your stance for the reader. Avoid jumping too quickly into your argument without clearly stating your position regarding the extent of your agreement or disagreement.

4. **Arguments and Descriptions**: You've provided several arguments to support your perspective, citing the importance of written communication alongside spoken communication. Enhancing these arguments with more specific examples or evidence could make them more compelling. For instance, when mentioning the preservation of culture through written language, including more detailed examples could illustrate this point more vividly.

5. **Spelling and Grammar**: While there are minor spelling and grammar issues, overall, your writing is understandable. Paying closer attention to punctuation, such as the proper placement of commas and periods, can improve readability. Consider revising phrases like “Last but not least,” to a more formal alternative, aligning with the tone of an academic essay.

Remember, practice in restructuring your arguments to directly answer the prompt, along with focusing on clearer topic sentences and more detailed examples, will greatly improve your essay writing. Keep refining your skills, and you’ll see significant progress in your ability to craft engaging and effective essays.

prompt: IELTS writing task 2 - different perspectives on changes
essay:
Q. 
 Some people prefer to change and think that change leads to new experiences. Others believe that it is better for their lives to remain the same. 
 Others believe that it is better for their lives to remain the same. 
 Discuss both these views and give your own opinion. 
 Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. 
 knowledge or experience. 
 A. 
 Changes occur in our lives, whether small or big. There is not much we could do but accept them. Yet when faced with changes, people react differently. Some people find changes frightening for which might take what they are familiar with away from them, whereas some others are thrilled for the excitement and differences that come with changes. Personally, I tend to look forward to changes and endless possibilities they bring. 
 From my standpoint, it is completely reasonable for certain people to consider changes scary given the fact that anyone could feel insecure in an unfamiliar situation. Going through dramatic changes can be extremely stressful and hard to handle even for those who were excited about changes at first place. Take becoming parents as an example. Despite the satisfaction of creating a new life with the loved one, it has been proven that having and raising a baby can possibly cause mental disorder resulted from major changes in all the different aspects. Thus, it is not a surprise that people regard such changes terrifying. 
 However, changes are essential to our lives. Regardless of how changes might seem disturbing at first, they are what keep living interesting and spice up our daily life. Changes give us an opportunity to make things better. In addition, they also enable us to break free from the draining cycle of the same day playing repeatedly. Although seemed frightening at first glance, changes could actually broaden our horizons and lead to tremendous brand new experience. Therefore it is crucial to remain open-minded when it comes to changes. 
 All in all, despite the fact that changes are inevitable regardless of our attitude toward them. I firmly believe that instead of being afraid of changes, we should stay positive and attempt to look on the bright side of a new page of life.
feedback:
The essay addresses the topic about whether it's better for lives to remain constant or embrace change. However, the structure and discussion required for this type of essay were not adequately followed. For improvement, focusing on structuring the essay according to the discussion requirements is vital.

Firstly, the essay should have been organized into five paragraphs. This includes starting with a paraphrase of the question, followed by two paragraphs presenting the differing public points of view, then a paragraph expressing personal opinion with supporting examples from personal experience, and concluding with a summary. The initial paraphrase was well done, but the transition to a clear thesis statement that outlines the intent to discuss both viewpoints before stating a personal opinion was missing.

To clarify, your personal perspective came too early in the essay. After the introductory paragraph, dedicate one paragraph to each viewpoint, ensuring that these are clearly indicated as public perspectives using phrases like “When people say that…” or “However, when members of society believe that...”. This helps to distinguish your discussion of the public views from your personal opinion.

For the body paragraphs, introduce each viewpoint with a clear topic sentence. Provide examples or further explanation within these paragraphs to explore each viewpoint before moving on to express your own opinions. Make sure your personal opinion is supported by examples from your experience or knowledge, as this strengthens your argument.

The conclusion should summarize the points discussed, briefly revisiting the public viewpoints and your own stance, ending with a restatement of your opinion as a closing thought.

It’s also important to avoid repetition. For instance, the phrase "Others believe that it is better for their lives to remain the same" was repeated. Tightening the language to remove unnecessary repetition will make the essay stronger and clearer.

In terms of grammar and stylistic issues, while the essay is mostly well-written, some sentences could be simplified to ensure clarity, keeping in mind the audience's English proficiency level. For example, complex sentences with multiple clauses could be broken down into simpler sentences.

Remember, the goal is not only to state opinions but to engage in a structured discussion that clearly presents different perspectives before offering your own view. Reading sample essays and focusing on their structure can be incredibly beneficial. Look at how these essays introduce, discuss, and conclude their arguments. Paying attention to these aspects can substantially improve your essay writing for future tests.

prompt: Writing task 2 Is offering online courses a positive or negative development?
essay:
It is true that online courses are becoming a common feature of university education system. Even though there are some disadvantages of Internet-based learning, I believe that benefits of it far outweigh its drawbacks. 
 Three cons of online education should be mentioned. The main problem is lack of direct interaction between students and teachers which is a crucial learning process. For example, students can ask teachers questions after class, but it seems not possible if online platform replaces classroom. Another concern is that it is difficult to ensure students attendance. Due to omission of rigorous attendance counting and punishment, playing truant is easy to do with no cost. The last negative possibility is the effectiveness of online courses is still questionable as there is insufficient scientific evidence to prove it. 
 Despite the drawbacks mentioned above, offering online education is still a reasonable decision owing to several factors. Learning online is a more convenient way to study because students can choose the best time to learn and have a flexible timetable which favours students to learn something other than university courses. In addition, geographical location is no more a limitation because online courses are available as long as Internet service is available. For instance, students in Africa do not have to travel thousands of milometres to Finland to attend lessons there. It also helps facilitate the free flow of knowledge because Internet is a convenient "place" to connect people around the world and their possessed wisdom and experiences. 
 In conclusion, while I recognise the aforementioned disadvantages of online learning, I consider it to be a positive development overall. ( 267 words)
feedback:
This essay addresses the topic of online courses in the university education system, weighing the benefits against the disadvantages. However, it appears there has been a slight misunderstanding of what the prompt requires. The task is to discuss whether online learning represents a positive or negative development, focusing solely on that viewpoint. Instead, the essay explores both advantages and disadvantages, which strays from providing a clear stance as requested by the prompt. To enhance the essay, a more focused discussion on either presenting online learning as purely positive or purely negative would be necessary, depending on the chosen perspective.

Regarding the structure and content, the essay does a decent job of outlining several key points. However, it could benefit from clearer and more direct arguments relating to the chosen stance. For instance, if arguing that online learning is positive, emphasize how its benefits significantly overpower any potential negatives without dedicating equal space to disadvantages.

There are a few spelling and grammar issues to note:
- “Internet-based learning” and “Internet” should not be capitalized unless at the beginning of a sentence. 
- “milometres” should be corrected to “kilometres” to ensure proper spelling. 
- To maintain consistency in academic writing, try to avoid contractions like "it's" and instead use "it is."

Moreover, while the arguments provided do offer insight into the pros and cons of online learning, making these arguments more vivid with specific examples or statistics could strengthen the essay. For instance, when discussing the convenience and flexibility of online learning, mentioning a study or survey results could add credibility.

The perspective of the essay is somewhat clear in that it leans towards viewing online learning positively. However, this standpoint could be made more explicit by emphasizing it in both the introduction and conclusion, ensuring that the reader is left with no doubt about the author's view.

In conclusion, refining the focus to align with the prompt's requirements, correcting minor spelling and grammar issues, and reinforcing arguments with specific examples or data would significantly improve the essay. By honing in on these aspects, the essay would not only respond more directly to the given topic but also present a more compelling and well-supported argument.

prompt: Governments think that economic progress is their most important goal. Some people disagree
essay:
While there are a lot of countries that only aimed for economic developments, there is a portion of people who say there are a lot of aspects for a country to count it as a strong one. Both points of views shall be discussed along with my own ideas about the subject. 
 On one hand, in today's world, money plays an important role. From the government's perspective, a great economy will give them the power to prepare better lifestyle for their own people. For instance, countries that have a good economy, their citizen's are happier than other countries. 
 On the other hand, there are a lot of other aspects involve, namely; healthcare, sports, and culture. There are people that argue these types of development is as crucial as the economic one. Because the economic itself does not guarantee the well being of citizen's life. For example, there are countries that have a lot of resources but spend all of it for wrong purposes, like war missiles. 
 Lastly, in my own opinion, a good economy can give advantages to the country. In fact, it is a leverage that can be used in international talks or to prepare a wonderful healthcare system for their people. It is the matter of how to use the resources, whether care about the citizens or not. 
 In conclusion, both points of view about the importance of economy were discussed, in addition to my personal view on the subject, which is, even though economics is the most important aspect of a country, it is also important how to use it. 
 (267 Words)
feedback:
The essay provided addresses the topic of whether economic development alone can define a country as strong. The response introduces both sides of the argument as well as a personal viewpoint, which is a good structure for an essay topic like this. However, there are several areas where this essay can be improved to make the argument clearer, more engaging, and better structured.

1. **Response to the topic**: The essay successfully addresses the topic by discussing the importance of both economic and other types of developments such as healthcare, sports, and culture. The point of view is introduced but could be developed further. Each point mentioned could be expanded with more detailed examples and a clearer explanation of how these aspects contribute to the strength of a country. 

2. **Spelling, grammar, or stylistic issues**: There are some grammatical mistakes that need attention. For instance, "countries that have a good economy, their citizen's are happier" should be "countries that have a good economy have happier citizens". Paying attention to sentence structure can make the argument more coherent. Also, "citizen's" should not have an apostrophe when used in a general sense. It's important to proofread for these small errors, as they can distract from the message.

3. **Clarity of the point of view**: While the essay mentions a personal viewpoint, it could be more explicitly stated and supported. Instead of simply stating a belief, explain why this belief is held with clear, specific reasons and examples. This will make the argument more persuasive.

4. **Support for the point of view**: The essay starts to support the arguments with examples but stops short of fully developing these ideas. For each paragraph, aim to include a topic sentence, at least two supporting sentences that elaborate on the reason, and a clear example that illustrates the point. This approach will help in fully explaining the thought process and making the argument stronger. Using this structure can also improve the score in both the Grammar Range and Accuracy (GRA) and Cohesion and Coherence (C&C) criteria.

By extending the discussions and ensuring that each paragraph is fully developed, the essay will become more engaging and informative. Finally, regularly practicing this structured approach to writing will increase confidence and improve writing skills over time.

prompt: [ Task 2 - Discussion ] Schools are no longer necessary
essay:
There is no denying that with the wealth of information available on the Internet, students can study by themselves at home just as effectively they do at school, and therefore some people believe that schools are not needed anymore. To some extent, I agree that students can study well at home with the help of the Internet, I feel that schools still play a vital role in our society and cannot be replaced no matter what. 
 On the one hand, the opinion to learning from the Internet is attractive for several reasons. First and foremost, most of which are either free or affordable for almost everywhere. One great way is from online newspaper and video websites such as National Geographic, Youtube, Khan Academic ... which offer a wide range of topic areas suitable for people of different ages. Children can gain a great deal of knowledge about history, culture, science and many other areas which they are taught at school. They also can participate in online courses favored by a growing number of youths nowadays. As a result, this type of learning is even more advantageous in the sense that children can flexibly choose to study whatever subjects or topics that they are interested in. 
 Apart from the benefits above, I believe that formal education is irreplaceable in any society and country. It is true that students can acquire valuable knowledge at home very easily with the help of the Internet, however, the lack of teacher guidance and support is a clear disadvantage of this type of learning. For example, if students want to learn about history, there is a huge range of websites that furnish information about these topics. As a result, they may get confused and face many difficulties when choosing which one to read. Furthermore, knowledge and skills are not the only things to expect from formal school but social relationships and mental development. Children who go to school and establish friendships and can both have fun and improve their learning outcomes. 
 To draw a conclusion, while there are some benefits to learning from the Internet at home, I am of the opinion that school is irrelevant to children's learning due to the fact that it can significantly increase their understanding as well as social skills.
feedback:
The essay provides a thoughtful perspective on the topic of whether the wealth of information available on the Internet can replace traditional schools. One of the essay's strengths is the use of examples, such as online resources like National Geographic and Khan Academy, to illustrate the accessibility and variety of learning materials on the Internet. This effectively shows the potential for self-directed study at home.

However, the essay does not fully adhere to the requirements of an opinion essay. In an opinion essay, it's essential to choose and thoroughly support one clear stance. The essay starts by acknowledging the advantages of Internet-based learning but also argues that schools play an irreplaceable role in society. This creates confusion about the essay's main argument. To improve, it would be beneficial to focus solely on one viewpoint and develop it further. A more focused thesis statement, such as "I strongly believe that schools cannot be replaced by the Internet for two specific reasons," would set a clear direction for the essay.

Additionally, the essay discusses both benefits of learning from the Internet and the importance of traditional schools, which can dilute the main argument. For an opinion essay, elaborating on why schools cannot be replaced, backed by specific reasons and examples, would make the argument stronger and more convincing.

There are some areas for improvement in terms of spelling, grammar, and style. While the essay is mostly clear, careful proofreading could help refine these elements. For instance, paying attention to punctuation and consistency in list formatting (e.g., using commas or semicolons correctly) can improve readability.

The point of view is somewhat unclear due to the mixed stance on Internet learning versus traditional schooling. Clarifying this by decisively supporting one viewpoint would enhance the essay's effectiveness.

Lastly, while the essay mentions important aspects of traditional school experiences, such as social relationships and mental development, these arguments could be further developed. Providing more detailed examples and explaining how these aspects uniquely contribute to a student's education could strengthen the case for the irreplaceability of schools.

In summary, focusing on a single, clear viewpoint and expanding on the reasons and examples supporting that stance can significantly enhance the essay. Additionally, refining the spelling, grammar, and style, alongside further development of the arguments, will improve the overall quality and persuasiveness of the writing.

prompt: IELTS Task 2 - The increasing influence of the young generation
essay:
Why is this the case? 
 What impact does this have on the relationship between old and young people? 
 Young generation rules 
 Answer: 
 In today's society, it seems like the older generations are no longer a figure of authority. Rather, young people are becoming unprecedentedly influential in a number of ways. The results of this trend are various changes in the young - old generation relationship. 
 The influences that young people possess today are largely a result of technology development. Firstly, the wide availability of Internet provides not only unlimited sources of knowledge, but also new schools of thoughts and immediately updated events around the world for the youth. Such knowledge is a profound means of empowerment, as it provides young people with critical thinking skills and a more accurate view of the world around them. In addition, new means of communication, especially social media, offer a convenient platform for the young to express their opinions. As a result, young people nowadays constitute a major, influential part of public opinions on social matters. 
 As a result of this trend, the relationship between the old and young generations is undergoing profound, and mostly positive changes. Specifically, preceding generations used to be the powerhouse in the society. They were typically more knowledgeable, and thus carried more weight to their words. As young people start to be empowered by knowledge, the relationship seems to demonstrate more equality, which allows more converstion and understanding between the generations. 
 In conclusion, the rapid development of technology has given young people a more influential role in the society. Such change has made the relationship between young and old generations more equal. This appears to be a positive change since it allows generations to nurture more understanding in the inter-generation relationship.
feedback:
The essay presents an engaging perspective on the shifting dynamics between younger and older generations, attributing this change mainly to technological advancements. Here's how it can be further improved for clarity and effectiveness:

This addition would not only back the essay's claims with concrete examples but also add to the depth of analysis.

5. **Conclusion Improvements**: The concluding paragraph currently introduces a new idea, which makes the conclusion feel less like a summary and more like an ongoing discussion. 6. **Grammar and Spelling**: While the essay is generally well-written, a careful review for minor grammatical or typographic errors is always recommended to improve readability and maintain a professional tone.

By addressing these points, the essay's effectiveness and coherence would significantly improve. Ensuring each paragraph has a clear focus, directly addressing the prompt, and adequately summarizing the discussion are crucial steps for crafting a compelling argument.

prompt: Should mathematics and philosophy be optional in schools?
essay:
Learn by heart is the most common way for learning the many subjects, but, this method does not always go with maths and philosophy as these subjects mainly depend on logical thinking and broad understanding. This situation makes them more difficult and incomprehensible for many students. However, I strongly believe that making them optional in the school syllabus would not be a smart decision as at least the basic concepts of these subjects need to be learned to get on with the life. 
 Firstly, Mathematics is one of the most important subjects which is frequently using in our day to day life, and most of the mathematical concepts can practically apply to several real-world problems. Similarly, knowledge in mathematics is crucial for several professional fields such as engineering and management, therefore lots of career opportunities available around the globe for people who have extensive knowledge of mathematics. 
 Likewise, Philosophy also considered as one of the essential subjects for improving the logical thinking and inner qualities of a person. Unlike other subjects, philosophy not targets to any professional specific skills, but it helps to change the thinking style of the person to make an outstanding personality. Philosophy can improve discipline and leadership qualities which play an essential role in being a successful person. 
 However, It is true that not everyone needs to be experts in mathematics or philosophy and the choice of selecting the future career is a personal choice. But from my point of view, making them mandatory in school level would not make any unfavorable influence on child's ambition, as they can choose preferred paths at the tertiary level education targeting their future career. 
 In short, I tend to believe that the both Mathematics and Philosophy are kinds of useful subjects and every child should have at least basic knowledge about them.
feedback:
The essay provided does tackle the assigned topic by discussing whether mathematics and philosophy should be mandatory subjects in schools. However, to better align with the requirements of an opinion essay for an English proficiency test, there are several areas where improvement is necessary.

A better start might be, "While mathematical and philosophical concepts can be challenging for many, there's a debate on whether these should be optional in schools. I believe they should remain core subjects." This sets a clear direction for the essay.

2. **Structural and Stylistic Issues**: The essay should adhere to a structured format typical for Task 2 essays, which includes an introduction, three to five body paragraphs, and a conclusion. 3. **Clarity of the Author's Point of View**: Your viewpoint is evident throughout the essay; however, its presentation can be enhanced. Directly state your opinion in the introduction and use the conclusion to reiterate your stance clearly, ensuring there's no confusion about your position on making mathematics and philosophy mandatory in school curricula.

4. **Arguments and Support**: The arguments provided in favor of keeping mathematics and philosophy in the school syllabus are relevant but need to be more detailed and supported by examples. For each subject, mention specific ways they contribute to daily life, professional success, and personal growth. Also, ensuring each paragraph contains one clear idea will enhance readability and persuasiveness.

In terms of language, focusing on enhancing your vocabulary and grammar will aid in expressing your ideas more effectively. Mistakes in verb forms ("learn by heart is" should be "learning by heart is") and article usage ("the Mathematics" should just be "Mathematics") detract from the overall clarity.

Lastly, although touching on opposing viewpoints can add depth to your essay, when the prompt doesn't explicitly ask for a discussion of both sides, focus primarily on developing your argument. Incorporate the improvements suggested, particularly in organizing your essay and strengthening your thesis statement, to better meet the expectations for Task 2 essays. prompt: Student part time jobs while learning at campus
essay:

I completely agree with the idea that students should be encouraged to engage in part-time work to gain more than just money. 
 To begin with, there is no doubt that money is necessary in order for undergraduates to meet their basic needs. Therefore, a part-time job will allow them to at least pay for their tuition fees, as well as having a reasonable quality of life. Furthermore, it is evident that people nowadays are likely to find it hard to earn money, and working during school years will teach students to fully understand the true value of money in life, so that they will be able to form a saving habit, use money wisely and build spending plans, which are highly beneficial for their future. Although they might struggle to balance work and study, overcoming this will help them master time management to deal with deadlines effectively and achieve their goals as scheduled. 
 In my opinion, working while in college or university can offer many different advantages to students. Firstly, through earning, students may gain a feeling of confidence, independence, and pride in themselves, therefore they can realize their own value and have a sense of maturity. More importantly, these jobs will provide them with essential skills and useful experience that certainly improve their career prospects. For instance, because personal skills and practical experience are the key consideration when employing, candidates who have worked part-time in the past tend to be more attractive to employers when compared to those with no job experience at all.

prompt: Nothing can be done to prevent crime. To which extent do you agree or not?

As far as I concerned, infractions prevention is within our grasp if various methods are executed, such as enhancement of overall living environment of societies and incarceration process. 
 First of all, the quality of living environment plays a determining role in crime rate of a community. As opposed to those who attain high standard of living, citizens residing in poverty-stricken areas would run a much higher risk of unemployment, poor health care, discrimination and so on. Should sufficient allocation of funds be factored in, people would not turn to illegal activities at the expense of making ends meet. Such investment would not only bring about stabilization of the crime rate in a particular area, but also create equal opportunities for people to obtain, hence improving the overall prosperity and sustainability of a society. 
 Secondly, authorities should take rehabilitation as a priority over stringent punishments. To illustrate, the vicious cycle of recidivism is a pressing issue for that retribution would constitute a contributor to lawbreakers' tendency of violence rather than expected remorse for their wrongdoings. Above all, the practice of vocational training and life skills education would act as a precursor to offenders' reintegration as they are no longer have to commit crimes to make a living. Moreover, sympathy should be raised towards citizens who used to be inmates, otherwise isolation and discrimination would act as a potential catalyst for repeat offences. 
 In conclusion, the prevention of law violation is a tough process for societies to go through, but still an attainable goal if proper measures like transformation of the overall living environment and reformation be carried out.

prompt: (Task 2)Topic: Technology is being used to monitor people. Will the pros of this outweigh the cons?
essay:
Nowadays, technology is increasingly being used to monitor what people are saying and doing (for example, through cell phone tracking and security cameras). In many cases, the people being monitored are unaware that this is happening. Do you think the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages? 
 In the current society, it is widely believed that authorities are using more and more technological devices, such as CCTV and phone tracking, to keep an eye on what is done and said. In a number of situations, the individuals being observed do not know that this is happening. Although there are several positive effects of this phenomenon, they certainly cannot surpass the drawbacks associated with this trend. 
 On the one hand, there are some pros of this that are worth considering. First and foremost, because of GPS, tracking other people would certainly become less challenging. This could be used as evidence when a crime is committed. As a result, crime rates would plummet owing to the fact that people would be afraid of going to jail. To depict this point, an example worth mentioning is that in 2018, a group of robbers broke into a bank and stole all the money, but with the help of CCTV, the police caught them the following day without any noticeable efforts. 
 Nonetheless, these benefits are definitely outweighed by the drawbacks. Firstly, everyone should have their own rights of doing anything they want unless it is against the law, therefore under no circumstances should they be monitored. A crucial point worth noting is that being monitored could bring a sense of fear due to the fact that what the one being monitored has done could be publicly available on the Internet if there were a data breach. Consequently, this could lead to the death of an increasing number of people if sensitive data were leaked. A specific example of this is that in 2019, a sex tape of an internationally acclaimed singer was leaked and she committed suicide since she could not stand a chance against the general public. 
 In conclusion, even though there are some possible benefits of using technology to monitor people, the potential downsides of this are more significant.
feedback:
Your essay engages with an important and contemporary issue: the use and implications of technology for surveillance. There is a clear attempt to address the question of whether the advantages of technological surveillance outweigh the disadvantages. However, there are several areas where this essay can be improved to make your argument clearer and more compelling.

Firstly, your introduction could benefit from a more original restatement of the topic. While you’ve correctly identified the key issue at hand, your presentation closely mirrors the language and structure of the original prompt. This not only makes your essay more interesting but also showcases your language proficiency.

Secondly, since this essay asks for your viewpoint on whether the advantages outweigh the disadvantages, it's essential to focus your argument more clearly. This shows a clear line of reasoning and helps to persuade your reader. If you believe the disadvantages outweigh the advantages, as you’ve stated, ensure that the body of your essay consistently supports this perspective with clear arguments and examples.

On the matter of spelling, grammar, and stylistic issues, your essay is relatively well-written but could benefit from closer attention to detail in these areas. For instance, ensuring that your sentences are complete and your ideas are clearly expressed can make your writing more persuasive and easier to follow.

In terms of supporting your position, you’ve provided examples to illustrate both the advantages and disadvantages of surveillance technology. However, ensure that these examples directly support your viewpoint. For instance, if discussing the disadvantages, the examples should clearly show the negative impacts of surveillance rather than inadvertently presenting its benefits.

Finally, your conclusion successfully restates your position but could be strengthened by summarizing key arguments that support your viewpoint. This reinforces your stance to the reader one last time and makes your essay more memorable.

Overall, your essay has a good foundation and engages with an important topic. With more focused argumentation, original expression, and careful attention to language and structure, it can be significantly improved. Remember, clarity and consistency in your perspective and arguments are key to a strong and persuasive essay.

prompt: IELTS writing task 2: The causes and solutions of reoffending
essay:
Nowadays, there are more and more released offenders who tend to commit crimes again. The unaltered pattern of a criminal's behaviour and people's discrimination against them contributed to this phenomenon. 
 Numerous criminals choose to reoffend because prisons do not affect their mind, they still act as they did before they stayed in a cell or even worse than before. Prisons should do more to educate and rehabilitate prisoners than only to punish or imprison them. Punishment will genuinely make those offenders feel suffering, but suffering does not necessarily make them want to be proper citizens, they may still commit crime as before. They will still use illegal means to acquire others' assets or use violence to solve problems when they are out of gaol, if prisons fail to drive home to these criminals that committing crime is a shame, and the price of crime. 
 Secondly, people's prejudice against these people released from prison (even though they hope to become proper citizens) can also lead them to reoffend. Due to this discrimination, it is difficult for a former criminal to find employment, not only that critical units of the state would not accept them, but also small businesses and even they cannot be a courier or cleaner. Numerous former criminals are unable to find a job and cannot even feed themselves and their families, so they can only rob or steal others' property to make sure they can survive. 
 This trend can be tackled in two ways. First, prisons should strengthen the psychological construction of criminals, rather than just focusing on using stiff punishment. Making criminals not want to commit crimes is far more effective in reducing repeat crime than making criminals fear punishment. If an ex-criminal deeply believes that crime is shameful, he will not commit it again even if he has the ability and the opportunity. The second solution is that the government can teach these released prisoners skills which can let them survive in society and strengthen their employment. For these released offenders who want to become qualified citizens, if they can feed themselves in a legal and decent way, they are less likely to commit another crime. 
 In conclusion, prisons should pay more attention to the psychological education of prisoners. And in the meantime, offering jobs to ex-offenders could also help tackle the rise in reoffending. ( 389 words)
feedback:
The essay provides a thoughtful discussion on why released offenders might reoffend and suggests solutions to mitigate this issue. Here are some points for improvement, focusing on the essay's alignment with the topic, spelling, grammar, stylistic issues, clarity of the author's viewpoint, and the support for their arguments.

1. **Response to the Topic**: The essay directly addresses the assigned topic by discussing the reasons behind reoffending and proposing ways to reduce it. This strength ensures the essay remains focused and relevant throughout.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, and Stylistic Issues**: There are minor errors and opportunities for stylistic improvement. For example, more varied sentence structures could enhance readability and engagement. Be cautious with word choice to avoid repetition and to maintain a formal tone suitable for an essay. Also, reviewing the difference between "gaol" and "jail" might be beneficial, considering the context and audience.

3. **Clarity of Point of View**: The viewpoint is clear: the essay argues that to reduce reoffending, more emphasis should be placed on the psychological rehabilitation of prisoners and support for their reintegration into society. This perspective is consistently maintained throughout the essay.

4. **Arguments Support**: The essay successfully employs descriptive arguments to support the viewpoint. However, to strengthen these arguments, incorporating evidence, such as statistics or studies, could be highly effective. Moreover, ensuring each argument directly ties back to how it addresses the issue of reoffending would solidify your position.

5. **Structure and Conciseness**: While the detailed discussion enriches the essay, maintaining conciseness is critical. Aim for a maximum of five sentences per paragraph to keep your writing focused and impactful. This approach not only aligns with the standard essay format but also helps in clearly conveying your messages without over-discussion. The suggestion here is to streamline the content to fit within a more compact structure while still clearly presenting your thoughts and findings.

6. **Additional Recommendations**: Consider dividing the essay into four distinct paragraphs to match the standard essay format more closely. This structure typically includes an introduction, two body paragraphs, each addressing a key point, and a conclusion that summarizes the arguments and reiterates the main stance. This organization could aid in clarity and make the essay more navigable for readers.

In conclusion, your essay demonstrates a strong understanding of the topic and presents valid points. Focusing on refining the structure, enhancing the clarity and precision of your arguments, and addressing minor grammatical issues will significantly improve its effectiveness and readability. Keep up the good work, and continue to develop your essay writing skills by incorporating this feedback.

prompt: Cooperation and competition are imperative and children should master both of these skills
essay:
While some are in favor of nourishing a competitive schooling environment, others hold the belief that children are more likely to be valuable team players when collaboration is cultivated. In my opinion, these skills are equally important and children will vastly benefit from sustaining a proper environment where both cooperation and competition are deliberately nurtured. 
 On the one hand, being competitive could bring about a number of advantages. Firstly, it helps bring out the best in children. In spite of criticisms regarding its rather catastrophic consequences on children physical and mental development, competition is an indispensable trait for those who thirst for triumphs in both sport and scientific fields. For example, if inventors had been content to sustain the status quote, steam locomotives would have been the only mean of long-distant transportation. Secondly, children are prone to develop critical social skills through competing with other students. Regardless of the result which is either win or loss, they will be able to learn the value of hard-work, strengthen their self-esteem and tenacity. More importantly, they would acknowledge that life is a series of ups and downs, and failure will not be the end of the world. 
 On the other hand, no one could deny the magnitude of cooperation. In addition to providing cooperative skills that are necessary later in their working lives, students also recognize that everybody has their own limitations. In other words, each of them is excellent in something but is dreadful at another thing and there is no mean to achieve success rather than working closely together. Moreover, collaborating helps ease pressure on kids, which is a major drawback caused by intense competition. A child who is lagged behind in math would benefit from the aid of their classmates in exchange for a free art lesson that he or she excels in. Consequently, students become more tolerant and proud of their aptitudes. 
 In conclusion, cooperation and competition are imperative and children would be best benefited from mastering both of them to the extent that a proper setting is promoted. 
 (341 words) 
 =======
feedback:

1. **Response to the Topic**:

Yet, it's crucial to refine how the introduction is crafted. The initial part of an essay should paraphrase the prompt and briefly introduce the discussion points without going into detailed arguments. Avoid presenting your full opinion or detailed discussion in the introduction; instead, save the in-depth analysis for the body paragraphs.

prompt: Shortage of physical exercise is a prevailing situation among citizens
essay:
Shortage of physical exercise is a prevailing situation among citizens 
 This essay will examine the main causes of physical exertion loss and possible solutions to this problem. 
 The two main causes of workout shortfall are citizens' busy work schedules and the popularity of sedentary leisure activities. Since living costs in metropolises are tremendous, citizens tend to spend most of their time working, even at the weekend. As a result, they hardly ever have time for physical activity. According to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, Americans worked an average of 34. 4 hours per week. Besides, engaging in screen time exercises such as watching TV or playing computer games seems to be a trendy way to relax these days. Hence, time spent doing sports or outdoor games has reduced significantly. A new study shows that the average American has more than five hours of leisure time a day, while only 20 minutes is for exercise. 
 a number of possible solutions to this problem are raising people's awareness and installing more fitness equipment. When metropolises residents are fully aware of regular exercise's significance, they would invest more time participating in active exercise or doing workouts. Additionally, since more training device is set up in parks and other public areas, people tend to join in more exertion. Take Le Thi Rieng Park in Vietnam for example, it has attracted an increasing number of local residents after being equipped with more equipment. Besides, the government should build more bicycle lanes and make sidewalks safer in order to inspire more citizens to cycle or walk to walk. 
 To conclude, hectic city life and new leisure activities are the cause of the reduction in time for physical exercising. However, we can significantly boost by raising alertness and providing more appliances
feedback:
Your essay effectively addresses the topic by identifying the main causes and potential solutions to the issue of decreasing physical exercise among citizens. However, to enhance your essay and align it with English proficiency test standards, consider the following points for improvement:

1. **Response to the Topic:**

It was noticed that the essay could have been stronger by directly linking the causes and solutions to your personal stance on the issue.

   - Work on sentence structure to avoid overly long sentences that could confuse readers. Break complex ideas into simpler, clearer sentences.

3. **Clarity of the Author's Point of View:**
   - Make your viewpoint more explicit throughout the essay, starting from the introduction. Clearly state your position on the issue at hand to guide the reader through your argumentation.

4. **Arguments and Support:**
   - Each paragraph should fully develop one main idea. For instance, when discussing causes or solutions, ensure each is explored thoroughly rather than briefly mentioned. This can be achieved by expanding on each point with examples or further explanation rather than listing them.
   - Avoid single-sentence explanations as they tend to undermine the development of your arguments. Each cause and solution should be adequately explained and supported with evidence or examples where possible.

5. **Conclusion:**

prompt: IELTS: ... To what extent do you think laws are needed to make people recycle more of their waste ?
essay:
Recycling is one of the key topics in our modernization life, especially when there are many issues is occurring on our planet such as Global Warming, Climate Changes, Animals Extinction and so on. It's a critical responsibility of human beings to protect our environment, to safeguard our future. But in fact, the amounts of waste are being recycled is just minimal and it is not fast enough to catch up with the rate the human are disposing the trash into natural habitat. In such scenario, governments should enforce some kind of movements to make recycling activities more efficient. 
 The legal requirement which is given by the government is the most powerful facilitator for the changes to happen. The truth is most people understand the responsibility of recycling plastic bags, disposed papers,... but very few of them take it seriously. It is their habit that makes them tend to resist of recycling seemly because they are getting used to what they do every single day. In order to change a habit, it has never been easy. Law enforcement to some extent is the necessary switch that kills these harmful habits and forcing people adapt to the new changes. Let look at Singapore in the 1900s, people are used to splitting chewing-gum on the rail train and causing the disruption of the subway system. Singapore government subsequently had issued an official ban on chewing-gum consumption to prevent further breakdown of their railway system. The law requirement has put an end to the way Singaporean habit of eating chewing gum definitely and furthermore, Singapore government has even addressed high penalty on throwing waste in the public. As a result, Singaporean tend to be extremely careful whenever they try to dispose of the garbage; and there will be no surprise that Singapore is one of world cleanest country. 
 On the other hand, the law is simple acted as an awareness activity. People will not know what they need to do until they are told to do so. When children are born, they hardly know what is right, what is wrong. It is the parental guidance, social etiquette and principal laws that show them the right things. For instance, we won't know whether crossing the street when the traffic light is red is wrong until the laws mentions. Government laws are general agreements amongst people in society which create boundaries to shape our behaviors. Through conventional consensus, people will practice actions unconsciously in a long-term run. One way or another, it might put a seed of awareness or educate our next generations to protect their future home and their environment. 
 After all, recycling is still an individual awareness and responsibility at the moment; yet legal requirements might need to be issued to generalize the actions and to enforce the changes of old bad habits.
