 On the one hand, helping other people and contributing to the community have the merits of a student's mental health and career path. Firstly, a lot of assignments, continuous exams in universities sometimes make students become stressed. Volunteering can help them to fight against the negative effects of the school. By helping others, dopamine, which reduces stress and increases positive and relaxed feelings, is released. Furthermore, by volunteering, students have the opportunity to gain many valuable skills such as problem - solving and teamwork which can secure their dream jobs after college. 
 On the other hand, being a volunteer might not be feasible for all university pupils. The first reason involves students with disabilities. These people have difficulties in finding a volunteering job which often demands a good physical condition. Moreover, they might suffer from negative attitudes by others and tend to feel lonely. The second reason is that the idea can create pressure on introverted people who tend to live their lives behind closed doors. Volunteers need to be able to work well with others, whereas introverts are not interested in networking events and meeting new people. 
 In conclusion, while there are many advantages for students to participate in voluntary projects to help local communities, it is unrealistic to expect all college students to be a part of voluntary organizations.

prompt: The international community should reduce or eliminate the debt of the world's poorest countries
essay:
Nowadays, it has been observed that the developed countries provide financial aid in terms of debt, to the under-developed nations. There is a proposal to either completely waive-off or lower down the debt given to these countries. I partially agree with the proposal. 
 On one hand, completely writing-off or reducing the debt of the poorest countries will help in the growth and development of these countries. By taking financial aid from the developed nations, the underdeveloped countries are trapped in a vicious circle. They utilize this amount to improve the infrastructure of the country and in providing an efficient and advanced healthcare facility to its citizens. However, in order to pay back the loan amount along with huge interests, they end up utilizing their nations reserve. Henceforth, by waiving off the loan amount, they would concentrate on implementing measures on improving the economic conditions and the standard of living of the population instead of diverting their focus on exploring options of paying back the amount. 
 On the other hand, lowering or nullifying the debt amount of the underdeveloped nations would create a negative impact on the developed countries. As per the international treaties, legal and ethical rules and regulations have been laid down to provide financial aid to these countries. Exempting the poor countries from financial liabilities will be considered, a biased approach. This would create negativity and may disturb the peace and harmony of the nations across the world. 
 In my opinion, it is a good option to lower down the debt amount of the underdeveloped nations to boost their economy. However, the amount should not be completely waived-off. As these nations could take undue advantages in the future, by making it a practice. They could completely get dependant on these financial aids for the development of the nation. 
 To conclude, reducing or eliminating the loan amount of the poor countries can contribute to the overall growth of these nations. However, this could lead to unrest in different parts of the world. Henceforth, the proposal should be planned wisely before executing it.

In crafting future essays, remember to directly answer the question posed by the prompt with a clear expression of your stance, then build your arguments around that position with specific evidence. This approach will make your essays stronger and more focused on the task at hand.

prompt: IELTS task 2 - opinion: whether the personality we re born with or life experience matter more
essay:
The root of persona has always been a mystery since human began to study about ourselves. There are researches suggesting that our original personality has more impact on our life than any the experiences that we have endured. Personally, I believe that life experience plays a more important role in crafting our personality than the one that we are born with, and this essay will further outlined my opinion. 
 The first reason is experiences can make changes in human psyche. Humans have a tendency to create or alter a personality trait after overcoming circumstances they have experienced before. When encountering a situation in life, the emotions that a person felt in similar circumstances have been memorized and become a natural response, also known as characteristic. In 1990, the American Psychiatric Association has carried out a research on 50000 US soldiers that had joined the war in Viet Nam to see how impactful a traumatic experience is to human personality. The results supported their prediction, as 78% of the participants were diagnosed to have PTSD and other relating symptoms, the most common symptom recorded was changes in personality. 
 Furthermore, not only the feeling relating to events, but also the lesson that we collected from those events can cause severe transformation in personality. Past experiences teach us many valuable lessons and sometimes are able to completely alter our ideal and perspective which result in changes in characteristic. For example, if an individual met a very good and influential mentor in the past, he or she will adopt some of the beneficial personality traits from the mentor. The mentor helps that person to change the way of thinking, by teaching both academic knowledge and knowledge about basic savoir vivre in life. As the result, a lot of the habits that make up the traits of personality are replaced by the learned traits. 
 To sum up, experiences in life contributes lately to the making of personality than the ones we were born with, because of its severe psychological and perspective alteration. Therefore, being aware of the change and their negative effects is crucial, as preventions should be made to cause no further damage to ourselves and others.
feedback:

2. **Length and Structure:** This essay is quite lengthy for the time constraints typical of English proficiency tests. 5. **Argumentation and Evidence:** The essay makes effective use of examples to illustrate how life experiences can influence personality. However, referring to specific studies or data, as seen with the mention of the American Psychiatric Association and PTSD statistics, should be approached with caution. In conclusion, while the essay demonstrates a thoughtful consideration of the topic, focusing on conciseness, simplification of language, and careful selection of evidence within the constraints of an English proficiency test will make your argument stronger and more compelling. prompt: IELTS Writing -- Are the older generations' ideas still useful nowadays?

prompt: An IELTS task 2 essay on children under pressure in modern society
essay:
Today many children find themselves stressed out because of pressure from by schools, companies, and society. While reasons for this vary, we can take some actions to help kids remove their emotional baggage. 
 A number of factors contribute to the pressure put on children in modern society. First of all, from the academic aspect, young students are forced by adults, such as teachers and parents, to study harder and get good grades. While this pressure is not intentionally harmful, it might create more anxiety for young students. Secondly, children can be abused by a huge crowd via social media. An innocent kid using Facebook can be attacked by Internet trolls and fall into depression, while the culprits remain at large. Regarding pressures caused by business, many children, who have no regular income, struggle to stifle their impulse to buy new and fancy things such as toys and clothing coming out every day. As a result, kids can feel disappointed if not satisfied, and in long term, this may lead to mental issues. 
 There are some endeavours could be done to reverse this alarming situation. Adults should encourage children to take part in entertainment activities such as sports or singing to divert them from academic pressures. In addition, a punishment system should be introduced to keep hate speech at bay and keep cyberspace a safe place for teenagers. Finally, the government may restrict commercials that target children as a way to help them cope with insatiable desires. 
 In conclusion, adults are responsible for the burdens put on kids today, and it is our job to make sure that every child has a carefree childhood.
feedback:
Your essay addresses an important issue - the stress children face due to various pressures from schools, companies, and society. You've showcased an understanding of the topic and offered relevant suggestions to mitigate this issue. However, there are a few areas that could be improved to enhance the clarity and effectiveness of your essay.

1. **Language and Style**: Your essay leans towards a casual tone in certain parts. For example, the phrase "emotional baggage" is more common in casual conversations than in formal academic writing. Academically, we aim for precision and clarity without relying on colloquialisms or slang. This ensures that your argument is taken seriously and understood by all readers. Consider replacing such phrases with more formal alternatives that accurately convey the complex issues being discussed.

2. **Organization**: The current structure of your essay merges several critical points into one long paragraph, which makes it challenging to follow your arguments. A more effective approach would be to adopt a three-paragraph reasoning format, dedicating one paragraph to each major point you wish to discuss. This structured approach allows you to explore each argument fully, providing the reader with a clearer understanding of your perspective. For instance, separating reasons for pressure on children from solutions can make your essay more coherent.

3. **Focus on Clarity**: There's a sense that the essay attempts to showcase a wide vocabulary, which is commendable. However, the primary goal of academic writing is to communicate ideas clearly and efficiently. Focusing on creating coherent and concise sentences will improve the overall readability of your essay. Aim to be informative rather than impressive - it's about making sure the reader understands and is persuaded by your arguments.

4. **Development of Arguments**: While you've identified significant sources of stress for children, further elaboration on these points could strengthen your argument. Additionally, the solutions proposed would benefit from more detailed explanations on how they can be effectively implemented. It's crucial that each idea is fully explored to convincingly support your position.

In summary, your essay tackles an important topic with relevance and insight. By adopting a more formal tone, organizing your points more clearly, focusing on clarity, and fully developing your arguments, your writing will not only meet the requirements of a Task 2 essay but also communicate your ideas more effectively. Remember, the goal is to inform and engage your reader through clear and coherent writing. Keep practicing, and you'll see improvement in your ability to express complex ideas in a structured and compelling manner.

prompt: The methodology of interacting with individuals have changed through time
essay:
Question: 
 Nowadays the way people interact with each other has changed because of technology. In what ways has technology affected the types of relationships people make? Has this become a positive or a negative development? 
 Answer: 
 Yes, with the reference to the present technology, the methodology of interacting with individuals have changed through time. It has both positive and negative influence on the kinds of relationships people create these days. 
 Decades back when communicative devices were not invented, people used to communicate with each other by writing letters from one place to another. In some cases, if the letter had to be dropped to far away lands, it would take few days or weeks or even a month or two. Presently, an individual's access to other people has extended widely all due to the flourishing technology. Firstly, the innovative gadgets have effortlessly made it easier for people to interact with others residing on any nook and corner of the globe which has given ways of perceiving each other's cultural disparity. Secondly, there are several social networking sites and applications such as Facebook, Instagram, WeChat, etc which has enabled people to make new friends anytime. Finally, technology has fostered the efficiency of people who are involved in specific businesses. Internet has become a magnificent source of advertising their products and also in gaining online customers. For an instance, many entrepreneurs have been successful in attracting their products to the customers by using their expertise in maintaining professional relationships with customers via internet such as "Daraz" i.e an online shopping application. 
 On the contrary, it is depressing to note that people have started urging for validation from social networking sites. Their level of happiness has solely become dependent upon the number of likes and comments they acquire on their posted pictures or videos. Moreover, people are connected to millions of users across the globe but virtual interactions cannot justify the significance of a real conversation. While, scrolling down to the list of hundreds of friends, there may be very limited amount of people to whom an individual looks up to in the real world. People's negligence of their surrounding loved ones due to their obsessiveness to technology has been realized these days. Furthermore, chances of scams and fraudulent accounts are very high which might make people fall under heinous cyber crimes all because of trusting a deceitful account. 
 Thus, technology have had both positive as well as negative enhancement to the kinds of relationships people make these days.
feedback:
The essay provided is a direct response to the question of how technology affects the types of relationships people make, and whether this development is positive or negative. However, there are several areas where improvements could make the essay more effective and clear.

Firstly, the introduction needs to thoroughly set up the topic by paraphrasing the original question and clearly stating your position or thesis towards the end of the paragraph. As it stands, the opening statement jumps directly to acknowledging the impact of technology without properly setting the context or declaring a clear stance.

Regarding the essay structure, it's important to note that it should consistently support a single, clear opinion throughout, rather than presenting a comparative view of both positive and negative aspects. This task calls for a definitive stance to be argued convincingly across the essay, which is not fully achieved in the current presentation. The analysis of how technology affects relationships should therefore focus on defending one viewpoint with reasoned arguments and examples, rather than straddling both sides of the debate.

Moreover, while the essay does a good job of providing examples to illustrate how technology impacts relationships, it falters in delivering a compelling argument for a singular viewpoint. Strengthening the essay requires selecting either a positive or negative stance on technological impact and then deeply exploring this angle with clear and descriptive arguments.

The conclusion also mirrors the introduction's shortfall by not summarizing the key points discussed or reaffirming the thesis statement effectively. A well-crafted conclusion should recap the discussion, restate the essay's main argument in a new way, and leave the reader with a lasting impression of the essay's significance.

In terms of language and style, the essay generally communicates ideas clearly but could benefit from closer attention to grammatical structures and variety in sentence construction for a more engaging read. Ensuring that each sentence flows naturally into the next will improve the coherence and readability of the essay.

Lastly, while the use of examples such as social media platforms and online business relationships is pertinent, it would enhance the essay to dive deeper into how these examples specifically support the chosen stance. Demonstrating not just the existence of technology's impact, but its profound influence on the quality and nature of human relationships in line with your argument, will make for a more persuasive essay.

By focusing on these areas for improvement—clarifying the thesis, committing to a single viewpoint, refining the introduction and conclusion, and enhancing the depth of argumentation—the essay will become more coherent, compelling, and aligned with the task's requirements.

prompt: IELTS task 2: The Duty to Educate Children
essay:
There is much controversy about whether schools and teachers should take the responsibility to educate children to become people who can bring positive effects to our society. However, I believe that parents should be the role models for their children and educate them. 
 There are several reasons why some people might think school is a suitable place for children to learn to behave. Firstly, the main purpose of attending school is to acquire knowledge and socialize. Students can not only learn fundamental knowledge but also study how to communicate with others at school. As a result, teachers should focus on students' performance at both academy and social behavior. Secondly, peers play an important role on affecting children' behavior. Since teenagers can easily be influenced by their classmates and friends, a good environment and education become crucial for leading them to become good members of society. 
 In spite of the above arguments, parents should take more responsibility for their children. The main reason is that parents have to take care of their children whom they give birth to. Parents should spend more time than teachers to educate and company their children when they grow up. Another factor is that children imitate their parents' action. Parents should act as a positive role model to encourage their children to become good members of society and prevent them from setting up negative habits, such as smoking, gambling and breaking laws. 
 In conclusion, although schools can educate students to have good behavior, I think that parents, the people give birth to their children, should take more responsibility and put more effort on teaching their next generation.
feedback:
Your essay tackles an important topic regarding who should bear the responsibility for educating children to become positive members of society. You have made some good points in your essay, but there are areas that require improvement to enhance clarity, alignment with the topic, and the presentation of your viewpoints. Let's consider these aspects more closely to see how you can refine your essay further.

1. **Response to the Topic:**
It's essential that your essay directly addresses the question or statement provided. In your case, the focus is on whether schools or parents should play a significant role in the moral and social education of children. While you did touch upon this subject, you primarily concentrated on one viewpoint, advocating for the role of parents, without thoroughly examining the role that schools might play. Moreover, the way you introduced the essay suggested a broader controversy than what the topic might explicitly state. Instead of stating "there is much controversy," more directly acknowledge what the discussion is about, such as: "The topic of who holds the primary responsibility for educating children to be good members of society - schools or parents - is an ongoing discussion."

2. **Spelling, Grammar, or Stylistic Issues:**
Your essay is generally well-written, but there are moments where clearer and more precise language could be used to strengthen your argument. Additionally, watch for the correct use of plurals and possessive forms ('academy' should be 'academic performance', 'company' should be 'accompany'). For a smoother flow, try varying your sentence structures and ensure your ideas logically progress from one to the next.

3. **Point of View Clarity:**
Your perspective on the issue, while present, should be stated more distinctly and developed further. In an essay that discusses two opposing viewpoints, it’s crucial to explore both perspectives before presenting your own. This helps provide a balanced argument and highlights your ability to consider multiple facets of an issue before drawing a conclusion. Integrate your viewpoint as a separate section within the body of your essay, rather than introducing it for the first time in the conclusion. This structure allows for a more comprehensive exploration of your perspective.

4. **Arguments and Support:**
You've provided arguments mainly supporting the role of parents, using examples such as role modeling and time spent with children. To strengthen your essay, it would be beneficial to also discuss how schools and teachers contribute to a child's education in morality and social behaviors. This is not only about presenting another side of the argument but about enriching your essay with a broader understanding of the topic. Ensure each argument is clearly stated and supported with examples or explanations.

In conclusion, while your essay presents a valuable perspective, greater balance in discussing both parental and school roles, clearer articulation of your viewpoint, and attention to language details would greatly improve your essay. By addressing these points, you'll be able to craft a more compelling and comprehensive argument that more effectively addresses the topic.

prompt: Discuss "Globalization: a positive or negative development?"
essay:
With the relentless development of society come novel conceptions for global citizens, which include globalization. From all accounts, ones should get accustomed to life in times of globalization for the advantages it brings about, while a minority of people disagree on its benefits. From my perspective, humanity would benefit more from a world without globalization rather than regard it as a positive development. 
 On the one hand, extreme rate of globalization can result in culture shock, as some cultures that are considered appropriate in one region can be deemed as unusual or even immoral in other parts of the world. For instance, while in most of the western countries, childless couples are becoming increasingly common, a majority of residents of the eastern culture believe that the final purpose of marriage is to have children to continue the bloodline. Moreover, the over-integration of one culture into another may lead to culture homogenization on grounds of some individuals' propensity to abandon their own culture and replicate the others to affirm their uniqueness in public. Likewise, religious conflicts can happen more frequently due to disputes over diferent faiths and religions. 
 One the other hand, globalization at a suitable rate can serve as a tool of education for those who want to broaden their horizon about other cultures and prevent culture shock for those who intend to study abroad or reside in a foreign country. On top of that, the global economy can be stimulated by the promotion of international and intercontinental trade and international communication will be facilitated, resulting from the emergence of cultures and, hence, universal languages. 
 In conclusion, I believe that globalization at the present time does not have the adequate capacity to make its upsides outweigh the drawbacks.
feedback:
The essay provides a thoughtful take on the topic of globalization, presenting both its advantages and disadvantages. However, to align more closely with the original prompt, which focuses on the negative aspects of globalization, there are adjustments that could enhance the clarity and persuasiveness of the argument.

1. **Response to the Topic:**
   The essay initially addresses the prompt by mentioning globalization's impacts but diverges by discussing both positive and negative aspects. The task requires a focus on the negative impacts of globalization only. Concentrating on these aspects would make the essay more relevant to the prompt. Try to adjust your argument to emphasize the negative consequences more directly and exclusively.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, or Stylistic Issues:**
   There are minor spelling errors (e.g., "diferent" should be "different") and some sentences could be simplified for clearer understanding. Consider breaking down complex sentences into simpler ones to enhance readability. Paying attention to spelling and simplifying language can significantly improve the overall quality of your essay.

3. **Point of View Clarity:**
   Your point of view that globalization has more downsides than upsides comes through, but it's slightly diluted by the comparative discussion of positives and negatives. To make your viewpoint clearer, try to focus solely on the negative impacts, as required by the prompt. This will also help strengthen your argument and make your position more evident to the reader.

4. **Arguments and Support:**
   The essay provides descriptive arguments on both sides of the globalization debate, which shows a good grasp of the subject. However, to comply with the essay prompt, modify your discussion to employ a comparative method more strategically: mention the positive aspect of globalization followed by a more detailed elaboration on its negative impacts. For example, while globalization facilitates international trade, it could also be argued that it exerts pressure on local businesses and laborers, threatening local cultures and economies. This approach would not only adhere to the prompt's requirements but also make your arguments more compelling and focused on the negative implications as requested.

By refining the focus on the negative effects of globalization, addressing minor language issues, and adopting a comparative method that highlights the downsides more starkly, the essay can be significantly improved. This will not only align your work more closely with the guidelines but also enhance the coherence and persuasive power of your argument.

prompt: IELTS2 When you are in Rome, do as the Romans do; visitors should follow local customs and behaviour
essay:

This essay will discuss both views in detail and give the conclusion. 
 On the one hand, following suit to the traditions of a country is believed to be the stolid proof indicating that travellers are respectful to other different cultures and assisting to broaden your horizon about the new civilization. For instance, when you traverse to a destination, you do not have any foggiest idea about their social norms, you want to ask for a direction to somewhere but gesticulating a strange gesture considered impoliteness in the host country, the local citizens would not want to guide you anymore because your manners make them feel offended.  On the other hand, every individual is explicitly nurtured in multi-cultural surroundings, thus their perceptions and social manners are not the same, that's why they cannot gain an insight into other's customs. However, if the local habitants don't criticize but welcomely to impart the visitors what are your customs and traditions and address how vital they are in your nation, it would render an attraction about the local hospitable behaviours that rivets a good image to the travellers which bring them back to your country consecutive times, creating a great deal of beneficial aspects in terms of tourism and economy.

prompt: Parents or school? Who will teach children to be good citizens?
essay:

 The responsibility of adults is how to teach children to be good citizens of society. While others suppose that children are taught at school, which educates children to be good members of the community. Nevertheless, I strongly believe that parents can teach children to be good citizens. 
 Firstly, schools are admitted that have a standard educational curriculum. So that their educational procedure in instructing children is thorough and wide knowledge Also, it bases on the abundant experiment of teachers. Secondly, teachers in school are more tough and strict with their students. Because teachers have no blood relation with their students so they will not pamper children too much. In addition, they are willing to use forceful measures in order to help children recognize children's fallibility. 
 On the other hand, parents are the closest people beside their children. Thus, children are being affected by every action and speech throughout children's adulthood so that parents can teach children the right things in children's own life easily. For instance, they have relevant teaching methods with their children because of understanding children's personality. Moreover, parents who are experienced people can instruct children best. The reason for that is parental love, which leads them to always hope and teach their children to avoid mistakes in parent's past. 
 In conclusion, I think that parents are always the people nearby and proficient adults who educate children to be good citizens in the future.
feedback:

However, it’s important to accurately represent the perspectives mentioned in the prompt. Instead of stating it as a general fact that it's the responsibility of adults, it should be clarified that some people believe parents specifically (not adults in general) should be responsible for this. This distinction is crucial for accurately addressing the essay prompt. Additionally, the stance should be articulated as what one believes should happen, rather than what can happen, to align with the essay's argumentative nature.

It would help if specific reasons were given as to why schools might not fulfill this role as effectively as parents, making the author's point of view more understandable.

Clarifying why the characteristics of schools (e.g., a strict environment) might not be as conducive to teaching citizenship as parental influence would strengthen the argument. Also, incorporating examples or more detailed reasoning could make the case more convincing.

Improving these aspects would make the essay stronger, clearer, and more persuasive. Aim to use specific and accurate language that directly addresses the essay prompt, and ensure that both sides of the argument are explored and supported with clear, logical reasoning before stating a personal opinion. This approach will not only improve the coherence of the argument but also help in making a more compelling case for the reader.

prompt: Is it true that the vegetarian diet is more beneficial for health than eating meat?

 There is currently a contentious argument over whether the vegetarian diet is more beneficial for health than eating meat. I somewhat agree with this idea because the following reasons. 
 The main reason why I agree that raising many poultry and cattle to supply food for humans is unnecessary is because vegetable and cereal contain vitamins, minerals, proteins, and vital others which are sufficient to maintain life functions for humans. To illustrate, people could replace cow's milk with soy milk to implement Calcium and still ensure that the quality and the content of Calcium derived from the bean is equivalent to the ones in animals. 
 The second reason why I support the notion that eating some kinds of meat could be harmful to health is due to the consumption of meat is associated with an increased risk of cancer as well as heart disease. For example, saturated fat which is found in beef and pork causes the cancers of breast and colon. Moreover, methods of cooking meat at high temperature would create toxic compounds, this leads to not only nutrient loss but also unwanted health consequences such as cardiovascular diseases. 
 However, pregnant women and children are not suitable for a vegetarian diet because the vegetable products could not meet their increased demand at that time. The lack of meat-derived nourishment in a daily meal would lead to malnutrition. 
 In conclusion, I partly agree that eating meat is unnecessary because vegetable consumption could supply nutritive substances inadequately for daily actions, and eating some kind of meat has a bad effect on health. However, pregnant woman and children need to eat meat to ensure that their body is not malnutrition.

prompt: The older generation tend to have very traditional ideas about how people should live, think, behave
essay:
It is sometimes argued that traditional values are useless for young people in this continuing changeable modern world. While I agree with the idea that some of these ideas are unhelpful, I would argue that others are still valuable. 
 Indeed, some traditional views from the elderly are undeveloped and end up resulting in harmfulness to specific groups. The first unreasonable one is gender biases regarding the condition of the woman. In some of the Arabic nations, women do not have the right to attend schools. Even some of them do have acquired higher education certifications overseas, the proportion of female holding a higher is still low. Second, gender definition is more flexible nowadays. An increasing number of people in the LGBTQ group out of the closet and are willing to show the world who they really are. But such behaviours are completely unacceptable for people holding very traditional ideas. These people tend to believe that either transgender or gay/lesbian is a sin or mental illness. Such opinions limit the right of minorities to some extent. Therefore, there is no place for such ideas in this open-minded era. 
 However, despite these prejudices, conventional ideas do play a vital and functional role in society, especially for a region's culture. For example, every Chinese read and learn the philosophy of Confucianism, from learning how to enhance the relationship with families, friends or even the world, to behaving brave, honest and gentle, respecting not only the elders but everyone around them. Such values came from 5000 years ago, and still play a central role as a guidebook in Chinese culture. And I do believe that these qualities are still valuable now. Besides, whether an idea is practical or not should be concluded after being practiced. 
 To sum up, although some of the conservative ideas are useless or even harmful, I would believe that most of them still need to be valued by every generation. In addition, the attitude towards traditional thoughts should not be single-sided, whether useful or not should be proved by human beings and the time.
feedback:
The essay provides a thoughtful perspective on the relevance of traditional values in the modern world. It highlights a balanced view, acknowledging both the limitations and the importance of these values. However, there are several areas that could be improved to enhance clarity, coherence, and alignment with the essay prompt's expectations.

1. **Response to the Topic:** The prompt likely asks to what extent you agree or disagree with the view that traditional values are obsolete for today's youth. Your response should more explicitly reflect this by using phrases like "to a partial extent" or "I agree to a high/low extent because..." This will directly address the question and make your position clearer.

2. **Word Count and Time Management:** Consider practicing writing under timed conditions. Aim for an essay length of 250-275 words to mirror test constraints, allocating time for planning, drafting, and revising. This discipline will help you write concisely and allocate sufficient time for editing, which is crucial for refining your essay.

3. **Sentence Structure and Grammar:** Be cautious with sentence structure. Avoid starting a sentence with "but" or overly relying on commas, which can lead to run-on sentences. Instead, aim for a mix of simple and complex sentences. Creating complex sentences by attaching clauses with commas before conjunctions can help avoid abrupt topic shifts and improve readability.

4. **Paragraph Organization:** Each paragraph should focus on a single topic. The essay occasionally mixes multiple ideas within paragraphs, which can dilute the argument's effectiveness and clarity. By dedicating each paragraph to a single idea, your essay will have a stronger, more coherent structure. This approach will also help avoid presenting a scattered discussion.

5. **Use of Examples and Arguments:** The arguments supporting your views, such as the examples from Chinese culture, are valuable but need to be succinct and directly related to the topic. Ensure each example clearly ties back to your main argument about the value of traditional ideas in the modern context.

6. **Clarity of Opinion:** While your essay presents a nuanced view, ensuring that your opinion is clear from the outset and consistently supported throughout can strengthen your argument. Make sure to reiterate your stance in the conclusion to leave a lasting impression on your reader.

By addressing these points, you can enhance the effectiveness of your essay. Focus on clearly articulating your stance, organizing your essay well, and adhering to time management strategies. This will not only make your arguments more persuasive but also align your writing more closely with English proficiency test expectations.

prompt: Media focus far too much on the personal lives and relationships of different celebrities
essay:
Nowadays, the media is expanding at a faster rate than ever before. It focuses far too much on the personal lives and relationships of such celebrities as actors, singers, and football players. Although this type of program is very popular among people, particularly youngsters, I personally believe it should pay more attention to ordinary people's lives instead. 
 Firstly, it is normal men and women who also devote their entire lives to uplifting the country. These citizens should be portrayed in the best possible way so that they can feel encouraged and get the motivation to strive for better performance. For example, volunteers taking part in a non-profit organization which assists the needy will find it overjoyed and heart-warming if they know that their positive actions have spread the message of love and help to those around them, and have given them the inspiration to join meaningful activities. 
 Secondly, excessive news about celebrities' personal lives might be an infringement of their privacy. It will be tremendously annoying and perhaps stressful for famous people to be observed by hundreds of cameras that have been set up for celebrity "spotting". Their daily activities, meetings and even love affairs, for instance, can be revealed without their permission. In fact, if there are bad rumors about them, their hard-earned reputation and trustworthiness may be ruined before they can prove that rumors are false. 
 In conclusion, I firmly hold the opinion that the mass media should spend more time reporting the lives of ordinary people instead of concentrating solely on the lives of stars.
feedback:

1. Organization and Structure: To make your argument more impactful, consider rearranging your paragraphs. Starting with the discussion on how the excessive focus on celebrities can infringe upon their privacy sets a strong foundation for your argument. 2. Conclusion: The closing segment of your essay needs to encapsulate your main arguments more effectively. Currently, it reiterates your stance without summarizing the key points made throughout the essay. A well-crafted conclusion should briefly recap the arguments presented, reinforcing why more media focus on ordinary people's lives is beneficial. Aim for at least two sentences, summarizing your discussion points to solidify your argument.

3. Spelling, Grammar, and Style: There are minor spelling and grammar issues that need attention. Additionally, consider varying your sentence structure to enhance readability and keep the reader engaged. Aim for a mix of simple and complex sentences to provide clarity while also demonstrating proficiency in English.

4. Supporting Arguments: Your arguments are clear and you've provided examples to support your view. To further strengthen your essay, consider adding statistics or studies to support your claim about the negative effects of focusing too much on celebrities. Adding this type of evidence can make your argument more convincing.

Overall, your essay is on the right track with a clear and relevant point of view. By focusing on reorganizing your content for flow, refining your conclusion, and addressing minor spelling and grammar issues, your essay will be much stronger and more coherent. Remember, detailed examples and evidence are key to a persuasive argument. Keep writing, and use this feedback to improve your next essay draft.

Therefore, by wearing the trendy items, people can upgrade confidence, personal's image and even social status.  On the other hand, I do not agree that young people take much time and money to following the trends of fashion and technology. First of all, buying too much items can lead to be harmful for environment. Nowadays, youngsters purchase numerous clothes and devices which is redundant for their wardrobes, hence, they tend to throw away many old pieces of clothes which are still good condition. By doing so, many fashion and technology wastes are released to the environment and seriously contaminate to the natural habitat. Furthermore, young people bear large debt due to purchasing too much luxury clothes and following trends without having the large finance. To illustrate, many young people have a big loan from financial firms or banks with an aim to buy their favorite season items. As a result, young people can dramatically push them to the brink of bankruptcy. 
 To conclude, the widespread of Internet and technology allows young people to access their trendy items. However, i believe that spending too much time and money for the following to the latest items is unnecessary in modern age because of the contamination and debt.
feedback:
Your essay presents a viewpoint on the topic of youth spending on fashion and technology. Let’s explore areas where this essay succeeds and areas where improvements can be made.

However, based on your writing, you seem to address a stance on youth's spending habits. Ensure your essay directly responds to the question asked. Always restate the original prompt for clarity.

Keep practicing your expression and structure, and you will see continuous improvement.

prompt: Report: Evaluation of the 'International food' course in the Superior school of cookery.
essay:
You have just completed a cooking course. As part of the school's research and efforts to offer superior classes, they have asked you to write an evaluation of your experience as a student. Your report should discuss what you learned from the class and what you thought of the teachers and their instruction methods. Mention any ways you think the class could be improved and say whether you would or would not recommend the course to a friend or relative. 
 To: The School of Cuisine. 
 From: Isabel. 
 Subject: Evaluation of the 'International food' course. 
 Date: 9/9/2021 
 The aim of this report is to evaluate the 'International food course' offered by the School of Cuisine, which I have completed. 
 The first observation to make concerns the cooking techniques that I have learned during the course sessions. It was extremely valuable to learn how to improve simple cooking methods, such as frying and boiling. Specially, I have learned a Spanish frying system to fry vegetables with the specific oil measures so that, I can recognise when the fried elements are ready to be served. 
 With regard to the teachers and the instruction methods they have satisfied my expectations. One of my teachers possesses some traditional gastronomy awards, i.e. The III National Competition of innovative typical dishes'. Concerning the instruction methods, since the trainers must cooperate with other professional chefs and their own classmates, the instruction methods are highly interactive and intuitive for the future culinarians. 
 To improve the classes, it would be practical to use more spacious classrooms, so that the student would be more comfortable when practising cooking activities. Moreover, the cookery equipment should be renewed since they are a bit obsolete. 
 Finally, I would strongly recommend taking this course to my friends because it can widen their scope of international dishes.
feedback:
This essay provides a clear and structured evaluation of the "International Food" course. However, there are several areas that could be improved to enhance clarity and effectiveness in communication.

1. **Response to the Topic:**  
You have successfully addressed the prompt by discussing what was learned, your opinion of the teachers and their methods, suggestions for improvement, and whether you'd recommend the course. However, be careful with the use of terms like "observation." It's important to distinguish between what you observed and what you learned directly. For example, describing cooking techniques learned would be more appropriate under your learning experience rather than an observation.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, and Stylistic Issues:**  
Your essay is mostly free from spelling errors, but it could benefit from a review of grammatical structures and stylistic choices. For instance, the use of "specially" should be corrected to "especially" when detailing the cooking techniques learned. Aim for consistency in tense and more varied sentence structures to keep the reader engaged. Also, consider clarifying phrases like "cooking techniques" with specific examples to strengthen your points.

3. **Clarity of Point of View:**  
Your position is clear; you value the course and would recommend it. However, the essay can be enhanced by explicitly stating this opinion in the introduction and conclusion for more significant impact. When discussing improvements or criticisms, clearly label them as such to maintain a structured flow of ideas.

4. **Arguments and Support:**  
You've provided good support for your viewpoints regarding what was learned and the effectiveness of the instruction methods. To strengthen your arguments further, consider providing specific examples of how the teachers' expertise contributed to your learning. Instead of just stating the need for more spacious classrooms, explaining how this would directly impact the learning experience could be more persuasive.

Regarding the conclusion, it's essential to choose a single phrase to indicate the essay's end. The use of both "finally" and "in conclusion" can be confusing. Decide on one to maintain a coherent structure. Additionally, when recommending the course, instead of saying it would "widen their scope of international dishes," it would be more accurate to say it "widens skills in relation to cooking international dishes." This clarifies that the course offers practical skills, not just a broader understanding.

Finally, when suggesting improvements, ensure these are directly tied to enhancing the student’s learning experience. For example, when mentioning the need for newer cookery equipment, describe how current equipment limits the learning process.

In summary, your essay effectively communicates a positive experience with the course, supported by examples of learned techniques and appreciation for the teachers. Focusing on specific, actionable feedback, utilizing clear and varied sentence structure, and refining your conclusion will make your evaluation even more compelling and coherent.

prompt: With the enhancement of new technologies, there are a variety of choices available
essay:

 Firstly, with regards to education, students have more than one option to choose from in modern society. In former days, it was compulsory for learners to fully attend offline classes to gain a solid understanding of the studies. However, in digital era, aside from registering for face-to-face studying sessions, students are able to learn from their home with a laptop of a smartphone connected with the Internet. Thus, the development of the latest technologies has offered learners at any ages a wide range of studying methods. 
 Secondly, it is evident that there has been more means of transports manufactured to meet individuals' traveling demands. Taking Vietnam as an example, to travel on their regular basis, workers are free to choose different kinds of vehicles, such as buses, motorbikes, planes or even electric ones, based on the affordability or convenience. In the past, the old generations have fewer options regarding commuting in distance because of undeveloped technologies. For instance, some people went on foot, or rode a bike to pay a visit to their relatives, which was challenging in long distances. Therefore, thanks to the numerous availability of transportations, individuals have the freedom to choose better alternatives serving their purposes. 
 To conclusion, following the emerging technologies, there are a range of choices for human beings to select, which makes our life easier and more enjoyable.

However, the emphasis on technology might have shifted the focus too much from the original prompt's intent, which appears to have been broader than just technological advancements. Future essays will benefit from closely aligning with the given prompt and carefully selecting examples that directly support the topic, ensuring your thesis and the body of your essay remain on point.

Regarding spelling, grammar, and style, your essay is well-written with few errors, showcasing a good command of the English language. However, simplifying complex sentences could enhance clarity and make your essay more accessible, particularly for English language learner audiences.

Overall, your essay demonstrates a strong understanding of the topic and presents clear, descriptive arguments. Focusing on aligning more closely with the prompt, refining your thesis statement, enhancing transitions, and broadening your conclusion will significantly improve future essays.

These subjects including mathematics, physics and literature are necessary because they offer elementary understanding of calculating and linguistic skills, accordingly provide students with adequate knowledge for their study in university and improve career prospects. Therefore, the primary subjects are beneficial to students in terms of further study and job opportunities. \n On the other hand, the science and preparation of food are increasingly significant in modern life. Currently, the essay sometimes blurs these distinctions, making it challenging to discern the essay’s original standpoint from public discourse. This clarity is critical in conveying your argument effectively and demonstrating a thorough examination of the topic.

While the arguments presented are valid, ensuring they're backed by a mix of personal insight and commonly understood facts will strengthen the essay. For instance, discussing the importance of traditional subjects and the growing significance of food science shows a well-considered viewpoint. However, integrating how your personal experiences or observations align with these arguments could offer a more solid foundation for your stance.

Regarding language and structure, the essay is mostly clear and follows a logical flow. Simplifying language does not mean diluting the argument but rather making it more straightforward for a wider audience to grasp.

prompt: Young people today spend too much money and time following fashion trends (clothing, technology)
essay:

 Young people today spend too much money and time following fashion trends (clothing, technology) 
 To watch extent do you agree or disagree? 
 It is undeniable that people are running after many fashion trends, especially young people because the society are developing day by day so a lot of new trends will appear and attract young people. Some arguments may think that it's totally fine if they want to become flashier and more fashionable in front of other people. But the other assume that they spend too much money and time following fashion trends. And I agree that this young generation are wasting too much money and time to run after the latest fashion trend. 
 First and foremost, youth is a very important time of your life. In this time young people should invest in themselves and build up a strong range of knowledge and life skill so they can be confident with every situation. And instead of using that money that they have earned to buy trendy clothes or technology, they can use it to invest or trade on the stock exchange or buy more books to read to enhance their knowledge and imagination to a higher level. Secondly, there is nothing to be ashamed of when young people are wearing old clothes or using old-fashioned technology, because they can use that time and money focus on more vital things such as their future, their career to reach their goals. For example, if a boy want to be a doctor, between some trendy clothing, technology and some reference medical book, that boy would choose the second choice because he has defined himself as a future doctor so he has to spend their time and money to achieve his dream. 
 Thirdly, young people should only spend their time to something that help them to make money not something that take their money out of pocket. Because they have a lot of fees to pay such as the house rent, the electricity bill, the water bill and even their high school/university fee. If they continue spending money on trendy fashion like clothing or technology, they will be in lack of money and don't have enough money to pay for all those kinds of fees. Finally, young people don't have to wear trendy clothing or buy trending technology because after a short period, they will be "out of trend" so they only need to choose causal clothing or affordable technology because they will last for a long time and no one will judge them for their normal sense of fashion. For instance, a university boy brought a white T-shirt and a trendy color shirt which was very hot at that time. For the first two weeks, the boy only wore his trendy color shirt because it is a very popular shirt but a few years later, it is no longer suitable for young people so his white old T-shirt is more likely a safe option for him to wear for the rest of his life because it is normal and comfortable. 
 In conclusion, young people should use their youth to do more helpful things instead of spending all their money on fashion trends.
feedback:
Your essay on the influence of fashion trends on young people presents a clear stance on the topic, emphasizing the view that the youth spend too much on fleeting trends. Here's a detailed breakdown of how your essay could be improved to enhance clarity, coherence, and relevance to the prompt.

**Response to the Topic**
Your introduction attempts to set the stage for discussing the impact of fashion trends on young people. However, it falls short in directly responding to the question of whether young people spend too much time and money on fashion. It's crucial to restate the topic question more accurately and then provide a clear, direct opinion on it. For example, instead of general statements, specify that the essay will explore your agreement with the idea that young people overly invest in fashion trends. This direct approach ensures relevance and alignment with the task at hand.

**Spelling, Grammar, and Stylistic Issues**
Throughout your essay, there are several instances where grammatical and stylistic choices could be improved for greater clarity and impact. For example, phrases like "Some arguments may think" could be refined for clarity and accuracy—arguments don't think, people do. Consider rephrasing to "Some may argue" to avoid personification of abstract concepts. Additionally, maintaining consistent verb tenses and subject-verb agreement will enhance the readability of your essay.

**Clarity of Author's Point of View**
Your stance is somewhat clear as you express agreement with the idea that young people are overly focused on trends. However, the essay's impact is diluted by ambiguous statements and a lack of first-person perspective where necessary. When stating your opinion, using the first-person narrative, such as "I believe" or "In my view," can make your position stronger and more personal. Ensure that each paragraph consistently supports your viewpoint with clear, direct statements.

**Descriptive Arguments Supporting the Position**
You provide several arguments to support your viewpoint, such as the importance of prioritizing investments in knowledge over fashion and the fleeting nature of trends. These are good starts. However, your arguments could be strengthened by providing more specific examples, data, or personal observations. Additionally, directly addressing potential counterarguments could further enrich your essay by showing a balanced understanding of the topic.

**Actionable Recommendations for Improvement:**
1. Begin with a more direct and specific restatement of the prompt, clearly stating your position on the topic.
2. Use the first-person narrative when expressing your opinions to clarify that the essay reflects your personal viewpoint.
3. Work on grammatical accuracy—pay attention to subject-verb agreement, tense consistency, and clear sentence structures.
4. Support your arguments with specific examples or evidence. Consider both sides of the argument to add depth to your analysis.
5. Conclude your essay by succinctly summarizing your viewpoint and the arguments that support it, reinforcing the significance of your perspective on the topic.

Focusing on these areas will not only make your argument more compelling but also ensure that your essay is well-structured and clearly aligned with the task. Keep practicing, and remember that each piece of writing is a step towards mastering the art of persuasive and coherent essay writing.

prompt: A nation can be both prosperous and able to protect environment

prompt: Writing task 2- nature or nuture influence human development
essay:

Some studies have suggested that no nexus exists between genes and behaviour patterns while other research indicates that the characteristics we are born with have much more influence on your personality and development than their life. This essay is to discuss these two schools of thoughts, with some facts being closely examined. 
 There is no denying the fact that genetics plays a large role in the determining a person's character. Nativists take the position that all or most behaviours and characteristics are results of inheritance. Genetic traits handed down from parents influence the individual difference that makes each person unique. For example, researchers found that identical twins were twice as likely as non-identical twins to share the same personality traits, suggesting that their DNA was having the greatest impact. 
 By contrast, some experts now argue that our genetic inheritance has virtually nothing to do with our personalities. They believe that a child's behaviour signals the accumulative effect of the environment where they grow up. Studies show that many young criminals come from problem families who have a history of violence and crime. Without good job prospects, they end up finding solace in gangs. Another example to show parent's effect on their child's behaviour that children with fine upbringing normally show their courtesy and professional etiquettes in coping with real-life problems, similarly, offspring of nurturing mother tended to be less anxious than those of more lackadaisical mother. 
 To sum up, people are made by both learned and born traits. There is no need to reach a conclusion that either environment or nature plays a decisive part in one's character and behaviour development. Although the effect of genetic heredity is overt, one can not afford to ignore that of environment where a child is nurtured. 
 (305 words)

Also, pay attention to the use of singular and plural forms (e.g., 'mother' should be 'mothers' when referring to more than one). Simplifying complex sentences and ensuring correct punctuation will also enhance the clarity of your arguments.

3. **Clarity of the Author’s Point of View:** While you attempt to cover both perspectives of the debate, the essay's requirement is to articulate a singular viewpoint. Clearing up this misunderstanding by selecting one perspective (either nature or nurture) as the primary influence on personality and behavior will make your argument stronger and your essay more aligned with the prompt.

4. **Arguments Supporting the Author's Position:** You have provided examples and discussed studies to support both sides of the debate. However, to improve, focus your essay on providing clear, descriptive arguments that support your chosen viewpoint. Detailing specific studies, incorporating personal experiences, or discussing public perceptions that back up your stand will make your essay more persuasive and cohesive.

In summary, revising your essay to focus on a single influence (either nature or nurture) on personality development will make your argument clearer and more compelling. prompt: Communication via calling or texting?
essay:

Some people tend to call their beloved ones, while others seek getting in touch through text messages. I personally find phone calls a better method of social interaction rather than using text messages, for the following reasons that will be demonstrated in this essay. 
 To begin with, phone calls have various merits in favor of better communication. Concerning work field, people are usually tense and frustrated, but with the help of phone calls, this provides a great chance to get each other's point across in the middle of a conflict. In order to solve efficiently any crucial problem at work, giving a call is a step forward towards reaching an agreement between colleagues. In addition, to be able to catch on the intonation of someone, one will probably need phone calls, as people can say words that gives two different meanings which can be clarified just by their tone in speaking. For instance, if you ask a team in any company, when any clash between the team outrages? Colleagues tend to reply that texting starts off many clashes as people probably don't really get the intentions of their partners in a team right; however, phone calls can set these conflicts aside. 
 On the other hand, text messages can drastically destroy skills needed for proper social interaction in the future. If people totally rely on communicating through messages, future generations will probably be more comfortable with minimal conversing between individuals. Not only face-to-face communication, but also phone calls may turn into rare methods for connecting with others, which in fact is quite disastrous. For example, youth face many social obstacles like having difficulty in getting along with new friends at school as they are unfamiliar with contacting people in real life. Thus, regarding all those drawbacks of text messaging, phone calls is obviously more beneficial to most individuals. 
 To sum up, communication has a vast influence on people's way of living, interactions. Calling someone is widely preferred than text messaging due to its numerous positive effects on society. Phone calling is essential to put conflicts aside and to know the true intentions of people. On top of that, calls help youngsters know how to interact and make new friends. Therefore, phone calling is a valuable way of communicating.
feedback:
This essay effectively engages with the topic by debating the merits of phone calls over text messaging, highlighting the impact of technology on communication. Your position is clearly in favor of phone calls for their ability to convey tone and solve conflicts more efficiently, especially in the workplace. However, to strengthen this essay and make it more aligned with the assignment’s requirements, consider the following insights:

1. **Personal Experience and Perspective:** The prompt specifically asks for *your* preference in communication methods, emphasizing personal experience and perspective. This means using first person pronouns ("I" and "my") more frequently to share *your* unique experiences and reasons for preferring phone calls over text messages. Include specific examples from your life that demonstrate why phone calls are more beneficial to you. Perhaps there was a time when a phone call resolved a misunderstanding that could have escalated had it been a text conversation.

2. **Simplification and Clarity:** There are parts of the essay where simplifying language could help in making your argument clearer and more accessible, especially considering English language learners might be your audience. For example, instead of saying, "Concerning work field, people are usually tense and frustrated," you might say, "At work, people often feel stressed."

3. **Spelling, Grammar, and Stylistic Issues:** Your essay is generally well-written, but keep an eye out for minor errors and opportunities to tighten your prose. For instance, in your conclusion, "phone calls is obviously more beneficial" should be "phone calls are obviously more beneficial" to agree in number (plural subject with plural verb). 

4. **Descriptive Arguments and Examples:** While you've outlined the advantages of phone calls in the abstract, grounding these benefits in personal anecdotes or more vivid descriptions could make your argument more persuasive. For instance, instead of broadly stating that phone calls prevent conflicts, share a brief story about a time a phone call helped you clarify a misunderstanding that text messages had exacerbated.

5. **Balance and Depth in Argumentation:** While focusing on the advantages of phone calls, don't forget to explore, even if briefly, what might make text messaging appealing to some. Acknowledging the opposite viewpoint can provide a more rounded perspective before explaining why, in your experience, phone calls still prevail.

In summary, your essay makes a compelling case for preferring phone calls over text messaging, focusing on the benefits of clearer communication and conflict resolution. To elevate your essay, integrate personal experiences that reveal why you favor phone calls, simplify and clarify your language, correct minor errors, and provide more descriptive arguments and examples. By doing so, you will not only meet the assignment's requirements more closely but also craft a more persuasive and engaging narrative.

 Learning a foreign language at primary could have some possible disadvantages. Firstly, it could be a waste of time since children need to focus on other subjects such as math, science, and their own mother tongue language, which they might need it more than the foreign one. Secondly, children may get confused because of learning many languages at the same time and this could have a negative impact on their development.  On the other hand, I think that children learn faster at a young age because they are less self-conscious and shy. So they can easily pick up the right pronunciation and try to copy it. Furthermore, children enjoy practicing languages through games. Thus, learning and copying others could be fun in itself for them. In other words, for children learning languages is not a hard task as it is for adults. In addition, languages nowadays are as important as science and math. Acquiring an international language like English could be very important for young people to get better job opportunities in the future. 
 In conclusion, it seems to me that the benefits of teaching children foreign languages as soon as possible outweigh the drawbacks.

prompt: [IELTS TASK 2] Some people claim that not enough of the waste from home is recycled...
essay:
Topic: Some people claim that not enough of the waste from home is recycled. They say that the only way to increase recycling is for governments to make it a legal requirement. To what extent do you think laws are needed to make people recycle more of their waste? 
 Whether governments should legislate for recycling is an issue of broad interest. While there are still disparate arguments, I personally concur with the need for regulation due to some reasons. 
 First and foremost, the detrimental impacts rising from free-of-law recycling are undeniable. Without restriction of laws, violation continues escalating, thus sparking serious repercussions. As unrecycled waste will be mainly brought to landfill, pollution will expand at an alarming rate, posing great environmental threats to different agencies working on the environment such as waste processing companies, tourism, economy, etc. Handling these problems would cause significant loss to the national budget, since governments have to allocate financial assistance to various related departments. 
 Furthermore, legislating for recycling ensures wider compliance in the community. Stringent penalties accompanied with laws such as forfeit, arrestment, imprisonment, etc. would stimulate people's rigorous adherence to the regulations as well as urge companies to address environmental problems. For example, a dairy company in Vietnam called Vinamilk has introduced bio-degradable bags and hydro flask metal bottles to consumers for recycling purposes. Their inventions under the influence of social media have resulted in great amount of consumption and support from customers, especially the adolescents, therefore not only contributing to the economy but also disseminating environmental messages. These productive approaches together with strong consciousness of people would enable further sustainable development targets in our community. 
 In brief, bringing in recycling laws is necessary to raise people's awareness and conformity. Governments had better come up with appropriate legislation in order to gain as much benefits as possible. ( 254)
feedback:
Your essay on the necessity of legal requirements for recycling presents a compelling argument with a well-defined stance. However, there are several areas where improvements can be made to better address the topic and enhance the overall effectiveness and clarity of your writing.

1. **Addressing the Topic Fully:** Your introduction partially captures the essence of the prompt but misses a crucial aspect of the debate, which is the focus on recycling from homes and why it has become a point of contention. This adjustment will provide a solid grounding for your argument and align your essay more closely with the prompt's requirements.

2. **Clarity of Opinion:** While your position is noted, the presentation of your opinion could be more directly linked to the question asked. The prompt seeks an evaluation of the extent to which laws are necessary. A measured response that more explicitly weighs the need for legislation against other possible measures to promote recycling could enhance your introduction. Consider stating your viewpoint more directly in response to the prompt and offering a brief rationale that sets the stage for your detailed arguments to follow.

3. **Spelling, Grammar, and Stylistic Issues:** The essay is generally well-written but watch for minor errors and strive for clearer expressions. Avoid complex and lengthy sentences that might confuse the reader. For instance, phrases like "free-of-law recycling" could be simplified to "recycling without legal enforcement." Aim for clarity and simplicity in your writing to ensure your ideas are easily understood.

4. **Supporting Arguments:** Your arguments are clear and backed by examples, which strengthens your position. The mention of specific instances, such as the efforts of the Vinamilk company, is effective in illustrating how laws can encourage positive environmental practices. Continue to use such descriptive examples to solidify your arguments, ensuring each supports your main point of view directly.

5. **Conclusion and Summary:** Your conclusion currently misses the opportunity to fully recap the discussion points made throughout the essay. prompt: Is technology useful for education in the modern time?

Presently, we could not reject that technologies are playing crucial roles in human society including education. That is why most schools and universities all over the world are well equipped with technology devices. Technologies have a great impact on education in terms of globalization, innovative teaching techniques, and eradicate illiteracy. 
 The first advantage that technologies affect education is globalization. Technology education expands the boundary of study, you can enroll every course from over the world without leaving for a house. Moreover, people can access all types of information with Wi-Fi-connected devices. 
 The second element that pushes educational capabilities is teaching techniques. Nowadays, studying becomes more active since students can find study material themselves instead of passively perceiving knowledge only from teachers. Furthermore, technologies support teachers in preparing new material for students; they can upload it online as an alternative to handwriting. 
 The final factor is technology eradicate illiteracy from developing countries. Many places in the world can afford the cost of building schools for children, so they are using technology devices to wipe out illiteracy from the children. 
 Even though technology beneficial education in many aspects, it is frequently harmful to human health when we overuse it. Moreover, students might distract from the study when they spend too much time on technology devices. However, we can deny the importance of technology in education.
