prompt: IELTS task 2: Will online newspapers / books replace printed ones?
essay:
People argue that the advantages of digital books or newspapers will lead to the disappearance of the traditional ones. I strongly agree with this opinion. 
 The primary reason why nobody will purchase the printed books and newspapers is due to their negative effects on environment. Conventional books and newspapers are made from wood, and hence a plethora of trees has to be cut to provide materials for paper manufacturing process. This could exacerbate the deforestation which is a headache issue of all countries around the globe. To address this critical problem, many goverments have imposed higher taxes on wood-made products, and books or newspapers are one of the bypass products of woods. As a result, the price of books and newspapers shoots up and forces people think about another economic way to replace printed books and newspapers. 
 On the other hands, there is a variety of advantages of electronic books and newspapers. Firstly, they do not need to be printed out on the papers so that they are very friendly to environment, and the manufacturing and printing of books and newspapers are significantly reduced. Therefore, their price is much cheaper than the printed books and newspapers, and people can afford to buy them. Secondly, people can easily update news or information anytime and anywhere as long as they have a smartphone connecting to wifi. This is an extraordinary benefit for busy people who has a limit of time per day. Finaly, the high quality and vivid image helps the digital books and newspapers outweigh the conventional ones. 
 In my conclusion, the purchase of printed newspapers or books will be decreasingly dropped and people will prefer to buy digital ones due to their obvious advantages.
feedback:
This essay effectively responds to the topic, presenting a clear viewpoint that the advantages of digital books and newspapers will overshadow traditional printed materials, leading to their decline. The argument is structured around environmental concerns and the benefits of digital formats, providing a persuasive stance on the subject. However, there are several areas for improvement to enhance clarity, correctness, and overall impact.

1. Revisit your essay to correct spelling, grammar, and punctuation mistakes. This step is crucial and can significantly improve the readability and professionalism of your essay. Remember, dedicating time to review and edit your work after writing can greatly reduce errors and increase your essay's quality.

2. Although the essay presents a strong opinion, it would benefit from an introductory sentence that outlines the supporting reasons for this viewpoint. A format like "I strongly agree with this opinion because of (1) the environmental impact of traditional books and (2) the advantages of digital formats," would set a clearer framework for your argument. Each supporting reason should then lead the following paragraphs, enhancing the flow and coherence of your essay.

3. The essay somewhat neglects comparative analysis. While the focus is on supporting digital books and newspapers, briefly acknowledging potential advantages or reasons some might prefer traditional formats before rebutting these points could strengthen your argument. It demonstrates a well-rounded understanding of the topic and further solidifies your stance.

4. Your conclusion should succinctly summarize the essay, restating the main topic, your viewpoint, and the reasons you've provided. By addressing these areas, you can elevate the quality of your essay, making your arguments more compelling and your writing more polished. Ensure that each paragraph solidly anchors to a reason supporting your viewpoint for greater clarity and impact.

prompt: Love always wins! REVIEW OF A FILM
essay:
REVIEW: 
 You are the arts review writer for a magazine. Your editor has asked you to review a film. Choose a 
 film that you have seen. Describe the plot and the characters involved. Say who the film is suitable for 
 and why. Mention any special effects or aspects of the film that stood out in some way. 
 Would you recommend the film? Why, why not? 
 Write your review. 
 Love always wins! 
 Yesterday, I watched an incredibly moving film. It's called 'The last letter from you lover'. It's a drama and romance film which is based on the bestseller romantic novel written by JoJo Moyes. 
 The film shows the unbelievable story of a journalist called Ellie (Felicity Jones), when she discovers an intriguing love letter. As she is getting more and more involved in the love story that the letters hide, she empathises a lot with the couple. They happen to be an enchanting couple that have to live their love in secret, they are just lovers, and they cannot live together. To make matters even worse, the girl, Jennifer loses all her memories in a car crush accident so, she has to retry all of them progressively. 
 The aspects of the film that I liked the most were the charming places where the film is set in and the incredibly realistic dialogues between the characters of the film. 
 Teenagers and adults will enjoy this film, since it makes the mature audience realise it is a story that could happen to everyone. You will want to help the couple to get together and restart their lives as I did when I watched it. 
 I strongly recommend watching "The last letter from your lover", it will make you realise the value of real love and appreciate the help of the people that surrounds you in your daily life.
feedback:
Your essay is a genuine attempt to review "The Last Letter from Your Lover," and you've done well in capturing the essence of the film's story and its romantic depth. Let's explore how we can enhance your review to make it even better.

1. **Response to the Topic:**
You’ve successfully addressed the main task by choosing a film and describing its plot and characters. However, to fully meet the requirements of a film review, remember to include more details such as the immediate cast names (which you did for Felicity Jones' character, Ellie), as well as the writer, director, producer, and year of release. This information provides a comprehensive background for your readers and sets the stage for your critique.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, and Stylistic Issues:**
In your review, there's a minor spelling mistake ("car crush" should be "car crash") and a consistency issue with the film title’s italicization. Remember, film titles should be either underlined or italicized for consistency and clarity. Additionally, breaking your review into smaller paragraphs could enhance readability, especially when shifting from summary to personal opinion.

3. **Clarity of Point of View:**
Your personal viewpoint as a reviewer comes through clearly when you express your recommendation and explain who would enjoy the film and why. To strengthen this, you might consider adding your personal critique on specific elements such as the actors' performances, the direction, and how the film handles the narrative structure, particularly its use of flashbacks.

4. **Arguments and Descriptive Support:**
While you mention enjoying the setting and dialogues, deeper exploration into why these contributed to the film's success would enrich your review. For example, discussing how the set design complements the two different eras depicted in the movie and how it supports the storytelling could offer a more detailed insight. Similarly, a discussion on the director's approach to handling the constantly changing timelines and the believability of actors in their roles contributes to a more rounded critique.

Remember, a film review is not just about sharing the plot but delving into the film’s execution, the performances, and its emotional impact on the audience. Also, consider your readers who may be looking for specific information that helps them decide whether to watch the film. By expanding on these aspects, your review will not only inform but also engage your readers on a deeper level.

Final tip: It's always beneficial to conclude your review with a summarizing sentence that encapsulates your overall opinion and recommendation. This leaves the reader with a clear takeaway from your critique.

You have a good foundation here, and with these enhancements, your review can become even more compelling and informative.

prompt: STUDYING IN TRADITIONAL CLASSES IS LESS BENEFICIAL THAN LEARNING ONLINE AT HOME
essay:
STUDYING ONLINE IS MORE BENEFICIAL THAN LEARNING ONLINE AT HOME 
 These days, it is true that studying online plays an important role in our lives now. While this development may be disadvantageous to a certain extent, I believe that its advantages are much more significant. 
 On the one hand, e-learning is not productive as studying in class. The reason is that by educating online, students tend to be more distracted and procrastinated by things around them. For example, instead of focusing on the lecture, some pupils could just let their phones there and play video games or watch TV, which is not allowed in schools. Consequently, their academic transcript would gradually fall. 
 On the other hand, I do believe the perks are on top of these drawbacks. Firstly, by teaching online, both teachers and students do not have to waste their time commuting. For instance, if in the past, educators and learners have to drive a long distance to get to school, which could take a lot of their time, now they just have to sit at their home with an electronic device connected internet to be able to study. Secondly, this teaching style would make a comfortable learning space for students. To illustrate, having excessive noise in the direct classroom could cause disturbance and thereby affect knowledge acquisition. Therefore, by distance education, students can learn in the most comfortable way, and then they can improve their understanding. 
 In conclusion, while the traditional classes may have some value, I hold the belief that they are eclipsed by the advantages above.
feedback:
The essay attempts to discuss the benefits and drawbacks of studying online compared to traditional classroom settings. Here's how it can be improved:

1. **Addressing the Topic:** The introduction suggests a comparison between online and traditional education but does not clearly align with the given topic, which is whether studying in a classroom is more beneficial than learning online at home. It's vital to directly address the question by stating whether you agree or disagree with the statement and ensure that the rest of the essay supports this viewpoint consistently.

2. **Clarity and Structure:** The essay presents both sides of the argument which may confuse readers about the author's stance. Since the task is to express the extent of agreement or disagreement with the given statement, focusing on supporting that stance throughout the essay will enhance clarity and effectiveness. Ensure each paragraph supports the main argument without presenting contrasting views unless they're used to strengthen the primary position.

3. **Specific Examples and Arguments:** The arguments provided about the distractions of online learning and the convenience and comfort it offers are good but need to be more detailed. In my opinion, socialization plays a paramount role in ones success. 
 To conclude, participating in different activities will help up build several condusive skills in the terms of socialization, discovering talents and time management. So as a result, we should choose to attend various activities rather than focusing on a single one.
feedback:
Your essay on the importance of participating in various activities for a well-rounded future is thoughtful and presents several compelling arguments. However, there are areas that need improvement to enhance clarity, accuracy, and overall effectiveness. Below are some specific points to consider:

1. **Response to the Topic:** You have effectively addressed the topic by arguing that participating in diverse activities helps in identifying interests, developing time management skills, and enhancing social skills. Your position is clear and directly responds to the prompt.

Correct spelling is crucial for clarity and professionalism in writing. Additionally, watch out for the correct use of words and their spellings to convey your message accurately.

However, they could be made stronger with more specific examples and clearer explanations. To improve your essay, consider these steps:
- Carefully proofread your work for spelling and grammatical errors. Using spell-check tools or asking someone to review your writing can be helpful.
- Improve sentence structure for better flow and coherence. Avoid starting sentences inappropriately with conjunctions and ensure correct phrase usage.
- Enhance your arguments with more detailed examples and clearer, more direct explanations. Connect your personal experiences closely to the points you are making.

Remember, practice makes perfect. Keep writing and refining your skills, and consider these feedback points as steps towards more effective and polished essays.

prompt: Age limit, Who is obliged to work?
essay: Does age really matter? We Filipinos are known as hard workers. No matter how hard our job and small our compensation is, we ignore the sacrifices we make just to supply our families. Sometimes we tend to go outside the country just to find a stable job that could sustain our "needs and wants". Known as OFW's (Over Seas Filipino Workers). Some mother even choose to babysit someone's child than babysitting their own child, they choose to leave the people they love just for them to eat three times a day. Most of them get abused by their own employer, sometimes it comes to a point that some of them die with no great injustice. Some of us are way beyond the age limit or was furlough and our contributions not enough to sustain our medications. Some of our Senior Citizens have to take care of their own grandchildren for some reasons. We are indeed helpless because of poverty. We were born poor, we lived beggarly and we are going to die broke. \n Now as a Filipino most of us cannot afford higher education but some are skilled workers with the help of TESDA. Most skilled workers are middle aged; some of them are 50 to 60 years older and beyond. Now put yourself in their shoe and imagine, if you are skilled you know what to do and you know "how" things work to a job you are willing to be employed and you need money but there is an age limit and you're beyond it. Or you were furlough that your employment position requires younger employee and you desperately needed a job for your expensive medication and thinking you may be beyond the age limit but still is able to work. I certainly disagree about the age limit of 50 to 65 years old as long as they could still be able to work and earn money in a fair way. I think age limit should be 70 years old and beyond because that is the age that a senior citizen should be resting and enjoying. \n If we work hard our sacrifices pays off no matter what, if we know our responsibilities, if we grab every opportunities and if we take nothing for granted every hard work always pays off. By believing in our selves being humble and confident, with a little dash of prayer that success and goal we are aiming will be aimed.
feedback:
Your essay presents a deeply emotional view on the challenges faced by Filipino workers, both domestically and overseas. To enhance readability and impact, consider reviewing your essay for grammatical correctness and clarity. 

3. **Clarity of Author's Point of View**: While your personal stance on the age limit for employment is evident, especially in the later parts of your essay, it would be beneficial to make your viewpoint clear from the beginning. Expressing your position early on would guide your readers through your argument more effectively.

4. **Supporting Arguments**: Your essay contains rich, descriptive examples of the hardships faced by Filipino workers, which effectively evoke empathy. However, your arguments would be strengthened by a more structured presentation of facts, statistics, or studies about age limits in employment and their impact. This evidence would lend more credibility to your position. prompt: IELTS SPEAKING PART 2 - Describe a job you would not like to do in the future
essay:
Well, a job I would not like to do in the future is singer. There are many reasons why I would not like to do this job. First of all, beginner singers have to practice enough to be comfortable singing in front of people. They have to take care of their vocal cords to make sure their voice is as good as it can be. Honestly, I really feel sick and tired of practising my voice every day. The weapon of singer's success in my view, is good looks and charisma combined with catchy songs along with a good marketing team. In fact, I don't have anything of them. Additionally, I am overwhelmed by the massive crowds and I feel claustrophobic in crowds of people. 
 Furthermore, loud music made my hearts beat faster and blood pressure go up. When A famous singer decide to hold a concert in a region and it quickly become a major news story, covered in all of our media from newspapers to TV, and most radio channels. 
 Actually, I don't like to be famous person because the negative news about me on news channels and in newspapers has a negative influence. I always think of it to be stressful and pressurizing .As a matter of fact, I personally never had keen interest in the musical field. 
 In conlusion, I also think that such stressful jobs are not meant for everyone as it will also affect one's personal life. The negative environment at the work place can also alter one's psyche. Therefore, a profession that would be my last choice would certainly not be the job of a well-known singer.
feedback:
Your essay discusses an interesting perspective on why you would not like to pursue a career in singing. However, there are several areas where improvements could make your arguments stronger and your essay more engaging.

1. **Topic Response**: You've clearly stated your stance on not wanting to pursue singing as a career, which directly responds to the essay prompt. However, enhancing your introduction with a more creative approach could make your essay more engaging. For example, starting with a scenario or a rhetorical question could hook the reader's interest. Consider setting the stage with a brief backstory before diving into your main reasons.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, and Stylistic Issues**: There are minor grammatical errors and stylistic issues in your essay that can be improved. For clarity and accuracy, remember to refer to the act of performing songs as "singing" and the individual performing the job as a "singer". Pay attention to verb tense for consistency and ensure proper sentence structure for easier readability.

3. **Point of View Clarity**: Your point of view against pursuing a career in singing is clear throughout the essay. However, emphasizing your personal reasons and experiences can strengthen your stance. Using "I believe," "I feel," or "In my experience" helps clarify that these are your viewpoints.

4. **Supporting Arguments**: While you present several reasons for not wanting to be a singer, delving deeper into each point would make your arguments more persuasive. Instead of briefly touching on many aspects, dedicate a paragraph to each reason, explaining it thoroughly before moving on to the next. This approach will allow you to develop each argument fully, making your essay more compelling.

5. **Going Off Topic**: Be cautious not to stray from the primary topic. The focus should remain on the challenges and personal disinterest in the profession of singing, rather than the fame that might accompany it. Not all singers are famous, so it's essential to separate the profession from the potential celebrity status, ensuring your discussion stays relevant to the job itself.

In conclusion, refining your introduction to engage readers, addressing each reason with more depth, staying on topic, correcting stylistic and grammatical errors, and emphasizing your personal perspective can significantly enhance your essay. These improvements will make your narrative more coherent, persuasive, and enjoyable to read.

prompt: The unpaid community service is not necessary to be a compulsory program in high school
essay:
Nowadays, more and more people are concerning about whether the credits of community service should be forced to set in curriculum in high school or not. Some believe that this activity can help students to learn empathy while others think that it is totally wasting time. I agree with the latter notion, here are some ideas as below. 
 First of all, it is crucial for students to decide their future during this period. The school should provide more opportunities of field experience instead of an activity far different with studies. For example, I was confused when I was facing the option between Arts and Science. Fortunately, our high school more emphasized on practical experience, we were assigned to proper department after aptitude test. Subsequently, we explored our interest and develop skills during our short-term intern in cooperative enterprise. We cannot deny that young people should learn empathy in their age, but it is not necessary to be a compulsory program in high school. School can create the club relative to volunteer activities, holding unpaid community service in weekends. 
 Secondly, it is negative for local unemployment rate when students work as free labor. Unpaid community service seems helpful for local citizen, in fact, free labor replace the original workers. In addition, the wage might be influenced by unpaid community service. It is indisputable fact that the citizens support unpaid community service, so they can cost down the expenditures. However, it is unfair to original workers, they accepted a series of training, but they eventually get lower wage or even are fired by employers due to this activity. The school should consider this condition when they setting the curriculum. 
 By way of conclusion, I once reaffirm my position that the unpaid community service is not necessary to be a compulsory program in high school because of developing the skill of future preference and avoiding the increase of unemployment.
feedback:
The essay provides a view on a topic closely related, but not exactly matching the original essay prompt. The intention was to discuss whether unpaid community service should be a compulsory part of high school programs. However, the essay somewhat deviates from this focus, veering towards discussing the utility and impact of such service, not its necessity within educational programs. 

1. **Relevance to Topic:** The discussion needs to more directly address the core of the prompt: the importance and implications of making unpaid community service a mandatory element of high school curricula. Refocusing on this specific inquiry will greatly enhance the essay's relevance and coherence.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, and Stylistics:** There are minor spelling and grammatical errors present, such as "concerning about" instead of "concerned about" and "with studies" should be "from studies". Additionally, the essay could benefit from more varied sentence structures to improve readability and flow. Pay attention also to more precise word choice for clarity.

3. **Clear Point of View:** The essay's stance is clear, opposing the inclusion of mandatory unpaid community service in the high school curriculum. This position is maintained throughout, which is a strength. To bolster this, ensure every argument directly supports this viewpoint rather than general commentary on community service.

4. **Arguments and Support:** The arguments presented, such as the importance of focusing on career decisions and the impact on local employment, are intriguing. Yet, these arguments would benefit from deeper analysis and more direct ties to the question of compulsory service programs. Consider adding specific examples or data to reinforce your points. 

By refining the focus on the essay prompt, eliminating grammatical and stylistic errors, and strengthening the connection between your arguments and your main thesis, you can significantly improve this essay. Remember, addressing the prompt accurately is fundamental and directly influences the effectiveness and strength of your subsequent arguments.

prompt: In the modern world it is no longer necessary to use animals for food, clothing or medicine. To what
essay:
These days, it is believed that productions made from animals like food, clothing, medicine are no longer people's necessities. In my viewpoint, I strongly agree with this idea for the following reasons. 
 Firstly, in place of meat products, vegetarian diets cultivate a healthy lifestyle. This is because plant-based foods not only provide a wide range of nutritions but also reduce the risk of suffering from many chronic degenerative diseases and conditions, including heart disease, cancer, hypertension, diabetes, and obesity. For instance, a survey conducted by Queen University shows that a vegetarian's life expectancy normally surpasses any other normal people's. Moreover, in terms of clothing, it is worthless killing animals for producing high-fashion products. Clothes and accessories made from hemp, bamboo, and other animal-free materials are now commonplace. As a result, with diverse materials to choose from, there's no excuse for animals to die violently and painfully for fashion. 
 Secondly, it is certainly the case that due to the innovation of science and technology, animals are no longer treated as a means for experimental research. In recent years, the advent of a synthetic tissue that closely resembles human skin helps several cosmetic companies test the potential damage occurring. By this way, harmful substances are easily analyzed without the pain, the suffering, and the deaths of animals. 
 In conclusion, animal products should be eliminated because their sacrifices are no longer necessary. They can definitely be replaced by such alternatives as vegetarian foods, artificial materials and so on.
feedback:
This essay demonstrates a good understanding of the topic and presents clear arguments in favor of reducing the use of animal products in our lives, covering areas such as diet, clothing, and science. Here are some points to help improve the essay:

1. **Topic Response and Structure**: The essay directly addresses the topic, acknowledging that the use of animal products in various industries is no longer necessary. However, the response could be more aligned with the essay prompt's requirements by providing a simple agreement or disagreement without extending the response more than needed. The essay could be structured more effectively by outlining the reasons for the position in the introduction, thereby setting a clear roadmap for the reader.

2. **Word Count**: The essay is slightly short of the recommended word count. Meeting the minimum word count is important for scoring purposes. Consider expanding your opening and concluding paragraphs to at least three sentences to provide a stronger introduction to the topic and a more comprehensive summary of your discussion and reasons. This will not only help meet the word count but also enhance the overall flow and clarity of your essay.

3. **Spelling, Grammar, and Style**: There are minor issues with spelling, grammar, and style, including the use of the term "nutritions" instead of the correct form "nutrition." Paying attention to such details can improve the readability and professionalism of the essay. Additionally, consider varying your sentence structures to make the writing more engaging.

4. **Clarity of Point of View**: The point of view is clear throughout the essay, with a strong stance on the unnecessary use of animal products. This strength could be further enhanced by providing concise, direct reasons in the introduction, as recommended.

5. **Argument Support**: The arguments presented are descriptive and support the essay's position well, especially with the emphasis on alternatives to animal products. However, avoid referencing specific studies or sources unless the essay prompt explicitly allows it. Instead, focus on widely acknowledged facts and personal opinions to fortify your arguments. For example, rather than citing a survey from Queen University, mention commonly known benefits of vegetarian lifestyles that relate to your personal knowledge and logical reasoning.

6. **Miscellaneous**: It’s also beneficial to use non-specific sources or gender-neutral pronouns to keep the essay universally applicable and focused on common knowledge.

By addressing these points, the essay will not only adhere better to the requirements but also present a more coherent, polished argument. Keep up the excellent critical thinking and commitment to improving your writing skills.

prompt: IELTS- Ad-Dis Essay. More and more people are starting to work from home.
essay:
The question of whether or not workers should do their jobs at home via online devices has been a matter of debate since the Internet age. While there are drawbacks affecting workers, there are some merits of this modern trend. The essay will discuss both negative and positive sides. 
 One of obvious negative effects of working inside the home is lack of concentration on tasks. Surrounding distraction from neighbor or family, for instance, my nephews always keeps insisting on playing some funny games with me or being himself surrounded by loud music all the time. This would also mean that I can not fully concentrate on my job, which results in less productive, mainly falling to meet its requirements by my supervisor. 
 Not only that, limit of human social interaction is another downside in spite of technological innovations. Indeed, most conversations occur through keyboards due to a worker sits in front of screen without exchange support from his co-workers. In a long term, some depressed or anxious symptoms have appeared in the first stage. As a result, he suffers from his inside persistent feeling of sadness and loss of interest in communicating with people. 
 On the other hand, there is no doubt employees get more benefits from remote work policies. The most remarkable advantage is we would achieve and maintain our work-life balance. This means flexible schedule, namely setting our own working hours, taking breaks, having meals, doing regular physical activity and enjoying quality time with our loved ones at any time we wish. Consequently, work and individual life will be adjusted to our desire. 
 In addition, home-based office is considered a practical step to solve financial problems. One clear example is that we often spend much money on expensive breakfast, lunch or unexpected expenses at luxury restaurants if our head office is located in an urban area or a cosmopolitan city. That is to say as we work from home, we can buy food from the market and supermarket nearby with reasonable price in which contribute to balance the budget monthly. 
 To sum up, although working at home may have potential problems, overall I tend to believe that two advantageous aspects, particularly harmonious life style and financial issues will have a dramatic impact on workers' living.
feedback:
Your essay addresses the topic of remote work, exploring both its advantages and disadvantages. However, for improvement and to adhere closer to test instructions, focus is key. The original prompt asked for a discussion on either the positive or negative development of remote work, not both. Choosing one perspective and defending it with two strong reasons would make your essay more direct and impactful. 

In terms of writing mechanics, there are several areas to refine:
1. **Grammar and Spelling**: The phrase "can not" should be "cannot," and "whether or not" can be simplified to "whether." These small changes help in making your language more precise.
2. **Punctuation**: Be cautious with the use of commas, particularly when listing items. Ensuring proper use can enhance the clarity and flow of your sentences.

For clarity and coherence, keep your arguments straightforward and supported by descriptive examples. In this essay, your concepts on both the negative effects (like distractions and reduced social interaction) and the perks of working from home (like work-life balance and savings) are good starts. Yet, narrowing your focus to either the positive or negative side, then expanding on it with clear, supportive details would strengthen your position.

Remember also the practical aspect of essay writing under timed conditions. The length of your essay suggests that managing your time effectively might be an area to practice. Aim for a realistic word count that allows for planning, writing, and reviewing within the given time limit. This ensures not only the completion of your essay but also the opportunity to check and refine your work for any errors or improvements.

By concentrating on a single stance, honing in on grammatical accuracy, simplifying language where possible, and managing your time effectively, your future essays will present your ideas more coherently and persuasively. Keep practicing, and focus on these areas for improvement to enhance your English proficiency test scores.

prompt: Some people think that renewable energy sources like solar and wind power should replace fossil fuel
essay:
In this day and age, there are a number of arguments that alternative sources of energy like solar and wind power should be utilized as a substitute for non-renewable fuels such as coal and gas whilst others believe that we should continue using fossil fuels on the grounds that they are affordable. In this essay, I will discuss both sides of the opinion in details and give revelant examples to explain why I vehemently accord with the former view. 
 On the one side, those who support the continued use of fossil fuels claim that they are the most economical way to produce energy. While renewable energy sources are becoming cheaper, they remain more expensive than traditional energy sources. Moreover, fossil fuels are more convenient and can generate other energy on demand, whereas renewable energy sources depend on weather conditions and other external factors. There is no doubt,in fact, that the development of renewable energy technologies is still in its infancy and needs significant investment and research to become more efficient and cost-effective. For example, the production of solar panels and wind turbines requires significant amounts of energy and resources, which currently come from fossil fuels. By continuing to use fossil fuels during the development of renewable energy technologies, we can ensure the sustainability of both conventional and sustainable sources. 
 On the flip side, opponents might agrue that we need to invest heavily in solar and wind power as soon as possible. This is because the environmental impact of fossil fuels is significant. It is the fact that solar and wind power are clean and sustainable, and they produce no emissions meanwhile the burning of coal and gas releases dangerous pollutants into the atmosphere, which contributes to climate change and respiratory problems. By dint of this , it is crucial that we transition to clean and sustainable sources of energy. In addition, renewable energy has other benefits beyond its environmental impact. It can create new job opportunities in the renewable energy sector, which can help to stimulate economic growth. Furthermore, renewable energy sources can provide energy security, as they are not reliant on finite resources that are controlled by a few countries. This can help to reduce geopolitical tensions and promote global stability. 
 All in all, It is clear that both sides have their own excecptional merits. However, I still believe that renewable power sources are the key to a better future.
feedback:
The essay provides a balanced discussion on the use of renewable versus non-renewable energy sources, highlighting significant arguments for both viewpoints. However, there are areas for improvement to enhance the clarity, structure, and effectiveness of the essay.

Firstly, the introduction attempts to cover too much in a single sentence, leading to a run-on structure that might confuse readers. It's crucial to break down complex ideas into simpler sentences. This will not only improve readability but also ensure that each point is clearly communicated. Instead of blending several ideas into one sentence, try separating them to allow the reader to understand each point on its own.

Furthermore, the essay repeats the instructions from the prompt as part of the opinion statement. In English proficiency tests, and academic writing in general, it's important to directly state your opinion without rephrasing the task prompt. This approach helps in making your argument clear and concise right from the start. Next time, aim to present your viewpoint directly, without including the essay instructions as part of your thesis statement.

The discussion on the pros and cons of renewable and non-renewable energy is well-explained, showcasing an understanding of the topic. However, the personal opinion of the author is not sufficiently developed and only briefly mentioned in the concluding part of the essay. For a more balanced and persuasive argument, it's crucial to devote an entire paragraph to elaborating on your personal stance, just as you did for the other arguments presented. This shows the examiner that you can discuss your viewpoint in depth, similar to how you've discussed public opinions.

Additionally, there are minor spelling and grammatical errors ('agrue' should be 'argue', 'excecptional' should be 'exceptional', etc.) and stylistic concerns that can be addressed. For instance, consider varying sentence structure to keep the reader engaged and using more precise language to convey your points more powerfully.

Lastly, though the concluding remark attempts to summarize the essay, it would be more impactful if it clearly restated your stance and briefly reiterated the key reasons for it. This not only reinforces your position but also leaves the reader with a clear understanding of where you stand on the issue.

In summary, the essay demonstrates an understanding of the topic but would benefit from clearer sentence structure, a more developed personal opinion section, and minor corrections for spelling and grammar. Focusing on these areas will significantly improve the clarity and persuasiveness of the essay.

prompt: More public parks or sports facilities should be built in new towns rather than shopping centers?
essay:
Some people argue that when new towns are built up, it is more necessary to construct public parks or sport facilities instead of shopping centers. Personally, I agree that building public parks and sport facilities should be encouraged in new living areas. However, I also believe that launching shopping mall is indispensable in the areas, because each item brings different benefits for society. 
 On the one hand, building public parks and sport centers is the necessity that will provide people places to do exercises or outdoor activities such as jogging, running, or cycling and so on. This helps residents to be more energetic and their body is relaxed after a long day of a sequence of stressful and pressure works, even, doing exercises help people to prevent the risk of diseases such as diabetes, obesity, or high blood pressure. Therefore, people's health will be improved and the average longevity of population will be higher. Another reason that advocates the idea is boosting interaction among people. Public parks will be places where people have chance to meet others and socialize with them. This is also another effective way that allows residents to relieve stress and pressure. 
 On the other hand, shopping centers play a vital role in society and they are indispensable in any living regions. That is because shopping malls are considered as suppliers of different kinds of product for people that are used to serve their lives such as foods, cloths, and so on. Thus, to meet the diverse needs of products of people, shopping malls should be invested and built on new town. Moreover, running shopping malls will bring benefits for society. Taxes that government collects from these centers will be used to invest in others such as health care, traffic system, education, etc, and citizens are beneficiaries from this. 
 In conclusion, parks, sport facilities and shopping centers are the indispensable projects, which government should invest to them, because they own many advantages that society and individuals are beneficiaries. 
 _________________
feedback:
To enhance your essay and align it more closely with the topic, consider focusing more strongly on demonstrating the extent of your agreement or disagreement regarding the construction of public parks and sport facilities versus shopping centers in new towns. Use descriptive terms such as "strongly," "partially," or "totally" to clarify your position. This approach not only meets the requirements of the essay prompt more accurately but also allows for a richer, more nuanced discussion of your views.

Your essay does well in presenting arguments for both sides of the debate, highlighting the benefits of public parks and sports facilities for health and community interaction, as well as the importance of shopping centers for meeting people's needs and contributing to society through taxation. However, to make your essay even stronger, consider adopting a more decisive stance on one side of the issue. This could allow for deeper exploration of your chosen perspective, leading to more developed paragraphs, complex sentences, and effective use of vocabulary.

Additionally, your conclusion could be more effective. Aim for a concluding paragraph that summarizes the essay's main points and restates your opinion more clearly. Ideally, a conclusion should consist of 3 to 5 sentences to fully address the prompt and avoid the creation of run-on sentences, which could negatively impact your score. A well-structured conclusion strengthens your essay by providing a clear, concise recap of your argument and reiterating your stance.

Please also pay attention to minor spelling, grammar, or stylistic issues. For instance, in phrases like "launching shopping mall" or "cloths," small errors distract from your message. Consider revising to "launching a shopping mall" and "clothes" for clarity and correctness.

Remember, clarity of your point of view and a fully developed argument that supports your position are key to a successful essay. prompt: Wide concern about the ability of making films by individuals instead of by big companies
essay:
Recently the phenomenon aroused wide concern about the ability of making films by individuals instead of by big companies. This writing would argue that the benefits of this trend are greatly more significant than the drawbacks it has. 
 One benefit of this trend is that independent filmmakers may explore their hidden talents in film industry. In other words, those who have a passion for media, particularly in making movies, may not have a chance to pursue professional careers. When embarking on making films by their own, they can realize their ability and it allows them further opportunities. Another positive aspect is that independent filmmakers can express themselves freely. To be specific, filmmakers by individuals do not have to allow the same demands that big box office films have to. For example, those who make films independently do not follow the stereotypes or the motifs that are old-fashioned. 
 Despite these benefits, many people still claim that the movies which were not produced by big companies can be at low-quality. They may believe that independent filmmakers are not able to afford to buy cutting-edge devices such as digital cameras with high performance or having camera crews to set up before filming. However, I would argue that this trend can create a competitive market so that major producers have to work hard to produce high-quality movies. In more detail, this forces all producers to be more creative and make impressive films which contain innovative contents or outstanding messages in order to satisfy their audience's taste. 
 In conclusion, the merits of this trend certainly surpass it demerits. Not only hidden talents can be discovered by also the freedom to deliver what independent producers want. Moreover, the worry about the quality of films is not a concerning issue as many people claim.
feedback:
Your essay provides a thoughtful discussion on the topic of individuals making films versus big companies doing so. However, there are several areas that could be improved to make your argument clearer and more effective. Here are specific suggestions:

1. **Topic Response**: Your introduction suggests a broad concern about individual filmmakers which seems exaggerated. It's important to directly address the topic given by presenting your viewpoint more clearly. The question asks whether this development is positive or negative, but your essay discusses benefits and drawbacks without clearly stating your position. For a clearer response, starting off with "I believe that..." could help clarify your stance immediately.

2. **Active Voice and Clarity**: Use the first person to make your position clear. Phrases like "This writing would argue" distance you from your argument. Instead, say "I argue" or "In my view". This makes your essay more direct and personal, fitting the task's requirements better.

3. **Vocabulary Usage**: Be careful with the vocabulary you choose. Words like "concern" and "phenomenon" are not wrong, but their usage in the context of your essay might not convey the precise meaning you intend. For instance, saying a topic "arouses wide concern" suggests a negative impact, not just interest or consideration. Also, when talking about the positive or negative aspects, stick to words that clearly indicate your viewpoint, such as "advantages" and "disadvantages" instead of "benefits" and "drawbacks", to match the essay prompt more closely.

4. **Spelling and Grammar**: Watch for minor spelling and grammar issues. For example, "surpass it demerits" should be "surpass its demerits". These small errors can distract from your message. Consider using spell check tools or asking a peer to review your work.

5. **Supporting Arguments**: Your arguments in favor of individuals making films are interesting and provide a good basis for discussion. However, make your examples more vivid and specific to strengthen your case. Instead of general statements like "independent filmmakers can express themselves freely", give a specific example of a filmmaker who did this successfully.

6. **Addressing Opposing Views**: You did well to acknowledge opposing viewpoints. Yet, reinforcing your arguments with more evidence or examples would make your position stronger. It's also beneficial to directly refute counterarguments with clear, factual information.

7. **Conclusion**: Your conclusion nicely summarizes your main points, but rephrasing it to directly assert your view would leave a stronger impression. Instead of saying "the merits...certainly surpass its demerits", you could assert "Overall, the positive impact of individuals creating films significantly outweighs any concerns regarding film quality."

This feedback is intended to help you refine your essay. Your ability to engage with the topic is commendable, and with a few adjustments for clarity, voice, and argument structure, your essay could more effectively communicate your insights.

 There are two compelling reasons as to the proliferation of the house or building history exploration. First and foremost, being aware of fascinating building history stories from media can instill individuals to investigate more about that. For example, various simulating narratives of the building history have been portrayed through various TV programs or films. In addition to this, people under an obligation of purchasing or renting new houses or apartments, call a demand for researching carefully about the history. 
 In order to address the aforementioned issue, people should administer the following measures. Firstly, investing time on the internet or social media is key to familiarizing people with information from google or online persons. Inasmuch as the internet is a global network with a host of persons from field and culture differences, people can gain any knowledge they have a soft spot. Another feasible solution could be to ask directly to local residents about the houses or buildings people appeal to explore the history. The help from such persons is irrefutably beneficial and necessary for people to have a comprehensive understanding of the history of these houses or even hidden secrets of them. 
 In conclusion, the general understanding of the history of the buildings or houses that we live in may stem from numerous underlying factors, and the proposed solutions can be executed to reverse the trend.

prompt: Ielts task 2: Discussion about happiness - condicive factors to reach it
essay:
The sole aim of every human being is to live happily. Thus we can assume that happiness plays pivotal role in our lives. However, it takes lots of effort to define the meaning of happiness. In this essay, I will argue the reasons for this issue and suggest some factors that are crucial to reach the true happiness. 
 In the sense that people's goal in livelihood varies widely the deinition of being happy of each individual also differs from that of other's. Possesing happiness in life, to some people, means having good health, owning a huge amount of material value or being in a romantic relationship. In addition, some people define the state less complicated as having a nice family or just being able to exist. 
 In order to achieve this feeling, there are two factors that should not be ignored. Firstly, those who target living happily must be patient. This is because not everything, which makes human happy, is easy to possess, for instance, a big sum of money, a fit body, love... Besides, proper conception is of the same importance. Today, so many people aim to reach happiness supposing that it should be wealth or career success but forget that taking care of their own family members is a kind of happiness as well. For this reason, many are unsatisfied with their lives on account of misunderstanding that their goals are not fulfilled although they have already possessed happiness. 
 In conclusion, happiness, though vital, is hard to give a general deinition by virtue of difference in thinking among individuals. Nevertheless, it is not a painstaking process at all to achieve this mental treasure, as long as we have patience and appreciate the presence of what we have already obtained.
feedback:
This essay introduces an interesting perspective on happiness, aiming to define its meaning and suggest how it can be achieved. The effort to address such a complex topic reflects a commendable ambition. However, there are several areas where this essay could be improved for clarity, coherence, and overall effectiveness.

1. **Response to the Topic:**
The essay attempts to explore the nature of happiness and factors contributing to it, which aligns with a thoughtful examination of personal fulfillment. This focus on happiness is appropriate, demonstrating an understanding of the essay prompt.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, or Stylistic Issues:**
There are noticeable spelling errors (e.g., "deinition" should be "definition") that need correction. Additionally, the essay suffers from grammatical inconsistencies and awkward phrasing that can confuse readers. For instance, the phrase "In the sense that people’s goal in livelihood varies widely" could be simplified to "As people’s goals in life vary widely." Simplifying language and ensuring correct spelling will greatly enhance the readability and professionalism of the essay.

Avoid using informal writing techniques such as ellipses ("...") in academic essays. These are more suited to creative writing rather than formal writing and can distract from the seriousness of your argument.

3. **Clarity of the Author's Point of View:**
The point of view is generally clear, with the essay arguing that happiness is subjective and depends on individual perspectives. However, this point could be strengthened by directly stating the essay's thesis in the introduction and ensuring that each paragraph consistently supports this thesis.

4. **Arguments and Support:**
The essay attempts to cover a broad range of ideas about what contributes to happiness, but in doing so, it becomes somewhat disjointed. Each paragraph introduces several concepts without fully exploring or connecting them. Focusing on a single idea within each paragraph and developing this idea more thoroughly would help maintain coherence and enhance the persuasive power of the essay. For example, instead of briefly mentioning health, wealth, and relationships, choose one, explain its importance to happiness, and support it with evidence or reasoning.

It's important also to avoid introducing new arguments in the conclusion. The conclusion should summarize the points you've made rather than bringing in new information. This recap can reinforce your argument and leave the reader with a clear understanding of your stance on happiness.

This essay shows promise and a strong understanding of the subjective nature of happiness. With attention to spelling and grammar, a more focused organization, and the development of clearer, more coherent arguments, this essay has the potential to effectively convey its insights on a complex and deeply personal topic. Keep exploring your ideas with enthusiasm and consider the feedback to refine your writing skills further.

prompt: Should school leavers take a year off before going to university?
essay:
It is common these days that many high school leavers choose to start their work or go on a trip before going to university. While a gap year can bring immediate drawbacks, I am convinced that it is more likely to have long-term benefits for their lives. 
 Looking at the disadvantages of taking a year off, that school leavers may find difficult to integrate into the university life due to the different environment and learning method is the main point most worth discussing. It can be understandable that students spare the time for revision in the gap year, but the teaching methodology can be unfamiliar with the way they perceive in high school causing many obstacles to absorb the new knowledge. It takes a high pressure on gap-year takers. Besides, the life out of university is mentally and physically overwhelming to inexperienced school leavers. They need a good preparation in order to avoid being exploited at work and dealing with potential dangers on the trip. 
 On the other hand, I would argue that the disadvantages are outweighed by the positive effects. A gap year is an ideal opportunity for students to clarify their future path. The modern society brings either benefits or challenges to youngsters, so they find arduous to choose the dilemma of pursuing their dreams. It is advisable to consider this decision vigorously by travelling or working. The practical lessons from the trips and the jobs will sharpen thoughts and help students become more mature. Moreover, when it comes to applying for a position in a company, the employer has a tendency to recruit the candidate who possess an intensive experience in life and occupation. 
 In conclusion, despite the negative effects, it seems to me that the benefits of a gap year are more significant for the reasons mentioned.
feedback:
The essay presented makes a solid attempt to discuss the topic of high school leavers taking a gap year before university. However, there are areas for improvement to make the argument more compelling and aligned with the essay prompt.

1. **Relevance to the Topic:**
The response to the topic is evident, particularly in the third paragraph, where the benefits of a gap year are discussed in detail. However, the introduction and the initial discussion about disadvantages somewhat deviate from the direct response required by the prompt. To improve, ensure that you understand the prompt fully and use terminology that closely matches the topic. For instance, instead of using broad terms like "drawbacks" and "long-term benefits," more specific language such as "adverse effects" and "favorable outcomes" could help maintain focus and clarity throughout the essay.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, and Style:**
The essay is generally well-written with few spelling or grammar errors. Nevertheless, the writing could benefit from varied sentence structures to enhance readability and engagement. Additionally, some sentences are overly complex or awkwardly phrased, making them difficult to understand on the first read. Simplifying these sentences could improve the overall flow and clarity of the essay.

3. **Clarity of the Author's Point of View:**
The point of view is clear, with a stance that supports taking a gap year despite the initial mention of disadvantages. To strengthen this point of view, directly addressing how the benefits outweigh the drawbacks—using specific examples and clearer arguments—would provide a more persuasive argument.

4. **Arguments Supporting the Author's Position:**
The essay contains descriptive arguments, especially when discussing the advantages of a gap year, like gaining clarity on one's future path and acquiring practical lessons that lead to maturity. However, these arguments could be further enhanced by providing evidence or real-world examples that support the claims made. Additionally, the discussion on disadvantages feels less developed. Balancing both sides with equal scrutiny would make for a more rounded essay.

To improve, focus on closely aligning your essay with the prompt by using appropriate terminology and ensuring a balanced discussion that fully explores both sides of the argument. Simplify and clarify your sentence structure for better readability and strive to include specific examples or evidence to back up your claims. By addressing these points, the essay could significantly improve in coherence, persuasiveness, and alignment with the prompt requirements.

prompt: SPORT CHAMPIONS ARE COMMERCIALIZED THESE DAYS
essay:
Sport is a big business and today 
 Topic: In the past, sporting champions used to be motivated primarily by the desire to win a match or to break world records. These days, they are more likely to be motivated by prize money and the opportunity to be famous. What message does this send to young people and how does this attitude to sport affect the sports themselves? Write an essay within 300 words on the topic above. 
 Answer: 
 Having throwback to the bygone days, it could be seen that sports competitions aimed to enhance sportsmanship and set a new world record rather than rewarding prizes and self-reputation. This essay will present the influence of this phenomenon on the young generation as well as the whole world of sports. 
 To commence with, sports matches had been special occasions on which athletes put enormous efforts to taste victory and reach a gold medal. Thus they were deemed ideal models of constancy and non-stop trying among teenagers. For instance, sportsmanship not only brightened up children who are disabled or suffering from serious mental problems but motivated them to make their dreams come true as well. 
 Contrary to these days, people invariably take notice of a great amount of money that winners and runner-ups reward after a sports league. As a result, their luxurious and flashy lives are increasingly becoming the hottest and most controversial titles in the newspaper every day. Apparently, the original value of sports champions is gradually obliterated in people's mindset. 
 Moreover, the sports industry is being commercialized as the result of paying much higher salaries and satisfying demands for sports stars. Firstly, in order to have enough expenditure to afford normal activities, organizers have to boost their profit by forming leagues. Consequently, that ticket price is utterly increased and more and more commercial advertisements are added during the intervals of matches becomes usual. Therefore, it will lose audiences' interest in sports and make them under the misapprehension that enjoying sports is solely for the wealthy class. Also, we are accustomed to transference contracts related to athletes between influential clubs all over the world. Hence, players are getting more competitive and dominant rather than devoting the best performance for audiences so that they can achieve certain fame and merits. 
 In conclusion, sport commercialization leads to a bad outcome for both young people and sports themselves. It particularly worsens the figure of athletes and causes detrimental effects to this entertainment industry in the long term.
feedback:
This essay does address the topic by exploring how the motivations of sporting champions have shifted from the desire to win to financial gain and fame, and how this change impacts young people and sports in general. However, there are areas for improvement to make the essay clearer and stronger.

1. **Clarity and Simplification of Language**: Certain phrases, like "Having throwback to the bygone days," tend to confuse readers and may also appear grammatically incorrect. It's better to use simple and clear statements such as "In the past, sports champions were motivated by..." Stick to direct expressions and avoid overly complex phrases that might hinder the reader’s understanding.

2. **Structure and Thesis Statement**: Make sure your essay has a clear thesis statement at the end of the introductory paragraph. This statement should outline the main points that will be discussed in the essay. Instead of saying, "This essay will present...," directly state your main argument. For example, "The current focus on prize money and fame negatively impacts young athletes and alters the essence of sports." This clear thesis guides the reader through your argumentation.

3. **Avoiding Unnecessary Words**: The essay sometimes uses excessive wordiness, which can distract from the main points. Focus on keeping the discussion streamlined and relevant to the topic. For example, instead of using phrases like "to commence with," simply continue with your argument. Reducing filler words and sticking to the primary discussion can make your essay more impactful and easier to follow.

4. **Spelling, Grammar, and Cohesion**: There are some minor spelling and grammar errors in the essay that need attention. Additionally, ensuring that all parts of the essay smoothly flow from one to the next will strengthen its overall cohesion. Aim for sentences and paragraphs that logically follow one another, building on your argument clearly and effectively.

5. **Support for Arguments**: While you've presented various ways in which the commercialization of sports affects both young people and the sports industry, expanding on these with more specific examples or clearer explanations would strengthen your argument. Make sure that each point is backed up with a solid rationale or evidence.

By focusing on these improvements, particularly on simplifying language for clarity, structuring the essay more efficiently, and refining grammar and cohesion, your essay will become more persuasive and engaging. Remember, it's not about the number of words but the clarity and strength of your argument that counts.

prompt: In recent years, more and more people are choosing to read e-books rather than paper books
essay:

This essay will first discuss the drawback of this trend, particularly the bad effect to the eyes that might not overshadow its benefit which is mainly related to mobility and environmental protection that e-books can bring about. 
 On the one hand, spending a massive quantity of time on electronic screens has the ability to become a root cause of some serious eye problems. This is because the specific light from e-books may harm the readers' eyes when they overuse it, and it could result in the sleep quality as well. A good example is that more and more children have been suffering from various genres of eye issues and a decline in sleep time due to the lack of time-management skill while reading e-books. 
 However, the readers can bring e-books anywhere and also protect the environment. On account of the small size of e-books that people are able to take or store it conveniently, moreover, they can download numerous books or documents from many sources to read without cutting down the trees to make paper like normal books. For instance, some governments in Asia encourage their residents to use e-books due to the climate change resulting from deforestation to manufacture paper for big companies. 
 In conclusion, reading e-books has more benefits such as the high flexibility and being environmentally-friendly than its downside including eye-harming. Only by using e-books can one maintain a dynamic and sustainable development for the environment.

However, making your position even clearer from the beginning can further strengthen your argument.

The mention of government encouragement in Asia for e-books as an environmentally friendly option is particularly effective. To improve, consider developing your arguments further with more detailed examples or evidence. Your care in reasoning and structuring your essay is evident, and with these adjustments, your writing will become even more compelling and coherent. prompt: Formal education at early age or later than 7. Discuss both views, give your opinion
essay:
Discuss both views and give your own opinion 
 Opinion essay 
 There is a long-running debate on the optimal age for children to commence formal school. While some believe that we should introduce structured education to children as soon as possible, I am of the opinion that the school curriculum should be delayed until the age of seven. 
 On the one hand, those with the former view argue that the sooner approach to academic learning methods could form a stronger foundation of phonological and literacy skills since young children are believed to learn at a more rapid pace than older ones. Early introduction of literacy and numeracy at school could also allow students "not to fall behind" others, giving them better chances to compete with their peers and gain more success in life. In addition, being familiar with academic-intensive curriculum and school regulations, those juniors could develop a range of skills in organizational behaviors, competitiveness and independence at the very early age, which enable them to more easily adapt to their future work. 
 On the other hand, I firmly believe that a later start of formal education, around age of 7, has outweighed benefits for children. There are several strands of evidence which all point towards the importance of play in young children's development, and the value of the extended period of playful learning before the start of formal schooling. A play-based early educational program could enhance crucial interactions between children and the environment, allowing them to strengthen their physical, social, emotional and cognitive development. It is noticeable that those skill sets, if under the application of formal structure of learning, are certainly hindered by the pressure of academic study load and the lack of access to active, creative and outdoor play. As for long-term impacts, the stress-free childhood, earned by the delay of formally taught lessons at school, could massively contribute to their later educational achievements. Recent research shows that in countries where playful experience and self-discovery methods are implemented until the age of 6 or 7 like Sweden and Finland, the rankings in academic results are significantly higher than those with earlier official school entry age. 
 In conclusion,while early academic education could benefit to some extent, I hold a belief that the delayed engagement in formal school could offer more foreseen advantages in the interests of children's future achievements and their emotional well-being.

feedback:

 Although cars powered by electricity are more environmentally friendly since they only need electricity to provide power and release no exhaust fumes, these vehicles are often sold with costly prices. Many people who have low incomes found electric cars to be unaffordable since these automobiles usually cost considerably higher price to purchase. This fact results in individuals struggling to purchase and maintain their own car to travel daily. For instance, in order to buy an electrically powered car, it cost around $19000 higher, on average, than its equivalent conventional car. 
 Another reason that can be justified is that time spent on charging could make commuting more inconvenient. If commuters are in a hurry and their cars run out of battery accidentally, a significant amount of precious time will be wasted on charging the vehicles. Such cars would be considered as a nuisance and, consequently, likely be refused by a number of people to drive them daily. For example, my friend was once reprimanded by his teacher for being late for an extra class due to his automobile's required charging time when traveling from his school. 
 In conclusion, I strongly believe that people should not be banned from driving gasoline-powered cars and accept electric ones as alternatives regarding the financial burden as well as troubles from battery charging time that electric-powered cars create. Each individual should be free to make their choice about which type of vehicles to purchase and run depending on their salary and preferences.

This is because when taking online courses, the students can study at home over their phones or computer without commuting to their university. It is, therefore, an optimal option for the learners since they not only can save money for traveling expenses but also avoid the risks of being exposed to the contagious virus in the context of the global pandemic. Additionally, students of these online classes can study at their own pace because they can replay the lessons as many as they want. Besides that, the availability of lectures on the internet can make high-quality curriculum from prestigious universities accessible to the students at their convenience. 
 On the other hand, there are hosts of compelling reasons why learning online brings with it many disadvantages. For one, online classes can reduce learning and teaching proficiency. In fact, teachers usually find it hard to organize the class because they lack real interaction with their students. In other words, the deficiency of teachers' involvement could cause the decline of students' discipline. As a result, students possibly cut class or cheat in the exams without supervision. Additionally, from the perspective of the learners, they can not fully concentrate on the lectures when they study at home and become surrounded by unwanted distractions such as noise or the temptation of the internet. 
 In conclusion, while it is irrefutable that online education has several benefits, I would contend that this is indeed a negative tendency.

Ensure each argument clearly supports the thesis without ambiguity. Use varied and engaging language to keep the reader's attention, and structure the essay in a way that each paragraph builds upon the last for a coherent and compelling argument against online education.

 Life on a Dole Better than Climate Pollution

 On the positive side, taking a year off makes transition to college study easier for the reason that it offers a wealth of advantages. feedback:

prompt: Countries should not replace their traditional culture with modern culture.
essay:
Traditional culture plays a vitally important role in the existence of a country. Many consider that modern culture can not take over traditional culture. In my opinion, I fully agree with the above statement, and this essay aims to present reasons for my agreement. 
 First of all, traditional culture attaches to the developed history (rooted in the country's history, religious beliefs, and customs) and it holds the values of a nation. These values become national identities. People from over the world can recognize this country through its traditions. One of the most significant Vietnamese festivals that can be taken as a typical example of the traditional culture is Lunar New Year and Banh Chung is mentioned as a special traditional food of Viet Nam that people would make during the Vietnamese Tet holiday. Some examples in other countries such as Kungfu, a traditional Chinese martial art, or Hinduism, the largest religion in India, or Sumo, a traditional sport that has a history of over 1500 years in Japan. In short, a country does not have traditions, does not have history, does not have present and future also. 
 Besides the importance of the traditional culture of a country, the modern culture also plays an indispensable role as the traditional culture in the cultural integration period. Modern cultures help people broaden their horizons by exposing them to new knowledge, and cultures in different countries, therefore, if people have a selective perception, they enhance their awareness of happiness, self-worth, lawful rights and interests,.... Removing backward social biases such as sexism, classicism, racism, and superstitious makes people more comfortable and happier. A country changes traditions that are no longer suited to the modern period so it makes that country can adapt to and has a long-term development in the globalization process. 
 In conclusion, modern culture actually can not replace the traditional culture of a country but in cultural integration, modern culture and traditional culture can complement each other to give a country access to advanced values and maintain the national's sustainable development.

1. **Response to the Topic**: The essay adequately addresses the given topic, presenting a clear stance that traditional culture plays an essential role in a country’s existence and cannot be replaced by modern culture. 

2. **Spelling, Grammar, and Stylistic Issues**: There are minor grammatical errors and awkward phrases that could be simplified for clarity. For example, "traditional culture attaches to the developed history" could be clearer. Consider using more straightforward language like "traditional culture is deeply rooted in a country's history." Additionally, watch out for run-on sentences and ensure each sentence delivers a clear point.

3. **Clarity of the Author's Point of View**: The author's viewpoint is clear - they believe in the irreplaceable value of traditional culture. However, making the reasoning more concise and direct could strengthen the argument. Also, it's crucial to balance the essay by briefly acknowledging opposing viewpoints before refuting them with your arguments.

4. **Arguments and Support**: The essay provides examples to support the importance of traditional culture, like Lunar New Year in Vietnam and Kungfu in China. However, these examples could be more effectively integrated into the argument by directly linking them to how they promote a country's identity and unity. Furthermore, while discussing modern culture's role, make sure to clearly differentiate how it complements rather than replaces traditional culture.

**Additional Points Based on Feedback**:
- Aim for brevity and clarity. Instead of using many words to explain a point, strive to convey your ideas concisely. This approach not only makes your essay easier to understand but also aligns with exam criteria favoring clear, coherent arguments within a specific word limit.
- Focus on the cohesiveness of your presentation. Ensure each paragraph transitions smoothly to the next, and all parts of your essay are clearly connected to your main argument. Using linking words effectively can help with this.

To improve further, consider rewriting a segment of your essay with these points in mind. Work on simplifying complex sentences and ensuring that each sentence directly contributes to your argument. Practice makes perfect, and refining your ability to argue effectively within a word limit is a valuable skill for essay writing in English proficiency tests.

prompt: Benefits of Student Exchange - This is my ielts writing task 2

Another downside is that many students are unable to read their international programmes by virtue of the difference of languages which makes the subjects become more elusive for them.  In my opinion, however, the benefits of international student exchange are deemed to be more significant than the drawbacks. Firstly, It is an opportunity that arises for them when they can cultivate their knowledge and social skills, the things that they might have not chance to learn in their home country. For instance, Education System in Vietnam believes that theoretical knowledge takes precedence over practical skills shown to cause many pressures on students. Secondly, It is common knowledge that they would be more well informed about different cultures when exchange students could gain valuable experiences in lieu of learning from newspapers and social media. prompt: IELTS Writing Task 2 - Owning a home is more important than renting

Therefore, in order to be able to afford house ownership, most people would have to work very hard and save money. Some people could also use credit schemes, which would make the house price more expensive. Sometimes it takes years until the loan pays off. 
 Overall, I think it's good that in some countries people strive to buy their own house even though it's not always an easy task.
