Despite I personally believe that children should move out of the family home as soon as they are grown up, this essay will examine both sides of the issue and provide with relevant examples. 
 First of all, it is undoubtful that living apart from parents enables an adolescent to develop into a mature person, both mentally and financially. As soon as an infant leaves a parental house, he has no choice but to acquire problem solving skills which are necessary in various aspects of life, such as performing household chores, handling his own finances, and tackling with social interaction. Moreover, in order to cover all the living expenses, a juvenile would endeavor best efforts to secure a well-remunerated job. For example, a recent research by a university of Cincinnati showed that 72 per cent of American adults aged 18, who live on their own, succeeded to secure a well-paid job. 
 Yet there are some opponents of this idea that are convinced infants would benefit a great deal more from settling in their parental house. Objectively, daily communication and timespending with a close-knit family could nothing but contribute to strengthening family bonds as well as preserving family traditions. For instance, it is widely common for the Italians aged 18 to 30 to live together with their folks without suffering from family estrangement. Additional benefit of staying in the parental house for a long time is being assisted financially. For example, a child supported by parents is likely to save up a desirable amount of money for tuition fees or pay off the student loan. 
 To conclude, I firmly believe that although encouraging children to live with a family may be fairly beneficial, the most valuable experience can be acquired through living separately from them, since only then can juveniles stand on their own feet and become self-sufficient as well.
feedback:

6. **Revisions and Proofreading**: Allocating time to review your essay can significantly enhance its quality. Look for opportunities to simplify complex sentences and correct any spelling, grammar, or punctuation errors.

In recent years, Indonesia, for example, has allocated a sizable budget for high school and college scholarships. As a result, the policy has benefited many students from low-income families. 
 On the other hand, some people think that when it comes to the country's goals, the government should consider other types of progress rather than just economic development. Another progress that takes into consideration is the unemployment rate. Indeed, this context is critical for a certain demographic of society because the more people who have income and become self-sufficient, the more prosperous a country will be. prompt: IELTS task 2 about "What are the changes of family structures and family roles"
essay:
In the past decade, there has been tremendous changes in the households worldwide, regarding to their structures and the distribution of family tasks. I think most of these changes are associated with adverse impacts on family. 
 To begin with, compared to the traditionally pervasive extended family structure, the majority of people now live in nuclear families, in which only parents and children live in one house or apartment. Children move out from their parents' home after 18 years old instead of staying with parents, and each single family normally lives independently with their cousins. In addition, rather than having multiple children in one family, children now rarely have siblings due to "one-child policy", and this is particularly the case in China. Meanwhile, unlike the previous period when it is the women who were responsible for taking care of their offspring, in modern family, there is a greater number of men who share this family role, and domestic status of two genders has become much more equal. 
 For the positive influences, firstly, thanks to the nuclear family structure and fewer children in one immediate family, the financial burden on families has been largely mitigated. This is because in this way current parents do not have to pay a high total tuition fee for several kids. Besides, women have earned more respect, because they play more social roles and make more contributions to the society. 
 However, there are also several potential risks stemming from these changes. Firstly, one-child family means that the child is likely to be spoiled, making them self-centred and less considerate, thereby impairing their personality goodness. In addition, considering that adults live far away from their parents or children, it is increasingly difficult for them to have family reunion, so they fail to bond with families, which leads to a weak feeling of belonging. 
 To conclude, I think although family can benefit from these changes financially, there are huge problems linked with this issue.
feedback:
The essay addresses the topic of changes in household structures and their effects on families, showing a clear understanding of the prompt. However, the focus on China's "One Child Policy" limits the discussion, making it too specific for a prompt that seeks a more general discussion. When writing essays, especially for tests like IELTS, it's important to keep the discussion broad unless the question specifies a need for personal opinion or focuses on a particular country or policy.

Regarding your opinion, it's briefly mentioned at the end of the essay, which is not the best practice. Opinions should be fully developed and presented in a separate paragraph before the conclusion. This allows you to explore and justify your point of view adequately, ensuring the reader understands your position on the topic. The conclusion should then summarize the main points discussed without introducing new ideas or opinions.

On grammar and style, there are some issues to note. The opening sentence mentions "tremendous changes," which would be more accurately described as "tremendous change." Additionally, certain phrases could be simplified for clarity, and there are minor spelling errors, like "concidering," which should be "considering." It's also important to maintain a consistent point of view throughout the essay and ensure that your arguments are clear and supported by descriptive examples or explanations.

Despite these areas for improvement, the essay does provide a coherent argument on the impact of changes in family structure. To strengthen your essay, try to present examples that apply broadly and avoid focusing on specific policies or countries unless required. Make sure every paragraph supports your main point clearly, and revisit your conclusion to ensure it effectively wraps up your discussion without introducing new information.

Improving these aspects will make your argument stronger and your writing more persuasive, helping you achieve a higher score on your essay.

prompt: Recent research has shown that business meetings and training are increasingly taking place online.
essay:
The survey shows that online business meetings, discussions and training are becoming more and more popular. In my opinion, although there are two aspects to this argument, I tend to believe that the disadvantages outweigh the advantages. 
 It is sensible for some people to think that online work is more convenient. This is because working online allows them to work at anytime and anywhere, they could attend more meetings and events, which is impossible without the Internet. However, I believe that they have forgotten the impact of network speed on online work. If the Internet gets stuck, their experience would be terrible because of the intermittent work. Their work's efficiency might not be improved, but also seriously decreased. This might contrary to their initial purpose and inherit the disastrous consequences. 
 On the other hand, working face-to-face seems to be more efficient. When people contact immediately, they could detect the change of other people's behaviors and emotions, and also measure how interested someone is in what are they talking about by reading their body language, which might be significantly essential for ideal communication. For example, if someone's legs are head to the door, that means they might want to leave. We could know it once we are seated in front of them and this is unfeasible when we work online. 
 In conclusion, I concede online works bring substantial benefits. Nevertheless, for the reasons mentioned above, I have a firm belief that the detriments of it gain the upper hand over the benefits.
feedback:
The essay addresses the topic of the increasing popularity of online business meetings, discussions, and training. It presents arguments concerning both the advantages and disadvantages of this trend, aiming to compare the two sides. However, there are several areas where improvements could be made to strengthen the essay's overall effectiveness and adherence to the task requirements.

1. **Topic Response and Presentation**: The introduction attempts to engage with the topic by referencing a survey but uses an incorrect phrase "The survey shows" instead of employing a more varied vocabulary. To improve, consider rephrasing it to "Recent findings indicate an increased frequency of..." to distance the language from the original prompt and prevent potential scoring deductions in the Lexical Resource (LR) section. The task asks for a comparative discussion, not for a personal opinion on the benefits and disadvantages. Thus, focusing on presenting the information in a balanced manner without inserting personal views would be more in line with the task requirements.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, and Style**: The essay contains minor grammatical and stylistic issues that could impact its clarity. For instance, the phrase "This might contrary to their initial purpose and inherit the disastrous consequences" is unclear and grammatically incorrect. A clearer alternative could be, "This might contradict their initial purpose and lead to disastrous consequences." Simplifying sentence structures and carefully reviewing grammar can make the arguments more accessible and persuasive.

3. **Clarity of Viewpoint**: The essay's point of view seems to lean towards the disadvantages of online work, despite the task not requiring a personal stance. To align more closely with the task, it would be beneficial to present the advantages and disadvantages more neutrally and avoid concluding with a personal belief on the matter.

4. **Arguments and Support**: The essay provides specific examples to support the discussion, such as the potential issues caused by unreliable internet and the benefits of face-to-face interaction for gauging body language. Enhancing the essay by including more varied examples and possibly citing studies or statistics could further strengthen the comparative discussion of online versus face-to-face work. 

In the final paragraph, rather than conceding and reiterating a personal belief, aim to summarize the discussion neutrally, highlighting the key points made about both advantages and disadvantages without expressing a personal preference. 

By addressing these points, the essay can more effectively meet the task's requirements, present a balanced discussion, and potentially achieve a higher score in both the Lexical Resource and Task Response sections.

prompt: IELTS task 2: Essay about fast food is becoming increasingly popular in most countries.
essay:
--- Here is my essay--- 
 In recent years, fast food has dramatic changes to our habitual diet and becoming well-known in the world especially in affluent western countries. Some people said that this kind of food has some benefits ,however in this essay, I intend to argue that these food have far more demerits than few advantages it offers. 
 First, in most of high standard of living countries prefer eating pre-packaged foods such as hamburger, chicken fried or chips rather than eating well-cooked foods. Although I certainly agree that fast food is both affordable and convenient, it contains a number of unhealthy additives like sugar, fat and salt. If people consume this kind of food as the way they add these to the staple diet in daily routine, they would get some serious health problems such as high blood pressure, obesity, depress and so on. In other words, while fast food is beneficial in the short term, its long-term effects are generally negative. 
 Second, fast food is gradually creeping in daily meals especially in children and a big brand like Ronald McDonalds is the particularly good example. The visual image showing that the way McDonalds clown standing straight and smiling which is appealing young children and also catch their parent attention. Having grown up eating in McDonald restaurants, people are likely to continue eating fast food throughout their adult lives. A number of people in most of western countries are now faced to the risk of obesity and the statics are more increasing significantly. 
 To conclude, I once again restate my view that fast food is detrimental to both individuals who eat it and to society at large. Authority health needs to increase public awareness about the dangerous effect of consuming to excess and giving the health risks associated with this trend.
feedback:
The essay presents a clear stance on the negative impacts of fast food on health and society, which directly responds to the topic. However, several areas require improvement to enhance the essay's quality and adherence to academic standards.

1. **Tone and Language**: The essay's tone can be improved by adopting a more academic and neutral style. Phrases like "I intend to argue" may come across as confrontational. It is more appropriate to use expressions such as "I believe" or "I would suggest". Maintaining an academic tone is crucial in delivering your viewpoint without seeming aggressive. This approach ensures your essay is received more positively by the reader.

2. **Depth of Argument**: The essay commendably uses the A/D single paragraph presentation, which is beneficial. The first reasoning paragraph offers a solid, though somewhat brief, discussion on the health risks associated with fast food. Expanding on these points with more details or examples could strengthen the argument. Conversely, the second paragraph about the influence of fast food branding, particularly the reference to Ronald McDonald, lacks depth. Connecting the discussion more closely to personal experiences or broader social implications could provide a stronger, more relatable argument. 3. **Accuracy and Clarity**: There's a minor error regarding the name of the fast-food restaurant. It's important to correctly refer to McDonald's, not Ronald McDonalds, to maintain accuracy. Furthermore, articulating the potential influence of marketing tactics like mascots on consumer behavior could be clarified. Explaining why and how these tactics may lead to increased fast food consumption among children and adults would provide a comprehensive argument.

4. **Grammar and Style**: There are several grammatical and stylistic issues within the essay, including the use of commas, conjunctions, and the overall flow of sentences. It is recommended to review punctuation rules, particularly around the use of commas and transitions between ideas. Aim for simpler, more concise sentences to improve clarity and readability.

5. **Conclusion and Call to Action**: The conclusion successfully restates the main viewpoint but could further motivate the reader by offering practical recommendations or solutions. Discussing ways of increasing public awareness or suggesting alternative dietary choices could make the closing remarks more impactful.

Improving these aspects will significantly elevate the quality of the essay, making it more compelling and academically appropriate. Reflecting on these points and revisiting certain sections of the text will likely result in a more effective and persuasive piece.

feedback:
The essay effectively addresses the topic, which is to discuss the impact of computers on our daily lives. However, it's important to refine the approach to better align with the expectations of an English proficiency test, such as the IELTS. Here's how to improve the essay:

1. **Introduction and Thesis Statement**: It's crucial to start your essay by directly addressing the essay question without offering your opinion or additional information right away. Your thesis statement should clearly present the topic under discussion. A more suitable introduction might be, "The advent of computers has significantly impacted our daily lives, with some arguing it simplifies tasks, while others see it as adding complexity. 2. **Transition and Structure**: Instead of marking transitions with numbers (Firstly, Secondly, Thirdly), try using more natural and varied sentence structures to lead from one paragraph to the next. To further enhance your essay, ensure your examples are directly related to the arguments made. Also, it's important to address potential counterarguments to provide a balanced perspective. For instance, discuss the common concern that computers can lead to misinformation and how critical thinking can help mitigate this issue.

For instance, "now are using" should be "are now used," and "has a computer" should be "have computers." Pay attention to agreement between subject and verb, and plural and singular forms. Enhancing your grammar and spelling will significantly improve the clarity and professionalism of your essay.

6. **Concluding Statement**: While your conclusion summarizes the essay well, it could be strengthened by briefly reiterating your main points and stating the importance of the subject. Avoid introducing new examples or arguments in this section.

By incorporating these suggestions, you'll be better able to structure your essay in a way that's aligned with English proficiency test expectations, making your argument more effective and your writing clearer and more engaging. Remember, practice makes perfect, and each essay is a step towards mastering the art of persuasive writing.

prompt: Some people say that physical exercise should be a required part of every school day. Others say that pupils should spend whole school day on academic studies. Which opinion do you agree with? Give reasons to support your choice.
essay:
These days, some schools have included physical exercise as a part of educational curriculum. Whether they should turn it into a daily compulsory activity or neglect it, only concentrate on academic learning is a debatable issue. My view is that regular exercise is significantly beneficial to the pupils for the following reasons. 
 First of all, frequent exercise optimize the quality of learning, which means helping students study more efficiently. Because stress and fatigue which usually stem from overload learning hours spent on the classes will be dispelled immediately when students are involved in bodily movement during the break time. Therefore, with refreshed mind and body, they have better preparation, more ready for the next lessons. A recent research of Learning Method Institute has reported that students who have physical exercise between two 45-minute lessons study 30 percent more efficiently than those who do not. 
 Moreover, it is obvious that physical exercise contributes positively to the student's overall health. Because sport activities help to maintain physical fitness, boost the immune system, improve mental health, strengthen the individual endurance and so on, students with daily exercise show more active, energetic and healthier than others. Acknowledging these benefits, instead of imposing long - day academic study on pupils, schools should provide them with more opportunities to engaging in sport movements. 
 That is not to say that academic knowledge is not important at all. It, of course, is a basic, required part of every learner's knowledge and plays a vital role in individual life and future. However, intensive learning this type of knowledge without any break points for relaxing is redundant and may be counter-productive. 
 In conclusion, daily exercise deserves to receive encouragement because of all advantages it has. Meanwhile, we should not under-estimate the necessity of academic study. Schools should schedule both of them properly, by doing so, the efficiency of student's learning will be promoted notably.
feedback:
The essay effectively addresses the topic, presenting a well-reasoned argument in favor of incorporating physical exercise into the educational curriculum. The points about enhanced learning efficiency, improved overall health, and the balance between academic and physical education are clearly made and support the author's viewpoint. However, there are several areas where improvements can be made to strengthen the writing.

1. **Grammar and Sentence Structure:** 
- There's a subject-verb agreement error with "optimize"; it should be "optimizes" to match the singular subject.
- When indicating possession for plural nouns like "students," use "students'" instead of "students."
- Avoid double comparatives; instead of "more ready," use "readier" for the correct comparative form.
- The phrase "both of them" is redundant; "both" is sufficient and clearer.
- Use "only concentrating" instead of "only concentrate" for grammatical accuracy in referring to ongoing actions.
- Be careful with starting sentences with "because." It's typically not used to begin a sentence. Instead, integrate it within a sentence to connect ideas more smoothly.

2. **Clarity and Coherence:**
- Aim for shorter sentences to improve clarity. Long, run-on sentences can be confusing and detract from your argument. Split complex ideas into multiple sentences for better understanding.

prompt: IELTS WRITING TASK 2: Free education or new technology in developing countries.
essay:
There are controversial perspectives fueling a debate over the method to improve people's life in many developing nations. While some believe that the key is to introduce new kinds of technology, others would argue that free education should be implemented. Although each has its own perks, I would regard myself as an advocate of the latter. 
 Undoubtedly, technological advancements are the keys to numerous dire issues in many underdeveloped nations. Given the fact that most of these countries' infrastructures are either outdated or the efficiency is relatively low, introducing a new sort of techs would help them to start industrializing and modernizing their countries to a new standard. Vietnam, which was a war-torn country, can be cited as an outstanding instance regarding this. The government rebuilt the country by overhauling the technical foundation of Vietnam, making Vietnam one of the fastest developing nations. Thus, a new implementation of technological advancement would bring tremendous benefits in emerging countries. 
 While the merits of applying new techs are widely acknowledged, I would argue that offering free education could result in a wealth of significant benefits. Considering that most of the population of these underdeveloped countries are either adolescents or young workers, it would be pivotal to provide them free and sufficient education. If they do not have enough general knowledge, technical advancement will be in vain. For example, a number of countries in Africa decided to heavily invest in technology in lieu of educating the younger generation. As a result, they could not catch up with the complexities of those machines. Hence, adequate education should be provided to all citizens in emerging countries. 
 In conclusion, despite investing national savings in technology might bring numerous advantages, I would argue that the authorities in developing nations should spend their budget on free education instead. 
 299 words
feedback:
The essay effectively addresses the topic, which concerns the debate over how to improve lives in developing nations, focusing on the dichotomy between technology and free education. There is a clear stance in favor of free education. However, a more balanced presentation that incorporates different perspectives could strengthen the argument.

There are no significant spelling mistakes, but there are some areas where grammatical and stylistic improvements could enhance readability and clarity. For instance, the use of “techs” could be replaced with the more standard term “technologies” for clarity and formality. Additionally, the phrase “controversial perspectives fueling a debate” might mislead by suggesting a more contentious debate than presented. It's essential to accurately represent the discussion without adding or exaggerating information, as this could impact the essay's credibility.

The author's point of view is clear throughout the essay, favoring free education over technological advances as a means to improve the lives of people in developing countries. This perspective is consistently supported with reasoning and examples, though the essay would benefit from exploring and acknowledging counterarguments more thoroughly to demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of the topic.

Regarding arguments, they are generally clear and descriptive, particularly with the example of Vietnam’s technological development and the emphasis on the necessity of education. However, the essay could be improved by deepening the discussion on how and why free education can provide more considerable benefits than technological advances. This involves not only stating the position but also demonstrating a balanced consideration of both sides of the debate. Adding perspectives that are not solely the author's—for instance, by referencing studies, reports, or a wider range of examples—could offer a more rounded argument.

In conclusion, while the essay presents a coherent argument in favor of free education, it would benefit greatly from a more balanced discussion, careful choice of terms, and a deeper exploration of how education serves as the foundation for technological advancements and overall development in emerging countries. Attention to these aspects can make the argument more persuasive and the essay more compelling.

prompt: The graph depicts the percentage of four different materials recycled over the period of 28 years
essay:
The graph depicts the percentage of four different materials recycled ( paper and cardboard, glass containers, aluminium cans and plastics) over 28 years from 1982 to 2010. 
 Overall, there was an upward trend in recycling paper and cardboard, compared to other materials, this rate was higher. Glass containers and aluminium cans had a rise throughout the period, whilst plastics was the least recycled between 1982 and 2010. 
 It is noticeable that 60% of paper and cardboard was recycled in 1982. This figure increased slightly to 70% in the year 1986 and dropped at 65% throughout the year 1990. Afterwards, paper and cardboard had a dramatic increase to 80% 4 years after, but suddenly had a decline and hit to 70% in the year 2010. This rate was higher, compared to other materials under 70%. 
 As we can see in the chart, glass containers were 50% in the beginning year ( in 1982), then significantly decreased to 40% in 1990. In addition, the recycling of glass containers shown an upturn and hit 60% for 20 years. It is interesting to note that aluminium cans recycled began in 1986. Although there were 5% of them were recycled, the rate started to rose enormously and picked up to 45% in 2010. Plastic recycling began in 1990 and remained the least recycled material ( less than 10%) throughout the given period.
feedback:
The essay provides an analysis of recycling trends for various materials over a period from 1982 to 2010. However, there are several areas where improvements could be made to enhance clarity, accuracy, and effectiveness.

1. **Clarity on the Type of Graph:** The essay starts by mentioning "The graph" without specifying the type of graph. It's important to clarify whether it is a bar chart, line graph, pie chart, etc. This detail helps set a clearer context for the reader.

2. **Sentence Structure in Introduction:** The initial attempt to describe the overall trend could be more effectively presented in two separate sentences. One can describe the general upward trend, and another can compare the relative rates of recycling among the materials. This separation will make the information easier to follow.

3. **Year References:** The essay sometimes uses vague references to time periods, such as "Afterwards" and "4 years after," which can be confusing. It's more effective to specify the exact year being discussed. If pointing to a change over time, directly stating the years (e.g., "from 1996 to 2000") could make the essay more precise and easier to understand.

4. **Avoid Phrases That Assume Visuals:** Phrases like "As we can see in the chart" are less effective when there is no image provided for the reader. Instead, aim to describe the data in a way that enables the reader to visualize the trends without seeing the graph. This involves more descriptive language that outlines key data points and changes over time.

5. **Grammatical and Stylistic Issues:** There are small grammar and spelling errors, such as using "rose" instead of "rose." Additionally, consider using a more formal tone in academic writing by choosing words and phrases that convey an objective analysis of data.

6. **Detail and Descriptiveness:** Though the essay attempts to describe trends, there's room to add more descriptive detail about the data. When significant changes in the data are mentioned, explaining possible reasons for these shifts or their implications could add depth to the analysis.

The point of view is relatively clear, focusing on the trends in recycling rates for different materials. The argument that paper and cardboard have seen significant increases in recycling rates over time is supported by specific data points, though these could be more effectively highlighted with clearer year references and a more detailed explanation of the changes observed.

By addressing these points, the essay can become a more comprehensive and engaging analysis of the trends in recycling rates over the examined period.

prompt: How individuals can contribute to environment protection.

 First of all, the bottom line of ever-growing pollution stems from the daily habits of people. Excessive energy consumption and wasting unrenewable resources like water or gas are the major culprits that exacerbate the environmental conditions day by day. In addition, switching off the appliances that are not in use can reduce the staggering number of electricity being consumed and thus indirectly curtail the exhaust fumes from the procedure of burning coal in energy factories. 
 Furthermore, splurging on advanced and modern merchandise can also effectively curb your carbon footprint emitted to the environment. Foster inhabitants to drive electric cars or hydrogen engine vehicles can facilitate the habilitating process of the ozone layers by diminishing the amount of emissions being released. Prioritizing using public services to commute and avoid traveling long distances on large transportation such as planes or coaches will stand us in good stead by cutting down on the greenhouse gases that jeopardize the air quality. 
 In conclusion, the earth is our only home and human should take responsibility for protecting the prosperity and beauty of this planet through varied solutions from individuals to organizations.

prompt: Write a reflection report on the group work you've done
essay:
Kebab rice noodles is one of the most popular dishes of Vietnamese traditional food. It is the favorite dish of many tourists when they come to visit Hanoi. Last week, I and my friends have done a comparative report about kebab rice noodles (or "bun cha" in Vietnamese) at two different places: famous Huong Lien restaurant and a small food store near Banking Academy. In this report, I am going to reflect about the progress of how we have done that comparative report. 
 The report is a home writing report and it lasts three weeks. Because it is a small project, it is divided into three steps. At the first step, we spent a week discussing on the topic. We brought up many ideas such as: drinks, game or cosmetic, but finally we chose foods as our topic and kebab rice noodles was the item to be compared. At the second step, we chose the places: Huong Lien restaurant and a small food store near Banking Academy. We went to each place and tasted the dish, took many photos as evidences. At the last step, we wrote the comparative report and prepared the presentation. Each member had her part of presentation and she had to finish it before the deadline. 
 During only three weeks, I leaned a lot. It surprised me when I tasted the dish of both places as the flavor is different from the other. It turned out each place had its own method of cooking. I also learned how to list out the basic standards to compare those two. It was not easy. 
 However, there were issues that I had to face when having the dish compared. It was not all about the flavor or the ingredients but it was also arrangement of the dish. It took time and effort to meet all the standards. In addition, we had different timetable and managed it together. Finally, I regretted that I could have done a better report. 
 What I do not like about the team work is that we spent much more time choosing topic than we should have, which makes us have little time writing personal report and literally no time for presentation. Fortunately, we did it quite well. Next time, I suggest we should spend just a week on topic and two weeks left for the other tasks. Plus, I find the comparative report a little time-wasting. The program should be narrowed down the topics as it is hard to choose a suitable one. However, this is the most interesting assignment have done. It is like trip to us and we had happy moments together.
feedback:
The essay on Kebab rice noodles, a popular Vietnamese dish, presents an insightful view into a comparative food analysis project. However, there are opportunities to refine and enhance the structure and clarity to effectively communicate your experiences and findings. Here’s a breakdown of how to improve based on the outlined criteria and the suggested structure:

1. **Response to the Topic**: It’s evident that the essay attempts to discuss a comparative analysis project of kebab rice noodles from two different locations. An introductory paragraph setting this scene will help readers understand why this project was undertaken.

For example, "I and my friends have done" should be revised to "my friends and I did." Also, ensure verb tenses are consistent throughout the essay, shifting from present perfect tense (“have done”) to simple past (“did”) where appropriate, as the project has already been completed.

3. **Clarity of the Author’s Point of View**: Your personal reflection and learning outcome from the project come through in the essay. To make your point of view even clearer, explicitly state your role in the project and your initial expectations. This approach will give readers a more personal connection to your narrative.

4. **Arguments Supporting the Author's Position**: The essay mentions various aspects of the comparative analysis, including the flavor differences and challenges faced. To strengthen the argumentation, elaborate on each restaurant's unique cooking methods and ingredient selection in separate paragraphs as part of your analysis. Emphasize your taste test criteria and how those standards impacted your final judgement. - **Tasting and Analysis**: Detail the tasting experience, comparing your expectations with the actual outcomes. Discuss any differing opinions within the group and how you reconciled them with your own assessment criteria.
- **Conclusions and Reflections**: Conclude with the challenges faced during the project, both in terms of content and group collaboration. prompt: Students should have the right to make comments about their teachers - IELTS Writing Task 2

From my perspective, while many people believe that this may be the precursor of indiscipline and disrespect in schools, it would seem that this trend is one of the most effective ways to increase educational quality. 
 There are a few reasons why some people resist the propose to allow students to criticise their teachers. The primary reason is that criticizing teachers may alleviate their influence to many students. As a result, those students may inferior the role of teachers on pedagogy, which can obviously lead to the disrespectful attitude of students to their teachers. Another significant reason is that some teachers have a very high self-esteem that can be undermined when they are criticised by their descendants. Consequently, they may significantly be discouraged from teaching so that the students's learning outcome may be exacerbated. 
 However, there are more compelling reasons to believe that this method can remarkably enhance the quality of pedagogy. On the one hand, students are those people who have the capability to judge and criticize their teachers most precisely because they are taught by those teachers. As a result, teachers can absorb those responses from students before starting to adjust their teaching methods to satisfy all students. On the other hand, the propose of pedagogy is to satisfy students's demands and enhance their knowledge so that students should have the right to make comments and criticize their teachers. For example, in many developed countries, the student-centred teaching method with two-way communication are employed in their school to respond to every students's perspectives about their school, which can substantially improve the effectiveness of teaching programs. 
 In conclusion, the perspective that students should have the right to make comments about their teachers is highly recommended.

prompt: Although more and more people read the news on the Internet, newspapers will remain the main source
essay:
Although more and more people read the news on the Internet, newspapers will remain the main source of news for the majority of people. 
 To what extent do you agree or disagree? 
 Write at least 250 words. 
 Nowadays, despite the fact that there is an increasing number of people reading online news, others believe that traditional newspapers will still hold the most vital position for most people. Personally, I disagree with this point for some reasons. 
 Thanks to the technology developing process, online news has an advantage over paper newspapers. Firstly, the higher speed of conveying updated news to people is the most important advantage of online resources compared with paper-based newspapers. For example, when a natural disaster occurs over the world, news websites can report on it within minutes, while newspapers take until the next day to report it. Secondly, when news readers move from one place to another, instead of picking up a magazine at stores, they only need to take their cell phones or some other hand-held devices to access the internet to read news. Finally, readers can leave comments, share articles and interact with each other on forums and social networks, which helps them exchange opinions and discuss reported issues. 
 On top of that, reading a newspaper digitally rather than in traditional paper form is probably less damaging to the environment. If the demand for reading newspapers increased, that would produce many papers involving cutting trees. Consequently, there can be a significant increase in the rate of deforestation throughout our planet. In addition, the production of newspapers can also result in pollution. Some of the chemicals utilized in paper manufacturing can be discharged into the air, water and soil, which pose a risk to the environment. 
 In conclusion, I believe that the evidence suggests that newspapers are declining in popularity and are likely to be replaced by online news sources as the main source of news for the majority of people in the future.
feedback:
Your essay provides a clear stance on the topic, which is that newspapers are likely to be replaced by online news sources as the main source of news for the majority of people. This stance is consistent throughout the essay, demonstrating a good understanding of the question being asked. However, there are areas for improvement to make your essay stronger and more aligned with the expectations of English proficiency tests.

1. **Response to the Topic:** You've addressed the topic directly, which is excellent. However, your argument would benefit from a more measured approach. Instead of simply stating that you disagree with the idea that newspapers will remain the main source of news, consider mentioning the extent or conditions of your disagreement. For example, saying "I disagree to a limited extent" and providing reasons why could offer a more nuanced view and meet the requirements more precisely.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, and Stylistic Issues:** Your essay is largely free from grammatical errors, demonstrating proficiency in this area. To enhance the readability and flow, pay attention to varying your sentence structures and using transitions smoothly between paragraphs. While the essay is well-written, careful proofreading can still enhance clarity and coherence.

3. **Clarity of Point of View:** Your point of view is clear throughout the essay, which is great. Remember, it is crucial to maintain this clarity while adding more depth to your argument by mentioning the extent of your agreement or disagreement as previously suggested.

4. **Arguments in Support:** You have provided clear and descriptive arguments in support of your view, such as the speed and convenience of online news and the environmental impacts of traditional newspapers. These arguments are well-chosen and effectively support your position. To strengthen your essay further, consider adding a counterargument paragraph where you briefly acknowledge the other viewpoint before reinforcing why you still hold your position. This addition would demonstrate your ability to engage critically with varying perspectives.

In conclusion, focusing on a more nuanced expression of your stance, enhancing stylistic elements, and potentially including a counterargument can significantly improve your essay. Keep practicing these strategies to improve both your writing skills and your scores on English proficiency tests.

prompt: Writing task 2: It is better to live in vertical city than horizontal city.

 From my perspective, despite concerns about the resilience of skyline towers, the advantages of vertical city outweigh those of horizontal residences. While vertical living boosts work productivity, horizontal neighbourhoods bond us together. However, it appears to me that vertical city will play a vital role as a future recourse compared to horizontal city.

prompt: Ads lead people to make unnecessary purchases or they just introduce new products to customers

 Others say that advertisements tell us about new products that may improve our lives. 
 The world has been far developing to such an extent that the role of "advertising" is supposed to change. Some people hold firm to their belief that ads lead people to make unnecessary purchases; whilst, opponents argue that they introduce new products to customers. From my perspective, although the first idea is true to some extent, the second seems much more reasonable. 
 On the one hand, it is undeniable that customers' driving force to buy unneeded items is a result of advertising. Firstly, the demand for a more convenient life has recently increased. Once brands have already recognised this, they will introduce new products qualified enough to meet buyers' basic needs. Hence, people will build a habit of purchasing a larger number of goods. Additionally, it is wise marketing strategies that also encourage people to buy more than what they want. Acknowledging their customers' tendencies, brands will apply a lot of approaches to direct their customers. For instance, Shopee becomes well-known among online purchasers for its celebrity endorsement and flash sale campaigns. 
 On the other hand, that advertisements are of great benefits to people's lives is without question. Obviously, customers cannot only be well-provided with more information about products but may also raise their awareness about social issues sometimes included in brands' advertising campaigns. Take Pepsi's 2016 video, which contains both their drinks and current political problems in the USA, as a prime example. Furthermore, the more frequently ads are shown to the public, the better varieties of products are available to customers. As a result, they will have more choices of goods; therefore, making better decisions of what to buy, which will gradually improve their living standards. 
 In conclusion, despite unnecessary purchases encouraged by advertisements, they undoubtedly do great wonders to us. Hence, it is imperative that we become discerning customers in order to gain best benefits from advertising instead of being manipulated.

3. **Developing Arguments**: The essay benefits from discussing both views on advertising; however, it's essential to ensure that the argumentation directly supports the position you have chosen. If the task requires a definitive stance, allocate more space to elaborating on why you support this particular viewpoint, using specific examples and clear reasoning.

4. **Task Response and Comprehension**: It's important to accurately understand and adhere to the instructions provided in the essay prompt. Practicing with a variety of prompts can improve comprehension and ensure task responses are on target. Before writing, take time to carefully read and analyze the prompt to ensure your essay will directly answer the question asked.

prompt: WRITING TASK 2: Every year several languages die out.
essay:

Some hold the belief that they do not have to concern about it due to the fact that life will be more comfortable when fewer languages are spoken in the world. I would say that I strongly disagree with this opinion because of its possible negative effects on our lives. 
 Language contributes to our lives in several ways. Apparently, language is the identity of a race. Every race in the world has its own language. It should be learnt by each individual so that they can pass on their particular language to their offspring. A research shows that not all Vietnamese children born abroad can talk with their relatives and friends in Vietnamese. Therefore, if people do not take any effective measures to reduce the disappearance of languages, they will soon end up with more and more languages. 
 Undoubtedly, fewer languages lead to the fact that cultures and traditions will eventually lost in the near future. Language of a region represents its cultures and traditions. They can only be learnt through language. Harshly, without learning language, they will be forgotten by themselves. Thus, if languages die out, as a consequence, these moral value will disappear. 
 In conclusion, I would agrue that the disappearance of languages should be considered correctly because of its unexpected detrimental impacts on our lives. There should be more solutions to tackle this problem which is certain to arise.

prompt: [IELTS Writing Task 2] Growing concensus on banning children usage of phones in schools
essay:
My response: 
 In today's world of readily available technological gadgets, children's ownership of smartphones is skyrocketing and, inevitably, leading to their widespread usage on campus. This has raised the alarm for many concerning parents as well as teachers and, thus, fortifying the growing concensus on banning children phones during school time. Despite cellphones's apparent usefulness, I still side with the opinion that it is necessary to implement a soft, appropriate ban on children usage of cellphones in classes. 
 On the one hand, we do need to acknowledge the undeniable benefits of smart devices in children's lives. At school, if used properly and wisely, smartphones and tablets can be an innovative, useful assistant for children. For example, a usually boring history class might be much more entertaining and captivating if children, in accordance with their teachers' lesson plan, can use their personal phones to play interactive quizz games about history on cloud platforms. Furthermore, cellphones, even obsolete ones, might become essential in connecting children to their parents in emergency situations. This is becoming increasingly true in light of more frequent school shootings, especially in the US. 
 On the other hand, the unregulated rapid development of addictive social media and fake news is an alarming reason to ban smartphones during school day. Children, a vulnerable and immature part of our society, might be exposed to harmful social network addiction and fake news if left unsupervised. Moreover, in a school setting, uncontrolled usage of cellphones will distract students from their classes and negetively affect their education. Last but not least, when educational institutions flexibly and appropriately implement a soft ban on cellphones, this will not prohibit children from using their mobile devices in case of emergency. Therefore, such versatile approach will not only negate smartphones' drawbacks but also garner their benefits. 
 In conclusion, while smartphones are undoubtedly of such vital importance in children's modern lives, I still believe that it is necessary for schools to flexibly and properly limit their usage during school time, as such soft ban will reduce electronic gadgets worst's effects on children while still promoting their good uses.

To improve, it is crucial to closely adhere to the original prompt, ensuring that the discussion directly reflects the question asked. Begin by clearly restating the prompt in the introduction to establish a solid foundation for your argument.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, and Stylistic Issues:**

Additionally, consistency in the usage of possessive forms, as in "cellphones' apparent usefulness," can enhance clarity. Consider varying sentence structures to keep the reader engaged and to articulate points more effectively. A thorough proofreading session could help in identifying and correcting these errors.

3. **Point of View Clarity:**
The essay successfully communicates a personal viewpoint, advocating for a balanced, regulated approach to smartphone use in schools. Nevertheless, the instruction to compare and contrast public opinions before stating a personal view was not met. Future essays can be improved by distinctly addressing different perspectives before concluding with a personal stance, ensuring that all parts of the prompt are thoroughly answered.

4. **Arguments and Support:**
The essay provides clear arguments for both the benefits and downsides of smartphone use in schools, including enhanced learning opportunities and the risks of distraction and exposure to harmful content. These points are supported with examples, which strengthens the essay. To further enhance your arguments, include more specific evidence or studies to back up your claims, and ensure that all perspectives mentioned in the prompt are explored and contrasted before you introduce your personal viewpoint.

In conclusion, while the essay shows promise in articulating a complex issue, greater adherence to the prompt, refinement in language use, and comprehensive coverage of all required viewpoints would significantly improve its effectiveness and coherence. Continuing to practice these skills will undoubtedly lead to writing stronger, more persuasive essays.

prompt: IELTS WRITING TASK 2 - FAST FOOD RELATED DISEASES
essay:
In different parts of the world, it is reported that there is a constant rise in the number of cases related to fast food. While I am of the opinion that the government should issue a heavy tax on this type of food, I also argue that other options could be taken to deal with this situation. 
 On the one hand, fast food restaurant chains have to pay a higher tax compared to other businesses. The first reason is that this is considered an effective approach to control the establishment of fast food stores. Specifically, a higher tax payment means that fast food owners are unlikely to earn much profit from their businesses. In addition, governments can use the amount of money collected to fund health care system as compensation to those suffering from fast food related diseases, which could help reduce financial burden when they are in hospital. 
 On the other hand, there are other alternatives that could be taken into account. One possible solution is that governments are advised to organise health campaigns to raise people's awareness of the negative impacts that fast food may cause. For example, the high volume of sugar, salt and fat in French fries, hamburgers or fried chicken will probably lead to high cholesterol or even diabetes. More importantly, there should be strict rules and regulations on food manufacturing in order to ensure the origin of ingredients as well as approved nutrients before reaching customers. 
 In conclusion, in addition to changing tax policy, it is necessary for governments to draw the attention of customers and put fast food restaurants under control to protect the public health.
feedback:
The essay addresses the issue of fast food and its impact on health, as well as proposing solutions, which show an understanding of the task. However, it deviates from the given prompt by introducing broader, global implications not mentioned in the original presentation. Focus on the specific scope given—whether it’s local or national—and avoid adding unrelated information. This maintains relevance and coherence.

There are instances where the essay could be more impactful by sticking to the information required. For example, introducing an international perspective where only a local or national one is necessary can distract from the essay's main points. Ensure that every claim or piece of information directly supports your argument without adding unnecessary details.

The essay's structure shows an attempt to organize ideas clearly, with separate paragraphs for discussing different solutions. However, it lacks a definitive stance on the extent to which the author supports the heavy taxation of fast food. Being more specific about your position will strengthen the essay and make your viewpoint clearer to the reader.

Regarding grammar and sentence structure, it's crucial to avoid run-on sentences and ensure each paragraph adheres to the expected format—typically 3 to 5 sentences for introduction and conclusion sections. This will not only make your essay easier to read but also help in conveying your ideas more effectively.

To improve, consider incorporating varied sentence structures and paying close attention to paragraph conventions to enhance readability. Additionally, though the arguments presented are logical, they would benefit from more detailed examples and evidence. This could involve citing studies or statistics that support your claims about the benefits of higher taxes on fast food and the effectiveness of health campaigns.

On the positive side, the essay does a good job of introducing potential solutions to the issues related to fast food consumption. However, more explicit connections between these solutions and how they could be implemented by governments would create a stronger argument. For example, when discussing the funding of health care systems through taxes on fast food, providing a more detailed explanation of how this would work in practice would be beneficial.

In summary, while the essay demonstrates a good understanding of the topic, focusing on clarity, relevance, and providing specific examples will make the argument more persuasive. Avoid unnecessary information, clarify your stance on the issue, use appropriate sentence structure, and ensure your solutions are directly related to the problem at hand with clear examples or evidence.

 Solution:

prompt: IELTS Task 2 - Opinion - The meaning behind traditional or religious festivals
essay:
Most people have forgotten the meaning behind traditional or religious festivals, during festival periods, people nowadays only want to enjoy themselves. 
 To what extent do you agree or disagree with this opinion? 
 Answer: 
 Some people argue that the underlying meanings of traditional and religious festivals are being forgotten, considering that most of us derive pleasure from enjoying holidays. While I agree that time spending for personal fulfillment should be appreciated, I do not agree that people no longer remember these festivals meaning. 
 On the one hand, positive vibes are the end of those celebrations, but to some extent, people are using them as an excuse for instant gratifications. People tend to be not patient enough to go through all procedures due to lack of time and even more, lack of interest. These seem to be the inevitable result of demanding working lifestyle, given the advent of globalization and the booming economy. By way of illustration, during Tet, which is Vietnam traditional festival celebrating the Lunar new year, people usually go shopping for clothes, gadgets, accessories then decorate their homes. Furthermore, some even book an overseas holiday for their families, to escape from urban noises. In other words, enjoyment is our priority. 
 Nonetheless, I disagree with the idea that people no longer remember origin meanings of celebrations. The key to any festival period is to strengthen the bonds within religious groups and families. To maintain such relationship, human beings, as known as social creatures from early ages, always hold celebrations in a variety of different ways. For example, Tet is an opportunity for family reunions. Besides a sense of nostalgia, we pray for a successful upcoming year, by traditional rituals such as making Chung cake, spring rolls and sticky rice, watching the firework display and giving lucky money to children. It is a particular aspect of festivals that make the celebration genuinely grand. 
 In sum, although people mostly enjoy themselves during festivals, I believe that they are still aware of the spiritual value of these celebrations. 
 302 words
feedback:
The essay addresses the topic of whether the significance of traditional and religious festivals is being forgotten in favor of personal enjoyment. However, it could benefit from a clearer stance on the issue. Instead of stating a partial agreement with the given statement, it's essential to present a more dominant viewpoint to make the essay's position more apparent to the reader. For instance, beginning with a revised introduction like, "There is a growing belief that people are beginning to lose the meaning behind traditional festivals, seeing them primarily as opportunities for personal enjoyment. I partially agree with this view for several reasons," would provide a clearer framework for your arguments.

In terms of writing mechanics, there's a need to pay attention to grammatical rules, such as using "an" before words that start with a vowel sound, to improve sentence structure. Additionally, be cautious with spelling variations between British and American English, especially when the context requires a specific version. For example, "fulfilment" should be used instead of "fulfillment" in tests based on British English.

The essay's paragraphs would benefit from more precise structure. Try to avoid overusing commas and creating run-on sentences. Break down complex ideas into shorter, clearer sentences, aiming for 3-5 sentences per paragraph. This will not only enhance clarity but also ensure that each paragraph sufficiently develops a single idea. The introductory and concluding paragraphs in particular need expansion to adequately set up and summarize the essay's arguments, respectively.

Concerning content, the essay presents valid points about the continued cultural significance of traditional festivals despite a focus on enjoyment. However, these arguments would be more persuasive with additional evidence and clearer, more direct connections to the thesis. Remember, it's crucial to maintain focus on how these examples support the essay's main argument.

Lastly, ensure that the concluding paragraph effectively summarizes the essay's key points and reiterates the stance presented in the introduction, providing a satisfying closure to the argument.

By addressing these aspects, the essay will become more coherent, persuasive, and aligned with the expectations of English proficiency tests.

While this has a lot of advantages such as stimulating the child to work harder and dream bigger, it also has some disadvantages like giving them false hope that could lead to depression.

Additionally, they could get burnt out from working too much midway and possibly have a myriad of health problems.

prompt: IELTS TASK 2 ON LOCAL LANGUAGE LEARNING VS ENGLISH
essay:
In your opinion, is it important for everyone to learn English? 
 Should we try to ensure the survival of local languages and, if so, how? 
 In many countries, acquiring knowledge in the English language is usually considered as being of greater importance than their local counterparts. Some languages are thus at risk of being diminished. To my mind, it is crucial to study both the English language and the local languages. 
 As the world enters the era of globalization, it is of utmost importance that everyone can communicate with others. English as one of the most frequently used languages therefore needs to be taken into consideration for many people who want to connect with the world. Especially for young people, having proficiency in English helps them apply to highly ranked universities in other countries, get decent jobs and might ensure a better quality of life. For the older ones, learning English still benefits them in some aspects. They could have a greater opportunity at improving in their career, or as simple as being more confident in going on holiday abroad. 
 However, being fluent in English doesn't compensate for the necessity of knowing one's own native language. The local language contains a region's identity and heritage, which is unique and indispensable. In order to ensure a rich legacy of a country being passed onwards to future generations, preservation of languages needs to be taken into consideration. In order to do that, the government first needs to enact laws that include local languages in primary education, while the citizens can also be of great help by studying them conscientiously. There are some countries that have already started implementing those initiatives, some even have financial aid for writers to produce books in their own language in order to promote the use of the language. 
 In conclusion, while studying English offers a great deal of benefits, people should also have a knowledge of their native languages.
feedback:
This essay addresses an essential question about the importance of learning English while also considering the preservation of local languages. Here’s some feedback to help improve the essay:

1. **Response to the Topic**: The essay thoughtfully addresses the importance of learning English but doesn't fully address the second part of the prompt about how to ensure the survival of local languages. Make sure to discuss both parts of the question equally to fulfill the essay's requirements.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, and Style**: Overall, the essay is well-written with few grammatical errors. However, pay attention to avoiding redundancy. Aim to express your ideas clearly and concisely without repeating the same points. This will make your essay more effective and engaging.

3. **Clarity of the Author's Point of View**: The essay clearly presents a viewpoint that both English and local languages should be valued and learned. This perspective is maintained throughout the essay, which is good. Ensure that all arguments directly support this viewpoint for coherence and strength.

4. **Arguments and Support**: The essay provides strong reasons for learning English, such as better opportunities in education and career, and it highlights the cultural significance of local languages. However, the arguments can be more balanced by expanding on specific strategies to preserve local languages. Examples of how governments and citizens can support language preservation would enhance this part of the essay.

5. **Length and Redundancy**: The essay is detailed but somewhat lengthy for an opinion essay, with some ideas repeated. Strive for brevity and directness in your writing. Express your ideas once clearly and avoid revisiting the same point unless you're adding new information or a different perspective.

6. **Conclusion**: The concluding paragraph needs to be stronger. A conclusion should summarize your main points in a new way and leave a lasting impression on the reader. Aim for at least two sentences that rephrase your introduction and thesis, reinforcing your stance without introducing new information.

In summary, you've made a solid start in discussing the relevance of learning English alongside preserving local languages. By balancing the discussion between both languages, eliminating redundancy, and strengthening your conclusion, your essay will become more compelling and cohesive. Remember, each sentence should serve a clear purpose in supporting your main argument. Keep practising, and consider these points in your future essays for a more powerful and concise expression of your ideas.

prompt: IELTS Writing Part 2: HEALTH TOPIC / Walking
essay:
Question: Walking is known to be beneficial for health and yet fewer and fewer people are walking these days. What are the reasons for this? What can be done to tackle this problem? 
 Answer: 
 The advent of speedy transportation is one of man's greatest inventions in minimizing distance, albeit at a cost of health degradation. Despite knowing the health benefits walking offers to humans, the number of people doing such activity is declining at an alarming rate. In the following essay, the principal reasons for this issue and some possible solutions to ameliorate this trend will be discussed. 
 It seems that there is an array of integrated factors that contribute to this phenomenon, and chief among the causes of this problem is the quickening tempo of modern society, along with the advancement of transportation infrastructures that leads to a rise in the number of people commuting by cars and buses. Further to this point, the need to travel long distances to work has also contributed partly to the fall in the number of people walking on the streets. It is indisputable that human's indolent behavior and hedonistic mindset actively seeks for pleasure and convenience, thereby opting to drive instead of walking, which consumes more time and energy. Furthermore, this problem also stems from the fact that there are no adequate facilities such as public parks and gardens in the city to allow people to walk leisurely during their leisure time. 
 Turning to viable solutions, probably the most practical countermeasure is for the authority to heighten people's awareness to lead a healthy life, which would increase the frequency of walking and reduce the amount of sedentary time. It is imperative for governments of developed and developing nations to allocate more money in building public parks and offer places of recreation for people to use. In addition, modules teaching students about the merits of exercising and walking must be taught at schools. If people make concerted efforts and put these measures into practice, it would greatly improve people's health to a great extent. 
 In sum, this problem is highly unlikely to be overcome in the foreseeable future; nevertheless, it is by no means insurmountable. It is of paramount importance for governments and individuals to encourage a better lifestyle and extol the benefits of walking. 
 (347 words)

prompt: IELTS 2: Country is already rich, any addition in economic wealth does not make its citizens happier
essay:
It is believed that citizens of an economically prospering nation will not benefit in terms of life satisfaction were they to be conferred with any further financial growth. From my point of view, I concur with this statement owing to my rationales in the forthcoming paragraphs. 
 To initiate, boosting an economy is accompanied by increased stress and pressure. To drive an economy forward, companies have to increase their revenues and focus on innovations, which would translate to a higher workload for employees. In developed nations, people may already be content with their work hours, only to be faced with extra tasks and work overtime, leaving them less time to recuperate and face an elevated level of stress. The resulting extra wealth created could furthermore present itself as an extra burden for them to maintain their status of being well-off, such as fears of being robbed and additional taxes. This can lead to feelings of burnout and depression, which ultimately outweigh the benefits of increased prosperity. 
 In addition, a continuous pursuit of wealth building also glosses over other important aspects of life. When people are consumed with earning money, they would pay no heed to quality time with family and friends. In the long run, such negligence would lead to strain and disconnection, leaving them in a state of loneliness. The situation is exacerbated when this obsession also can mislead people to a narrow perspective of life, whereby accumulating material possessions become the goal of their life. This deprives them of the ability to perceive the simple pleasures of life around them, and gives vent to a comparison and competition society where materialism shines. Although financial success can be achieved, people may be plagued with dissatisfaction and lack of fulfillment for the rest of their life. 
 In conclusion, attempts at augmenting economic prosperity in developed countries would not be able to increase its citizen's happiness due its associated rampant stress and people's tendency to belittle other aspects of life.

Make sure to keep your essay focused on developing your arguments rather than demonstrating vocabulary range. This will help you maintain a clear and concise essay within the word count and time constraints.

4. **Addressing the Essay Prompt**: While your essay does address the prompt, ensuring the arguments are directly linked to how economic prosperity affects happiness will strengthen your position. Each paragraph should clearly connect back to the main thesis to keep the essay cohesive and focused.

5. **Grammar and Spelling**: While there are minimal errors, paying close attention to grammar and spelling will polish your essay further. Minor errors can distract readers from your main arguments, so always proofread your work.

By focusing on these areas, your writing will not only become clearer and more engaging but also more effective in conveying your thoughts within the constraints of an English proficiency test.  First, Cooking is not as time-consuming as you think. With the inception of the modern era, There are many services, especially regarding raw ingredients delivery, for customers. All you need is to write down what you need to prepare for the meal on the software and click done. So you just need to focus on preparing the meal. If you still have concerns about dirty dishes after a meal, you can share the responsibility of cleaning up with other people in the meal or just buy a dishwasher to make it easier. According to my calculations, this only took less than an hour. 
 Secondly, it exerts a number of positive effects on people. As I mentioned, the materials we buy must be hygienic and healthy, so you can prepare the dish to suit your taste and ensure the food quality. Besides, this is an opportunity to heals relationships with people during meals and improves the cooking ability for an independent life. Think about it, after a hard-working day, you cook by yourself and enjoy it with your family, which will help you relax and tighten the family bonds and also enhance cooking skills in the transition to adulthood to better prepare for the future. Without this, we can lose the cohesion of social relationships and the ability to live independently. 
 In conclusion, my opinion is that home-cooked meal is not only healthy and hygienic but also improve personal skills and the family relationship.

prompt: Writing task 2: The main reasons to make people spend most their time working
essay:
In recent years, the advent of technology has significantly influenced to humans' life. Therefore, to keep pace with cutting-edge inventions, people seemingly have to work in longer hour than they did before. There are diverse reasons and effects have been expressed. 
 Apparently, this phenomenon is caused by three main reasons. Firstly, property prices are higher than ever, and without help, it would be impossible for many people to pay a deposit and a mortgage. Secondly, people seem to be more ambitious nowadays, and they want to provide a better quality of life for their families. Thirdly, the appearence of new technological innovations requires humans to study and work harder to know how to control and make uses of them in an effective way. 
 Having to work in a long-tern has two obvious impacts on humans' life such as physical and mental health. As for physical health, spending hours sitting at offices or carrying overweight can make our bodies exhaust. It is the lack of sleeping time that is responsible for having headache, losing feelings control,... People who do not sleep enough may usually be angry with everything around them. As a result, working in a long time brings many prevention to normal life. 
 In conclusion, it is undisputed that the expansion of technology is the main reason to make people spend most their time working. In addition, if we want to improve our health, we should take more exercise, participate in sports instead of working in a long period.

prompt: IELTS writing task 2 - Science - To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement?
essay:

I agree that our society could hardly survive if we shut down science, but I think keeping sapiens alive will never be its salvage. 
 It is hard to deny that the application of science has created a significant change in our society's development, displayed by the existence of technology. For instance, the Internet and electronic devices play crucial roles in how people, regardless of living in the urban, countryside, or even between nations, share information and build businesses. Furthermore, there is no doubt that science has been a giant accomplishment of humans that differentiates us from other species. Indeed, the way we manipulate tools and develop such complicated levels of communication and scientific theory leads us to get excellent health conditions, dominate the planet and conquer beyond any man's wildest dream. 
 On the other hand, chasing that dream at all costs is not what we are ready for. As we hold every means of changing the world, man must take responsibility, and protect our home. As a matter of fact, humans have witnessed countless natural disasters resulting from scientific practice, such as industrial emissions and plastic litter. Nevertheless, since we are staying in a shared home, it is unforgettable to conserve the natural habitats surrounding us. 
 To sum up, it is my firm belief that as well as to enhance our health, accommodation, and work, the final purpose of science is to advance and recover the lives of an enormous quantity of species living on Earth.
