While the essay presents arguments supporting the rewards policy and suggests alternatives, these arguments can be better structured and detailed. Each paragraph should focus on a single main idea, supported by examples or more in-depth analysis, rather than briefly touching upon multiple ideas. This approach will strengthen your position and make your reasoning clearer to the reader.

**4. Conclusion:**
The concluding paragraph should summarize the key points discussed and reinforce your thesis without introducing new ideas. Avoid abrupt endings by ensuring the conclusion offers a sense of closure and reflects on the overall discussion. The current conclusion nearly achieves this but could be expanded to offer a more comprehensive summary and final thought.

**General Tips:**
- Practice more on essay structure and work on aligning paragraphs with specific, singular ideas.
- Engage with well-written essays and observe how they handle similar tasks, noting the introduction strategy and how arguments are made and supported.
- The essay demonstrates potential, and with focused improvement on these aspects, it will significantly enhance both the readability and impact of your writing.

By addressing these points, the essay will not only become more structurally sound but will also convey its arguments more persuasively. Remember, practice and attention to detail are key in refining your essay writing skills.

prompt: How to support developing countries ?
essay:
In today's world, international support plays an essential part for the progress of developing countries. While some people claim that it is more realistic for global organizations to supply these countries with money. Nonetheless, from my perspective, practical aid and advice is more vitally important for developing countries than financial aid. 
 On the one hand, financial assistance can be such a driving force for countries with difficult conditions to thrive. It is inevitable that developing nations have to struggle with the shortage of revenue annually. National budget does not have enough financial resources to promote residents' life as well as motivate the social developments. Therefore, funding from global organizations helps governments tackle the issue of lacking money, meaning that the authority will have more chances to rebuild their nation without concerning about financial difficulties. Thanks to the contributions of world organizations, poor countries can utilize the huge amount of money to improve living standard of residents. It is obvious that the support from all over the world will certainly give rise to numerous positive impacts on many sides of poor nations, ranging from economics to commercial. Moreover, financial aid can be used to boost the quality of education and health-care system and some aspects that have low quality. 
 On the other hand, practical aid and advice is more necessary and beneficial for those nations with impoverished background. Simply because practical aid and guidance from specialists and researchers throughout the world has a long-term effect for poor countries to thrive. For instance, in many countries in parts of Africa, local civilians have to live below poverty line due to the lack of food and fresh water. The life, however, has become better because of volunteers from developed countries, who have come to these areas with updated machines to help some Africans the way to produce more food and have more water. In addition, volunteers also provide medicines for difficult places where people have to confront with the outbreaks of severe diseases. Practical aid such as methods to plant or produce food have been taught by foreigners are valuable to the developments of difficult nations. Volunteers also teach children, who do not have ability to read and write, so that they themselves can change their poor lives by their true talents and make contributions to their countries. It is clear that financial help only supports these nations in short-term period, while they need a long-term plan to prosper without the dependence on financial aid. 
 In conclusion, even though financial help can make poor nations develop economically, I believe that money is limited. It is better for nations with low quality of life to be equipped with some real tools. As all we know, the prosperity of the nation leans on people and their skills will help to change their country, not because of money from other countries.
feedback:
This essay discusses the importance of international support for the development of poorer nations, comparing financial assistance with practical aid and advice. There are several aspects to compliment and areas for improvement to make the essay more effective. 

Firstly, the topic is adequately addressed, as the essay compares financial aid with practical help and advice for developing countries. However, the introduction does not clearly state this comparison or your stance, which would have set the stage more effectively for the reader. In the future, include a brief overview of the points to be discussed and clearly state your opinion in the introduction to guide the reader through your arguments more clearly.

In terms of spelling, grammar, and stylistic issues, there are a few minor errors scattered throughout. Paying closer attention to conjugation, article usage, and preposition choice will enhance the readability. For example, “on many sides of poor nations, ranging from economics to commercial” could be revised to “in many aspects of these nations’ economies and commerce.” Additionally, using simpler language can make your essay more accessible, especially for an audience that may include English language learners.

The point of view is clear throughout most of the essay, but there is room for clarity. Your primary stance—that practical aid is more beneficial than financial help—is evident, yet it would be stronger with a more definitive introduction and a clearer separation of opinion from the rest of the text. It's suggested to start by outlining both views before elaborating on why one is favored over the other.

Regarding the arguments provided, they are generally clear and descriptive, illustrating the benefits of both financial and practical aids effectively. However, the arguments could be enhanced by providing more detailed examples and possibly citing sources or statistics to substantiate claims. Additionally, it's important to discuss the limitations or potential drawbacks of each type of aid to present a balanced view.

Lastly, bear in mind that the conclusion of an essay should not introduce new arguments or ideas but rather summarize the points made and restate your opinion clearly. Ensure that the closing sentence of your essay reinforces your stance without adding new information.

Improving these areas—introduction clarity, argument support, grammar, and conclusion structure—will undoubtedly raise the quality of your essay. By addressing these points, your writing will not only become more persuasive and coherent but also more engaging for the reader.

prompt: IELTS WRITING TAK 2: Replace parks and gardens instead of apartment buildings. Discuss both views.

Firstly, parks and gardens occupy a lot of areas which leads to some people living far from the city center will spend more time traveling to work. For example, people living in extramural areas will have a longer distance to go to work than those living in the city center. Secondly, it might be supposed that those places may be useless because of not being association with economic development.

This is particularly the case for those who go to parks or gardens on a regular basis, and they will find a sense of relaxation because they can be close to nature and relieve stress. Besides, trees in gardens and parks also facilitate an increase in the fresh air in the atmosphere.

prompt: IELTS - Fixed punishments nevertheless of circumstances?
essay:
Crime and punishment have always sparked debate in human history, and criminal laws are always being challenged and revised to suit the current societies. Regarding this matter, some people maintains that convicts of the same crime should receive the same punishment, while others argue for the circumstances and motivations in each and every crime to be considered in a trial. Although I agree with the latter, there are strong arguments for both views. 
 Fixed punishments ensure fairness for victims of each type of crime. However different the circumstances of these crimes may be, the damage that the defendant caused to the plaintiff is the same, as agreed by the jury. A case in point is the controversial death of a child in Vietnam, caused by a man who failed to comply with transportation safety standards. The public was confused how his duty to the country made up for his fatal negligence, seeing the devastating effect on the family was not reduced by having their son killed from a veteran. Another point is that the same-punishment law can negate corruption in court. If a criminal resort to connections and bribery, the proposed zero-tolerance policy will increase the chance that he will nevertheless be brought to justice. 
 However, no crimes are exactly the same, and taking that into account would make a lawsuit more nuanced and acceptable. Just as juries are picked from the community, the verdicts are expected to socially approveable, which absolutely requires empathy. For example, a person delivering drugs once under death threats being treated the same as a member of a drug trafficking ring would cause quite a stir in communities. To make sure lawsuits are being carried out sensibly, we need to allow for fair judgement of everyone involved, who likely have different circumstances and motivation. If the same punishment is applicable to every crime then the judges and jury would be redundant, as only the police would be needed to gather evidence and accuse someone of a crime. This process would go against the gradual development of our law systems. 
 To conclude, a criminal case should always be processed with as much information as possible, since considering different circumstances are necessary to deliver justice to each and every person involved. It is this flexibility that makes us human and allows for large, interconnected, and supportive communities. 
 (390 words)

prompt: Animals should not be exploited by people and that they should have the same rights as humans
essay:
Essay: 
 People's opinions differ as to whether or not animals should be used to serve human life. Although there are some strong arguments against the employment of animals, personally I still believe that it is a necessary aspect of food production and research. 
 On the one hand, there are two main reasons why animal exploitation should be banned. Firstly, it is recognized that animals have consciousness as well as the capacity to experience pain, fear, and even distress just as humans do. Supporters of animal rights therefore argue that humans have no right to subject animals to the trauma of being slaughtered or tested on, as the benefits to humans do not justify the suffering caused. Secondly, many biologists would agree that exploiting animals excessively can lead to biodiversity loss and disturb the ecological balance. For example, a considerable number of marine species such as tuna are on the edge of extinction mainly as a result of overfishing, and surely this will have a dramatic influence on the marine ecosystem. 
 In spite of the above arguments, I believe that abolishing all forms of animal use in human life is completely impractical. Livestock not only serves as a major source of meat and other products for humans, but also provides job opportunities for those in rural areas. Eliminating the use of these animals therefore may cause unnecessary difficulties, including food shortage and a rise in unemployment. Similarly, medicines and other products are routinely tested on animals to measure their effectiveness and make sure that they are cleared for human use. If animal experimentation is banned, I suspect that new, unproven drugs might be instead even directly tested on humans, and this is simply unacceptable from an ethical perspective. 
 In conclusion, it seems to me that it would be wrong, on balance, for humanity to stop using animals for our own purposes. ( 309 words)

prompt: IELTS Writing Task 2 - Statements about changing jobs
essay:
In our lives, career play a critical part: it allows us to earn money and feed ourselves. In a number of cases, sticking to a job, according to a group of people, will help us to get a satisfying career life, rather than who usually change jobs. On the contrary, some people think in reverse that getting a new job periodically is much better. Both approaches have their pros and cons but I lean towards the second one. This essay will discuss both statements to prove for my decision. 
 There are several reasons why we should be loyal to our current careers. First, working on a job in a fixed office will enable us to get accustomed to a working pattern. This pattern will help to create a 'safe zone' for us, which will ensure the quality of the work. Moreover, a long-term relationship with a fixed environment will increase our reputation in the office itself. As a result, we might get some promotions for our jobs. Second, in contrast to sticking to a job, changing job frequently are likely get us down in a career path. Perhaps we will lose the chance of being promoted to a higher position when doing this. 
 On the other hand, getting a new job periodically will have some benefits too. Accompanying by a company for a long time might make many people, especially young generations, feel so exhausted. This sense of tiredness will undoubtedly demotivate them, leading to the low performance when working. Furthermore, by getting a new job monthly or yearly can bring us more creativity. Many new ideas will be created by the employees. Last but not least, changing job will, in some ways, help a company to refresh itself. This is so precious to its existence and development since it need to turn over a new leaf constantly to adapt to a fast-paced society. 
 In conclusion, it seems that making us into a new career frequently is better for us when comparing with the choice of working in just an office. But it still has some drawbacks. Therefore, we should be cautious when it comes to the decision.
feedback:
The essay provides a comparative analysis of the merits and drawbacks of staying in one's current career versus frequently changing jobs. While the effort to present both sides of the argument is appreciated, the essay does not align with the expected response type for the given prompt. The prompt appears to call for an argumentative essay where a clear stance is taken and extensively supported. Instead, the essay presents a comparison without thoroughly arguing in favor of a singular viewpoint, leading to a deviation from the expected response format. To improve, it’s essential to adhere closely to the prompt's requirements, ensuring the essay directly addresses the topic and follows the prescribed format.

There are spelling and grammatical errors that need attention. For example, "career play a critical part" should be "careers play a critical part," and "changing job frequently are likely get us down" should be "changing jobs frequently is likely to get us down." These errors, along with others, can detract from the clarity and professionalism of the essay. 

Furthermore, the point of view, while indicated, could be made more evident through consistent and strong argumentation for the chosen stance. The transition between the discussion of each viewpoint lacks a clear declaration of which side the essay supports until the conclusion. A more explicit stance throughout the essay would enhance its persuasive power.

The arguments provided would benefit from deeper exploration and more detailed examples. The current arguments, such as the creation of a 'safe zone' in a fixed office environment and the invigoration brought by job changes, are valid but require further development and support to convincingly back the essay’s position. Incorporating real-world examples, statistical evidence, or more detailed hypothetical scenarios could strengthen these arguments.

To conclude, while the essay offers a valuable discussion on an important topic, focusing on clear adherence to the prompt, correcting grammatical and spelling errors, clarifying and asserting the essay’s point of view, and providing more detailed and supported arguments would significantly improve the quality of the essay. prompt: Task2: It is argued that because of globalisation we will lose our cultural identity
essay:
Because of the massive growth of global transportation and connection to each other, globalization is playing a more and more vital role in this day and age. Therefore, it is argued that we will lose our cultural identity unavoidably. I completely disagree with the opinion. 
 First of all, I believe that globalization contributes to cultural integration rather than the disappearance of cultural identity. It allows people to experience various cultures worldwide and provides a multicultural environment to integrate different cultures. For instance, people all over the world are fond of Japanese traditional cuisine, Sushi. An increasing number of restaurants are attempting to create a combined dish with both Eastern and Western recipes. Therefore, instead of forgetting the local food culture, people could think outside the box and combine new delicacies with their own food culture. 
 Secondly, globalization allows people not only to immerse themselves into another culture but also helps them to discover the beauty of their own indigenous culture. In other words, instead of losing cultural identity, people would cherish their distinguished local culture. The American film industry, for example, has a tremendous impact on every corner of the world due to globalization. People in India discover the fascination of their films from Bollywood and enjoy watching national movies filling with Indian characteristic institutions rather than watching Hollywood-centric movies containing with American popular culture. Thus, globalization helps people to find their cultural identity. 
 To conclude, I am of the standpoint that globalization does not contribute to a complete disappearance of cultural identity because it makes people know more about others and their own cultures.
feedback:

5. **Arguments and Support**: The first argument about cultural integration is compelling and well-supported with the example of sushi as a global culinary delight. However, the second argument regarding the American film industry's influence on Indian culture needs further development. Explain more clearly how global exposure to other cultures encourages people to appreciate their own, perhaps by offering more detailed examples or statistics.

6. **Conclusion**: Your summary should not only restate your stance but also succinctly recap the key points you've made in support of your argument. Aim for a comprehensive conclusion that reinforces your thesis statement by briefly revisiting your main arguments.

To improve your essay, consider refining the introduction for a stronger start, make sure to match your language closely with the prompt's original sentiment, and develop your supporting arguments more thoroughly, particularly where there's a noted disconnect. prompt: IELTS WRITING TASK 2 - Problems posed by cities population and measures that government may take
essay:
What are those problems? Should the government encourage people to move to regional towns? 
 Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. 
 Answer: 
 It is undeniable that people's life has now been improved a lot in comparison with the past, especially in the cities. This, however, comes with a price, the downside of it is the emergence of various problems faced by city residents. For this, some suggest that the government can resolve the problems by recommending people to live in regional towns, but is this a feasible solution? 
 It can be observed that city is a common choice for many companies to put their office, and this in turn causes the giant wave of people moving from rural areas to these employment hubs. Due to the large population in cities, problems have risen. The first very noticeable problem is the frequent traffic jams occurring in streets, especially at rush hours. As a result, people have to spend a substantial time of their day waiting in the streets, which wastes a lot of time. A second problem is the degradation of air quality in cities. The vast number of activities involving carbon dioxide emission, or any other gas emission in general, has contributed to the contamination of air in cities. Consequently, respiratory diseases are at extremely high rate among citizens in these areas. 
 Judging by the bad effects, though a lot of solutions have been proposed, I believe the best way is to make the distribution of people in these area sparser. With this argument, I agree with the proposal of governments making their people getting to live in other rural areas. Although upgrading traffic construction, equipping vehicles with optimal gas emission, etc. can potentially reduce the mentioned shortcomings, they cannot be completely removed. However, if reduction in the number of citizens in the area occur, obvious results can be achieved, no money will be spent on renovation of traffic systems nor production of modern vehicles. Besides, people can have chance to get better privacy in comparison to its shortage when many people live in a same area. 
 In conclusion, there are a lot of problems in large cities, and this can be thoroughly overcome if government take action to give terms to realize the migration of people from dense area to other sparse areas.
feedback:
Your essay provides a clear stance on the topic, addressing the issue of overpopulation in cities and suggesting government encouragement of relocation to regional towns as a solution. 1. **Response to the Topic**: Your essay addresses the given prompt by discussing the problems of city living and proposing relocation to less populated areas as a solution. To improve, directly answer the question in the introduction and restate it in the conclusion for a more robust response. This ensures that your essay remains focused and relevant throughout.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, or Stylistic Issues**: While your essay is generally well-written, it could benefit from a focus on being more concise. Aim to eliminate unnecessary words and repetitive sentences to make your points more directly. This will not only help with clarity but also enhance the overall readability of your essay. Additionally, pay attention to varying your sentence structures to create a more engaging narrative flow.

3. **Clarity of the Author's Point of View**: Your position is recognizable, but it could be articulated more explicitly, particularly in the introduction and conclusion. Clearly state your opinion at the beginning and reiterate it at the end to reinforce your stance.

4. **Arguments and Support**: You provide examples of the problems caused by overpopulation in cities, which is good. However, your essay would benefit from more direct and varied examples to support your argument for relocating to regional towns. Additionally, linking your ideas more clearly and transitioning smoothly between them would help maintain cohesion throughout your essay. Consider using five-sentence paragraphs where each sentence serves a specific purpose—introduce the problem, explain it, provide an example, suggest a solution, and conclude the paragraph. Secondly , this changes might not only to give prisoners motivation and interest , but also help them live a relatively normal life. prompt: Changes in the family structure and family roles. Are they positive or negative?

prompt: Many men and women are making the decision to have children later in life.
essay:
These days, the phenomenon of married couples deciding not to have children at a young age has become more popular. While this trend can be explained by some reasons, it has more pernicious impacts not only on the family but also on society. 
 There could be some driving factors for this trend in which young couples are delaying giving birth. To begin with, many individuals today have a tendency to pursue a career first. Therefore, they often delay starting a family until they seek a solid economic background to meet their kid's demands such as food, clothes and health care, and have achieved their professional goals. Another reason may lie in the widely thought that children are raised better by older parents. To be more specific, older parent would have more life experience than younger ones, which allows them to deal with their children's problems more effectively. As a result, their offspring can receive a better education and enjoy more comprehensive development. 
 The decision not to prioritize having babies early can indeed have detrimental effects on both family and society as a whole. Chief of these is that delaying parenthood leads to an increased age difference between parents and their offspring, which may create challenges in communication. This is because older parents may have different perspectives, values, and cultural references from their children, making the exchange of ideas challenging and unnecessary arguments frequent in their family. As for society, married couples choosing to have children later in life could potentially cause a decline in the overall birth rate. This may result in a shortage of young workforce in the future, which can lead to lower economic productivity for the country. 
 In conclusion, the tendency to delay parenthood among young couples today is caused by many reasons and the adverse effects of this development can be seen in society in general and families in particular.

This is essential for providing a comprehensive overview and ensuring the essay meets the criteria for an initial satisfactory assessment.

For example, combining shorter sentences can create more complex and sophisticated statements.

prompt: Pace of climate change, preserve wildlife - ielts writing task 2
essay:
Deforestation caused by human activity is happening in many parts of the world, with serious results for the environment. What do you think is the causes, effects and solutions of this problem? 
 My answer: 
 Deforestation has become the matter of great concerns in recent years. According to " The Guardian report in 2018", every second, a chunk of forest equivalent to the size of a soccer field is lost. This essay would discuss the causes, effects of the deforestation and also propose some solutions to the problem. 
 First of all, human acitivities are responsible for deforestation. It is estimated that farming, grazing of livestock, mining and drilling combined account for more than half of all deforestion. Moreover, forestry practices, wildfires, and in small part, urbanization account for the rest. Regarding agriculture, human cut down forests to grow foods and other commodities such as soy, palm oil and wood products. For instance, palm oil is cheap, versatile and can be added to both food and personal products like lipsticks and bamboo. Its popularity has spurred people to clear forests to grow more palm trees. Another example is the paper production requiring logging operations which fell countless trees each years. 
 Deforestation has brought negative consequences to our world. As forests are home to a wide variety of animals and plants, deforestation will lead to the loss of biodiversity. The amazon, for example, have the greatest concentrations of animal and plant species of any terrestrial ecosystem. As deforestation proceeds, the extinction of these species is unavoidable. Futhermore, according to FAO, deforestation is the second- leading cause of climate change. It not only remove vegetation, but the act of clearing the forests produces greenhouse gas emissions. It is obvious that trees play a crucial role in the climate mitigation as they absorb carbon dioxide which is exhaled by humans and the heat-trapping greenhouse gases emitted by human acitivity. The felling of trees would certainly obliterate all the benefits. 
 There are some measures which can be taken to mitigate the issue. To begin with, instead of cutting down trees for the aforementioned purposes, we should adopt sustainable farming practices, employ new farming technologies and crops to increase agricultural productivity. Moreover, trees should be replanted in cleared areas as the sooner a cleared area is reforested, the quicker the ecosystem can start to repair itself. On a personal level, individuals can take steps to curb deforestation by purchasing certified wood products, going paperless whenever possible, using eco-friendly products. 
 As the world seeks to slow the pace of climate change, preserve wildlife, and support billions of people, trees inevitably hold a major part of the answer. Therefore, it is urgent that we take measures to curb deforestation for the sake of ourself and the next generation.

- **Avoid Research-Based Evidence**: Given the exam context, where external research isn't possible, avoid citing specific studies or articles. Focus on general knowledge, logical reasoning, and personal insight to build your case. 

Improvement in these areas could not only adhere more closely to the expectations of English proficiency exams but also ensure the communication is clear, persuasive, and within the exam's constraints. Taking these suggestions into account can refine essay-writing skills, particularly for tests that evaluate English proficiency.

prompt: Travel during Public Holidays - Problems & Solutions
essay:
It is true that many people spend their public holidays visiting travel destinations. This essay will argue that turning tourist sites into huge rubbish dumps during these periods of time is a serious downside and a viable way to solve this problem is to prepare more waste disposal facilities. 
 The danger of litter comes into sight at tourist attractions during national holidays. This is because the number of visitors is increasing rapidly these days and they usually leave behind not just their footprints but a vast quantity of waste after their sightseeing there. Unfortunately, the rubbish generated by tourists is unable to be processed immediately due to the limited capacity of local waste management facilities. For example, travelers often outnumber the resident population in some well-known tourist destinations in Vietnam such as Hoian and Sapa on public holidays and the rubbish they leave behind turns the environment into a place which is under threat of these pollutants because it takes days for locals to clean and process them thereafter. 
 In order to cope with this issue, governments should provide enough landfill sites on the spot during peak holiday seasons. Although this solution cannot help to enhance the capability for processing on a daily basis of local refuse disposal systems, it can prevent leaving huge mounds of rubbish lying in the open public areas which not only are an eyesore but also breed germs and pests. Another good way to implement this approach is to install more trash cans at tourist destinations because these waste containers are more convenient and easily be removed. According to a survey conducted in 2015 by the Tourist Review Magazine, two fifths of tourists suggested that the provision of extra garbage cans in many places of interest would tackle the problem mentioned. 
 In conclusion, the huge amount of rubbish being generated by visitors on public holidays endangers the environment of tourist destinations and governments should provide more temporary disposal facilities during this period to deal with it.

Here’s detailed feedback based on the requirements:

This practice ensures your essay is accessible and relatable to all readers and respects the exam's constraints.

4. **Grammar, Spelling, and Style:** The essay is generally well-written, but attention to detail in spelling, grammar, and stylistic choices will enhance its readability and effectiveness. Ensure your sentences are clear, concise, and follow a logical structure to keep the reader engaged.

However, broadening your use of examples and ensuring they universally apply can strengthen your essay.  The two main causes of species' declines are habitat destruction and over-exploitation of natural resources. Firstly, clear-cutting for timber, farming land or urban expansion has done irrevocable damage to natural habitat. For example, it is reported that more than fifty percent of an original forest was converted to agricultural land by slash-and-burn. Moreover, if natural resources are seriously depleted, they will be degraded and running out. Consequently, different kinds of animals and plants will go extinct without human's recognition. 
 However, many conservation approaches can be adapted to improve the situation. The authorities should bring out policies and laws to ban over-exploitation and poaching to prevent wild species from dying out. Another important way to protect the ecosystem is promoting people's environmental conscience by informing about the dangers and threats to human beings caused by biodiversity loss. 
 In conclusion, human activities have made wildlife vulnerable and brought about the loss of biodiversity. Instead of worries or ignorance, people can gradually solve these issues by conservation and responsible awareness for environment.

prompt: Selecting a job to meet the living standards
essay:
A suitable career plays a significant role in one's life. Many people believe that when selecting a job, the most vital aspect that should be concerned is the payment. To the best of my knowledge, I partly agree with this point of view because whether the job helps people to improve or not is also considerable. 
 On the one hand, it is true that a well-paid job brings about many advantages. Obviously, without money, people cannot meet their basic needs. For example, everyone needs money to pay for housing, bills, education, health care, transportation fares and so on. Therefore, people tend to prioritize a job with high salary which not only covers their demand but also enables them to raise living standard easily. If people choose their jobs based on enjoyment or other non-financial factors, they might find it difficult to support themselves. For instance, artists and musicians, who are known for pursuing their loves, do not always have abilities to live comfortably and raise a family. 
 On the other hand, what position of employment gives should be taken into consideration as one of the most primary features in making a job decision. Personal relationships and working environment are extremely important. Having good employers and high-qualified colleagues can make a difference to workers' levels of happiness and general quality of life. According to many experts, working condition is a huge motivation that makes people try harder and devote to their job. Moreover, many people's feelings of job satisfaction come from their professional achievements, the skills they learn, and the position they reach, rather than the money they earn. 
 To sum up, I agree that people should select a job having a wage that is enough for their livings. However, people also ought to consider if the job helps them to widen their knowledge, gain more experiences, and reach great achievement. When people can balance between salary and what they receive, they will able to choose to most suitable job, which opens up their opportunities of success.
feedback:
Your essay provides a thoughtful exploration on the importance of choosing a suitable career, looking at both financial benefits and personal growth opportunities. Your effort to present a balanced view is commendable. However, there are several areas where improvements could significantly enhance the clarity and persuasiveness of your argument.

Firstly, it's vital to ensure that your essay directly responds to the stated topic or question. The discussion around financial versus personal growth considerations in career choice is engaging, yet it seems to miss a clear connection to a specific question or statement you are responding to. If there was a direct question or statement provided, make sure your essay addresses it head-on throughout.

Regarding your point of view, while you clearly state a partial agreement with the idea that salary is an important factor in job selection, the essay would benefit from a more focused exploration of how jobs contribute to personal improvement. To strengthen your argument, dedicate more space to examples and reasoning that specifically support the significance of personal and professional development in choosing a career.

In terms of structure and content, the comparative approach used in your essay, highlighting the advantages and disadvantages, is useful. However, it's important that each paragraph focuses on developing your unique stance more robustly. Specifically, expanding on how certain jobs contribute to personal growth—with concrete examples or statistical evidence—could provide a more compelling argument.

Grammatical, spelling, and stylistic issues are relatively minor, but they do impact the overall readability of your essay. For instance, consider using more varied sentence structures and precise vocabulary to enhance the sophistication of your writing. Also, pay attention to minor errors that could be easily fixed with a thorough proofreading session.

Lastly, the concluding paragraph adeptly summarizes your main points but could further emphasize the importance of balancing financial rewards with personal growth opportunities in career selection. Highlighting this balance as crucial to achieving success and satisfaction in one's career path would offer a strong, memorable close to your essay.

In summary, focusing on more specific evidence and examples to back up your stance, alongside careful proofreading, will make your argument more persuasive and your writing more impactful. Keep practicing, and your skills will continue to improve.

prompt: Flying all over the world. IELTS Task 2: Should air travel be restricted or NOT.

Air travel; although a dream travel for many people, is prevalent world wide now a days. It has a great contribution towards globalization and has made possible for people to travel to any destination but, at the same time comes with negative repercussions like global warming and extensive usage of non - renewable resources. If we discuss restriction of air travel, I totally disagree with this idea and would share my opinions in the following passages. 
 Collaboration among countries for development and business exchange has gone to such a high level and this has become possible only after advent of extensive air travel options. for instance, USA being the center of all operations and people from rest of world keep travelling.  In another important circumstances air travel is savior and that is air ambulance. In recent past, a news hit the newspaper that a human lever was transported quickly to another city and saved a life which would not been possible by road travel 
 Definitely, it is impossible to invent something with any negative impact and so is travel by air. Global warming and fer of exhaustion of expensive resources are obvious examples. Restricting air travel completely can never be an option but governments from different countries come up together can keep a check on over use of this. For instance, every individual especially in a developing country has this listed in her bucket list to travel in a plane however, opulent business executives travel by air even for short distances. This has become status symbol for many. How can this be reduced is altogether a different topic and certainly not easy.

prompt: In this era, people are facing major issue relating to the rising temperatures of the earth
essay:
In this millennial era, people are facing major issue relating to the rising temperatures of the earth which is depicted by a rising level of the sea as signals. There is a strong likelihood that unpredictable weather is the problem caused by this phenomenon and saving water is the most viable solution. 
 To begin with, the serious issue of the current high temperatures has shifted the weather patterns. This condition leads to farmers struggles for planning their planting schedule inasmuch as increasingly unpredictable water supplies which is a basic need of agriculture. In addition, a warmer atmosphere could trigger the increasing rates of evaporation. In other words, the plant leaves will lose their moisture. For example, in Indonesia, according to the Statistic Commission of Indonesia, the total of paddy production in 2018 decreased significantly approximately two-fifth percent since the farmer would not start to grow the plants because of dry season which was longer than the previous decade. 
 The most practical action to tackle this problem is to reduce water waste. This could decrease carbon pollution which is produced by activities related to water consumption such as pumping, heating, and water treatment. For instance, recent research conducted by the University of Indonesia depicted the total electricity consumption that would be saved in Jakarta per year was about 90 million kilowatt-hours. This is to avoid 70,000 tons of global warming pollution if one out of every 100 city dwellers uses the water efficiently. It suggests the citizens could take shorter showers, and turn off the tap while brushing teeth. 
 In conclusion, a changing global climate is a serious problem these days. The result of the rising in sea level can lead to the change of climate events. This problem can be solved through wise water usage.
feedback:
This essay addresses the critical issue of rising global temperatures and their consequences, particularly focusing on the unexpected shifts in weather patterns and the significant role of water conservation as a solution. This topic is timely and relevant, effectively responding to the theme of environmental challenges.

Firstly, it's essential to address grammatical and structural issues present in the essay. For example, the sentence "...every 100 city dwellers uses the water efficiently..." should be corrected to "...every 100 city dwellers use water efficiently..." to properly reflect subject-verb agreement. Additionally, unnecessary commas can disrupt the flow of reading, as seen in "...citizens could take shorter showers, and turn off the tap..."; removing the comma would enhance clarity.

Incorporating more descriptive adjectives could significantly impact the persuasiveness and depth of your arguments. Instead of stating the global climate issue as a "serious problem," using stronger language such as "severe problem" could convey a greater sense of urgency and importance. Expanding your vocabulary in this manner throughout the essay can enrich your expressions and strengthen your arguments.

Sentence structure needs attention, specifically the avoidance of run-on sentences. Each sentence should ideally present a single idea clearly and concisely. Furthermore, opening paragraphs should contain at least three sentences to adequately set up the essay's subject and standpoint, allowing each point to be introduced more smoothly and comprehensively.

While using specific examples and data can strengthen an argument, relying on detailed research or statistics that may not be universally recognized or accessible during an exam could potentially detract from your essay. It's advisable to draw from general knowledge or personal insights to support your points, ensuring your arguments remain accessible and engaging without the need for external validation.

On a positive note, your essay does an effective job of making its point clear and introduces relevant and descriptive arguments supporting your stance on the importance of water conservation in combating climate change. This demonstrates an understanding of the subject and an ability to engage with complex environmental issues.

Finally, it's beneficial to remember that the strength of an essay lies not only in the information it conveys but also in how it communicates that information. Clarity, coherence, and grammatical accuracy are as crucial as the essay's content. Emphasizing improvement in these areas can substantially enhance the overall effectiveness of your writing.

This essay provides a foundation with substantial room for enhancement in clarity, expression, and structure. By addressing these areas, your argument's impact will be significantly amplified, making for a more compelling and persuasive essay.

prompt: Writing task 2 : learn about family history or focus on present and future generation. Discuss view
essay:
People are facing a dilemma whether one should do research about their family tree or pay attention to the present and future generation. Recently, this phenomenon has been brought to public attention with people standing on two different sides and this essay will demonstrate my point of view. 
 On the one hand, it is argued that people should place an emphasis on focusing on the present and future generation mainly because they think that people can not learn anything from the past because they are obsolete. To elucidate, advocates have pointed out that since the world is innovating everyday, everything that happened in the past might have no influence on today's world. Therefore, many think that it would be better for people to focus on the present and future generation. Furthermore, advocates of this view also accentuate that the time one uses to comprehend and learn about the family tree can be utilized for addressing other issues such as how to deal with plagues that are labeled as incurable or how to tackle proliferation of joblessness, famine or global warming. 
 On the other hand, though the aforementioned statements seem compelling, some deem that they are inadequate for two chief reasons. Firstly, if individuals study their family history, they will have the opportunity to enrich and hone practical skills from their ancestors. To exemplify, this is because the bulk of the predecessors have engaged in a myriad of wars which involved a profusion of skills like interprofessional collaboration and how to overcome difficulties . Hence, the younger generation can learn from the previous one on how to cope with privations and how to collaborate with each other. Learning about the previous generation can foster emotional connection. Investigating about the past, discovering hardships and challenges that they have gone through can instill the later generation with a sense of gratitude and appreciation for the endeavors and contributions of the ancestor. 
 In conclusion, although focusing on the young and future generation can be conducive to the society because it will help people to have a clearer and more insightful view about what individuals are facing, I deem that people can be ameliorated from learning from the past since it will help the younger generation to comprehend what the forerunners have done and to facilitate them to be better.
feedback:
Your essay presents a thought-provoking discussion on whether individuals should invest time in researching their family tree or focus on present and future generations. The topic is well-chosen, and you've structured your essay to cover both sides of the argument. However, to enhance your essay for English proficiency tests and ensure it meets scoring criteria, consider the following improvements:

1. **Clear Position from the Start:** It's crucial to express your stance clearly in the introduction. Mentioning that the essay will demonstrate your point of view is a step in the right direction, but explicitly stating your opinion at the beginning will help meet test requirements. For instance, after introducing the debate, briefly mention your lean towards learning from the past or focusing on the future to guide readers from the start.

2. **Earlier Presentation of Personal Opinion:** Your personal opinion, which is a critical component of the essay, currently appears towards the end. To align with test scoring criteria, it's important to present this opinion earlier, preferably by the third paragraph. This adjustment prevents the essay from seeming open-ended and ensures it adheres to the expected structure of presenting a clear argument within the given parameters.

3. **Spelling, Grammar, and Stylistic Issues:** Your essay is generally well-written, but watch out for minor grammatical mistakes and ensure sentence structures are varied to maintain reader interest. Phrases like "people can not learn anything" could be replaced with "people cannot learn anything" for correctness, and varying sentence lengths can enhance readability.

4. **Supporting Arguments:** Your essay benefits from strong, descriptive arguments on both sides of the debate. For further improvement, ensure that these arguments are closely tied back to how they inform your opinion. This might mean elaborating on how past experiences, like overcoming hardships, specifically contribute to society today or how focusing solely on future generations might overlook valuable lessons.

5. **Simplification for Clarity**: There are sections where the language could be simplified for clarity, especially considering English language learners are the essay's audience. For instance, instead of "to elucidate," simply saying "to explain" makes the text more accessible without sacrificing precision.

By incorporating these suggestions, including a clear, early statement of your stance, refining your grammar and style, and ensuring your arguments are directly leveraged to support your viewpoint, your essay will not only be more aligned with proficiency test expectations but also more compelling and coherent for readers.

prompt: IELTS Writing task 2 - Economic developments result in losing traditional values
essay:
Economic growth is likely to contribute to a thriving business in a country. While some people argue that economic developments lead to the loss of traditional cultures, personally I completely disagree with this point of view. 
 It might be reasonable that authorities are trying their best to foster their country's economy in order that their basic needs have been improved. To begin with, they allow foreign companies to build industries in their country to provide more employment opportunities for native people. Furthermore, overseas companies are also able to cooperate with local businessman. As a result, many products in their country can be exported to foreign nations, helping their country's status on a global stage in terms of trading power. Lastly, their citizens can receive excellent pay packages from corporations due to the increase of companies' profits, which can help them improve their living standard. 
 However, I believe that traditional values seem to be unaffected by boosting the country's economy. On the contrary, this is likely to maintain and develop traditional factors. To give just one example, today Vietnam has many traditional handicraft villages to meet their own needs but several households that create handicraft works have changed their jobs due to low revenues. Fortunately, their skillful products have been known by foreign enterprises and therefore have sold in many different countries around the world. Local people have turned back their careers and have continued to create sophisticated handicrafts. 
 On the whole, it seems to me that traditional ways of life have been lost as a result of economic developments. By contrast, it can be considered as an important factor to preserve the traditions and customs of their own cultures. 
 ------
feedback:
The essay importantly addresses the theme of economic growth and its effects on traditional cultures, which is a poignant matter. However, there are several key areas for improvement that can greatly enhance the clarity, coherence, and direction of the essay to better align with the prompts of English proficiency tests.

1. **Response to the Topic:** The introduction needs refining to ensure it directly addresses the prompt. A more effective beginning would clearly state the main argument while encapsulating aspects of the prompt. For example, mention how economic development and traditional values are perceived to be in conflict and then clearly state your position. It's crucial to pick a stance and consistently support it throughout the essay, avoiding a discussion from multiple viewpoints when the prompt specifies an opinion essay.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, or Stylistic Issues:** While the essay maintains a good basic structure, attention to detail in grammar, punctuation, and style could strengthen the overall presentation. For instance, ensuring verb tenses are consistent and that sentences flow logically from one to the other would aid readability and coherence. Additionally, linking words could be used more effectively to connect ideas more seamlessly.

3. **Clarity of the Author's Point of View:** The point of view appears to waver and could benefit from a more assertive stance. After stating the thesis in the introduction, each paragraph should build upon that thesis with clear, supporting details rather than presenting new or conflicting viewpoints. Being decisive in your viewpoint and reinforcing it throughout the essay will help solidify your argument.

4. **Clear and Descriptive Arguments:** There are valuable points made regarding the potential for economic growth to coexist with and even support traditional cultures. To strengthen these points, specific, evidence-based arguments should be provided. For example, the mention of Vietnam's traditional handicraft villages is a good start but delve deeper into how economic growth specifically aids the preservation or enhancement of these traditions. Quantitative data or more detailed examples could enrich your arguments.

Moving forward, focus on clearly outlining your essay in response to the prompt, maintaining a consistent viewpoint, and supporting arguments with specific examples. Refining grammar and stylistic elements will also contribute to a more professional and convincing essay. Remember, specificity and directness are key to articulating and supporting your position effectively.

prompt: IELTS Writing Task 2- Influence of television and computer games on children.
essay:
Watching TV and playing video games are two of most important children's leisure activities since the turn of new millennium. However, there has been an intense debate regarding whether they are beneficial or harmful for children. From my personal perspective, they would bring more negative impact on kids than positive one. 
 Admittedly, TV shows and video games are of great educational and entertaining benefits. In fact, there is a large number of educational and inspirational TV programs which enable children to have fun in the learning process and facilitate their intellectual development. " Ten thousand questions", for example, is one of such programs providing knowledge involving not only natural science but also social life, thereby helping foster the young the morally values and outlook the world and life. Additionally, recreation is for sure a crucial function of television and computer. They are enjoyable for children of all age as they are the great way to relieve stresses after long-hour studying at school. 
 However, the negative consequences relating to physical and mental health caused by these technologies should not be overlooked. One of the downsides is that spending too much time on watching TV and using computer may give rise to sedentary lifestyles. Kids being couch potato would be isolated from the real world. This is because they do not have enough time to socialize and to engage with outdoor activities which are essential for their physical growth. Also, their eyesight might be weekened by staring at the screen so long. More over, arguable contents on TV will lead to unanticipated implication on children's later life. Children trait is curiousity, hence they would be impressionable and imitate violent actions and sexual scenes in movies and video games. This would obviously exert detrimental influence on kids development. 
 In conclusion, although the widespread technologies benefits children in learning and entertaining, the undesirable effects on children's health and development should also be taken into consideration. Parents should take time to guide and supervise these important activities.
feedback:
The essay provides an insightful look into the effects of watching TV and playing video games on children, discussing both the educational and entertaining benefits as well as the potential negative impacts on physical and mental health. However, there are several areas where improvements could make the essay stronger and more aligned with the task requirements.

Firstly, it's vital that the essay address the prompt's instructions more accurately. The task calls for a discussion of both viewpoints regarding the impact of television and video games on children before presenting your own opinion. The initial approach should present a balanced examination of the arguments from both perspectives without immediately stating a personal perspective. A revised thesis statement such as, "This essay will explore the arguments for and against the impact of screen time on children, followed by a conclusion reflecting my viewpoint," would set a clearer framework for what follows.

In terms of structure, remember to clearly differentiate between the general discussion of the topic and your personal viewpoint. The introduction and conclusion can frame the discussion, while the body paragraphs should delve into the specifics of each viewpoint and your analysis. To enhance clarity and coherence, use phrases that indicate whose perspective is being discussed, for example, "Some argue that...," "On the other hand, others believe...," "I contend that...". This strategy helps the reader follow the progression of ideas more easily.

Transition sentences at the end of each paragraph are also essential. They serve as bridges to the next point of discussion, contributing to a smoother and more logical flow of the essay. Incorporating such transitions will make your arguments more connected and understandable.

Another area for improvement is the sentence structure. Aim for clarity by avoiding overly long sentences that can confuse the reader. Breaking down complex ideas into shorter, concise sentences can aid in maintaining the reader's attention and comprehension. This approach also helps in structuring your arguments more effectively, allowing you to elaborate on each point with sufficient detail and evidence.

On spelling, grammar, and stylistic issues, the essay is largely well-written but watch out for minor errors and ensure correct word choices ("weekened" should be "weakened", "couch potato" is also a colloquial term that might be better expressed in a more formal academic context). Proofreading could assist in catching these slips.

Finally, ensuring your point of view is clear is crucial. After discussing both sides of the argument, reinforce your personal stance with a well-reasoned conclusion that reflects on the evidence presented. This conclusion should tie back to the introduction, providing a coherent and rounded end to your essay.

By addressing these areas, the essay could more effectively meet the task's requirements and present a well-reasoned, balanced, and engaging discussion on the impact of screen time on children.

prompt: Writing task 2 : Many governments think that economic progress is their most important goal.

Many governments think that economic progress is their most important goal. Some people, however, think that other types of progress are equally important for a country. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion. 
 People have different views about economic growth as the necessary goal in one country. While some people argue that other measures of progress are also really important. And I believe that other types of progress are just as important. 
 There are several reasons about many governments focus on economic progress. First, health economics creates more job opportunities for employees with high salaries and therefore an improvement quality of life for people. prompt: Discuss both views. Cheap products or long lasting product. This is an IELTS essay

People are of the idea because many people have felt the bitterness of advertising and marketing strategy. For instance, the toys shipped from China, the same manufacturer produces identical toys for many firms and the company charges significantly higher compared to others, with a large brand name. 
 In conclusion, I think both arguments are valid. However, I believe that long-lasting commodities have an advantage over low-cost items because long-lasting products may be used for a long time without requiring further maintenance.
feedback:
The essay touches on an important debate about whether it's better to have products that last a long time but may be more expensive, or cheaper products that may not last as long. This topic is clearly relevant and the essay addresses this prompt directly.

Firstly, it's crucial to ensure that words are used correctly to convey the intended meaning. The word "Populous" seems to be misused. Remember, the conclusion is not the place to introduce new ideas.

Additionally, there are minor spelling, grammar, and stylistic issues throughout the essay that could be improved. For instance, ensuring that subjects and verbs agree, using commas correctly, and reviewing word choice can all contribute to a more polished piece.

Overall, your essay presents a thoughtful discussion on an important topic. By refining the structure, clarifying your argument, addressing minor errors, and ensuring correct word usage, you can significantly improve the coherence and persuasiveness of your writing.

prompt: Punishment is necessary to help children distinguish between right and wrong
essay:
How to make children learn difference between right and wrong 
 Topic: 
 It is important for children to learn the difference between right and wrong at an early age. Punishment is necessary to help them learn this distinction. 
 To what extent do you agree or disagree with this opinion? 
 What sort of punishment should parents and teachers be allowed to use to teach good behaviour to children? 
 Essay: 
 Essay: 
 It is some time argued that whether parents should apply punishments to their offspring as a way to teach them to distinguish between right and wrong. While this could be true in a certain extent, I believe that punishment plays an important role in educating children. However, not all punishment can take positive effects. 
 Admittedly, controlling children's behavior when they are still in young age keep them in line and avoid social evils. This is because children are vulnerable to be affected by temptation from the surroundings such as electronic games, violent-contained videos or pornographic films. Certain punishments enable children to understand what behavior is beneficial to them and hence to stay away from bad doings. This is exemplified in the study undertaken by American professors. They indicated that kids lacking the control from their parents are more likely to become crimes rather than those getting a good education. Thus, it is completely plausible for parents to carry out punishments to protect their offspring from adverse effects. 
 However, this is not to say that all punishments are good for children. Some parents today tend to use violent actions causing serious influences on physical and mental health of children. Instead of that, parents should use minor punishments associated with valuable lessons for children. For example, some parents asked their offspring to clear their room as a way to teach them to give up untidy habits. Besides, parents could talk with their offspring and give them significant advices if the mistake caused is unimportant. 
 After discussing all the points mentioned above, I can conclude that punishment is necessary for teaching children. Parents should have considerations to choose the best educational measure to ensure children's development in the future.
feedback:
This essay addresses a significant topic: the importance of teaching children the distinction between right and wrong and whether punishment is necessary for this learning. The attempt to explore this complex issue is commendable. However, there are several areas for improvement to enhance the effectiveness and relevance of the essay in relation to the given task. 

Firstly, it's crucial to ensure that the essay directly responds to all aspects of the topic. In this case, while the need for punishment in teaching children is discussed, the essay lacks a clear stance on the extent to which the author agrees or disagrees with the necessity of punishment. Including teachers’ roles in disciplining and educating children would provide a more comprehensive response to the prompt.

The structure and clarity of the essay can be improved. Each argument needs to be distinctly developed with supporting examples or evidence. For instance, when mentioning the study by American professors, specifying the study or providing more detailed information would add credibility and depth to the argument.

There are also grammatical and stylistic issues to address. For example, the phrase "It is some time argued" should be corrected to "It is sometimes argued." Attention to such details will not only improve the readability of the essay but also enhance its grammatical accuracy.

In summary, focusing on a clearer expression of personal opinion, addressing all parts of the prompt (including the discussion on appropriate punishments by both parents and teachers), expanding vocabulary, and refining grammar and style are key areas for improvement. Addressing these points will significantly strengthen the essay, making it more relevant, coherent, and persuasive.

prompt: IELTS Task 2: Traffic and accommodation problems are increasing - moving from cities to rural areas

feedback:

prompt: IELTS WRITING TASK 2: Should mobile phone is banned like smoking
essay:
Some people believe that using mobile phones is equally harmful to society as smoking and it is, therefore, also expected to be banned. From my perspective, I am in complete disagreement with this opinion as now will be discussed. 
 Firstly, it is prejudiced that people compare the use of mobile phones equivalently antisocial as smoking. Since phone and tobacco are two distinctively different entities, which exist for different purposes, the comparison between them is unreasonable. Tobacco has long been proving to be detrimental to not only the smoker themselves but also the health of society at large. The use of mobile phones, admittedly, has some drawbacks, but it does not dangerous or threatens the life of anybody. For example, some critics might point out that the excessive use of smartphones is attributable to myopia, or the noise of cell phones might be an annoyance to the surrounding people. These problems, however, can be easily curbed by limiting the time on screen, or turning on the silent mode when in public areas. 
 Secondly, while it makes sense why tobacco should be prohibited for its deadly effect, phones have numerous benefits to our life. Ever since the introduction of mobile phones, it has revolutionized the way we communicate and how we live to the point that everybody needs a phone to work or study today. Most jobs require employees to be either available by phone, for example, doctors and police officers, or to use their phones throughout the day, as is common with businessmen and lawyers. Mobile phones even become more necessary in times of pandemic such as the Covid-19 when everybody is required to work and study from home. 
 In conclusion, I content that mobile phones, unlike tobacco, have insignificant drawbacks to our society. In contrast, its enormous benefits make the idea of banning phones sounds far-fetched.
feedback:
The essay responds directly to the topic by discussing the comparison between the harmful effects of mobile phones and smoking, and makes a clear argument against the idea that mobile phones are as harmful as smoking. However, there are several areas where improvements can be made to strengthen the essay. 

1. **Clarity and Construction of Argument**: The phrase "as now will be discussed" in the introduction can be more effectively replaced with a direct statement summarizing your forthcoming arguments. Instead of hinting at a discussion, clearly outline the reasons supporting your viewpoint to give readers a roadmap of your essay.

2. **Word Choice and Accuracy**: The use of "prejudiced" to describe the comparison between mobile phones and smoking is not correct, as prejudice is typically used to refer to biased opinions against people or groups, not objects. A more precise term could be "biased" or "unfounded comparison." Similarly, "I content" is a misusage. The correct term is "I contend," which means to argue a point. Ensuring accurate word choice is crucial for your essay's clarity and professionalism.

3. **Grammar, Spelling, and Stylistic Issues**: The essay is generally well-written, but attention to detail in word usage and ensuring the correctness of expressions will enhance your writing quality. Relying on a dictionary or a thesaurus can be highly beneficial for confirming the meanings and appropriateness of words.

4. **Support and Description in Arguments**: Your arguments against the banning of phones are supported with valid points, such as the distinction between the purposes and effects of mobile phones and tobacco, along with the benefits and necessity of mobile phones in modern society. To further strengthen your essay, provide more detailed examples and perhaps acknowledge counterarguments while refuting them. This will show a thorough understanding of the topic and a balanced perspective.

5. **Point of View Clarity**: Your point of view is clear throughout the essay; you disagree with the comparison between mobile phones and smoking. To further refine your stance, ensure your arguments are consistently supportive of your viewpoint and avoid any ambiguous statements that could undermine your position.

In summary, focusing on precise word choice, clearly structuring your arguments, and providing detailed support for your claims will significantly improve your essay. Remember to leverage dictionaries and other resources to verify your language use, and consider both sides of the argument to present a reasoned and balanced essay. Practice and attention to detail will elevate the quality of your writing.

prompt: The Crucial Role of School in Shaping Lives
essay:
Introduction: 
 School is a cornerstone of our society, playing a pivotal role in shaping the lives of individuals. It serves as a foundation for knowledge, personal development, and the acquisition of essential skills. This essay explores the multifaceted aspects of school, highlighting its significance in nurturing well-rounded individuals. 
 Body: 
 1. ** Academic Growth:** 
 School provides a structured environment for academic learning. It equips students with the necessary knowledge and skills to navigate the complexities of the world. Subjects ranging from mathematics to literature contribute to a comprehensive education that forms the bedrock of intellectual development. 
 2. ** Social Development:** 
 Beyond academics, school is a melting pot of diverse social interactions. It offers students the opportunity to forge friendships, navigate social dynamics, and develop interpersonal skills. These experiences are invaluable, preparing individuals for the complexities of relationships in adulthood. 
 3. ** Character Building:** 
 School is not just about facts and figures; it is a crucible for character development. Through challenges, successes, and failures, students learn resilience, perseverance, and the importance of integrity. The moral compass instilled in school often guides individuals throughout their lives. 
 4. ** Extracurricular Activities:** 
 Extracurricular activities play a crucial role in shaping a holistic individual. Whether through sports, arts, or other pursuits, school provides a platform for students to discover their passions, develop talents, and learn essential life skills such as teamwork and leadership. 
 5. ** Preparation for the Future:** 
 School acts as a stepping stone to the future, preparing students for higher education and the workforce. The knowledge acquired and skills honed in school lay the groundwork for pursuing diverse career paths, contributing to the advancement of society as a whole. 
 Conclusion: 
 In conclusion, school is not merely an institution for academic learning but a dynamic crucible that molds individuals into well-rounded, capable members of society. Its influence extends beyond the classroom, shaping character, fostering social skills, and preparing students for the challenges that lie ahead. As we navigate the intricacies of life, the lessons learned in school resonate, guiding us on our journey of personal and professional growth.

Your essay on the importance and multifaceted roles of school provides a solid framework and touches upon significant areas such as academic growth, social development, character building, extracurricular activities, and preparation for the future. prompt: Global warming - an environmental problem or event
essay:
I would like to present to you about Global warming. This is one of the most serious issues that the world is facing today. Global warming refers to the gradual increase in Earth's average temperature due to the accumulation of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere. This phenomenon is primarily driven by human activities such as the burning of fossil fuels, deforestation, and industrial processes, which release carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases into the atmosphere. 
 The consequences of global warming are profound and wide-ranging. It leads to the melting of polar ice caps and glaciers, resulting in rising sea levels and coastal flooding. Moreover, changes in temperature and weather patterns disrupt ecosystems, endangering plant and animal species. Extreme weather events such as hurricanes, droughts, and heatwaves become more frequent and severe, posing threats to human lives, agriculture, and infrastructure. 
 To address global warming, concerted efforts are required at both individual and collective levels. We need to transition to renewable energy sources, such as solar and wind power, to reduce our reliance on fossil fuels. Additionally, efforts to recyling trash, using public transport are essential to protect environment. 
 Finally, by taking proactive steps to reduce emissions and protect the environment, we can worktogether for solving this problem.

prompt: task 2 Ielts:In many countries around the world, life expectancy is increasing.
essay:

 In recent years, the expectation of life from all over the world has risen significantly; therefore, this passage will discuss how older is essential for younger generations and the problems of overpopulation. However, the benefits seem to outweigh the drawbacks. 
 The increase in life expectancy is beneficial for several reasons. First and foremost, it is claimed that the longer people live, the more experienced and wise they are. After a long and continuous period of studying and working, the elderly have an opportunity to learn skills and knowledge that are valuable. Therefore older people can pass down their life experiences to younger generations, which makes the world more developed. Secondly, another benefit of living longer is that elderly can work or do volunteer with the view of devoting more to society. For example, my 65 years old uncle is still doing voluntary work as a teacher in a mountainous area. 
 On the other hand, it is undoubted that the rise in life expectancy also results in some drawbacks. A longer lifespan would be a burden on the shoulders of the government. For instance, the General Office For Population And Family Planning organization has announced that 2 billion VND had to be added to cover the medical insurance of people above 60 in the past 15 years. Moreover, overpopulation would be a big concern for developed countries. 
 In conclusion, there are convincing arguments both for and against the rising lifespan, but I firmly agree that the increase in the length of life may bring more advantages than its disadvantages.

prompt: IELTS WRITING TASK 2 - ASSESSMENT TO ABILITY OF STUDENTS
essay:
Some proponents of exams argue that formal tests show more efficacy when it comes to assessing scholars' aptitude instead of regular observation or projects. From my perspective, I am opposed to this opinion for some following reasons. 
 The benefits of regular assessment are plentiful. Engaging students' in projects facilitates them in developing different skills which can reinforce their future career. Supposing that soft skills are nowadays highly entailed by many companies, schools should place more premium on creating opportunities for undergraduates to brush up on skills such as team-working skills, problem-solving and social skills. Those who brim with various skill assets and proficiency are certainly beneficiaries when it comes to the rigorous recruitment competition. Besides, from teachers' perspective, they are provided a comprehensive evaluation on their pupils owing to this method, thereby scheming appropriate learning strategies to employ each students' ability effectively. 
 Furthermore, regular assessments render transparency compared to formal examination. Tests only offer transient results at the moment the examinees proceed. The results are strenuously guaranteed whether their competence lives up to the grades. Additionally, the act of falsifying test scores is prone to jeopardise the clarity of exams as well as motivation of learners. There is a likelihood that other students regard the case of cheaters as prime examples to imitate, getting distracted from pursuing knowledge for themselves. Whereas projects criticise learners based on their aptitude to emerge the thing they learn with reality, forging the strong bond between theoretical knowledge and practical activities. 
 In conclusion, I concede that exams play a pivotal role in judging performance of students; however, they should be combined with continuous assessment to acknowledge their genuine adeptness.

   - The essay was expected to include a more measured response to the presented argument. Instead of choosing a direct agree or disagree approach, it would have been more appropriate to show a nuanced understanding of the benefits and limitations of both exams and continuous assessments.    - Your use of language is commendable, with sophisticated vocabulary that adds depth to your essay. However, ensure clarity in your sentences to avoid potential confusion.
