prompt: Leaf Economic Traits Vary with Stand Age in Cunninghamia lanceolata
essay: Leaf Economic Traits Vary with Stand Age in Cunninghamia lanceolata \n Abstract：There is a trade-off between the functional traits of plant leaves, and through the study of the economic characters of leaf functional traits, the dry weight investment-return rule of plant leaves can be explored. In this study, leaf dry matter content(LDMC), specific leaf area(SLA) and specific leaf mass(SLM) of cunninghamia lanceolata at different stand age were studied, and the differences of leaf functional traits and the relationship between traits in different developmental stages of Cunninghamia lanceolata were explored. During the 5-25 years development of Cunninghamia lanceolata, SLA first decrease and then rise, LDMC and SLM first rise and then drop, all at turning point of 10-15 years old. The 20 years old fir has the highest SLA, LDMC, and lowest SLM. It shows that the expected return of the unit leaf dry matter investment in the early stage of development is low, and the leaf dry matter of the unit leaf area is high invested. In the later stages of development, the reverse is the case. The growth rate of Cunninghamia lanceolata may be the highest in 20; The variation coefficients of LDMC in the 5-25 years old of Cunninghamia lanceolata were smaller than SLA and SLM. The variation coefficients of SLA and SLM of 5, 10 and 15 years old were higher than that of 20 and 25 years old and the variation coefficient of SLA of 5 years old is higher than that of other ages, and the SLM variation coefficient of 5 years old is second only to that of 20. It shows that the expected return and dry matter investment was more sensitive to the environment than metabolic activity and more sensitive in the young period. SLA is negatively correlated with LDMC, SLA is negatively correlated with SLM, SLM is positively correlated with LDMC. It shows that the more investment of dry matter, the lower metabolic activity of leaves, the lower activity of leaf, the lower expected return of investment, and the more investment of dry matter of leaves, the lower the expected return of investment of unit dry matter; The correlation between SLA and LDMC, SLM and LDMC is the strongest in 5 years. This shows that the metabolic activity is more closely related to the expected return and the investment in young fir; The regression coefficient between traits shows that the effect of metabolic activity on SLA is the largest in 5 years old, second in 20, dry matter investment has the biggest influence on metabolic activity and expected return in 20 years old (but except for the 5 years old, the models of LDMC with other traits of other ages are less fit).
feedback:
The essay provides a detailed examination of leaf economic traits varying with stand age in Cunninghamia lanceolata, exploring significant aspects like LDMC, SLA, and SLM across different ages. The analysis of how these traits interact over time offers insightful observations into plant leaf investments and returns. The focused investigation on the changes these traits undergo as the stand ages represents the essay's strength, showcasing an in-depth understanding of the subject matter. Furthermore, the use of correlations between traits to discuss their implications on metabolic activity and investment return is commendable for its clarity and relevance to the topic.

However, there are areas where the essay could be improved for a more comprehensive and accessible presentation. prompt: Rich countries often give financial aid to poorer countries, but it does not solve poverty

The issue of supporting those states has become widespread. 
 The first mean that rich countries use in order to support poorer ones is the financial aid. Even though this could partially help to pay the debts and so sustain them financially, this should not be viewed as the only option available.

Poorer countries are also the ones where daily cleaning is lacking, leading them to being more subjected to developing diseases.

Living in a state of poverty means not only not being able to pay for a flat, but also to pay for what concerns our everyday life, especially food. Easily families would decide to cut on what they can survive without, or at least with a minimum portion. Providing food and water supplies to those countries could be as much as pricey as financially sustain them. At the same time, if done in the right way, it could turn out to be a type of aid which could have a direct impact on those people's lives.

prompt: IELTS - Writing t2 - Mobile telephones have brought many benefits but they have also had negatives

This is because that people are able to study online subjects on websites in their domestic or another country. Besides, documents can be found easily through the mobile phone connected the Internet. Secondly, some functions on mobile phones can assist people to relax. People can listen to music or watch videos whenever they desire. 
 On the other hand, this idea has a few fundamental drawbacks. One problem is that the concentration can be decreased. For example, the person who is working or studying cannot focus on what he is doing if his phone bell ring many times. Another issue is that having mobile phones can make people lonelier. This is due to that most people contact with each other through their phone. Hence, the face-to-face communication is not usually used. In addition to this, many children and teenagers who are addicted game online stay at their home regularly instead of meeting or going out with their friends. 
 In conclusion, having mobile phones does not only bring convenience but also negative influences. Overall, I believe that there is a balance in benefits and drawbacks when people use mobile phones. 
 263 words
feedback:

prompt: TOEFL Independent Essay Sample ( The influence of information's availability in today's world )

These inventions, the Internet for example, provides widespread and easy-to-access information. Thus, Does this increase in the availability of information influence life in today's world? 
 As intriguing and admirably inventive as the easy access to information seems, the Internet, treated as an unusual phenomenon, might showcase some incontrovertibly dangerous effects on life nowadays. 
 Privacy has been brutally invaded. Private life events, achievements, relationships and even work status has become available to all. Hence, anyone has the ability to figure out anyone's responsibilities and engagements and even manipulate them through the little details overtly unfolded to the world.

prompt: IELTS WRITTING TASK 2 Question: some people argue that university students should be free to choose
essay:
Question: some people argue that university students should be free to choose their subjects. Others believe that they should only be allowed to study courses of future benefits like science and technology. Discuss both views and give your opinion. 
 In today's advanced education, the topic of freedom to choose subjects at university has sparked a fiery discussion among people across the globe. While some argue that students in universities should have the right to decide their subjects, others believe that it is better for them to only study subjects that will benefit their future careers, such as science or technology. In a broader sense, this essay contends that the advantages of voluntary decisions surpass the value of studying only academic subjects, especially in the long term. 
 On the one hand, those who consider students should have the liberty to make decisions on their subjects are likely to argue that students are more inspired to study if they have their own choices. Indeed, each pupil's own differing interests influence their application to the university's subjects. For instance, individuals with linguistic and literary ability tend to prefer to delve into history, geography, or social science rather than spend hours and hours in math or technology classes. Therefore, the freedom to choose subjects not only fuels students' motivation but also promotes their distinct talents. The creativity and strong points like negotiation or critical thinking equipped to students via the studying process lend assistance in their future occupation while at the same time promoting personal development. 
 On the other hand, other groups that value academic subjects have their merits, particularly in the way students are taught essential skills for their future careers. Various job opportunities are given to students while they have a profound understanding of the field, including mathematics, science, or technology. To be specific, those who take these courses are able to access a wide range of well-paying and in-demand jobs because the rapid expansion of these industries results in a high demand for skilled professionals with profound expertise. Additionally, the outcomes of advances in science, technology, medicine, or engineering benefit society as a whole. However, it is hard to keep students' enthusiasm for compulsory education for a long time. 
 In conclusion, granting students the autonomy to apply preferred subjects' advantages outweighs the positive potential of mandatory subjects. Learning and pursuing careers relevant to interests and talents help to maintain students' passions in adulthood. In my opinion, while it seems reasonable to make student study subjects serve in the future workplace, it is more important to allow them to choose what they want to study for the creativity and innovation that liberty brings about.
feedback:
This essay tackles the question of whether university students should be given the freedom to choose their subjects or be limited to studying courses that are deemed beneficial for future careers, such as science and technology. Here's an evaluation based on the essay's alignment with the topic, language usage, clarity of the author's viewpoint, and the strength of the arguments provided.

1. **Alignment with the Topic**:
Your essay does address the topic by examining both viewpoints regarding the selection of university courses. However, the introduction mistakenly amplifies the prompt by suggesting a global debate, which deviates from the simple statement of the original question. Sticking closely to the prompt without exaggerating its scope would better serve your essay.

2. **Language and Style**:
There are no significant spelling errors, but there are areas where grammar and style can be improved for clarity and effectiveness. For instance, using simpler language can enhance understanding, especially for readers who are English language learners. Instead of saying, "this essay contends," it's more direct and powerful to state your perspective with phrases like "I believe" or "I think." This direct approach asserts your position clearly and makes your essay more personal and engaging.

3. **Clarity of Point of View**:
Your opinion seems to be saved for the conclusion, which is not the most effective structure for this type of essay. Introducing your viewpoint earlier and integrating it throughout the essay would make your position clearer and strengthen your argument. Remember, it's important to "own" your opinion by using first-person pronouns and directly stating your stance.

4. **Arguments and Descriptions**:
You provided clear and descriptive arguments for both sides of the discussion, which is commendable. You discussed how freedom in choosing subjects can enhance motivation and personal development, and also how focusing on courses beneficial to future careers might offer practical advantages. However, incorporating more specific examples and evidence earlier in the discussion could further bolster these points. Also, remember to link these arguments more explicitly to your opinion throughout the essay, not just in the conclusion.

Overall, your essay demonstrates a good understanding of the topic and presents thoughtful considerations on both sides of the argument. By making sure your language is clear and direct, presenting your own viewpoint more assertively, and closely aligning with the prompt without overstatement, you can significantly improve your essay. Keep up the good work, and remember that practice and attention to feedback are key to refining your writing skills.

prompt: Purchasing printed magazines, books may be dispensable since we can read all the information online
essay:

Some people believe that purchasing printed magazines or books soon be dispensable since we can read all the information from online sources for free. I completely disagree with this statement and I will illustrate some reasons in this essay. 
 On the one hand, some documents related to politic or the government or laws must all be written or printed on papers. As they are the important evidence of an event or a lawsuit, which may be easily edited or deleted by hackers if they are share on online websites. Incorrect information will lead to several misunderstandings and some severe arguments, which later deteriorate the situations. 
 On the other hand, lack of mobile phones or contemporary gizmos is also a vital reason. People from poor countries or who have financial difficulty cannot afford for any Internet-connected devices. For instance, many people who are homeless or living in slum rarely have enough money to pay for their daily living expenses so they do not really consider about buying a phone. Therefore, online news cannot replace printed newspaper books because not everybody is able to read things online. 
 In conclusion, I believe that although reading things online maybe more convenient than traditional manner, printed books and newspapers will never be replaced by them. Since printed documents play a crucial role in our society and worth more values, they are always essential as a source of information in today live and in the future.
feedback:
The essay makes a clear statement about the value of printed documents and magazines in today’s digital era. However, there are several areas for improvement that would make the argument stronger and more aligned with the requirements of an English proficiency test essay.

1. The introduction of the essay should directly address the topic from the very start. The initial sentence introduces a personal viewpoint that strays from directly restating the topic and presenting the author's opinion. Instead of suggesting all online information is free – which it is not universally – the discussion could be refined to emphasize disparities in access to technology. 5. The conclusion reiterates the main point effectively but could benefit from a more dynamic summary of the reasons provided. Highlighting the key arguments made in support of printed documents would provide a stronger closing and reinforce the author’s viewpoint.

Improving these aspects would significantly enhance the essay’s coherence, alignment with the prompt requirements, and overall persuasiveness. Focusing on presenting well-supported arguments within the stipulated format, and paying attention to clarity and accuracy in language, will contribute to a more compelling and successful essay.

prompt: Vietnamese eating habits from the past and now
essay:
Vietnamese eating wonts are very important and people are often serious about how they enjoy their meals. Up to now, the eating habits of Vietnamese people also have some differences. 
 Both past and present Vietnamese habits have a distinct community character. During the meal, each member has a separate bowl but all dishes are shared and served on the same tray. Vietnamese people often use chopsticks in meals. A pair of chopsticks is a miraculous eating tool that can replace many other tools such as forks, spoons, and knives,... because of its flexibility. 
 A long time ago, in traditional meals, Vietnamese people had a custom called "eat-calling". It was just a short speech from children to other members which expressed their politeness and respect for the older in the family. Additionally, in standard traditional meals, people paid special attention to eating speed. If you eat too fast or too low, it will reflect whether you are good or bad. 
 In modern days, eating is very comfortable and convenient, it is changed to suitable with the new age. Today, people are more open-minded, comfortable and positive in eating habits. They reject some rules to make members feel relax and sastify in the meals. Besides that, everyone is often busy and they don't have enough time to enjoy a standard meal. So, they eat something both delicious and quickly cooked like hamburgers, pizzas or packed food.

feedback:

However, the arguments could be further strengthened with more detailed examples and a deeper analysis of how these habits reflect broader cultural changes.

prompt: IELTS Writing task 2 - Memorising facts is the most important way to succeed in education.
essay:
TOPIC: Memorising facts is the most important way to succeed in education. 
 To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement? 
 Many people believe that learning by heart is an intriguing method to be good at studying. To some extent, I agree with that opinion, yet I disagree that it is the key of education success. 
 Most of the school programs comprise of known subjects, which are the proven facts or written knowledge, such as history, geography, literature, etc. The students who possess perfect remeberance would definitely have a certain advantage to get remarkable records in such subjects. When I was at school, top three of my classmates either were good at remember everything or studied like a hardy bee all the time. 
 However, memorising facts also bring some backwards. Those who rely on memorising would only know what have known and hardly can apply such knowledge into a different sector. People could never invent planes just by remembering the wings of birds! Moreover, if the knowledge are remembered as separate facts rather than finding connection among tons of events, someday the memory will be full and things can be forgotten. 
 On the other hand, the ultimate goal of education is to nurture brains, using brains to discover and apply theories into practice and to bring benefits into life. The lessons taught are just the foundation for learners to freely imagine, create new ideas and make evolution. Indeed, human beings have invented tons of marvelous products based on imagination and creativity and no limitations are set for creation. 
 In conclusion, it is impossible to deny the benefit of memorising to education, especially in elementary school and secondary school. However, the crucial keys for students in advanced education programs to reach the final objective of education success, is to learn how to apply the fundamental knowledge and encouraging free imagination and creation.
feedback:
Your essay demonstrates an understanding of the topic, which is a positive start. However, to improve, let's focus on several key areas.

1. **Response to the Topic:** The essay attempts to discuss the importance of memorizing facts in education but lacks a clear stance. Rather than presenting both agree and disagree perspectives, it's crucial for the essay to express a singular, well-defined opinion. This clear perspective helps structure your essay more effectively and makes your argument stronger.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, and Stylistic Issues:** There are noticeable spelling mistakes, such as "remembrance" incorrectly spelled as "remeberance" and "backwards" which should be "drawbacks". These errors can distract readers and impact the clarity of your message. Paying closer attention to spelling and grammar will enhance the professionalism and readability of your essay.

3. **Clarity of the Author’s Point of View:** Your essay's point of view seems divided. It hints at both the benefits and limitations of memorizing facts without firmly taking a side. For a more compelling essay, choose one viewpoint and develop your essay around that perspective. This will enable you to create a more focused and persuasive argument.

4. **Arguments and Support:** Your essay includes examples and reasons, like the reference to how memorization impacts creativity and innovation, which is good. However, the arguments could be strengthened by more detailed examples and a clearer connection between your claims and the supporting evidence. For instance, when mentioning historical inventions or creativity, providing specific examples could make your argument more convincing.

5. **Structure and Cohesion:** Aim for a structure that allows for a clearer development of your argument. Typically, an effective essay would include an introduction stating your viewpoint, body paragraphs that present reasons and examples supporting your stance, and a conclusion reinforcing your viewpoint. Each paragraph should smoothly transition to the next, maintaining coherence throughout the essay.

6. **Polishing Your Writing:** It's important to review your essay for spelling and grammar errors actively. Depending on spell-check might not catch all mistakes, so manual proofreading is essential. Quality should always be prioritized over quantity; an essay that's shorter but clearer and more correct is better than a longer one with many mistakes.

By focusing on these areas, you can significantly enhance the quality of your essay. Remember, expressing a clear, singular viewpoint and supporting it with well-explained reasons and examples is key to a strong essay. Keep practicing, and don’t hesitate to revise your work after your first draft.

prompt: IELTS writing task 2: Should we attend schools until we are at least 18?

 First of all, receiving an education helps the youths to find out what type of subjects they are interested in the most. During the education stage, they learn at least more than 5 subjects in one semester at school, consequently this may be the best time for them to inspire their interests. Even though this will take much time for them to figure out what specific fields of subjects do they actually like, they still can learn different knowledge at the same time. This also helps those young people, confusing about their future career, to find out a career path that really suits them well. 
 Another reason why the youths should stay at school until they are adults is that schools assist students to distinguish between right and wrong. In other words, students will understand how to apply knowledge, use the correct language, and have right behavior to operate some specific work properly. For example, an advanced English level for being a businessman is required because this type of job needs particular language to communicate with corporations. 
 In conclusion, before becoming an adult, attending schools is an efficient way for the young people to develop their potential and prepare them for the near future.
feedback:

1. Responding to the Topic:
The essay needs to address the specific question or task given more clearly. For instance, if the task is to discuss to what extent you agree or disagree with a statement, make sure your response is explicit in this context. Use phrases such as "I am in full agreement/disagreement" or "I partially agree/disagree" to express your stance unambiguously at the beginning of your essay. This will help set the stage for your arguments and ensure that you're directly answering the prompt.

2. Clarity and Structure:
Be mindful of the essay's structure and clarity. Each paragraph should have a clear main idea, supported by examples or arguments. The transition between paragraphs should be smooth, guiding the reader through your discussion. An outline might help organize your thoughts before writing. For instance, sketching out the main points you want to cover and ensuring they directly respond to the essay prompt can improve coherence and relevance.

3. Spelling, Grammar, and Style:
Your essay exhibits a good command of language; however, paying closer attention to spelling and grammatical correctness could further enhance your writing. Also, consider varying your sentence structures to keep the reader engaged and to articulate your points more dynamically.

4. Providing Support for Your Arguments:
You've made several compelling arguments on why education is crucial for young people's development. To strengthen these arguments, include more specific examples, statistics, or studies. This evidence adds credibility to your claims and makes your essay more persuasive.

5. Point of View:
Your point of view is present but could be articulated more strongly at the beginning and throughout the essay. Remember to reinforce your position in the conclusion to make your stance unforgettable to the reader.

6. Conclusion Enhancements:
The concluding sentence could be expanded into a more robust paragraph that summarizes the key points discussed and reiterates the importance of your stance. A stronger conclusion will leave a lasting impression on the reader.

In summary, focus on explicitly addressing the essay prompt right from the beginning, organize your points clearly, enhance grammatical accuracy, and fortify your arguments with specific evidence. Lastly, conclude with a summary that encapsulates your viewpoint effectively. Practicing these strategies will undoubtedly elevate the quality of your essays.

prompt: towns constructed in previous centuries that were more suitable for residents.problem and solution
essay:
Over the past few decades, many ancient towns were built to serve residents' lives and became a historical site in a host of countries. There are some opinions that these buildings are not relevant to the modern standards of living. This essay is going to discuss the consequences of this issue and also offer several solutions. 
 Initially, this problem can cause traffic congestion in some parts of several nations. Due to having less transportation in the past than now, people in modern day face the difficulty in going through the roads easily with their vehicles. In Azerbaijan, for instance, Ichery Sheher, a well-preserved city since the VIII century, was prevalent for the traffic jams because of having no permission to expand the street. Another noticeable issue is that the constructive materials are getting worse day by day. Because the heritage sites have existed for a long time, they might be destroyed by oxidants. This may cause death and the extent of property damage for surrounding accommodations. 
 To address this complication, there are two certain approaches including widening the roads and developing tourism. Regarding the former, many old constructors which have no cultural values should be knocked down to make room for the vehicle movement. As a result, there will be less traffic congestion and can make the drivers feel comfortable when moving through the street. With the latter, historical heritage plays a crucial role in boosting the economy of the nations by attracting tourists. In addition, the local authorities may set up public facilities such as restaurants or coffee shops for visitors to relax and enjoy delicious meals. 
 Ultimately, despite the challenges of remaining ancient heritages, many measures can deal with this problem for further innovation and the safety of people.
feedback:
This essay aimed to address the relevance of ancient towns to modern standards of living, touching upon challenges and proposing solutions. However, there are several areas that could benefit from refinement for improved clarity and effectiveness.

1. **Response to Topic**: The essay begins with an intention to discuss the consequences and solutions related to ancient towns and modern living standards. While it does follow this direction, the introductory statement lacks a clear thesis or personal stance, which is crucial for guiding the reader through the argument. It's important to clearly state your position on the issue right from the start. Instead of saying "This essay is going to discuss...," assert your viewpoint directly to make your argument stronger.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, and Stylistic Issues**: 
   - The word "decades" was misused to describe a period that spans across centuries. For accuracy, referring to periods over 100 years should be described as "centuries" rather than "decades."
   - In the mention of "residents’ lives," the apostrophe suggests possession when it was intended to pluralize. Simply saying "residents" without the apostrophe would be more appropriate unless indicating ownership.
   - The essay could benefit from more careful attention to tense consistency and the correct use of plurals and singular forms to enhance readability and precision.

3. **Clarity of Point of View**: The essay outlines negative impacts of preserving ancient towns and suggests solutions. However, the author's personal stance or viewpoint is not prominently showcased. Strengthen your essay by clearly stating your perspective on whether the preservation of ancient towns outweighs the presented challenges, providing a compelling reason for your stance.

4. **Arguments and Support**: The arguments presented for traffic congestion and degradation of construction materials due to age are understandable but need to be supported by more specific examples or data for stronger persuasion. Additionally, when proposing solutions such as widening roads or developing tourism, explaining how these actions would directly address the concerns raised could make the argument more compelling. For example, detailing how specific measures in tourism development can preserve historical integrity while accommodating modern needs would enrich the essay.

In summary, focusing on clearly stating a thesis, improving grammar and word choice, clarifying the author’s viewpoint, and providing detailed support for arguments would significantly enhance the effectiveness of the essay. By addressing these areas, the essay could offer a more persuasive and engaging discussion on the relevance of ancient towns in contemporary society.

prompt: Applying a strict tax level on fast foods?

 Junk food obviously has multiple adverse effects on people's health, especially weight. The high contents of fat and carbohydrate in fast food are the main cause of obesity. Fried chicken and deep-fried potatoes, which are made with a thick coat of bread-crumb soaked in repeatedly-used oil, can be taken as a good example. Its popularity affects everyone's daily diet and adds an excessive amount of calories to their bodies. Obesity and other diseases not only diminish their lifespan but also hinder their working ability. Thus, a strict measure should be taken on a national or even international scale to prevent further consequences. 
 Applying a high tax is surely a good point because the primary reason for enormous fast-food consumption is its low price. With the addition of tax, it is no longer a cheap and available choice. People will instead opt for purchasing fresh ingredients to make better-valued and healthy meals. Moreover, we could ensure the reduction in the number of junk-food suppliers because if there is a higher tax, the business will seem less lucrative. This also means fewer people can have access to fast-food and related illnesses. 
 In conclusion, an urgent rate of diseases associated with the use of junk food should be well-aware and tacked. Applying a strict tax level is an effective measure in this case.
feedback:
The essay brings an important perspective on the impact of fast-food consumption and the potential benefits of imposing heavy taxes on such food items. However, there are several aspects that could be improved to make the essay more effective and aligned with the assigned topic. 

Firstly, it's crucial to directly address the specific question or topic given. In this case, the main focus should be on discussing the proposal to tax fast food as a means to encourage healthier eating habits, rather than broadly stating the health issues caused by fast food. The essay should begin by clearly stating your position on this specific proposal (whether you agree or disagree with it) and provide a clear rationale for your stance. This will set a focused direction for the essay and ensure that all arguments presented are relevant to the core topic.

In terms of structure, it's essential to ensure that each paragraph contributes directly to the argument you are making. While discussing the health implications of fast food is related, the primary focus should be on how taxing fast food could influence consumers' choices and health outcomes. This would mean emphasizing the relationship between cost and consumption habits, and how increased prices might lead to healthier choices.

There are also some minor spelling, grammar, and stylistic issues to address. For example, ensuring consistent tense usage and reviewing sentence structure for clarity. Additionally, try to use a variety of sentence structures and vocabulary to make your essay more engaging.

The conclusion should succinctly summarize the main arguments made in the essay and reinforce your stance on the issue. It's important to ensure that your concluding statement directly addresses the topic and reflects the discussion within your essay. 

Overall, strive for clear articulation of your views with direct relevance to the topic, supported by logical arguments. By refining these areas, your essay will become a more compelling and focused piece of writing.

prompt: IELTS - WRITING TASK 2 - hosting an international sports event is good or bad for the country

prompt: IELTS Task 2 - Teaching Situation in Classroom No Longer Exist by 2050 (Education)
essay:
It is considered by some that the teaching and learning environment of teachers and pupils in a room in reality will disappear before 2050. In my opinion, I do not agree that there will no longer be any learning interactions between the two group of people in the real world, but the virtual classroom may somehow replace the functions of a physical classroom. 
 Firstly, technology becoming more advanced may be the main reason leading to the disappearance of teachers teaching in a classroom. The invention of different communication applications favours the exchange of ideas online, through the Internet in any place at any time, which lowers the importance and uniqueness of a real classroom. In other words, applications like Skype, Facetime or even other teaching and learning websites can link up teachers and students conveniently, allowing them to meet and interact at their homes or offices, without needing them to gather together at the same place. 
 However, the importance of the existence of classrooms cannot be ignored, as they provide a platform for people to socialise and learn to get along with others, which this cannot be fulfilled and replaced by online learning sites or lesson videos. Teachers are not only teaching what are told in textbooks, but also the manners and communication skills which are essential to students. To illustrate, students are learning to respect teachers and classmates when having regular face-to-face lessons in the classroom. Such vital skills required as an individual living in the society ensure the stable and unreplaceable position of real classroom. 
 In conclusion, classrooms will still exist for a long time in the next few centuries as places for teachers to teach and students to learn, since new popular learning methods, in particular the commonly used of the Internet, can only take up part of the functions of classrooms.
feedback:
Your essay presents a detailed view on the future of classrooms and the influence of technology on education. However, there are several areas where improvements can be made to enhance clarity, coherence, and overall impact. 

Firstly, stating your position more clearly in the introduction would guide the reader through your arguments more effectively. Rather than expressing disagreement in a complex manner, consider a more straightforward approach, such as, "I disagree to a certain extent that physical classrooms will become obsolete by 2050 because..." This sets a clear stage for the arguments that follow.

In terms of spelling, grammar, and stylistic issues, your essay is well-composed, but careful attention to smoother transitions between ideas could improve readability and flow. Also, ensuring consistency in tense and more varied sentence structures could elevate your writing style further.

Your point of view is present, yet could be strengthened with more explicit statements of agreement or disagreement throughout the essay. This would not only reinforce your stance but also make your reasoning more persuasive to the reader.

While your arguments are indeed relevant, they could be enhanced by offering more specific examples and elaborating on how technology could complement rather than fully replace the traditional classroom setup. For instance, discussing potential limitations of virtual learning — such as the challenge of replicating hands-on experiences or the importance of physical presence for certain types of social learning — could offer a more balanced perspective.

Your conclusion introduces new ideas, which might confuse readers expecting a summary of discussed points. A stronger conclusion might reiterate your main arguments, emphasizing the enduring value of physical classrooms alongside technology's role in education's evolution. For example, you could conclude, "For these reasons, I believe physical classrooms will not become obsolete by 2050. Instead, they will evolve to incorporate technology, enriching the traditional learning environment rather than replacing it."

Remember, good essays not only present arguments but also engage the reader by clearly stating and supporting the author’s point of view. By refining your introduction and conclusion, clarifying your position, and enhancing the depth of your arguments, your essay will become a more compelling and persuasive piece of writing.

prompt: [IELTS WRITING TASK 2] GETTING OLD IN THE MODERN WORLD
essay:
In modern society, while a number of individuals suppose that aging is somewhat terrible, others disapprove of this as they believe the average living standard for older people has become increasingly desirable compared to the former days. This essay shall conduct a thorough assessment of both viewpoints so that a reasoned conclusion can be drawn. 
 On the one hand, the elderly nowadays are more prone to certain illnesses due to environmental pollution. The technology era has brought about a plethora of problems regarding our natural environment. A prime example of this is air contamination, a result of excessive carbon dioxide emission. Seniors, whose immune systems have significantly reduced in efficiency with the passage of time, may be more vulnerable to respiratory diseases such as asthma or lung cancer. As a matter of fact, when an older person suffer from those illnesses, they would not be able to take care of themselves, as well as need full-time provision of others. In the meantime, the majority of individuals detest the concept of a life with such lethal diseases, since they believe that translates to being a burden to their family members. Therefore, an increasing number of people in today's world consider getting old unfavorable. 
 On the other hand, the advancement in technology has ameliorated the living conditions for seniors. Nowadays, there are a plethora of robotic inventions that are intended to make life easier for sick older people. For instance, Japanese scientists established the "Care Robot" that can keep track of the health index of the elderly, and even be a recreational device that can read books or play music. Another point to be mentioned is that the ascent in the number of nursing homes. Many old people seem to be let down by the fact that their offspring can not allocate enough them to them, and nursing homes may be a suitable resolution for this. There, they can meet and befriend with people of their age, who have a tendency to share similar favorite pastimes. Seniors, therefore, can still derive great pleasure from the latter half of their lives. 
 All in all, albeit getting old may lead to seemingly detrimental health problems, the elderly in modern society are now accessible to a variety of means of entertaining. From my way of thinking, I firmly believe that aging in today' world should not be deemed negative.
feedback:
This essay engages with the prompt effectively, discussing perspectives on aging in modern society. Its exploration of how technological advancements and environmental factors impact the elderly is insightful. However, there are several areas where improvement is needed for a stronger, more effective essay. 

1. **Response to Topic**: The essay attempts to explore both sides of the argument regarding aging, which aligns with the topic. However, the instruction to thoroughly assess viewpoints doesn't mean to conclude definitively. The essay should present the perspectives and your opinion without aiming to make a final decision for the reader. The essence of this task is to inform and present viewpoints rather than provide a closed conclusion. 

2. **Spelling, Grammar, Stylistic Issues**: Overall, the spelling and grammar are accurate. However, there are areas where sentence structure could be simplified for clarity. Phrases such as "a plethora of robotic inventions that are intended to make life easier" could be simplified to "many robotic inventions designed to simplify life." Simplifying language makes your arguments more accessible to all readers. 

3. **Clarity of Author's Point of View**: Your point of view seems to lean towards viewing aging positively due to technological advancements. Yet, placing your personal opinion prominently towards the end without adequately developing it throughout the essay weakens its impact. Integrate your opinion gradually alongside the presented viewpoints to strengthen the coherence of your argument.

4. **Arguments and Support**: Each paragraph presents clear arguments regarding the impact of environmental and technological changes on the elderly. Including specific examples, like the "Care Robot," effectively illustrates your points. However, ensure that each argument equally contributes to your overall viewpoint. Expanding on how these examples relate to broader societal trends or personal observations could enrich your discussion.

To enhance your essay:
- Avoid definitive conclusions that might close off discussion. Keep the essay open-ended to invite readers to consider the presented viewpoints.
- Integrate your personal opinion more organically throughout the essay. This strengthens the connection between your viewpoint and the arguments presented.
- Simplify complex sentences to improve readability and ensure your points are clearly understood.

By focusing on presenting viewpoints in a balanced manner and refining your expression, your essay will become a more compelling and informative piece.

prompt: Why many prisoners commit crimes as soon as they released? - IELTS WRITING TASK 2
essay:
Response: 
 Many prisons turn over a new leaf after they released from prison; nevertheless, not all the case are true. Some criminals commit crimes as soon as they get out of prison, and personally, I believe there are reasons to justify this. 
 Firstly, it is people's prejudice that indirectly make those prisoners give up the idea of re-integrating. Back to the past, criminals were considered a threat to the society, and undoubtedly, people tended to distance themselves from prisoners. That presumption had rooted deeply inside people's mind and made them turn their back at people who commit crimes, even if he or she is only a little thief. As a result, these released prisoners no longer feel they are parts of the society anymore, instead, they feel left-out and abandoned. Without the warm welcoming and the sympathy of the society, these prisoners find no incentive in changing for the better since all of their efforts would meet with negligence and underappreciation. 
 Secondly, our society lacks of job opportunity for the prisoners. After coming out of prison, a job is of the utmost importance on the grounds that offers the prisoners stable incomes to live by and makes them feel that they have values to the society. However, finding a proper job is a challenge to every prisoner since their crimes are often regarded as acts of fraudulence and untrustworthiness. Clearly, no employers would like to take on these people in their working places. Struggling to find a job, most released prisoners would end up facing financial difficulties. Eventually, they would resort to committing crimes in order to make some money. 
 In conclusion, reasons why many prisoners commit crimes right after being released could be put down to people's prejudice and the lack of job opportunity for the return criminals.
feedback:
The essay makes a strong case regarding the challenges faced by prisoners upon their release, highlighting two main issues: societal prejudice and the lack of job opportunities. The reasoning provided is sound, and the examples given are relevant and effectively illustrate the points being made. This makes the body paragraphs both coherent and cohesive, demonstrating a clear understanding of the essay topic.

However, there are areas that need improvement to enhance the overall quality of the essay:

1. **Response to the Topic:** The essay successfully addresses the given topic, presenting well-thought-out arguments regarding why many prisoners re-offend after being released. This shows a good grasp of the subject matter.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, and Stylistic Issues:** While the message is conveyed clearly, there are some grammatical and vocabulary issues that need attention. For instance, consider simplifying certain terms to ensure clarity. Instead of "negligence," which might not perfectly fit the context, "ignored" might be a more appropriate choice. Also, there are instances of run-on sentences, especially in the opening and closing paragraphs, which could be broken down into shorter, clearer sentences. Breaking down complex thoughts into simpler statements can help with readability and clarity.

3. **Point of View Clarity:** The essay effectively communicates the author’s point of view, which is that societal factors significantly impact the likelihood of reoffending. This perspective is consistently maintained throughout the essay, offering a solid stance on the issue.

4. **Arguments and Support:** Your arguments are clear and supported with relevant examples, particularly in the body paragraphs. These sections do a good job of highlighting the reasons behind recidivism, supported by logical explanations. 

To further improve your essay, consider the following specific recommendations:
- For the opening paragraph, aim for conciseness to avoid run-on sentences. A more direct introductory sentence could provide a clearer entry point into the topic.
- End each paragraph, including the conclusion, with a stronger closing sentence to reinforce your main points. Ensure the conclusion succinctly summarizes the essay’s arguments without introducing new ideas.
- Make sure each paragraph adheres to a minimum of three sentences, as this structure supports clearer argument development and helps with the overall flow and readability.
- Pay attention to the punctuation and sentence structure to avoid the grammar issues noticed.

Adjusting these elements can significantly elevate the quality of the essay, making your arguments more persuasive and your writing style more engaging and easier to follow. Keep these tips in mind for future writing tasks, as they can help in consistently producing well-structured and compelling essays.

prompt: WRITING TASK 2 TOPIC: Team sports and individual sports - which is more favourable?
essay:
Sports selection has polarized public opinion, with a number of people believing that playing individual sports is more advantageous than taking part in team sports and others holding an opposite belief. Personally, I am an advocate of the first group. 
 There are several justifications why some people prefer participating in sports activities alone. First of all, these sports not only improve players' physical and intellectual health, but also facilitate the development of some personal skills, especially building up independence. In terms of self-reliance, while a team member can receive help from other teammates when playing football, basketball and so forth, there is often no one that an athlete could rely on during a solo game. This has players thinking solely to make their own decisions and tactics precisely. In addition, playing individual sports also gives more flexibility to their schedules. For instance, players can freely decide wherever or whenever they practice without depending on others' approval. This somehow has some positive effects on sportspeople's emotion, which could improve their performance. 
 However, I strongly agree with the opinion that team sports provide us with far more advantages. Solidarity is one of the obvious benefits that players could gain from such sports. For example, take football into account. The key factor contributing to the victory of a team is not how many points their attackers could score but how they could coordinate from the defenders to the forwards and could they sacrifice themselves for the mutual benefits. The more successful a team is, the more sense of unity is instilled into each individual, which not only helps players in social situations but also benefits them in their workplaces. 
 In conclusion, although some people say that we should choose to play solo sports such as golf or tennis, I believe that team sports like football provide us more benefits.
feedback:
The essay demonstrates a clear understanding of the topic, effectively restating the prompt and presenting a well-developed argument. The transition within sentences is notably smooth, and the essay effectively communicates a personal stance on the importance of team sports over individual sports. This clarity in expressing personal opinion is a strong aspect of the essay.

However, there are several areas that could be improved to enhance the overall quality of the essay and better align it with the task requirements. 

1. **Balance Between Views:** The essay task requires a discussion of both public opinion and personal perspective, with an examination of the reasons behind each viewpoint. While the essay does introduce the notion that opinions are divided, there is a missed opportunity to explore the validity of the opposing view in depth. Expanding on why some people might prefer individual sports, including potential advantages not mentioned, and then contrasting these with the benefits of team sports from a more neutral perspective before stating a personal opinion would strengthen the essay. Providing specific examples or evidence to support both perspectives before concluding with your stance would offer a more balanced and comprehensive discussion.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, and Style Issues:** The essay is generally well-written but could benefit from minor improvements in spelling, grammar, and style. Paying attention to the consistency in verb tenses and ensuring that sentences are complete will improve readability. Additionally, varying sentence structure could enhance the stylistic appeal of the essay.

3. **Clear and Descriptive Arguments:** The essay makes a strong argument for the benefits of team sports, emphasizing solidarity and the potential for personal development beyond physical health. To further improve, consider detailing how individual sports might also offer unique benefits that are not found in team sports, such as the development of self-motivation and the ability to set personal goals. Providing clear and descriptive arguments for both views would create a more balanced essay.

4. **Conclusion Strength:** The conclusion succinctly states the personal opinion, aligning with the introduction. To make the conclusion even stronger, briefly summarize the key arguments for both sides discussed in the essay before reaffirming the personal stance. This summarization would not only reinforce the essay's main points but also demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of the debate.

In summary, while the essay effectively conveys a personal opinion and is structured in a way that is easy to follow, greater balance in discussion, attention to grammatical detail, and the inclusion of more varied and specific examples to support each viewpoint would enhance the overall effectiveness and coherence of the argument.

prompt: The question whether the children should read stories themselves or with a help from parents

 On the one hand, there are several reasons supporting that the children should read books and watch TV, movies by themselves. Firstly, this is a way which developing young people's ability of self - descipline. For example, if a child learns from the stories, TV or movies by themselves, they have ability to analyse the problem as well as understand the information. Secondly, parents are too busy to spend time reading or telling stories to children. Instead of waiting for parents, the children can arrange their timetable to read materials whenever they want. 
 On the other hand, listening to parents reading or telling stories is better than reading by themselves. Firstly, this fosters the intimate bonding between parents and children. Reading together is simply an enjoyable and easy way for parents to take out and focus on the family. Secondly, some small children need guidance and explanation when reading books. For instance, there are many enigmatic and complicated topics which the children can't understand without helping. 
 To sum up, I believe that it is always better for the parents as well as children if parents read or tell stories to their children.

prompt: It is argued that schooling from early age would be ideal for the children' development
essay:
TOPIC: Some people say that children should go to school as young as possible, while others believe that children should go to school of at least 7 years old. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. 
 It is argued that schooling from early age will be ideal for the children to develop themself, while some think that the primary education can be able to teach for the pupils who are at least 7 years old. While children can benefit from going to school as young as possible, I completely believe they should be over 7 years old to enroll to school. 
 On the one hand, the younger the children, the better the education. Young kids can become accustomed to studying environment easily. As a young age, children is likely a paper that can absorb the new information and learn everything in a very fast and effective way, which exactly likes how they learn to craw or walk. Furthermore, since attending school earlier than the normal age, the pupils can finish their course sooner than average; meanwhile, they still enhance enough knowledge for their coming career in adult's life. At this point, having more time to explore the world or do whatever they want would be a positive side for early education. 
 On the other hand, education is much more suitable for children who is at least 7 years old. The students at this age can be mature enough to learn advanced lessons from the school's curriculum. Some subjects require children higher conscious level to understand the theory from the teacher and also be aware of what they learn. In addition, 7-year-old pupils tend to have proper behaviors towards education such as self-discipled or independent. Without any kinds of punishment or reminder, these children can do self-study at home or at school to use their best period to learn as much as possible. 
 In conclusion, early age seems to be a logical time for children to learn something, but without some benefits mentioned, they should be old enough to be schooling with a range of academic subjects.
feedback:
Your essay on whether children should start school at an early age or at least 7 years old has a clear topic and presents arguments for both viewpoints, which is a good structure to follow. However, there are several areas where improvement can make your essay stronger and more effective in communicating your ideas.

1. **Clarity and Grammar**: The introduction attempts to restate the prompt and present your opinion, but there are grammatical inaccuracies that make it slightly difficult to understand. Pay close attention to your grammar, especially verb forms and subject-verb agreement (e.g., "develop themselves" instead of "develop themself," "children are" instead of "children is"). Improving your grammatical accuracy will make your argument more persuasive and easier to follow.

2. **Structure and Organization**: Your essay could benefit from a clearer structure. Consider dividing your essay into three paragraphs: the first two discussing each viewpoint using third person pronouns to show these are general opinions, not yours personally. The third paragraph should then introduce your own opinion using first person pronouns, making it clear it is your perspective. This structure not only makes your essay clearer but also helps to distinguish between general opinions and your personal viewpoint.

3. **Depth of Argumentation**: While you present both sides of the argument, your explanations and reasoning could be more detailed. For each viewpoint, try to delve deeper into why people might hold these opinions. What are the specific benefits or drawbacks they see? Providing more detailed arguments and examples will make your position stronger and more convincing.

4. **Word Choice and Sentence Structure**: Some sentences are awkward due to word choice and construction (e.g., "exactly likes how they learn to crawl or walk" could be simplified to "just as they learn to crawl or walk"). Simpler language that clearly conveys your meaning is preferable and more effective in making your argument. Avoid overly complex sentences as they can confuse the reader and detract from your point.

5. **Personal Opinion Clarity**: Your personal opinion is present, but it could be expressed more clearly and confidently. It's important to directly state why you support a particular age for starting school, basing this on evidence or personal experience. This helps the reader understand your perspective and the reasoning behind it.

To improve your essay, focus on grammatical accuracy, a clear and structured presentation of public and personal opinions, deeper argumentation with detailed examples, simpler language for clarity, and a confident expression of your own viewpoint. By addressing these areas, you will make your essay more engaging and persuasive.

prompt: IELTS TASK 2: Some people think that the government should pay one of the parents

 On the one hand, one of the negative aspects of this policy is this that it increases the conflicts among the family. This is because if both the parents have a prominent education qualification, then they both want to continue their career. Therefore, it will be the tough situation for them that which one will sacrifice their job and look after their children. Furthermore, money is not the only thing for which individual works, there is also the passion which drives them for their job. For instance, one of the newspapers gave evidence through survey that more than 60 percent both parents want to work after marriage. Thus, use of this policy might create problem in families. 
 On the other hand, positive aspect of this policy is that the children will get the enormous care and will grow in a healthy environment provided by one of their parent. The reason for this is if one of the parents stay at home and at the same time gets paid by the government for same, this will automatically relax their mind and they will joyfully spend their time with their kids. For example, according to the survey done by the Nascom surveyor company it is found that those children who spend full time with their parents are more emotionally attached with them in comparison to others. As a consequence of this, strong bond will be developed in the family. 
 In conclusion, while there are some disadvantages of the policy like it may result in dispute among parents due to their career aspect, it also has advantage like the kids will get more love and care which results in a happy family.

prompt: IELTS task2- It is often said that governments spend too much money on projects to protect wildlife?
essay:
Q: It is often said that governments spend too much money on projects to protect wildlife, 
 while there are other problems that are more important? 
 Do you agree or disagree? 
 Ans: 
 It is sometimes argued that governments invest a considerable amount of money in preserving wild animals as opposed to other more serious issues existing in society. While I agree with this point of view to some extent, I believe that the monetary support to wildlife protection should not be neglected. 
 On the one hand, governments would be likely to give priority to address the problems of economy, education, public health and social inequality instead of wildlife conservation as allocating financial resources. For instance, If the problem of an economic recession in certain countries is unable to be tackled, they do not have sufficient money to assist wild creatures. By spending a great deal of money on regenerating some natural habitats, such as regrowing trees or rainforests, there is a wide range of wildlife that can be saved. Furthermore, without making an endeavour to educate citizens that requires an increase in government funding, they would be less aware of environmental issue. 
 On the other hand, the large proportion of governments expenditure on how to efficiently preserve wildlife should be maintained, otherwise humans may suffer irreversible damages. For example, the huge areas of forests are cleared leading to the disappearance of natural habitats, and that people exploit these lands as farming lands. This inappropriate behaviour breaks the food chain and causes an imbalanced ecological system. Therefore, governments should spend more money on this in case of losing unique species forever. 
 In conclusion, it seems to me that governments should apportion the equal ratio of financial assistance between the national problems and wildlife issues so that we are able to peacefully coexist with the majority of creatures on Earth.
feedback:
Your essay addresses the topic effectively by presenting a balanced view on government spending on wildlife protection versus other societal issues. However, there are several areas in which the essay can be improved to make your arguments clearer and more compelling.

However, it's crucial to ensure that your introduction succinctly presents this stance without delving into detailed reasoning or examples. Reserve the detailed discussion for the body paragraphs to maintain a clear and organized structure.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, and Style:** Your essay is generally well-written, but there are minor grammatical errors and stylistic choices that could be refined. For instance, consider breaking down complex sentences into simpler ones, which can help clarify your thoughts and make the essay more accessible to your readers. Additionally, be mindful of verb tense consistency and the correct use of articles ("an," "the").

3. **Clarity of Point of View:** Your point of view is evident throughout the essay, but it can be made clearer with more precise language and a stronger thesis statement in the introduction. Formulating a concise thesis that directly responds to the essay question can guide your readers through your arguments more effectively.

4. **Arguments and Support:** The essay presents arguments for both sides of the discussion, which strengthens your position. However, ensure that each paragraph focuses on a single idea or argument to avoid confusing your readers. Providing clear, specific examples to support your points is excellent, but each example should be thoroughly explained and directly linked to your central argument to maximize its impact.

**Recommendations for Improvement:**

- In the introduction, briefly summarize your stance without including examples or detailed reasoning. This will help set a clear direction for your essay.
- Aim for simpler sentence structures to enhance the clarity of your arguments. One idea per sentence is a good rule of thumb.
- Ensure that each body paragraph focuses on one main idea. This structure allows for a deeper and more organized exploration of your arguments.
- In the conclusion, strive to summarize the key points discussed rather than introducing new reasoning. The conclusion should reflect on what has been said and reaffirm your stance in a concise manner.
- Pay attention to grammatical details and stylistic choices to enhance the overall flow and coherence of your essay.

By focusing on these areas, you can make your essay more structured, clear, and persuasive. Remember, practice and attentive revision are key to improving your writing skills.

prompt: Television has had a significant influence on the culture of many societies. Do you agree?
essay:
In the era of advanced technology, television is more and more ubiquitous and is owned by most families all over the world. Thus, it is believed that apart from being an important source of valuable information and news, television has considerably contributed to the changes and formation of a variety of cultures. Personally, I suppose that television has both positive and negative impacts on cultural development. 
 On the one hand, it can not be denied that television plays a significant role in maintaining and developing cultural values in many societies. Firstly, by launching documentary films, historical programs, and others related to cultural identities, television helps young generations access to their traditional values in their nations. For instance, people will pay respects to their ancients and brave heroes who sacrificed for peace when they watch historical films which mention wars in the past. In addition, daily news channels which talk about good examples of kindness and honesty everywhere also contribute to educating people about moral lessons which our ancients had taught. Gradually, such lessons play a key role in creating a developed society with talented and gentle citizens. 
 On the other hand, there are some detrimental aspects of television that should not be ignored. First of all, the fact that people can access to various cultures in the world thanks to television results in the problem that they will follow such cultures and forget their original ones which are heritages of each nation. For example, with the dominance of Hollywood films around the globe, some Eastern countries are facing the risk of losing their national identities. Indeed, in Vietnam, most young people pursue the western lifestyle and even forget traditional principles which are transmitted through thousands of years. Secondly, although most programs published on TV are controlled strictly, there are still some illegal channels that publish improper information or some films having too much sexual and violent content. Such programs have a considerably negative impact on the moral development of viewers, especially children who are likely to imitate what they saw. Moreover, some films which exaggerate the story unintentionally make people misunderstand about images of certain countries. For example, people may think Malaysia is dangerous with mafia and drugs through action films about this country. 
 In conclusion, everything has pros and cons and television is no exception. While it can contribute to the development of cultures, in some aspects, it may be harmful if the people do not know how to avoid its downsides.

prompt: What are the benefits of bilingualism or multilingualism?
essay:
Being monolingual in today's world may do little harm to a speaker; however, those mastering more than one language does have an edge over monolingual speakers. In order to adapt to the current setting in which globalization is happening so rapidly and explore miscellaneous cultural aspects expressed through languages, one should aim to venture beyond their mother tongue. 
 The first benefit of knowing many languages is relatively self-explanatory: that is being able to communicate with various corners of the world. This applies to not only leisure activities such as travelling but also to working and collaborating. In fact, being bilingual or multilingual is now a plus for promotion candidates or for job interviewees. Furthermore, access to materials is more open than ever when people can read in different languages. To better understand this point, simply think about fantastic foreign books and movies that are not subtitled yet . That is when we aspire to be fluent in those languages. 
 Second, languages reflect cultures, and each language is a different lens through which people look at life. In other words, the more languages people know, the richer and deeper their life experiences may get. Cultural aspects such as belief, values and perceptions are demonstrated explicitly in their respective languages. For example, in Chinese, while the word "xin" is commonly translated into the "heart", yet it also means the mind and emotions. That is to say, in Chinese culture, the heart as we know it is not only a physical one, it is also a mental representation of emotional world, the will and desires of a person and the wisdom. In other cultures, rarely does the "heart" mean this much if not influenced by the Chinese. A further implication of this is that those learning foreign languages might have access to a set of beliefs and concepts that do not exist or are obscure in their culture. Through this process, they may come to respect cultural diversity as well as appreciate the unique features of their culture. 
 To conclude, I truly believe that bilingualism or multilingualism eases people into the process of globalization and brings about a variety of cultural perspectives that one may not be acquainted with in their mother tongue. Therefore, much more emphasis should be placed on teaching foreign languages.

prompt: Is technology (television, computers, cell phones, tablet devices, MP3 players) beneficial for child

Although recognizing technological benefits in many aspects, there are a lot of disadvantages that can influence holistic and safe growth for those under 5 years old. 
 Firstly, screen time too much can make those under 5 years old become passive and timid. Under 5 years old is the age that kids should explore and be active outside your house. Spending too much time exploring technology can make those kids reduce their interest in outside activities, which may create barriers to connecting with everyone. The screen can create barriers also means that kids become timid when encountering anything in the outside world. 
 Secondly, using technology without parental guidance can make children encounter harmful content. With the expanding popularity of information technology, those under 5 years old can click on harmful content so easily. Sometimes, lack of parental carefulness is the reason kids are exposed to age-inappropriate content. Today's technology is too convenient, and kids easily approach trash and dangerous information.

Entertainment beneficial in technology can make children reduce time to activate and connect to others. Technology can disrupt a child's sleep at night. 
 Some argue that the positive impacts of technology, such as entertainment, connecting with friends, and studying, can make children improve their independent ability and thinking when they are exposed to new knowledge through technology. Nevertheless, the downside of technology is crucial to interest in. It may lead to biased thinking in under 5-year-old kids, influence the way children shape their self-perception, reduce outside connection, and raise concerns about information safety.

In summary, aim to directly answer the prompt with a focused and concise essay, support your arguments with specific evidence, and pay close attention to grammar and style. Practicing these aspects will help improve your essay writing skills for the test and beyond.

prompt: IELTS 2; Men and women can work in any professions. Gender equality at work

 Men and women can work in any professional work. They should have a similar chance to get a job. If they have enough competency, workplaces should not consider them based on gender. Nevertheless, workplaces should think about based on their experience, educational background, and other capabilities that they have. 
 Some professional requires a certain skill in women and men such as physical strength. However, women and men can educate themself to fulfill their competence for a requirement in workplaces. For instance, if men want to be able to work in a beauty salon, they should learn about the makeup field. Besides, if women want to be police, they should train themself to have a physical appearance suitable for police demands. 
 Furthermore, equal gender in workplaces has some benefits. For example, workplaces will have a variety that can make a better atmosphere. As a consequence, there is an influence on workers and can increase productivity and motivation for work. Moreover, they will be increased profit in companies. 
 In conclusion, both men and women have the same opportunity to apply for a job. They should be judged by their competency in the job applied by them. On the other hand, they can train themself to fulfill company needs. The equality of gender in the workplace will give advantages for workers and influence profits in companies.
feedback:

However, ensure that your introduction accurately paraphrases the essay question. For instance, instead of saying "both women and men should have the freedom to apply for the job that they want," you could refine this to more closely match the task by stating, "I believe that gender-specific issues should not prevent individuals from seeking employment in any occupation." Each body paragraph should ideally include:

4. **Clarity and Description in Arguments**: You've presented some arguments and examples, such as differing job requirements for men and women, which is great. 5. **Conclusion**: Your conclusion effectively reiterates your main point. To further improve, make sure it thoroughly summarizes your arguments made in the body paragraphs without introducing new information. It's your chance to reinforce your stance and leave a lasting impression on the reader.

By focusing on a clear structure, ensuring each paragraph is cohesive and contains a full argument, and refining your grammar and style, your essay will become more compelling and persuasive. Remember, practice and revision are key to improving your writing skills.

prompt: Resources should be spent more on animals or human population ?

prompt: IELTS Essay: Influence of parents to boys and girls
essay:
People often contend that boys are under the greatest influence of their father while the mother has the most significant impacts on their girls. In my opinion, I strongly agree with this idea. 
 Right after being aware of their gender, children were attracted by parental actions, in which the same-sex influence was of the much more popularity. Day by day, they noticed the way their parents communicate to each other, react to life situations, handle with their work, play with them, and they mimic everything from their parents to gradually form their personality. 
 Most boys think that they were born to be brave, strong, powerful, who do the big things and will become breadwinners like their father. They idolize their father and see them as the strongest model, especially during their childhood. Trying to imitate their father's actions give them the feeling of becoming a real man. Boys are the most loyal followers of their father in both playing sport and cheering sports matches. They show their interest in sports since the early ages and consider physical activities needing much strength not a topic for girls. Another example that worth discussing relates to colors. By looking at their parent's daily clothes, they can jump to the conclusion about the color distinction between girls and boys that the colors used by their father are also for men and colors like pink, red will be definitely out of their color board. 
 By contrast, maternal influence is shown the most clearly in the girls' personality. Little girls admire their mother not only by their sacrifice, diligence, tolerance, and faithfulness but also by their wealth of knowledge. From the girls' eyes, the greatest teacher, the best chef, the most interesting storyteller, the smartest financial manager and the most reliable friend is the same person- their mother. The significant mother-daughter relationship affects the behavior as well as emulation of girls.  To conclude, although gen decides mostly the difference between the two sexes as well as the similarity in terms of personality between the same-sex members in a family, children are still affected by both their parents and use parents as a place of emotional repairs.
