 In many parts of the world, youth are encouraged that if they do their best, they can be successful and gain anything as expected. Although it has some benefits to give children this message, there are also many drawbacks. 
 On the one hand, it is clear that telling children that they can achieve anything if they are industrious would bring about several advantages. One evident strength is that it would give children motivation to do their best. In other words, it brings them the reason to be more industrious thus to make every effort in their study and reach their goals. Another reason is that it would help children raise their awareness about planning for their success. It means they should envisage steps to prepare for the future. For example, it is vital to schedule learning time and practice a lot if a student wants to have flying colors in their exam. 
 On the other hand, there are some obvious disadvantages that would arise if the children believe in what the adults say about making an effort to succeed. First, the children can be negatively obsessed about failure. It means that they might be disappointed because of their failure and it makes them depressed. Doing a test would be a good example, if the exam result doesn't meet their expectation, it can dampen children's enthusiasm in learning. It causes children to not want to try hard anymore in their studies. Secondly, young people may not develop their cognitive skills. It means they will ignore such skills like critical thinking, problem solving and they lack creativity in finding a good method to study and work effectively. Learning English is another good example for this, young people may keep learning a list of every English vocabulary multiple times with the hope they will remember those words well, while they can find other better ways such as using flashcards or making sentences to comprehend those words. 
 In conclusion, there are many positive things about telling children that they can achieve anything if they are industrious regarding giving them motivation and helping them to plan for things. However, it could be negative in terms of disappointment and stress and the lack of non-linear thinking of young people in study and work.

In terms of suggestions for improvement, exploring and integrating more varied sentence structures and transitions between paragraphs could elevate the essay's overall flow and readability. prompt: Essay topic: Making films and the advancement of digital technology

 On the one hand, I believe that when videos are produced by an unprofessional filmmaker, several problems can be anticipated. Initially, viewers such as youngsters or children may be exposed to inappropriate videos in terms of violence or offense, leading to many detrimental effects on them. This is due to the fact that while companies specializing in this industry have to testify to the quality of films before publishing in the society, films produced by individuals may not have to undergo censorship. Furthermore, there are numerous websites, apps, and technical devices that enable people to create their videos, triggering copyright infringement. If independent filmmakers do not obey the regulations and they imitate others' ideas, they may be sued for this fault that results in compromising their profits as well as their reputation.

Nevertheless, nowadays people are able to make a video with their own mobile phone or computer, which demonstrates the fact that it is a favorable environment for talented people to develop and have more opportunities for designing and writing their own stories. In addition, making films freely could expand the variety of genres or topics, which assist the public to enhance their knowledge and broaden their horizons about new aspects. While big organizations concentrate more on the prominent types of films that appeal to a huge number of audiences, people working freely could share their daily activities, or their own stories to encourage other people.

prompt: IELTS writing task 2 - Living in a country where you have to speak a foreign language

Some people argue that speaking a language other than a person's mother tongue may lead to some worth-considering social problems as well as practical problems. I totally agree with this statement. 
 One of the biggest difficulties of immigrants living overseas is language barriers. He may find himself helpless and un able to deal with daily simple activities such as talking with neighbors, going shopping, contacting banks and local governments. A vast majority of immigrants cannot apply for high-paid decent jobs since most of these jobs requires language competence. Also, illiteracy and language misunderstanding may lead to mental health problems such as stress and depression. Therefore, language plays a crucial part in enabling a person to integrate into a new environment. 
 In conclusion, to adapt to new environment well, immigrants should be able to communicate well in the language spoken in their localities. Lack of foreign language ability may cause multiple troubles to any person living in a foreign country. Therefore, before deciding to relocate in a foreign country, people should learn the language beforehand.

prompt: [IELTS Writing Task 2] Discussion about online courses
essay:
Pros and cons of studying an online course 
 Task: 
 In the last decade, there has been a great increase in the number and variety of online courses available to adults. This has been welcomed as a great opportunity by many students, however, other students see these courses as less effective than classroom teaching. What are the advantages and disadvantages of studying an online course? 
 The recent decade has witnessed a significant increase in the quantity and variety of courses on the Internet for adults, which are argued to be beneficial for some reasons. Nevertheless, other people claim that these courses are not able to replace the study in classroom. This essay will discuss some benefits and possible risks of this teaching method. 
 On the one hand, online courses have several positive effects. One key benefit is its flexibility, which means that online classes allow learners to choose their favorite study time and place. This is extremely necessary for those who cannot go to classes due to far distance or their working schedule. Besides, studying on the Internet helps reduce the course fees as the location and facilities rental is saved. Taking moon.vn (a website organizing online courses for Vietnamese high school students) as an example, each month they save 40% more than average budget of other offline teaching centers, meaning that they have more to spend on enhancing their curriculum's quality. 
 On the other hand, there are also some negative impacts which must be considered. One important issue is that there are currently hundreds of online courses, which are not easy for the government to verify their quality. Unreliable sources could be dangerous as they provide unprecise and subjective information. Furthermore, compared with traditional classes, there is less interaction between students and teachers and their peers. This makes it more difficult for learners to fully understand the lesson because they receive only little support from others. For instance, with lessons which are previously recorded and played back later on, learners cannot give questions straightly to teachers and the discussion with other students need hours or days to be responded. 
 In conclusion, while online courses can benefit the study of learners thanks to their flexibility and savings, they also have some obstacles compared with traditional classes.
feedback:
The essay effectively addresses the topic by examining both the advantages and disadvantages of online courses, presenting a balanced view. However, there's an opportunity to more accurately frame the debate in terms of advantages and disadvantages rather than benefits and risks—as the latter implies potential for harm, which deviates from the essence of the prompt focusing on positives and negatives of the education method.

In terms of spelling and grammar, the essay demonstrates a good command of the English language but can benefit from minor improvements for clearer expression. There are instances where the use of synonyms and a broader vocabulary can enhance the argument and avoid repetition of terms directly from the task description. For example, instead of repeating "great increase in the number and variety of online courses," consider saying "Over the past 10 years, adults have witnessed a significant expansion in the diversity of virtual classes available."

The essay's point of view is clear, advocating for a comprehensive examination of both sides of online education. However, greater effort to use a wider range of vocabulary and avoid repeating words from the prompt could strengthen the author's command of English and the overall argument.

Arguments on both sides of the online education debate are adequately supported by examples and logical reasoning. The flexibility and cost-effectiveness of online courses are well articulated, as are concerns about quality control and reduced interaction. Yet, it could be beneficial to delve deeper into each point. For instance, elaborating on how online platforms can enhance their curriculums with the savings from not having physical classrooms might provide a stronger support for the advantage of cost-effectiveness. Similarly, exploring how the lack of immediate interaction in online courses could affect different types of learners could offer a more nuanced view of its disadvantages.

To make the essay more compelling, consider including a brief introduction to the contrasting views prior to delving into the specifics of each side's arguments. This could offer a smoother transition into the discussion and show an understanding that the topic is multifaceted.

In conclusion, by refining the expression of the argument to enhance clarity and precision, expanding the vocabulary to avoid repetition, and deepening the exploration of each point made, the essay can achieve greater effectiveness. This will not only demonstrate a better grasp of the English language but also present a more convincing and rounded argument on the advantages and disadvantages of studying an online course.

prompt: IELTS Opinion Essay Writing Task: "Prevention is better than cure".
essay:
In the current climate where our health is seemingly on the line, both preventive measures and finding possible cures are equally important. I agree to a certain extent that preventive measures are important and should be enforced to everyone to minimize the possibility of getting sick, however, I also believe that investing in finding the proper cure is just as important. 
 Proper preventive measures also stem from extensive research through understanding how the diseases and viruses work and whether they will regenerate into something worse in the future. With the COVID-19 pandemic on the rise, vaccines are one of the best preventive measures for it, but in developing those vaccines, a lot of resources were needed; perhaps, as much resources it would need to find a cure. 
 From my friends and family's experiences, terminal diseases such as cancer are difficult to detect and prevent. Some of my cancer-ridden friends and family don't even know they had it until the symptoms were felt. It is difficult to prevent something you didn't know you had, especially when diseases like cancer don't really care whether you exercise every day or drink alcohol every night. Because of this, it is just as important to invest in finding cures for diseases, especially when they are undetectable by the naked eye.

prompt: Studying with a group of students in a classroom is more beneficial than learning online at home.

 Despite the lack of face-to-face communication, studying online still has various benefits. Firstly, parents can save money as they can cut down on school bus service fees or reduce the amount of used gasoline if they carry their children to school by personal vehicles. Secondly, children can avoid traffic jams which is a time-consuming and harmful problem. For instance, particularly in Vietnam, heavy traffic and carbon footprints from all sources of vehicles are associated with each other which consequently have negative impacts on children's health. Finally, due to the reduction of face-to-face communication, children can minimize the ability to contract infectious diseases through close contact.

Secondly, learning a new language at an early age help to prepare a better life for the child when they grow up. This can make the child have a fear for learning, or maybe it can deprive the peaceful childhood of the child. In addition, learning the language when too young can also cause many language disorders. Teaching language for a child is not an easy-going job, it requires many experiences and techniques, thus the wrong educational method can result in many troubles that affect negatively the child.

prompt: Two main tendencies in choosing subjects among different gender students

Arts subjects, on the other hand, are deemed as a means to emphasize emotions, which is believed to be more suitable for women. This has led to a situation where course selection becomes an identity resource, resulting in students choosing a certain subject to not only build up their self-image but also establish their gender credibility with their peers. 
 There are compelling reasons to change this situation. To begin with, having to conform to those gender stereotypes would prevent students from reaching their full potential. To be more specific, they would not be able to learn subjects which they are really good at just because those courses are dominated by people of the opposite gender, and having to study a subject for which they have neither talent nor passion would be wasteful.

prompt: Article: Causes of teen depression

The great frustrations and beliefs about academic ability can lead to depression in teenagers. The Paper cites statistics from The Economist, which show that China's teen suicide rate ranks first in the world, of which the cause due to school pressure accounts for 26%.

Many of my classmates from school were live examples, because they could not bare the financial expenses of post-graduate education and remained without a job because they were not prepared for it. 
 Additionally, even if someone enrolls in a university, that person must still work in order to keep up with the university's financial expenses. This is because unlike school, where education is free and the expenses that do come up are paid by the either the student's guardian or parent, universities have greater costs and students are expected to pay for It themselves. For instance, I had to take up a part time job to make sure that I was able to get all the required textbooks and other required material in time. Thus, the more you are ready to take jobs, the easier your life will be without concern for your educational choices. 
 In conclusion, I believe schools should teach skills needed for jobs rather than preparing students only for universities. This is mainly because many students are unable to pursue higher education after school and even if they do, being job ready will certainly prove fruitful.
feedback:
Your essay addresses the topic well by arguing that schools should focus more on preparing students for jobs rather than post-graduate studies. You clearly state your opinion, which is a strong point of your essay. However, there are areas where you can make your essay even stronger and more effective.

1. **Response to the Topic**: You have effectively responded to the topic by stating your agreement with the idea that schools should prepare pupils for jobs. Your introduction and conclusion echo this perspective, which provides a clear structure to your essay. However, your introduction could be more concise. Aim to restate the prompt and your opinion in a couple of sentences to make your point clear from the beginning. This will help grab the reader's attention and make your stance unmistakable.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, or Stylistic Issues**: Overall, your essay is readable, but there are minor grammatical errors and stylistic choices that can be improved. For instance, the phrase "many of my classmates from school were live examples, because they could not bare the financial expenses" could be corrected to "...were live examples because they could not bear the financial expenses." Paying attention to small details like this will strengthen the professionalism of your writing. Additionally, consider varying your sentence structure to keep the reader engaged.

3. **Point of View Clarity**: Your point of view is clear throughout the essay, which is excellent. You consistently support the idea that education should be more job-oriented. To further improve, ensure that each paragraph starts with a strong topic sentence that directly supports your viewpoint. This makes it easier for readers to follow your argumentation.

4. **Arguments and Descriptions**: Your arguments are relevant and support your perspective well, especially when you discuss practical examples such as your own experience and those of your classmates. To strengthen your essay, consider adding more specific examples or statistics to back up your claims. This will make your arguments even more convincing. Also, be mindful of overgeneralization; terms like "everyone" or "everywhere in the world" could be replaced with more precise language to avoid making assumptions.

Finally, remember that writing is a process of continuous improvement. Reviewing grammar and practicing concise writing can significantly enhance your essays. Keep focusing on clearly supporting your arguments with specific examples, and your writing will continue to improve.

prompt: To the beach or to the mountains on vacation time? Writing Task 2

Generallly, I agree that both of them have some beneficial itself. For example, hiking to mountain have relaxing effect for individual and going to the beach give the best alternative to having fun with friends. 
 It is important for people to consider about the leisure time with hiking to the mountain, because looking the mountain would give positive effect to relaxing mind and refreshing the eyes. By enjoying the best creature in this world, it can be result to increasing the positive energy that so powerful. It is clear that spending holiday in the mountain is the best consideration. 
 It is important to someone who wants spending time with closest friends to going the beach, because in the beach we can doing fun activities with friends. feedback:

However, without the original essay prompt, it's challenging to assess its full relevance. For future essays, always include the essay prompt to ensure your response is on target.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, and Style Issues**:

Additionally, always remember to proofread your work for grammatical accuracy. With practice and attention to these details, your writing will undoubtedly improve.

prompt: Day-by-day people's lives are becoming increasingly stressful. What is the reason and how to solve
essay:
Nowadays, people have become wealthier than before. However, people also confront the high-speed lifestyle at the same time, which is an extreme stressful lifestyle. In this essay I will discuss some of the causes of this stress and how it could be alleviated. 
 In this generation, people work hard for a high quality lifestyle; however, some of whom turn out to be a workaholic to be able to cope with their occupations, which has become social issue. Take Taiwan for instance, after economic depression, around 10 years ago, many people were unemployed, so they needed to fight for their positions in case of losing the job they just had. They accepted an excessive workload without any complaints. However, a few years later, there were many incidents about overloaded employee's deaths, and people were starting to consider about their rights and thinking about the lifestyles they had. Now, in these few years, high-tech replacements are also changing people workstyle, and the work environment has become much more competitive. People should find the balance between their jobs and lives; because the job environment has been changing and will be continuing. 
 In order to achieve their life ambitions and being competent workers, people work under stress. I believe that they need to take time slowly sometimes to think about the future life they want and learn more about loving. People only focus on jobs, and ignore family and friends, and even become selfish who only have money without people's accompany. I think that although they look rich, they are poor in mind. Learning to share and care about people and society will be a good start. 
 In conclusion, nowadays, people are making an effort at being accepted workers to be hired and to acquire their goals in thier occupations. However, as time goes fast, people should take break as a demand for their healthy and balanced lifestyles. If it is ignored, people might be regret it after they have lost. it.
feedback:
Your essay provides a thoughtful discussion on the causes and potential solutions to the stress caused by modern work demands. However, there are several areas for improvement to enhance the clarity, accuracy, and overall effectiveness of your essay.

However, the introduction does not accurately paraphrase the prompt. To improve, the introductory statement should more closely reflect the prompt, focusing on the everyday stress people experience and indicating that the essay will examine causes and propose solutions. A better introduction might start with: "In today's fast-paced world, many people experience significant stress, influenced by various factors. For instance, explicitly stating, "I argue that achieving a work-life balance is essential for mental and physical health," at the outset can set a clear perspective for the reader.

4. **Arguments and Support:** Your essay presents relevant examples and rationales, such as the case of Taiwan and the trend towards workaholism. However, these could be further developed with more specific details and a direct explanation of how they support your main point. To enhance your essay:

- Conduct thorough proofreading to eliminate spelling and grammatical errors.
- Use clear and straightforward language, avoiding complex or convoluted sentences that may confuse readers.
- Enhance your arguments with more detailed examples and clearer explanations of how they support your viewpoint.

By addressing these points, your essay will become more coherent, engaging, and effective in conveying your message. Remember, clarity and precision in writing not only reflect mastery of the language but also the depth of your understanding of the topic.

prompt: Heated debate as to whether increasing the price of petrol can address environmental problems
essay:
It has been a subject of lively heated debate as to whether increasing the price of petrol can address environmental problems. While I acknowledge that this measure can be favorable to some extent, I am of the opinion that there are other sustainable and effective solutions. 
 On the one hand, it is reasonable that raising the cost of fuel used to power cars and other vehicles is advantageous to some extent. One of the major benefits might be the improvement in the urban's air quality. In fact, imposing higher taxes on fuel will significantly discourage people from using their private vehicles for daily commute, which in turn forces the government to upgrade and expand public transport provisions to fulfill the city dwellers' traveling demand. As a consequence, the amount of CO2 emission released from private automobiles will considerably reduce, resulting in the alleviation of air pollution. 
 On the other hand, the national authorities should adopt transport policies which would be more effective in a long run. The first policy would be for car manufactures to design more environmentally-friendly cars. Instead of fueling cars using traditional and limited natural sources, car production companies should invest in renewable and infinite energy sources such as solar power or hydrogen, which proportionally spares future generations the pending energy crisis. Another policy would be to raise the public's ecological consciousness. Indeed, one of government's unavoidable obligations is to instill the urgent need of protecting our environment into the psyche of each and every member of our planet. As a result, people would be fully aware of the gravity of the situation and willing to take immediate actions to prevent further environmental degradation. 
 In conclusion, although raising the price of petrol may be advantageous to a certain degree, I espouse the notion that other solutions would be more efficacious due to the aforementioned reasons.
feedback:
Your essay provides an interesting perspective on whether increasing the price of petrol can help solve environmental problems. You've done well in structuring your essay, presenting your opinion, and arguing for alternative solutions. However, there are key areas where the essay could be enhanced to meet the requirements of the task more effectively. Here is some specific feedback to help you improve:

1. **Relevance to the Topic**: It appears that your initial approach is to balance the advantages of raising petrol prices with the argument for other solutions. However, the prompt demands a focus on presenting clear, alternative solutions rather than comparing extents of effectiveness. It would be beneficial to directly state the environmental issue you're addressing and explicitly argue for your alternative solutions right from the introduction.

2. **Clarity and Cohesiveness**: Your essay somewhat divides the discussion between acknowledging a partial benefit of increased petrol prices and arguing for alternate solutions. This creates a comparative format, which isn't ideal for the task. To enhance clarity and cohesiveness, dedicate your body paragraphs to fully explaining and supporting the alternative measures you propose. Make sure each paragraph focuses on one main idea and provides detailed support for that idea.

3. **Language and Style**: Your use of language is generally good, but the essay would benefit from simpler and more direct expressions in places. For example, instead of starting with "It has been a subject of lively heated debate," you could simply say, "Many people discuss whether increasing the price of petrol can address environmental problems." This makes your writing more accessible, especially for English language learners. 

4. **Spelling and Grammar**: There are no significant errors in spelling or grammar, which is great. However, pay attention to the use of terms and phrases to ensure they accurately represent your arguments. For instance, discussing the "advantageous to some extent" could be simplified to "has some advantages" to maintain focus on your viewpoint.

5. **Arguments and Support**: You've identified key areas such as improving vehicle design and raising ecological consciousness. These are strong points. To further strengthen your essay, ensure you dive deeper into these solutions, explaining how exactly they address the problem and why they are preferable to increased petrol prices. Providing specific examples or data can also enhance your argument.

In conclusion, your essay presents valuable ideas on addressing environmental issues beyond just increasing the price of petrol. Focusing on directly stating and supporting your proposed solutions, simplifying your language, and ensuring a cohesive argument will all contribute to a stronger, clearer essay. Keep up the good work, and continue to refine your approach to writing on complex topics.

prompt: IELTS WRITING TASK 2_SELF-DRIVING SYSTEMS FOR VEHICLES
essay:
As the advent of modern technology, there has been a common belief that automakers of smart cars may cause some adverse issues to the society and pose a threat to the old generation for not updating these new high-tech equipment. However, from a personal perspective, I do believe that auto system obviously brings more merits than the bad ones. 
 There are many compelling reasons why peoples consider automobile manufacturers as a complex system. On the individual level, the old seems it is hard for them to learn how to use these transportations and apparently transforming into this new trend must cost an arm and a leg on a wide scale. In addition, technological advances in self-driving automobiles can reduce the security of their owner's privacy. For instance, to keep track of users destinations, auto system can hold a host of informations which can be served as detrimental purposes if there are any hackers want to use it. 
 Nevertheless, automobile vehicles will help us reduce remarkably accidents and become one of the most convenient devices according to its self-driving program. The system based on algorithms designed to overcome human errors by working orderly. In fact, a recent survey has shown that about 60 percent of automobile accidents can be prevented by using self-driving systems. This is because they can monitor the paths more carefully, keep a safe distance from other vehicles. Extrinsically, they do not depend on personal emotions and work efficiently without human's cognitive. This can lead to a decrease in human error and accident rate so everyone can drive safely and minimize negative consequences. 
 To sum up, although community still has some controversial prejudices about applying self-driving system for their transportations, it is evident that using this process will properly increase the life standard of citizens and create a number of advantages.
feedback:
The essay provides a general view on the subject of modern technology and smart cars but misses addressing the specific topic of safety considerations entailed in the use of automated cars. Instead, the essay shifts focus towards a broad comparison of old and new technologies and their societal implications, rather than honing in on the safety aspects of driverless cars, such as potential on-board computer failures, the risk of technology hijacking, and the impact on driver attention – all crucial points that directly relate to the safety theme.

2. "Peoples" should be "people" as the former is not the correct term in this context.
3. The sentence structure and clarity can be improved by breaking up long sentences and ensuring that ideas flow logically from one to another. 
4. Pay attention to the singular and plural forms, such as "informations" which should be "information", to maintain accuracy.
5. Consider using more specific and varied vocabulary to convey your points more vividly.

The point of view is clear; you support the idea that automated cars bring more benefits than drawbacks. However, you could further strengthen your argument by offering more detailed examples and exploring the specific safety-related issues mentioned in the feedback, which were not adequately covered.

While your second paragraph does a good job of outlining the benefits of self-driving cars, such as reduced accident rates and improved efficiency, incorporating safety considerations into your argumentation would bring a more balanced and focused perspective in line with the essay prompt. This includes discussing not only the positive outcomes but also critically analyzing potential challenges and how they can be addressed.

The conclusion of the essay needs to articulate your arguments more clearly. It's advised to use up to five sentences to summarize your points effectively. This will help in giving your readers a better understanding of your position and the reasons behind it.

Overall, while the essay has strengths, such as a clear perspective and good reasoning regarding the benefits of automated cars, there are significant areas for improvement. These include addressing the specific topic as outlined in the prompt, rectifying spelling and grammar issues, and providing a more structured and detailed argumentation, especially concerning safety considerations. By refining these aspects, the essay will deliver a more compelling and rounded discussion on the subject.

prompt: Fossil fuel and renewable resources - IELTS task 2 essay
essay:
People have different views about whether it is better to utilize fossil fuels' energy for human consumption or renewable resources such as wind, solar or water. While there are some detrimental impacts in the use of wind or solar power, I would argue that using finite sources instead of fossil fuels brings more benefits to human lives 
 On the one hand, the use of solar or wind energy is more likely to have various cons to some extent. Firstly, visible strong energy like sunlight or a lake may have some extra effects which might severely influence the human race. Since those energies start from the prime resources of the universe, it is more inclined to form some alternate negative substances to our health, or even more, it will overwhelm our electrical devices. For instance, some houses in some countries were on fire due to the overwhelming technologies run by solar panels. Secondly, it is not relatively affordable for some developed or poor countries to own the number of technical machines to transfer the power into useful sources for our human consumption. As a result, they hardly catch up with developing and affluent countries and be obsolete. 
 On the other hand, I would claim that it is highly dominant to use more energy from the Sun or tidewater. Firstly, reducing the amount of oil, gas, and coal and encouragingly using the power from solar or tide energy might cut down on the running-out of those non-renewable resources. According to statistics, the recent UK's environment record is getting decreased due to policies for operating solar energy for human necessity. Furthermore, wind and solar power are more likely to be the most powerful infinite resources to keep providing energy for the necessity of human lives. If we do not take the action for that issue, the fossil resources will be used up soon. 
 In conclusion, while using renewable resources such as solar or wind energy is not a preferred option to some countries, I would believe that it would be the best method to save up the reserves from fossil fuels.
feedback:
The essay attempts to tackle the issue of whether it's better to use fossil fuels or renewable resources for energy. It presents arguments for both sides but ultimately advocates for renewable energy sources. Here are some points for improvement:

1. **Understanding and Response to the Topic**: The essay mistakenly focuses on the "benefits to human lives" rather than directly addressing if using renewable energy over fossil fuels is a positive or negative development. This shifts the essay away from the specific question. To improve, ensure that the thesis statement directly answers the essay prompt. For instance, stating clearly whether the move towards renewable resources is positive or negative would align better with the question's requirements.

2. **Essay Structure**: The structure includes arguments for both perspectives, which could be confusing since the prompt seems to ask for a defense of one perspective. It's essential to choose a clear stance and support it throughout the essay to avoid any ambiguity. This approach would also ensure the essay is coherent and focused, making it easier for readers to follow the author's line of reasoning.

3. **Spelling, Grammar, and Stylistic Issues**: There are several grammatical errors and awkward phrasings that hinder clarity. For example, phrases like "visible strong energy like sunlight or a lake" can be confusing and could be simplified for clarity. Pay attention to sentence structure and word choice to improve readability. Using tools or consulting guides on grammar and style could be beneficial.

4. **Clarity of Author’s Point of View**: While the essay attempts to present a clear stance in favor of renewable energy, the initial discussion on the disadvantages of renewable resources may dilute the author's point of view. To clarify, it would help to start with a strong thesis statement outlining the essay's argument and consistently support that argument in each paragraph.

5. **Arguments and Descriptions**: The arguments could be more compelling and evidence-based. For instance, the negative impacts of renewable energy technology on human health and devices are mentioned without solid evidence. Strengthen the essay by providing specific examples, statistics, or studies to support claims. Additionally, addressing how the transition to renewable energy can be managed in less developed countries would strengthen the argument.

6. **Conclusion**: The conclusion reiterates the stance but could be more persuasive by summarizing key arguments supporting renewable resources over fossil fuels. It’s a chance to reinforce the essay's main points and leave a lasting impression on the reader.

By addressing these points, the essay can become more focused, persuasive, and aligned with the task's requirements. Working on clarity, structure, and evidence will make the arguments more convincing and improve the overall quality of the writing.

prompt: Ielts task 2 : The title is magical inside, plz make it more magical
essay:
It is widely believed that tertiary education plays such an important role, for it breeds young talents and these students after courses gain more chances to work with high-paid salary. However, I believe not all students should participate in these training programs 
 At first, financial burden drives certain students away from furthering education. Students who are from poverty-stricken backgrounds face this problem, which induces them to rather opt for vocational programs and earn for a living with a less appealing income, compared to those gaining bright certificate and working for international corporations. Although certain universities provide financial aids but these can not live up to a large number of disadvantaged students. Therefore, these people are encouraged to rather become craftsmen or ordinary workers. I believe being responsible for any tasks regardless of any jobs is appreciative. 
 Moving to the second reason, there is no guarantee for every students who have attended the tertiary vocational programs secure a job after completing. For example, in certain industrialized countries such as America or Singapore, agricultural major students who even gain the brightest certificate may not find appealing working positions. This leaves those ones to be unemployed and be a burden for society. Another case in this point is that not all students attending after-university programs study what they dream of yet other people, especially parents drive them to do and that these students become unmotivated and under pressure trying their best to live up to parents' expectations. Vietnam is a good example of this point. Therefore, tertiary education should not be for everyone but for real promising students pursuing their true passion. 
 In conclusion, I reassure my points that the vocational training courses after graduation should not be for all students as they are either unaffordable or unsuitable for certain people.
feedback:
The essay presents an opinion on the importance and suitability of tertiary education for students, particularly touching upon the issues of financial burdens and job guarantees post-graduation. However, there are several areas where the essay could be improved to be more aligned with the expectations of an English proficiency test and to more effectively communicate the author's point of view. Here's a detailed feedback focusing on the aspects you've asked about:

1. **Response to the Topic**: The main issue with the essay is that it narrows down the broad subject of tertiary education to specifically discussing vocational training and its challenges. The prompt seems to ask for a discussion on tertiary education in general, including a variety of educational paths such as ongoing professional seminars, master's degrees, and Ph.D. studies. By focusing solely on vocational training and the issues surrounding it, the essay changes the original subject and does not fully respond to the general discussion intended by the topic. It's crucial to carefully read and stick to the prompt to ensure that the discussion remains relevant.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, and Stylistic Issues**: The essay demonstrates a strong command of language, but there are minor spelling and grammatical errors that need attention. For instance:
   - Use of "every students" should be corrected to "every student".
   - The phrase "Although certain universities provide financial aids but" is structurally awkward and could be simplified to "Although certain universities provide financial aid, this does not meet the needs of many disadvantaged students."
   - Consider refining the sentence structure and ensuring subject-verb agreement throughout the essay to enhance readability.
   
   Stylistically, the essay could benefit from varying sentence structures to make the argument more dynamic and engaging. Additionally, clearer transitions between paragraphs could help in reinforcing the logical flow of the essay.

3. **Clarity of Author's Point of View**: The essay clearly communicates the author's stance that tertiary education, particularly vocational training, may not be suitable for everyone due to financial constraints and a lack of guaranteed employment opportunities. However, by broadening the scope of your discussion to include a variety of post-secondary educational paths and explaining how these considerations apply to tertiary education as a whole, the position could be made more robust and comprehensive.

4. **Arguments and Support**: The essay provides specific examples and reasons to support the argument, such as financial burden and the lack of job guarantees. These examples are relevant, but the essay would benefit from a broader range of evidence and a more in-depth discussion of how these issues affect students' decisions on tertiary education in general, not just vocational training. Incorporating statistics, research findings, or more diverse examples could strengthen the essay's arguments.

To enhance the essay, focus on directly addressing the prompt, correcting language errors, broadening the scope of discussion beyond vocational training, and providing a wider array of evidence to support your claims. By making these adjustments, the essay can more effectively communicate a nuanced and comprehensive argument that reflects the complexity of decisions surrounding tertiary education.

prompt: IELTS Task 2- Government should pay one of the parents of very young children to stay at home
essay:
The topic of whether the government should give financial support to one of the parents of a very little children to take care of their children at home has stirred up much controversy. This essay will illustrate the benefits and drawback of this policy by using relevant examples. 
 To start with, funding can increase the willingness of parents to stay home, and thus improve the relationship between parent and children. On one side, by spending more time together, parents get to know more about their children. On the other side, the child likes their parents more since they always spend time together. A striking illustration will be me. I have a good relationship with my parents as my childhood memories are full of them. In view of this, this policy definitely benefits the bonding of a family. 
 Furthermore, parents from poor families can get the chance to stay at home for their kid. Adults in lower class families spend most of their time working, since they want to try their best to earn more money for the families. Workers in developing countries, for instance, have the longest working hours among the world. Their beloved children are then being left alone at home as a result, which is dangerous as accidents may happen to them. Similar problems can be solved by this policy, because poor families will get paid and they do not have to worry about their income. 
 However, this policy may lead to misunderstandings among parents on the responsible of taking care of children. They may receive an incorrect message that they are staying at home just for the money given by the government. It is sad that they do not get the real aim of this policy, which is to encourage parent staying at home for their child. 
 What must also be taken into consideration is that some people may take advantages of this policy. Some parents who has no urgent need of money may take this policy as a way to generate income. Money of the government, which is full of potential to be used in other useful purposes, such as medical and education, will be wasted in such case. Judging from this, this policy will waste resources and has no good to the society. 
 In my opinion, everything has two sides. This policy can benefit lots of new families, especially those in financial needs. It is hoped that the government can set strict regulations on the enforcement of this policy to benefit the people.
feedback:
Your essay addresses the topic of government financial support for parents of young children, presenting both benefits and drawbacks. The structure you've chosen facilitates a balanced discussion, which is a strength. However, let's work on refining your essay to ensure clarity and effectiveness.

1. **Adherence to Topic:** You've done well to stay on topic, though the introduction could more directly paraphrase the prompt. Remember, clarity begins with your first sentence, so ensure your initial statement closely aligns with the essay question without suggesting a debate or controversy if it's positioned as a straightforward discussion.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, and Style:** Overall, your essay is understandable, but there are several areas that could benefit from attention. 
    - Be mindful of verb tenses and subject-verb agreement. For example, "Some parents who has no urgent need..." should be "Some parents who have no urgent need..."
    - Watch out for pluralization; "benefits and drawback" should be "benefits and drawbacks."
    - Pay attention to the consistent use of singular and plural nouns, especially when referring to collective subjects like families or parents.
    - To improve readability, consider shorter sentences and more varied sentence structures.
    - It's important to check for typographical errors (like "concider" instead of "consider") and use more specific language where possible to make your arguments clearer.

3. **Clarity of Point of View:** Your viewpoint emerges clearly in the conclusion, indicating a balanced perspective on government policy. To strengthen this earlier in the essay, ensure each paragraph has a topic sentence that signals the key argument you’ll discuss.

4. **Arguments and Examples:** Your examples are relevant, showing the potential impacts of the policy on family bonds and economic situations. However, make your examples more descriptive to vividly illustrate your points. Instead of general references like "Workers in developing countries," specify which countries or sectors you mean to provide more concrete evidence.

Additionally, managing your time effectively can greatly improve your written work. Practicing with a timer can help you allocate sufficient time for planning, writing, and revising. Aim to leave the last 5-10 minutes for proofreading to catch and correct any errors in spelling, grammar, or punctuation. This approach will also assist in developing your ideas more concisely, ensuring you stay within the recommended word count and complete your essay confidently within the given timeframe.

Keep these pointers in mind as you continue to practice. Each revision provides an opportunity to enhance your clarity, coherence, and control over language, moving you closer to achieving your desired score.

prompt: CBEST writing - individual efforts to improve environment and preserve the planet
essay:
There's no doubt that protecting the planet and helping our environment is a major concern. Some people believe that even one person's contribution to preserving our planet is making a difference in the way we live our lives. Others believe that individual efforts to reduce pollution, fight global warming and avoid natural resources depletion are not going to change anything. I strongly agree that each of us can make a difference in saving our planet and environment. 
 There's no secret that when we buy certain kinds of products, manufacturers produce more of them. The same rule works when we are buying more environmentally friendly products. For instance, when we buy more electric cars, using which is helping to reduce carbon dioxide emission, the market will produce more of these cars to satisfy the buyers' needs. Another example is when people are buying chemical sunscreens that contain no elements damaging coral reefs, which are one of the most valuable ecosystems on Earth. A few years ago you barely could find this type of sunscreens, however today they are becoming more popular each year and you easily can find them in-store and online. 
 In addition to that, individual action is a part of the collective. prompt: In the past, people wore their traditional clothes and followed their culture.
essay:
It is common in modern society that people have tendency to choose similar outfits for their daily activities, rendering the disapperance of traditional clothes. Notwithstanding some positive aspects regarding to personal images, personally, I am more convinced that the drawbacks are by far serious and should not be overlooked. 
 On the one hand, it is undeniable that traditional outfits are often bulky and not comfortable outfits. For example, Ao Dai, which is a famous traditional clothes of Vietnam has a complicated designs, making them bulky and not suitable for activities, resulting in only being wore on special occasions. Another reason why people usually opt for modern clothes as their daily outfits is because they enhance people's confidence in social situations. In other words, more often than not people associate following the newest fashion trends with a sign of modernity, making people obsessed with appearing trendy in the eyes of others. 
 On the other hand, traditional outfits are more than types of clothing but representations of culture and identity, making them indispensible items. Wearing these outfits helps people to be in touch with their ancestral culture and symbolizes unity. As a result, let go of them will be like discarding their own culture. Moreover, if people wear similar outfits and become undifferentiated from others, they become confued about their identity and not have a deep connection with their roots. These implications could leave negative impacts on the preserve of national culture values. 
 In conclusion, although modern outfits bring convenience and confidence for people, the absence of traditional clothes leads to the loss of culture and identity. Therefore, I am an opinion that negative impacts of this trend outweight its positive ones.
feedback:
Your essay addresses an important topic about the impact of choosing modern outfits over traditional ones and its effect on culture and identity. Your efforts to discuss both sides of the argument are appreciated; however, there are areas for improvement to make your essay more persuasive and clear.

1. **Response to the Topic**: You have chosen an interesting and relevant topic. Your essay addresses the prompt by discussing the advantages and disadvantages of wearing modern outfits instead of traditional ones. However, your argument would be stronger if you focused more on supporting your main viewpoint without giving equal weight to the opposing perspective. Remember, the goal is to convincingly argue in favor of your position.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, and Stylistic Issues**: There are a few spelling and grammatical errors in your essay that need attention. For example, "disapperance" should be "disappearance," "clothes" when referring to a single item like "Ao Dai" should be "clothing," and "indispensible" should be "indispensable." Additionally, be cautious of repetitive phrases and aim for a variety of sentence structures to enhance readability and engage your audience.

3. **Point of View Clarity**: Your point of view is present but could be stated more definitively. The introduction mentions your stance, but the essay then explores both sides equally. This can make your own viewpoint seem less convincing. Strengthen your argument by clearly emphasizing your reasons for supporting the preservation of traditional clothing and culture over adopting modern fashion trends.

4. **Arguments and Support**: Your arguments about the importance of traditional clothing for culture and identity are compelling. However, the support for your viewpoint could be more detailed and persuasive. Instead of briefly mentioning negatives associated with modern clothing, delve deeper into why losing traditional clothing has significant cultural implications. For example, you could expand on how wearing traditional clothes contributes to cultural preservation and personal identity in a way that modern clothing cannot replicate. Include specific examples and perhaps even statistics or studies to back up your arguments.

Overall, your essay presents a thoughtful discussion on an essential topic. By focusing more on reinforcing your point of view, clarifying your arguments with stronger evidence, and making some grammatical corrections, you can significantly enhance the quality and impact of your essay. Keep writing and refining your skills, and remember that each piece of feedback is a step towards becoming a more persuasive and effective communicator.

prompt: Government: Conserve endangered species or human being is more important. Both views and opinion?
essay:

While many people consider that the interests of human welfare should be a government priority, I agree with those who argue that steps must be taken to prevent the further loss of animal. 
 On the one hand, dealing with issue which exert its detrimental effect on human is high on the government agenda. Firstly, government should spend their budget on this healthcare system. Hence, although maintaining stable health system is of great expense, national budget should be most prioritised with a view to ensuring good public health. For instance, almost countries are greatly investing in scientific research such as simulation of these viruses to find a cure and develop antibiotics for this risky disease. Secondly, in terms of education, nations and individuals must place the importance on tackling education problems. Since education serves as a remedy for heightening people' intellect, the number of illiterate people must be low as much as possible. In poor countries, especially regions suffering from extreme weather, students are unlikely to be given permission to go to school due their financial burden. government, as a consequence, should build up educational infrastructures and support people with destitute living by fully charging tuition fees for them to encourage their children to follow formal education. 
 On the other hand, I concur with those who argue that nations and citizens also need to conserve species which are on the brink of extinction. The red list of endangered species is increasing every year. If wildlife extinction continues, then humans may face an ecological crisis which impacts their own survival. For example, if the practice of whaling by using electrical pulse fishing is not halted, the ecosystems of our oceans will be altered forever, affecting the fish stocks on which so many communities depend for living. Secondly, conserving wild animals means protecting the habitats in which they live, such as rainforests and wetlands. Without preserving animals, habitat destruction would occur, triggering climate change which pose an imminent 
 to our food productivity and environment. 
 To recapitulate, endangered species must be preserved by countries and humans as these animals play an integral role in the development of human beings. National and local authorities should combine expenses on both protection of animals as well as human population
feedback:
The essay extensively discusses the allocation of resources to wildlife protection versus other pressing human issues, such as healthcare and education. However, there are several areas for improvement to make the essay more effective for an English proficiency test.

1. **Essay Length and Focus**: The essay exceeds the ideal length of 250-290 words for a Task 2 essay, making it more akin to a research paper than the required opinion piece. Aim for conciseness in expressing your opinion without over-explaining. This will help in presenting your thoughts clearly and within the expected word limit. Remember, the goal is to demonstrate your ability to express ideas in English clearly and directly, not to cover every aspect of the topic in depth.

This helps in creating a well-rounded discussion and in presenting various perspectives on the issue.

3. **Grammar, Spelling, and Stylistic Issues**: There are a few grammatical errors and awkward phrases that hinder the clarity and professionalism of the essay. For example, "dealing with issue which" could be refined to "dealing with issues that," and "almost countries are greatly investing" should be corrected to "many countries are greatly investing." Paying attention to these details will improve the overall quality of your writing.

4. **Arguments and Support**: While the essay includes arguments for both human welfare and wildlife protection, some arguments could be made clearer and more descriptive. Instead of broad statements, provide specific examples and explain how they support your point of view. This will make your arguments more persuasive and easier to understand.

5. **Clarity of Author's Position**: Your position on the importance of preserving endangered species is clear, but the essay could benefit from a stronger conclusion that succinctly states your viewpoint again, reinforcing the importance of balancing investment in human welfare with wildlife protection.

In summary, aim for a more concise essay that clearly presents different points of view, including your own, uses a variety of pronouns to distinguish these views, and is free from grammatical errors. Focusing on these elements will not only improve the coherence and persuasiveness of your essay but also enhance your overall score on English proficiency tests.

prompt: Film import in comparison to self-production
essay:
People have conflicting opinions about the effectiveness of foreign film import as opposed to self-production. While importing foreign movies could benefit one nation in many aspects, I believe that it would be better for a country to create movies for their citizens. 
 There are certain reasons for which governments should permit film import. First of all, broadcasting various types of movie can increase the number of viewers, which will certainly bring more profit for film companies. It is obvious that diverse range of movie types will undoubtedly appeal more viewers as there are more options to choose. Another reason is local citizens can have a deeper insight into different cultures and traditional values of other nations. As they have access to distinct customs, they can draw some good lessons from other peoples. For instance, there are many good manners of Japanese that locals can learn and alter their behaviors such as the habit of queuing or people can learn the way Western people say "thank you" and "sorry". Lastly, importing films from other countries is an effective way to study second languages. 
 On the other hand, I argue that local programs and movies will exert more positive influences on national art and culture. As we all know, self-producing movies and programs can create more careers for citizens. National production can lead to an increase in jobs for those who have a burning desire to be actors, actress or film makers. Another advantage of creating domestic programs is it will make native values survive, and even flourish. By watching local documentaries, locals can have a good understanding of cultural identity and therefore, it will help to preserve native culture and local lifestyle. In sharp contrast, one possible consequence if international programs have become so pervasive in one country is people may underestimate and lose interest on local tradition and values. 
 In conclusion, even though purchasing international programs gives rise to numerous merits,I believe that self-making films plays an indispensable role in cultural development.
feedback:

1. **Response to the Topic**: The essay addresses the general topic but falls short of fully responding to the prompt's requirements. The task requires discussing two distinct viewpoints: one that supports the importation of foreign films and another that advocates for local film production. After presenting these perspectives, it's essential to conclude with a personal stance. The essay should dedicate separate sections or paragraphs to each viewpoint before sharing a personal opinion.

2. **Structure and Development**: The essay's current structure attempts to cover both viewpoints in a combined manner, which impacts the clarity and development of the discussion. To improve, consider organizing the essay into clear, distinct sections: one paragraph for the benefits of importing films, another for the advantages of local production, followed by a paragraph that introduces and explains your personal perspective. This approach will enhance the essay's coherence and ensure a balanced discussion of the prompt.

3. **Understanding and Following Instructions**: It is crucial to closely adhere to the essay prompt's instructions. This includes accurately paraphrasing the prompt in the introduction to show a clear understanding of the task at hand. The essay should equally discuss both the public viewpoints outlined in the prompt before moving on to the personal opinion. Deviating from these instructions can significantly affect the essay's effectiveness and the overall evaluation.

4. **Conclusion Development**: The concluding statement requires further development to effectively summarize the discussion and restate the personal viewpoint. A strong conclusion should reflect on the main arguments presented for both importing foreign films and local film production, culminating in a clear, concise restatement of your position.

5. **Spelling, Grammar, and Style**: The essay is generally well-written but watch out for minor grammatical errors and aim for stylistic clarity. Ensuring correct spelling, grammar, and punctuation will improve readability and the overall professionalism of the essay.

6. **Clear Point of View**: While the essay attempts to present a personal point of view, it's essential to express this perspective more distinctly and after a balanced discussion of the other viewpoints. Make sure your personal opinion is clearly differentiated and supported by specific arguments.

7. **Supporting Arguments**: Both sides of the discussion benefit from clear, descriptive arguments. Enhance these arguments by providing more examples, evidence, or explanations to support your claims. prompt: Obesity is an increasing public health problem in some parts of the world. Explain some possible reasons for this problem and suggest some solutions. \n Give reasons for your answer, and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge and experience. Write at least 250 words.
essay:
It is true that obesity has been a serious health issue in many developed countries. There are several causes of this problem, but there are also solutions. One cause is a poor diet. Another cause is lack of physical activity. People should try to have healthier meals and take regular exercises. 
 The first reason for obesity is that most people do not have a balanced diet. Specifically, they prefer eating out at restaurants that serve fast foods such as fried chicken and hamburgers. These kinds of food contain a great amount of unhealthy fat and calories which make people who consume them gain weight. Besides, many of them have late night dinners, which, according to scientists, may increase the risk of obesity because the body does not have an opportunity to burn the calories. 
 The second reason is that obese people do not take regular exercises. As a result of the fast pace of modern life, these people tend to have a sedentary lifestyle. In simpler terms, they often sit long hours at their offices and spend less time for outdoor activities. Moreover, the harder they work, the more stress that places on them, which can also encourage a passive lifestyle. In other words, stressed people tend to eat and sleep more and feel lazy to take physical activities. 
 In order to curb the obesity epidemic, it is important that people have healthy eating patterns that contain less fat and sugar. Instead of eating too much junk food, they can try to spend more time cooking healthy food at home and try to consume less meat and more vegetables. Furthermore, they should exercise on a daily basis as well. By this way, people not only reduce the risk of getting obese but also prevent many other dangerous diseases like diabetes and heart disease. 
 In conclusion, there are two main reasons for the rising rate of obesity in many western countries, which are the lack of healthy food and physical exercises. However, this issue could be tackled by making appropriate changes to our lifestyle and eating habits.
feedback:
Your essay on the topic of obesity in developed countries effectively addresses the causes and solutions of this health issue. However, some improvements in structure, style, and grammar can make your argument stronger and clearer. Let's delve into specifics to enhance your essay:

1. **Introduction Structure**: Your opening paragraph directly dives into discussing the causes and solutions of obesity. The start of your essay should focus on paraphrasing the question or statement given. Instead, try to offer a more general statement about obesity before outlining the causes and solutions you will discuss. This approach will help show off your paraphrasing skills and set up the essay effectively without directly jumping into the argument.

2. **Transition and Development**: The essay relies on a simple counting system ("One cause", "Another cause") to present ideas. This method makes your essay seem less sophisticated. Improve this by using transitional phrases and topic sentences that flow naturally. For example, instead of saying "One cause is a poor diet," you could start with "A primary contributor to obesity is the modern dependency on processed foods." This helps demonstrate your language skills more impressively.

3. **Sentence Variety**: There are instances where your sentences are quite long and could be considered run-on. Ensure you vary your sentence structure – mix simple, compound, and complex sentences to show your range. Shorten long sentences and break them up to meet the minimum sentence requirement per paragraph, improving the readability and flow.

4. **Clarity and Coherence**: Your points are valid and well-thought-out, yet the execution can be polished for clarity. Each paragraph should smoothly transition to the next with clear, coherent arguments that reinforce your position. Try to connect your ideas more clearly and ensure each paragraph reinforces your thesis.

5. **Point of View and Arguments**: Your viewpoint on the causes and solutions to obesity is clear throughout the essay, which is great. Your arguments are mostly supportive of your viewpoint, though expanding on them with more examples or evidence could strengthen your position even further.

6. **Spelling, Grammar, and Stylistic Issues**: There are minor grammar and style errors in your essay. Reviewing verb tenses, article usage, and preposition choices will be beneficial. It's also helpful to read your essay out loud or use writing tools to catch these errors.

Remember, every essay is a chance to showcase your language proficiency. By refining your structure, developing your ideas more cohesively, and polishing your grammar and style, you will improve not just this essay but your overall writing skills. Keep practicing, and you will see great progress in your ability to communicate complex ideas effectively.

prompt: Task 2: Increase the cost of fuel for cars and other vehicles to solve environmental problems.

As a result, there will be a shift to using more public vehicles such as buses or electric trams and this will, in turn, help reduce the greenhouse effect. However, this measure would only be beneficial in the short term since the extra expense does not account for much in total. 
 Hence, I strongly believe that the better option is to raise tariffs on private modes of transport, instead. Korea perfectly exemplifies this situation. In Korean, the local authorities put a high tariff barrier on cars which eventually led to a plunge in the number of car users and also a considerable increase in the number of journeys made by buses and underground trains. Moreover, the government should also upgrade public transport infrastructure to facilitate the transportation around the city even more so that more and more people will choose it over riding private transports. Both aforementioned measures will result in a cut down on exhaust fumes from personal cars and help in the effort to combat global warming. 
 In brief, a surge in the cost of petrol would be a useful environmental-friendly solution, although, in the long term, I have the belief that imposing high taxes on cars and improving public facilities would be optimal.

Nonetheless, it's vital to ensure that arguments are thoroughly developed and supported by descriptive examples or evidence. prompt: Short piece of writing on 'The Negative Impacts of Winter Season'

 First of all, during this time, temperatures are relatively low and the weather is cold. This means there is every risk of chilling and catching a bad cold or a deadly fever. 
 Also, the season is quite dry which is why our skin tends to become dry and brittle. In winter, we wear warm clothes covering much of our body. We, therefore, are less exposed to sunlight. This causes our skin to turn colourless and moistureless. 
 At daybreak, often thick fog or mist forms. For this, car drivers cannot view their surroundings properly and accidents take place not infrequently. A criminal is free to roam around and can easily commit crimes without anybody seeing it. In conclusion, the rates of street accidents and crimes rise during winter season. 
 A point worth mentioning is that we tend to feel lethargic during winter. Nobody actually wants to get out of the blanket and wake up early in the morning at winter. It is only circumstances that bounds most of us to do so. Our sense of responsibility forces us to combat the lethargy and work. Furthermore, water turns icy-cold and becomes difficult to use. We need to warm the water and then use it. This takes time and effort. Due to this inconvenience, our daily lives get hampered even though slightly. 
 In a nutshell, winter has many negative sides to consider. However, it's a general truth that good and bad go along. Everything consists of both good and bad in different ratios. One is incomplete without the other. The more easily we will learn to accept this fact, the easier and better our life will become.

prompt: TOEFL: it has become an issue of whether advertisements make products seem more appealing or not.
essay:
Topic: 
 Do you agree or disagree with the following statement? 
 Most advertisements make products seem much better then they really are. 
 Use specific reasons and examples to support your answer 
 . 
 In contemporary society, it has become an issue of whether advertisements make products seem more appealing or not. People's opinions vary from person to person. Some claim that we will assume that products are better than they are if they are advertised. Others hold the opposite viewpoint. In my opinion, I would prefer that advertisements mislead us into believing that the products are better than they are for a couple of reasons. 
 Firstly, advertisements always show the best sides of the product, it is difficult for us to find its flaws unless we use it. It reminds me of an example that matches my idea to the fullest extent. I bought a dishwasher which is the most expensive one in the store. I bought it because the advertisement claimed that it could remove all the dirt from dishes and it also could save time because we didn't need to spend time washing dishes. It turned out that the advertisement was right, nonetheless, it wasted lots of water and electricity, I saved my time but lost money to pay the water bill and electricity bill. 
 Additionally, advertisements may persuade us to think that we need a useless product. To illustrate my point, the experience of buying an electronic toothbrush can be cited as an example. I bought the electronic toothbrush because an advertisement said that all of us should have an electronic toothbrush because it can clean out all the dirty things in our teeth, even something that is stuck in our teeth. However, after I used it, it didn't perform as perfectly as the advertisement said. What's worse is that a traditional toothbrush outperforms it. That is to say that I didn't need an electronic one, I just needed a traditional one. 
 In conclusion, I believe that advertisements convince us that products are better than they are. This is because advertisements always show the best sides of the product and because advertisements make us think that we need the product.

Improving these aspects of your essay will enhance both its clarity and persuasiveness. Equally importantly, though, psychology issues also give rise to childhood obesity. Some negative emotions particularly in stressful or bored frequently appearing in adolescents make them lost control in weight. Clearly, there are so many unprejudiced and subjective reasons existing around us. 
 While being obesity has some adverse effects, there several measures can be implemented to address it.

 Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. 
 In the recent past, the issue of the increasing crime rate has presented itself as a vital challenge in this day and age. This essay will examine the main causes of the rising crime level and possible solutions to this problem. 
 The two main causes of the upward trend of crime are the thrive of nationalism and the deteriorating living conditions of impoverished people. Some people might have more stereotypes and biases while confronting another foreign culture due to globalization. Instead of respecting, they attempt to insult and even attack others which are viewed as villainous enemies to their race or nation. For instance, it is reported that there is an increasing number of immigrants from the Middle East are under attack by residents in East Germany. Also, the worsen circumstances make poor people have no choice but to commit the crime to live on. Moreover, the next step in fighting rising crime percentage is passing more bills to improve social welfare such as providing employment guaranty, extra allowance, and job insurance. This way, governments could improve the living environment for people in need and retard the steady growth of crime effectively.

feedback:

In conclusion, your essay shows promise through its structure, clarity, and intention. A stronger alignment with the essay prompt, coupled with a broader exploration of the causes of crime and more direct solutions, will significantly enhance your writing.
