prompt: Writing - Task 2 - IELTS - Protect wild animals
essay:
Wild animals have no place in the 21st century, so protecting them is a waste of resources. To what extent do you agree or disagree? 
 Some people believe that the protection of wildlife is unnecessary due to its waste of time and money. In this essay, however, I will change this school of thought. 
 Granted, one could argue that investing in wildlife conservation is a waste of money. This is anticipated on the assumption that such an investment would force countries, especially underdeveloped ones, to allocate substantial amounts of money to animal protection campaigns and programs, putting more burden on their financial situation. According to this theory, while these poor countries should prioritize their national budgets to invest more in education, the growth of economics, and healthcare, this matter should be addressed by powers such as the US, the UK, or the United Nations. In addition, the protection of wild animals, especially endangered species, often undergoes a multitude of experiments to find workable measures to save these species, but there is no way to ensure all these experiments succeed, irrespective of how hard scientists work, leading to a waste of time and money. 
 However, this line of reasoning is not sound because protecting animals is to save humankind. Take, for example, the many vaccinations that have been produced stemming from animals such as snakes, which play an important role in successfully treating thousands of people each year. Thus, the benefits that could be gained from animals are tremendous. In addition, by protecting wild animals, the world's ecosystem balance would be guaranteed. This means that if the extinction of any species occurs in habitats ranging from rainforests to the sea, there will be impacts on the survival of other species. For example, if all herbivore species disappeared radically, this would lead to the disappearance of carnivores such as tigers and lions due to their food chains being destroyed. 
 In conclusion, to protect the earth's ecosystem and the invaluable resources serving human beings, the protection of wild animals is necessary. 
 (316 words)
feedback:
Your essay addresses an important and challenging topic: whether it is worthwhile to protect wild animals in the 21st century. You’ve tackled this subject with enthusiasm, showing a good understanding and bringing valuable points to the discussion. However, there are areas that can be improved to make your essay more impactful and align more closely with the expectations of English proficiency tests.

Firstly, your essay sets out to change a particular school of thought about wildlife protection. While it’s commendable to aim for persuasive writing, it’s crucial to ensure your argument aligns directly with the provided question. The prompt asks to what extent you agree or disagree with the statement that wild animals have no place in the 21st century and that protecting them is a waste of resources. Your introduction should clearly state your position in response to this. For instance, saying “I strongly disagree…” or “I partly agree and disagree…” helps clarify your stance from the outset. This clarity is essential for the reader to understand your perspective throughout the essay.

When it comes to spelling, grammar, and style, your essay is quite strong, but watch out for small errors and ensure your sentences flow smoothly. For example, the term "anticipated on the assumption" could be simplified to "based on the assumption" to enhance clarity. Additionally, ensure consistency in terms like "growth of economics," which would be more accurately expressed as "economic growth."

Your reasoning paragraphs are one of the strengths of your essay. They demonstrate a deep understanding of the subject and provide compelling arguments for why protecting wildlife is crucial, not just for the animals themselves but for human beings and the entire ecosystem. Make sure that each paragraph focuses on a single main idea, supported by clear examples or evidence, as you did with the example of vaccines derived from animals.

However, ensure your conclusion directly reflects back to the question. Restate your position on the subject and summarize the key points you’ve made in defense of your view. This ties your essay together and reinforces your argument to the reader.

In summary, your essay has a lot of potentials. Focus on clearly stating your agreement or disagreement with the prompt, maintaining clarity and simplicity in your language, and ensuring your arguments are well-structured and supported. By making these adjustments, your essay will be more persuasive and better aligned with the expectations of English proficiency tests. Keep up the good work, and continue refining your skills in essay writing!

prompt: The debate on whether enterprises should value appearance, or the work performance of the laborers
essay:
Some organizations believe that their employees should dress smartly. Others value quality of work above appearance. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. 
 Give reasons for your answers and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge experience. 
 There is much debate on whether enterprises should value appearance or the work performance of the laborers. In my point of view, I hold the belief that both criterion have their own bright sides. 
 In a world that is increasingly interested in beauty, dressing appropriately opens up many opportunities for the employees. To begin with, individuals who wear professional attire may have a higher chance to get successful transactions. Because people often feel pleasant to beauty and gorgeous appearance easily makes a good impression on the customers. In addition, dressing smartly is also one of the best ways to show the specialist of the workers. This would result in the fact that companies gain a higher trust and more definite commitment from the clients. 
 On the other hand, the efficiency of workers also brings numerous advantages to the enterprises. Firstly, there are many staff who can bring value and create annual profit to the company just based on their highly specialized skill. For instance, architects or IT experts often wear casual clothes whenever they work at home, meanwhile the outcomes of the products remain effective. Secondly, well-qualified employees help the operator system of the company take place more stably and efficiently. Because laborers with advanced skills supervise the work more meticulously and make fewer mistakes compared to those who lack professional skills. 
 To sum up, I totally agree that the efficiency of workers plays a crucial role in the success of the company. Nevertheless, dressing professionally also creates many opportunities for the career of the workers and helps expand many relationships.
feedback:
This essay addresses an interesting debate on whether organizations should prioritize the appearance or work performance of their employees. Your essay provides viewpoints on both aspects before presenting a personal stance, which aligns with the task requirements. However, there are several areas where improvements could significantly enhance the clarity and effectiveness of your argumentation.

Firstly, it’s important to choose words that accurately convey your meaning. For instance, using the term "laborers" suggests individuals who perform physical labor, whereas this context seems to refer to all types of employees, including those in office settings. A more fitting term would be "employees" or "office workers" to avoid confusion and ensure precision in language.

Regarding the structure, while your essay endeavors to discuss both viewpoints before stating your own opinion, the transitions between these sections could be made clearer. Each paragraph should ideally start by clearly indicating whether you're discussing a commonly held view or your personal perspective. This practice will help maintain a logical flow and make it easier for readers to follow your line of thought.

Moreover, it’s essential to adhere to academic writing conventions. Starting sentences with conjunctions (e.g., "Because", "And") can disrupt the formal tone expected in such essays. Instead, try to rephrase sentences to avoid beginning with conjunctions, maintaining a professional and academic tone throughout your essay.

On a positive note, the essay commendably incorporates reasons and examples to support its arguments. Enhancing these with more specific instances or personal experiences could further strengthen your essay. Providing concrete examples helps illustrate your points vividly, making your argumentation more persuasive to the reader.

In summary, focusing on precise language use, improving structural clarity, adhering to formal academic writing conventions, and enriching your arguments with detailed examples will significantly elevate the quality of your essay. Being mindful of these aspects can help you more effectively communicate your insights and persuasions, ultimately making your essays more compelling and impactful.

prompt: IELTS WRITING TASK 2: Why national leaders should spend more money on public transportation
essay:
People have argued that the authorities should utilise their funds and budgets on developing streets and highways rather than on public transportation areas. As far as I concerned, the advantage of investing in public transport systems always outweighs that of remain option. 
 On the one hand, a group of people think that the government should focus on improving their street and highway facilities since several reasons. First of all, having a better quality of them would raise the levels of safety for people and clear traffics. To be more specific, adding and enlarging more lanes and routes make not only fluent traffic of means of transportation but also declining in road mortality and injury rates. Secondly, enhancing on road networks helps restrain traffic congestion. Because of broad roads, everyone has maximum free-flowing traffics instead of limit of moving in rush hour times from 8.00 AM to 4.00 PM in Ho Chi Minh city and it is an outstanding example. 
 Although, investing in road networks possesses immediately potential advantages, it can not be compared with public transport. First reason is that high-capacity public transport can accommodate larger number of passengers in comparison with vehicles at same time. Take a bus has double size towards a sedan could carry forty people instead of four spaces as an clear example. Finally, a mode shift from private to efficient public transport systems contributes to a green environment. Besides, taking public transit, carpool or riding a bicycle play a vital role in progressing of low-carbon lifestyle. 
 It is obvious to me to conclude that national leaders should spend money on public transportation is a potential step to come to the sustainable development for high quality of social life.
feedback:
This essay aims to address the topic of whether authorities should prioritize funding for the development of streets and highways or focus on enhancing public transportation systems. While the essay presents arguments on both perspectives briefly, it leans more towards the benefits of investing in public transportation. 

Firstly, it’s important to ensure that the essay directly addresses the given topic. The prompt asks for a discussion of both views and your personal opinion on the matter. The essay's introduction should clearly outline that both perspectives will be explored before stating your viewpoint. Remember, adhering to the prompt’s requirements is crucial for a favorable evaluation.

Regarding structure and content, the essay tries to present two sides of the argument but ends up primarily supporting one side. It's essential to balance the discussion by dedicating a similar length and depth of analysis to each viewpoint before concluding with your reasoned opinion. This approach shows critical thinking and fairness in evaluating different arguments.

Spelling, grammar, and stylistic issues are present throughout the essay, affecting its clarity and readability. For example, phrases like “As far as I concerned” and “remain option” are unclear or incorrect. These could be revised to “As far as I am concerned” and “remaining options” or a more context-appropriate term. Consistent verb tenses, correct plural forms (“traffic” instead of “traffics”), and avoiding run-on sentences will vastly improve the essay's quality. 

The point of view is stated, but the transition between examining public opinions and expressing a personal viewpoint could be smoother and more explicit. Using transitional phrases to bridge different sections of the essay can help clarify the progression of your arguments.

In terms of supporting arguments, the essay mentions several advantages of public transportation and road development. However, these arguments would benefit from being more detailed and supported by evidence or examples. This would make your position more persuasive and impactful. 

Finally, considering the original intent of the essay prompt, it's crucial not to deviate from the asked discussion. Avoid changing the discussion instruction or comparing topics not requested by the prompt. Understanding and adhering to the prompt's requirements are key to a successful essay.

In summary, focusing on directly addressing the prompt, balancing the discussion, correcting language issues, clearly stating and supporting your point of view, and presenting well-structured arguments will significantly enhance the essay. Practice and revision, based on these points, will lead to improved writing skills and better performance in future essays.

prompt: A family outing - Describe a memorable memory in my life
essay: During my recent holiday, I had a family outing in Binh Thuan, and I had a memorable experience there. I still remember it was very cool that night, so after eating dinner, my brother and I decided to stroll by motorbike. But we got lost because we were absorbed in enjoying the beautiful scenery here. Unfortunately, at that time, our motorbike was almost out of gas, and neither of us had a cell phone so we couldn't contact our parents. I felt very nervous. Fortunately, I found some money in my pocket, enough for us to fill up with gas to continue our way home. Moreover, we met a friendly policeman who lent me his phone and showed us the way home. At that time, I felt fortunate to have made it home and was very grateful to the policeman that day.
feedback:
Your essay provides a concise recount of a personal experience during a holiday in Binh Thuan, which is a good start. However, there are several areas where the essay could be greatly improved to make it more engaging and effective in communicating your point of view.

1. **Response to the Topic:**
The essay does paint a clear picture of an adventure, but it could be enhanced by adding more context around the setting. Mentioning specific details such as the season, the reason for the holiday, or even the time of year could help set the stage more vividly for your readers. While the year might not be crucial, a bit more background would enrich the narrative.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, or Stylistic Issues:**
Your essay is generally free from spelling or grammatical errors, which is excellent. However, the writing style could be improved to better capture the reader's interest. Consider varying sentence structure and using more descriptive language to bring your experiences to life.

3. **Author's Point of View:**
Your point of view is present but could be communicated more powerfully by deepening the narrative. Exploring your emotions, thoughts, and sensory experiences in more detail will help the reader understand and empathize with your situation.

4. **Arguments and Support:**
Your recounting of the events supports the narrative of a memorable experience. Nonetheless, the essay lacks depth in illustrating the adventure and the emotions involved. To address this, consider introducing elements like dialogue between you and your brother or the policeman. It would also add to the suspense and excitement if you heightened the storytelling by expanding on the worry, confusion, and eventually the relief you felt. This could involve describing how your heart raced, how the silent night seemed to echo your fears, or even how the warmth of relief washed over you when help was found.

In summary, your essay has a solid foundation and recounts a memorable experience effectively. To elevate your narrative, focus on providing more background, utilizing descriptive and varied language, delving deeper into your emotions throughout the experience, and incorporating dialogue for a more dynamic and engaging account. These adjustments will certainly make your essay more captivating and enjoyable to read.

prompt: Music cannot be substituted. People can't live without it.
essay:
Nowadays, people have a variety of different musical styles to listen. Listening music have turned into indispensable part of a life for a wide range of reasons, and I would argue that traditional music outweighs the international music. 
 The reasons why this activity have become the necessity comes from our childhood, as most kids enjoy listening music. As a result, in their later life, they have a tendency to consider the music as an essential tool which cheers them up. Apart from the type of entertainment, in most countries, listening music is regarded as an effective method to contribute learning process ranging from different languages to basic skills. Music is also an integral part of typical adult's life. Due to the fact that music can express and arouse our feelings which we cannot explain with words, most people see it as a need of the soul. 
 In the light of increasing presence of the international music, some people think the traditional music used up its time. I completely disagree with this idea, as the traditional music carry more meanings than the international music such as the culture or history of the country. It can easily be understood the traditions or lifestyles of the people in early days just by listening such kinds of music. On the other hands, the international music is a commercial product, so put more emphasis on catchy notes rather than meaningful words. It will be so disappointing if one day the traditional music disappears from the music lists because of growing popularity of the pop music. 
 In conclusion, music cannot be substituted by any other activity for aforementioned reasons, I restate that traditional music is more valuable than new types of international music because of the hidden meanings behind it.
feedback:
Your essay effectively addresses the topic, presenting a clear stance on the importance of traditional music over international music, which is commendable. However, there are several areas where improvements could enhance the clarity and strength of your argument, ensuring a more compelling and structured presentation.

1. **Topic Response and Structure**: Your introduction and conclusion need to directly reference the essay question to ensure the reader is fully aware of the context. This means paraphrasing the question, such as "Is the traditional music of a country more important than the international music that is heard everywhere nowadays?" at the beginning, and summarizing your key points in the conclusion. This will help to frame your essay more clearly and ensure that your argument is coherent throughout.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, and Style**: There are several grammatical errors that distract from your overall message, such as using "have" instead of "has" (e.g., "Listening music has turned into an indispensable part..."), and inconsistencies in verb tense. Additionally, consider varying your sentence structure to add more rhythm and interest to your writing. Simplifying complex sentences may also help in making your argument more accessible.

3. **Clarity of Point of View**: Your perspective—that traditional music is more valuable than international music—is evident, which is a strength of your essay. However, deepening your analysis and providing more specific examples or evidence could bolster your argument.

4. **Arguments and Support**: While you effectively argue for the importance of traditional music by mentioning its connection to culture and history, contrasting it more directly with international music could strengthen your position. Highlighting specific qualities of traditional music and providing examples could make your argument more persuasive. Also, consider exploring why international music's commercial nature might make it less meaningful, as this is a claim that would benefit from further elaboration.

To enhance your essay, focus on clearly restating the question in your own words at the beginning and summarizing your main points in the conclusion. Attend to grammatical accuracy and stylistic variety to make your writing more engaging. Providing a more structured comparison and deeper analysis will also help in making a more compelling case for the importance of traditional music. By addressing these areas, your essay will become a more powerful and clear piece of writing.

prompt: Writing task 2: Academic knowledge vs Life skills
essay:
Some people argue that schools should focus on academic performance of students rather than their practical skills like dressing or cooking. From my perspective, I completely disagree with this statement. 
 On the one hand, it is true to say that academic knowledge plays a pivotal role in schools. This is because academic performance directly influences the scores that students achieve in the exams which are an important factor when they apply for a job after graduation. Furthermore, without fundamental understandings, students can hardly succeed and progress in their domains in the future. However, I believe that placing excessive emphasis on academic learning can also be detrimental since not all students want or are able to pursue a career of a mathematician or a historian. Therefore, focusing attention on academic knowledge can be a waste of time and effort for those who desire to work in non-academic fields such as cooking or fashion. 
 On the other hand, there are several reasons why schools need to teach practical life skills. Firstly, those skills are indispensable for people who want to become independent and self-reliant. For example, when college students live far from their families, knowing how to cook enables them to prepare the meals by themselves without having to dine out. Secondly, students who have acquired practical skills and been able to complete self-care tasks are likely to become more confident and possess a sense of responsibility. Finally, attending skill building classes can also be seen as an hobby which helps students to unwind after spending many hours on theoretical subjects. 
 In conclusion, I hold the view that while test-taking expertise is important, students also need to learn practical life skills such as cooking, cleaning or dressing in order to be capable of taking care of themselves.
feedback:
Your essay addresses the debate on whether schools should prioritize academic performance over practical skills like cooking and dressing. You articulated a clear stance, disagreeing with the sole focus on academic achievements, and provided reasons supporting both academic and practical skill development in schools. This thorough approach forms a strong foundation for your argument.

1. **Response to the Topic:** Your essay responds well to the given topic by presenting a balanced view on the importance of both academic performance and practical skills. However, make sure to directly address the essay prompt at the beginning to make your stance even clearer to the reader.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, and Style:** Generally, your essay is well-written. To improve readability and maintain a formal tone, avoid long sentences that might confuse the reader. Break complex ideas into simpler, shorter sentences. Pay close attention to punctuation and sentence structure to enhance clarity.

3. **Clear Point of View:** You've effectively used the first-person perspective, particularly strong in the paragraph where you state, "I believe that placing excessive emphasis on academic learning can also be detrimental...". This personal touch adds depth to your argument. In future essays, consistently use this personal insight to enrich your discussion.

4. **Arguments and Support:** Your arguments are relevant and mostly well-explained. However, focus on providing a singular, clear topic sentence for each paragraph and expand on it with no more than two closely linked reasons. This approach will help maintain focus and offer thorough explanations rather than just listing reasons. For example, when discussing the importance of practical skills, delve deeper into how these skills enhance independence and confidence, rather than quickly moving through multiple ideas.

Improvement Tips:
- **Paragraph Structure:** Ensure each paragraph has one main idea, supported by 1-2 specific reasons, followed by a detailed explanation or example. This structure will strengthen the coherence and persuasive power of your essay.
- **Personal Experience and Insight:** Try to include personal insights or examples that further illustrate your points. This will make your arguments more relatable and compelling.
- **Balance and Depth:** While it's good to present a balanced view, make sure to delve deeply into each point you raise. Depth of analysis often impresses more than the breadth of coverage.

Remember, effective essay writing combines clear argumentation with personal insight and a focus on depth over breadth. Keep practicing these elements, and your writing will continue to improve!

prompt: Recidivism - Ielts writing: Many offenders commit more crimes after serving the 1st punishment
essay:
It is a fact that there are a large number of first-time offenders released from jail that reoffend. Behind this alarming phenomenon are various reasons and measures that can be taken by the government to eliminate this issue. 
 There are two primary reasons for recidivism. Firstly, it is almost impossible for offenders to find proper jobs. Due to their criminal records, people still consider them a threat to society, consequently, employers usually avoid hiring wrongdoers. Secondly, the prison system is partly to blame for prisoners' committing crime again since they are locked up with other offenders. Being exposed to bad inmates will only make prisoners more susceptible to immoral intentions and thoughts. 
 Apart from imposing tougher punishment for criminals who reoffend, government should concentrate on rehabilitation. Vocational training is highly recommend to equip prisoners with essential skills and knowledge so that they can have a better chance of reintegrating into society and finding jobs. Another resolution to reform offenders is community service. By performing duties under the observation of supervisors, offenders are encouraged to be responsible and useful to their society, which can reduce the likelihood of reoffending. 
 In conclusion, recidivism is believed to be one of the overwhelming problems facing our community, however, it can be tackled if drastic measures are implemented by the government.
feedback:

This stance is consistently supported with reasons and potential solutions, making the essay's arguments coherent and persuasive.

However, to improve, it's recommended to further develop these arguments with more detailed examples or data where possible. For example, mentioning specific vocational training programs or community service activities that have been successful could make the case stronger.

Expanding on existing points or introducing a broader range of solutions could help reach the required word count while enriching the essay's content.

Moving forward, aiming for a greater depth of analysis and ensuring all requirements are met, including word count, will significantly improve essay quality and effectiveness.

prompt: [IELTS writing task 2] Rising pressure on students, positive or negative?
essay:
The ever-rising tension for modern students to excel in every aspect has sparked concern. I firmly believe that this trend is only riddled with problems, in a sense that it overrides the joy of learning and limit the potential of such young minds, as will be explained in this essay. 
 To begin with, education only achieves good outcome when learners are nurtured in a positive and encouraging environment, which is opposed the reality today. Some school systems are now obsessed with a narrow definition of success - with standardized testing, ranking, comparison and competition. This, not surprisingly, puts an unbearable burden on students, resulting in disinterest and misconception of learning as well as several mental illnesses such as anxiety, depression or even suicidal tendency. Such alarming pattern has been recorded in countries like Japan, Korea and possibly more in the upcoming time. 
 Furthermore, vast majority of young people do not yet gain enough experience to make a decision of their career paths. Restricted within the setting of parents, teachers and classmates, these minds are still being molded, their understanding of many other issues are inadequate. Narrowing down a person's focus and options is a way to steal from him or her the opportunity to be broad-minded and creative. Whereas, the opposite direction, which means allowing students to explore the world from various perspectives, can have a wonderful effect. This has been proved in Finland, where education system routinely ranks top worldwide and is famed for minimizing testing and homework. 
 In brief, despite the fact that pressurizing students may help them to be more ambitious, it seems to me that such pattern is rather problematic. Learning should be full of positivity instead of pressure. It is vital for schools, parents and students to be aware and cooperate to aim for a better education approac[h. 
 [303 WORDS]
feedback:

However, there are areas that require attention to enhance overall coherence and adherence to the essay prompt.

While the body of the essay successfully argues against the pressure on students, the initial misalignment with the prompt could impact the clarity and direction of the argument. To improve, ensure that your opening statement closely mirrors the essay prompt, accurately setting up the discussion without altering its intended focus. An effective introduction prepares readers for the arguments that follow, without changing the scope of the essay.

Additionally, the conclusion of the essay does not fully serve its purpose of summarizing and closing the discussion. Instead, it introduces new ideas, which might leave readers with unanswered questions or a feeling of incompletion. A strong conclusion should reflect on the arguments presented, reinforcing the thesis without extending the discussion further. Consider revisiting your closing paragraph to ensure it succinctly encapsulates your main points and reaffirms your stance, providing a clear and satisfying end to the essay.

On a stylistic note, the essay demonstrates a good command of language, but there are minor spelling and grammatical errors, such as the incorrect use of "concider" instead of "consider," and the misspelling of "approac[h" which should be "approach." Paying attention to these details will polish your essay and make it more professional.

To enhance your essay further, focus on:
- Aligning the introduction more closely with the essay prompt.
- Ensuring the conclusion effectively summarizes and ends the discussion.
- Proofreading for spelling and grammatical errors to enhance clarity and readability.

By addressing these points, you can strengthen your essay, making it more coherent, persuasive, and aligned with the expectations of English proficiency tests. Your analytical abilities and the relevance of your arguments are clear strengths; refining the structure and presentation will only enhance your essay writing skills.

prompt: IELTS Writing Task 2: Printed vs Online Newspapers and Books - support your opinion
essay:
Write at least 250 words.

It is commonly speculated that they will eventually take over traditional printed books and newspapers. In this essay, I will give my opinion on why I think such a scenario is not possible.

prompt: Maths and business success - IELTS Writing Task 2 Opinion Essay
essay:
To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement? 
 Essay: 
 It is sometimes argued that good math skills are the key for employees to attain success in the workplace. While I recognize the importance of mathematics in business, I also believe that there are other factors that more significantly contribute to company achievement. 
 On the one hand, I agree that math proficiency is certainly necessary in the workplace. There are a number of jobs essential in a business that require high levels of calculations, such as accounting and financial analysis. Therefore, those with solid math skills are more likely to carry out these tasks with greater effectiveness and precision than others. Perhaps more importantly, I believe math skills - particularly numeracy and numerical problem solving - are closely associated with broader cognitive ability. This ability really matters because it is reflective of a person's capacity to think critically and solve problems, both of which are key skills that contribute to employees' job performance. 
 On the other hand, I believe that one still can achieve success in business without a background in math. In the modern age, we already have access to computers and calculators that are clearly able to take on more complicated math functions using a large amount of data. This means that highly calculative work in a business will no longer require humans to perform. Furthermore, I would argue that such factors like leadership style, organizational structure, and innovation are more important from a business perspective, and surely these things do not require any excellent math skills. For instance, effective communication and collaboration among employees as well as managers are non-math-related factors crucial to drive the company to success and growth. 
 In conclusion, while math is an integral part of managing business, I do not see it as the most significant contributor to a business's success. ( 296 words)

In conclusion, your essay has a solid foundation and addresses the topic from an interesting perspective. It’s critical to summarize your discussion points in the thesis to showcase your understanding of the topic. For example, you could state, "This essay will explore how lack of education and inadequate government policies contribute to poverty and propose solutions through education reform and employment opportunities."

2. **Word Count and Development of Arguments:**

Expanding your explanation can help meet the word requirement and provide a more comprehensive analysis. Ensure that both the causes and solutions to poverty are discussed in detail. prompt: Topic: Fast food and taxing it higher
essay:
Health issues are closely associated with people's consumption of fast food so that a higher tax on this kind of food is suggested as a good measure. Personally, I completely disagree with this view. 
 In my opinion, a higher tax might play no role in improving the situation if people don't have awareness of protecting their health as well as having knowledge of the consequences of eating too much fast food. Take me as an example, m weight is rising every year as I have a habit of eating after 10 p.m and whenever I feel hungry. Therefore, it is highly important in your endeavor to improve your health by keeping yourself away from unhealthy food. 
 Another reason for government should not impose a higher tax on junk food is because it would be a financial problem for people who earn less. Sometimes, hamburgers or processed food are familiar to poor workers due to their cheap prices. Junk food helps them not only save time but also have more hours at work as they don't have much time to prepare a nourishing meal. Thus, instead of raising the tax, the government can reduce the amount of food produced in the sale market every day. Besides, introducing healthy food through social media or by doing propaganda are also good ways to limit fast food consumption. 
 In conclusion, I disagree with the view that government should impose a higher tax on fast food because I believe that there is more than one way to make the situation better.
feedback:
The essay effectively addresses the topic by providing a clear stance against the imposition of higher taxes on fast food as a means to combat health issues. The argument is well-structured, with each paragraph introducing distinct points that support the author's position. The use of personal experience to illustrate a point is a good approach; however, there is a slight oversight in differentiating between "fast food" and "junk food". While the essay uses these terms interchangeably, it's worth noting that fast food can include healthier options, such as pre-made salads and sandwiches. Clarifying this distinction can strengthen the argument by demonstrating a nuanced understanding of the subject matter.

On the linguistic aspect, the essay is mostly well-written but does have minor spelling and grammar issues that can be easily fixed. For example, "concider" should be corrected to "consider", "m weight is rising" seems to have a typo and should likely be "my weight is rising", and "the government can reduce the amount of food produced in the sale market every day" could be more clearly phrased. Paying attention to these errors will improve the readability and professionalism of the essay.

The conclusion succinctly restates the opposition to higher taxes on fast food but could be further enhanced by briefly reiterating the two main arguments made in the body of the essay. This would provide a stronger, more rounded summary and effectively reinforce the author's viewpoint.

Moreover, it's important for the essay to maintain a consistent point of view throughout. The shift in perspective from personal ("Take me as an example") to a broader societal view ("Another reason for government...") is effective, but ensuring a smooth transition between these perspectives can improve the overall cohesion of the essay.

Finally, the essay would benefit from more specific suggestions on alternative strategies to address health issues related to fast food consumption. The ideas mentioned, such as reducing the amount of junk food produced and promoting healthier food options through social media, are a good start. Expanding on these ideas, with more detailed explanations or examples, could serve to not only strengthen the argument but also demonstrate a deeper understanding of the complex nature of public health initiatives.

Overall, the essay presents a well-reasoned argument, showing good capabilities in structure and reasoning. With slight improvements in clarity, differentiation of terms, and elaboration on concluding points, the essay has the potential for an even more impactful presentation of the author's standpoint.

 In conclusion, fat is not good for you, the two main causes are eat too much food which have many fat and a couch potato active. To get rid of bad habits everyone need limit eat fast food and training.
feedback:
The essay does address the topic of health and diet challenges in contemporary society, focusing on the causes of unhealthy eating habits and a sedentary lifestyle, as well as suggesting solutions. However, there are areas for improvement to make the essay clearer, more structured, and more impactful.

1. **Clarity and Structure**: The essay's ideas seem jumbled and jump from one point to another without a clear progression. It's important to organize thoughts so that each paragraph focuses on one idea at a time. A recommended structure for each paragraph could be:
   - State the cause of a problem,
   - Describe its effect,
   - Propose a solution,
   - Give an example to illustrate the solution,
   - Provide additional explanation for the solution and example.

This structure will help the essay flow better and make it easier for readers to understand the points being made.

2. **Use of Pronouns and Perspective**: The essay shifts between using “everyone,” “you,” and indirect references. For a more cohesive read, it's advisable to present viewpoints in a general manner, avoiding direct references to the reader ("you"). If personal opinion is being offered, use first-person pronouns ("I", "me") consistently, or consider avoiding pronouns altogether for a more formal tone.

3. **Grammar and Style**: Several spelling, grammar, and stylistic issues detract from the essay’s readability and professionalism. For example, using correct terms ("fewer people" instead of "less people") and avoiding repetitive language can improve clarity. Watch out for run-on sentences and try not to use conflicting punctuation marks like a comma followed by ellipses.

4. **Argument Development**: While the essay mentions causes and solutions, these points need deeper exploration and more precise examples. Rather than broadly stating that junk food and lack of exercise are problems, detail why these issues have become prevalent and how specific solutions can effectively address them. Remember, quality over quantity is key in making persuasive arguments.

5. **Word Choice**: There's a distinction between "ways to solve a problem" and "suggestions to help solve a problem". The latter is more accurate and suggests practical steps rather than definitive solutions. Paying attention to such nuances enhances the essay's credibility.

In summary, focusing on clarity, structure, perspective, and precise argumentation will significantly improve the essay. Ensuring grammar and word choice are appropriate will also make the essay more professional and easier to understand. Remember, the goal is to present a compelling argument that is well-supported and clearly articulated, making it both informative and persuasive to readers.

prompt: IELTS WRITING TASK 2 - Agree/Disagree - Cycling
essay:
The bicycle has become increasingly common in many countries, a great alternative to reducing carbon dioxide footprint. It is argued by many people that there should be a test that bike riders need to pass before being available to travel on the streets. Personally, I believe that this idea creates more drawbacks rather than benefits. 
 First of all, riding a bike is a simple skill that anyone can acquire after a few hours of practicing. Therefore, the idea of having a mandatory test for this vehicle's users is unnecessary. For example, a 6-year-old boy can ride a bike well after being trained by his father. Furthermore, the government will have to provide a large amount of money to execute this law, which is paid for the testing centers, extra police officers checking the riders' licenses. More importantly, it is reported that bike is one of the transportations that caused fewest accidents in the past few years, making money allocated for this proposal incredibly wasteful. 
 On the other hand, due to the negative impacts of air pollution, people worldwide are highly encouraged to use bikes. Hence, this restriction will deter them from using this environmentally-friendly transportation. Suppose the test requires a heft fee or complicated procedure. In that case, people are likely to delay obeying the law, making it longer to be completely effective. 
 Overall, the idea that requires bicycle users to pass a test is a fallacy because it will not only waste resources but also create more deterrents to using the bike instead of other less green vehicles. Instead, the government should put more effort into stimulating this vehicle's usage and ensuring the traffic system is safe for bikers.
feedback:
The essay addresses the topic of whether bicycle riders should pass a test before being allowed on the streets, offering a clear stance against it. Nevertheless, there are several areas for improvement to make the essay stronger and more aligned with standard expectations for English proficiency tests.

1. **Response to the Topic:** The introduction misinterprets the task by presenting the topic in a manner not specified in the original prompt. It's essential to accurately restate the topic as given and clearly present your viewpoint in the format required by the question. Rather than discussing "drawbacks vs. benefits," it would be more appropriate to state the extent of agreement or disagreement with the idea presented in the prompt. Reworking the introduction to align with these expectations is crucial for a positive assessment.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, and Stylistic Issues:** While the essay is generally well-written, attention to detail in spelling, grammar, and style can enhance its clarity and readability. For instance, consider the consistency in verb tense and the correct use of articles. Also, avoid overly complex sentences that may confuse the reader. Simplifying language without losing meaning can make the argument more accessible.

3. **Point of View Clarity:** The essay does an adequate job of maintaining a consistent point of view against the proposal for a biking test. This stance is clear throughout the piece, which is a strength. However, reinforcing this viewpoint with more diverse arguments and evidence could further enhance its persuasiveness.

4. **Arguments and Descriptive Support:** The essay provides several reasons and examples to support the author's position, such as the simplicity of learning to bike, the financial burden of implementing tests, and the potential deterrent effect on bike usage. These arguments are valuable but could be expanded with more detailed descriptions, statistics, or comparisons to other transportation methods. It would also be beneficial to address possible counterarguments to offer a more balanced and comprehensive perspective.

In conclusion, the essay has a solid foundation but requires adjustments to align better with the prompt's requirements and to improve its overall effectiveness. Focusing on accurately interpreting the task, refining the language and structure, and bolstering the argument with well-supported and clearly articulated points will significantly enhance the quality of the essay.

prompt: About advantages and disadvantages of working and studying from home
essay:
As people gain more access to technology, working and learning from home has become the method chosen by many grownups and children. From my perspective, although many people can be beneficial from this development, its negative impacts still outweigh and cannot be ignored. 
 On the one hand, it is understandable that people choose remote working and studying due to its merits. The first and also the main advantage is that working and learning from home is more convenient. As both adults and children can easily arrange their tasks based on their timetable and job priority, people no longer need to depend on a fixed schedule. Secondly, the development in technology makes it possible for everyone who is qualified enough to work and learn overseas through a computer. People have more chances to approach a wider range of knowledge and job positions. 
 On the other hand, working and studying from home also brings many significant disadvantages. Firstly, it badly affects life quality as people may lose real-life interactions when they spend too much time using technological equipment. Recent studies have shown that an individual's happiness is positively influenced by the quality and quantity of relationships with people around that person. Secondly, health problems related to the excessive amount of time used to look at screens may be caused by remote working and learning. For example, children can become short-sighted and adults may face heart diseases and obesity as the result of lacking physical exercise from spending too much time sitting in front of screens. Thirdly, it can be easily interrupted as the internet connection may not be stable enough to ensure working and learning from home. Moreover, there is a thread from personal information leaks as high-technology criminals are eager to exploit holes in information security and financially take advantage of these holes. 
 In conclusion, it is beneficial for people to work and learn from home. However, humanity must take its weaknesses into consideration.
feedback:
The essay effectively communicates an opinion on the rising trend of working and learning from home due to increased access to technology. The stance that the negative impacts outweigh the positive ones is clear and presented upfront, which is a strong aspect of the essay. However, there are several areas for improvement to make the essay more focused and impactful.

Firstly, the essay partly addresses the topic by discussing the shift toward remote work and learning but misses an essential element from the initial prompt: the role of affordable technology in facilitating this trend. Including this aspect would strengthen the introduction and provide a more comprehensive response to the question posed.

Regarding word count, the essay exceeds the typical limit for English proficiency tests, which might hinder the ability to thoroughly review and refine the content within the exam's time constraints. Striving for conciseness and relevance in arguments will not only help in adhering to the word limit but also in maintaining the reader's engagement.

It is commendable that a personal viewpoint is established, suggesting a preference for in-person interactions over remote engagements due to various outlined disadvantages. Yet, the essay ventures into discussing the positives of remote work and learning, contradicting the initial stance. The task requires a focus on defending one viewpoint instead of presenting a balanced discussion. Concentrating on reinforcing the chosen perspective with solid arguments and examples will enhance coherence and persuasiveness.

There are minor spelling and grammar issues, but overall, the language used is understandable. To improve readability and overall flow, paying attention to sentence structure and the correct usage of words is crucial. Simple language that accurately conveys the intended meaning is more effective, especially for English language learners.

In summary, refining the essay involves:
- Clearly restating the topic, including all its elements.
- Sticking to the word limit to ensure manageability and thoroughness.
- Focusing solely on supporting the chosen viewpoint without contradicting it.
- Addressing minor linguistic errors to enhance clarity and comprehension.

By concentrating on these areas of improvement, the essay will present a more coherent, focused, and convincing argument in response to the task at hand.

However, the introduction could be strengthened. An improved introduction should consist of at least three sentences, ending with a clear statement of your position using first-person pronouns (e.g., "In this essay, I strongly believe that…"). For instance, instead of citing specific studies, discuss observable patterns or widely recognized concepts that support your point, emphasizing your personal insight.

In summary, while the essay has a suitable foundation, focusing on personalized statements of opinion, grammatical accuracy, and the presentation of arguments through general knowledge or observed behavior, rather than external research, will significantly bolster the essay's impact and coherence. prompt: Is it true that technology makes our life too complex?

A number of people have divergent views that their life seems to be swamped with tons of things since technology revealed and they promote a life without high-tech. I do not advocate this statement by illustrating some reasons. 
 Firstly, the development of technology encourages plethora of positive result in the sphere of education. With the aid of cutting-edge technology, school-aged children get more golden opportunities of accessing to novel knowledge rather than exposing to theory knowledge. Both teachers and students are capable of discussing together which is backbone to maintain their good rapport and broadening their horizon in the real world. By showing a principle example, in history lessons, trainer would prefer to display the severe battles throughout the screen of TV to incentivizes students to be more effortlessly remember each special event in each day rather than learn by heart. 
 Secondly, the business domain has seen a surge in recent years. A sheer volume of work runs a higher risk of being figured out thanks to the latest technology. The white collar could eschew traditional communication methods in favor of more time and cost -efficient alternatives such as emails and video calls which is confidential for the information. The most principle example of this matter may be that in the Covid-19 pandemic, they could join in online correspondence meetings with their partner as well as those who are overseas in lieu of facing directly which is a cause for spreading the viruses. 
 To sum up, it is indisputable that living with technology has been gaining significant traction with people from all ages. I take the view that technology is more necessary for human in the future.
feedback:
Your essay provides an interesting perspective on the impact of technology on human lives, particularly in the fields of education and business. However, there are several areas where improvements could help clarify your argument and ensure your essay fully addresses the given topic. Below are some points to consider:

1. **Topic Response and Clarity:** Your essay aims to discuss the positive impacts of technology, which aligns with the prompt's general direction. However, it's essential to respond more directly to the specific question asked. For example, discussing the extent to which you agree or disagree with the given statement would strengthen your essay. Ensure your conclusion reiterates your stance clearly, giving the reader a concise summary of your viewpoint.

2. **Language and Style:** When referring to technology in general, avoid using "the" before technology, as it implies you're talking about a specific piece of technology. This choice of wording can confuse readers about your broader discussion on technology's impact. Additionally, try to maintain an academic tone throughout your essay. Phrases like "swamped with tons" feel too informal for an academic paper. Opt for more formal language that reflects the seriousness of your analysis.

However, it would be beneficial to develop these examples further and ensure they directly support your argument. For example, when discussing the benefit of technology in education, elaborate on how this technology specifically aids learning beyond just providing access to information. Using precise and descriptive arguments will make your position clearer and your essay more convincing.

5. **Avoiding Slang and Non-academic Phrases:** Remember, your audience includes academics seeking a professional and thoughtful presentation of ideas. Therefore, avoid using slang or overly casual language that might detract from your essay's credibility.

6. **Clear Point of View:** It's crucial to assert your opinion clearly and confidently. While you state your disagreement with the idea that life is better without high-tech, explicitly mentioning the strength of your conviction would help. Do not hesitate to clearly outline your viewpoint and support it with strong, well-explained reasons throughout your essay, especially in your conclusion.

By addressing these points, you'll improve the structure and clarity of your essay, making your arguments more compelling and your writing more aligned with academic standards. Keep practicing your essay writing, focusing on these areas for improvement, and your skills will continue to develop.

prompt: ESSAY ABOUT THE REASONS AND SOLUTIONS OF WATER POLLUTION

 Because of many negative effects to water resources if long-period pollution. We should have many achievable solutions. First of all, we should put the waste in the bin and sort garbage. prompt: Is the extinction of individual plant and animal species the main environmental problem today?
essay:
Whether the extinction of individual plant and animal species should be the main environmental problem of our time is debatable. Some people consider this loss of species to be less important than other environmental issues. 
 It is true that the disappearance of particular flora and fauna can have a detrimental effect on both the ecosystem and human lives. When one species die out, other species in this food chain will be affected considerably. Aside from having less food, the number of some species will increase dramatically while the population of others will reduce. In other words, the ecosystem is no longer in balance when one species become extinct. Furthermore, the next human generation has no opportunity of observing the diversity of our ecosystem as well as witnessing and learning more about certain species because of their extinction. 
 However, some people believe that the falling number of particular species is just one of Nature's ruthless tests to cross out the weak and keep the fittest. They think that instead of focusing on protecting rare or dying species, we should pay more attention to other important issues such as climate change and pollution. Over the past few years, climate change has resulted in rising sea level that leads to frequent flooding in low areas and the gradual shrinking of habitual land and islands. Apart from that, pollution also affects many aspects of our lives negatively. As a consequence of pollution, food and home become increasingly scarce while human health deteriorate. If the main contributors to these problems take no urgent actions to cease or delay them, there will be no hope for the human future. 
 Although the loss of certain flora and fauna is detrimental, I believe we should focus more on ceasing climate change and pollution because if they continue, there will be less land and less food for everyone, including animals and plants. 
 In conclusion, people should pay more attention to other important environmental issues that are more significant than the extinction of particular flora and fauna.
feedback:
The essay you've written engages with a significant environmental debate: whether the extinction of individual plant and animal species should be deemed the central environmental issue of our time. Overall, you've made an effort to address this topic, but there are key areas that can be enhanced to strengthen your argument and improve the structure and clarity of your essay.

1. **Response to the Topic:** The essay attempts to tackle the given topic by discussing the importance of biodiversity loss versus other environmental issues like climate change and pollution. However, it seems to lean more towards personal opinion rather than thoroughly exploring public opinions on the matter. For a more balanced approach, consider dedicating separate sections or paragraphs to discussing general public perspectives on both sides of the argument before introducing your view. This structure not only adheres to the essay requirements but also provides a solid foundation for comparing these public opinions to your stance.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, and Style:** While the essay is generally well-written, paying closer attention to grammar and sentence structure could enhance readability and clarity. For example, be mindful of verb tense consistency and subject-verb agreement ("one species become extinct" should be "one species becomes extinct"). Additionally, simplifying complex sentences may help ensure your arguments are clear and more easily understood by a broad audience.

3. **Point of View Clarity:** Your point of view is clear; you believe that while the loss of flora and fauna is crucial, more attention should be given to issues like climate change and pollution. To strengthen your position, it would be beneficial to compare and contrast this viewpoint more directly with public opinions. This juxtaposition would not only clarify your stance but also provide a deeper understanding of your reasoning.

4. **Arguments and Support:** Your essay presents arguments for why other environmental issues may be considered more significant than species extinction. However, the reasoning would benefit from deeper development and more explicit comparisons between the impacts of species loss and other environmental challenges. For instance, discussing specific examples or studies that illustrate the direct consequences of ignoring biodiversity loss could make your argument more compelling. Moreover, addressing counterarguments to your position can also provide a more comprehensive view and reinforce your argument's validity.

In conclusion, focusing on creating distinct sections to explore public opinions before presenting your viewpoint, improving sentence structure and grammar, and providing deeper, more comparative reasoning could significantly enhance your essay. Remember, the goal is to clearly present a balanced discussion that considers multiple perspectives before convincingly arguing for your stance. This approach will not only strengthen your essay but also demonstrate your ability to engage critically with complex environmental issues.

prompt: Is hard work always good? Children are told that they can achieve anything if they try hard enough
essay:
There is a message that children are able to reach every goal by making enough effort. While it not only makes children persistent people but also inspires them, a drawback, particularly pressure, should also be taken into consideration. 
 On the one hand, some people told children that hard work helps children to make every dream come true because of some benefits. First, undoubtedly, children are likely to become more persistent when they are encouraged to try hard to reach anything. By realizing that everything takes much time and effort to reach, they will not give up when getting failures. Moreover, children who make serious attempts to achieve goals set a good example for the same-aged. An example is Joseph Schooling who had spent his teenage years practicing swimming professionally to surpass his idol Michael Phelps and won a gold medal in 2016, which is a motivator to children, particularly those who have a passion for the sport. 
 On the other hand, holding a belief in this message, children are under great pressure, which is also a downside. There is no doubt that children will feel stressed when they have to try as hard as possible to reach lots of different goals. My cousin, for example, studies with a hectic schedule to get good scores in all subjects in order to fulfill his parent's high expectations. Therefore, he has less time to relax, feels extremely stressed and worried when he does not perform well in exams. Moreover, making every effort to be good at all subjects, he cannot exactly know what his strength is. 
 In conclusion, the message to children emphasizing the need of working hard to be successful brings some advantages and puts great pressure on them
feedback:
Your essay provides an insightful exploration of the impact of encouraging children to work hard to achieve their goals. You've done a commendable job of presenting both the positive aspects and the pressures associated with this message. However, there are several areas where your essay could be improved for clarity, coherence, and effectiveness.

1. **Response to Topic**: Your essay addresses the topic well, presenting a balanced view of the message that hard work leads to success. You've successfully outlined both benefits, like persistence and inspiration, and drawbacks, such as pressure and stress. This balance is key to a nuanced argument.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, and Stylistic Issues**: There are minor errors that can be easily fixed. For instance, "same-aged" should be "same-age peers". Also, be mindful of avoiding redundancy in your phrases. You used "undoubtedly" and "there is no doubt" close together, but these phrases mean the same thing. Choose one way to convey your certainty to prevent repetition and to make your argument stronger.

3. **Clarity of Point of View**: Your point of view comes through in the essay, but it could be made clearer. When discussing the benefits and drawbacks of hard work, ensure your language reflects your analysis without strong bias unless your task requires it. Instead of using phrases like "there is no doubt", which suggest a very firm stance, consider phrases that offer your analysis while leaving room for discussion. This approach will make your argument more robust and reflective.

4. **Supporting Arguments**: You have provided clear and descriptive arguments, like the example of Joseph Schooling, which strongly support your viewpoint. However, ensure that your examples and arguments flow logically from one to the next. Each paragraph should lead into the next smoothly, with a clear connection between your discussion of benefits and the drawbacks.

5. **Avoiding Redundancy**: Avoid using phrases with similar meanings close together unless you are comparing or contrasting concepts. This keeps your argument clear and concise. For instance, discussing the absence of doubt effectively in one part of your essay is sufficient; repeating it might weaken your stance.

6. **Engagement and Description**: Finally, you're encouraged to delve deeper into your examples and explore them more fully. This will not only strengthen your argument but also engage your reader more effectively. For Joseph Schooling’s example, briefly mentioning the years of effort and the specific challenges he overcame can enrich your argument.

In conclusion, your essay shows promise and understanding of the topic. Focus on refining your language, supporting your arguments clearly, and ensuring that your point of view is evident but not overwhelmingly biased. With these adjustments, your essay will become more articulate and compelling.

prompt: IMPORTANT FACTORS TO CHOOSE A JOB.

From my perspective, I disagree with the statement. My view is there are certain aspects which are more significant than the salary when people choose their jobs. 
 First of all, a passion for one job plays an indispensable role when people decide their occupations more than high salaries. In other words, career choices must be based on people's likes and what they have burning desires for. Job seekers should look for careers which are suitable with their personalities and their dreams instead of following high-paid jobs. Simply because a favorite career gives rise to high job satisfaction. It creates joyfulness and make employees delighted in working. As a result of high job satisfaction, workers will run their business more efficiently and in a much more productive way. Employees will be motivated to work and be creative during working time as they are doing what they have passions for. It is obvious that career choices will affect long-term life. Consequently, job seekers should look for a favorable working conditions which provide people an incentive to work harder in place of a high salary job but cannot work satisfactorily.

Workers cannot apply an occupation without considering about what they have strong feelings for or how good the working conditions are. Consequently, when applying a job, aside from the salaries, job satisfaction must be taken into consideration.

prompt: A group is able to find better solutions that if they were to try to solve the problem individually

 When people solve problems as a group, they come up with better solutions that if they were to try to solve the problem individually. Use specific reasons and examples to support your answer. 
 Teresa said that "There is nothing more terrible than to be alone among human beings". It is clear that when we have a problem in the life if we become a solitary person, we will face difficulty to find solutions in any situation. From my perspective, I agree that working as a group not only results in better solutions than individually but also carry an efficient and progressive process. 
 Firstly, working as a group can finish their tasks in more efficient manner. As a person not always has a suitable competency to solve or analyze the problem. Therefore, the knowledge and skills of each member a group can also be used to strengthen a solution. For example, in many sports such as football, a player would not scorer if not helps from the team. Moreover, working with a team will help people save time, solve complex problems and to complete a difficult task faster. In addition, working in a group may bring responsibility for team member because they know that their work will directly result in whole group. 
 Secondly, working as a group help people become more creative. Teamwork helps in increasing collaboration and has a scope for brainstorming which results in getting more ideas. As a result of the exchange of ideas can act as a stimulus to the imagination, encouraging individuals to explore ideas they would not otherwise consider. Moreover, the people can improve their skills while working as a group. For example, a team will be having people with different skill and abilities such as communication, presentation or leadership so that working closely with others, the people will have more chances to share various work experiences, educational background. 
 From the reasons mentioned above, I believe that working as a group brought advantages to people not only solution efficient but alo necessary skills in work as well as life.

prompt: IELTS Writing II: Compare importance of parks and sports facilities to shopping malls in a new town.

In my opinion, it seems that public parks and gyms are as crucial as shopping malls in a town. 
 There are a couple of compelling justifications why evolving public parks and sports facilities is vital in a new town's plan. The first reason could be that they provide suitable spaces and convenient equipment for citizens on the grounds that cities lack them seriously in these days. Take jogging in the park as a prime example, it helps to keep bodies fit and it also lightens their mood during a day. The second factor could be related to a fact that it is a good opportunity for inhabitants to socialize with their neighbors in the light of connection through playing team sports such as basketball, volleyball, soccer or walking and talking together in the park. This could probably lead to a harmonious relationship between residents that helps build a friendly neighborhood. 
 Developing shopping malls plays the same essential role to town dwellers. It is apparent that they meet all shopping requirements' local residents, regardless of entertainment in their free time or their daily needs. Shopping centers make shopping more and more convenient with less effort and lower cost because of not including extra shipping money. Furthermore, not only do they solve shopping problems more easily but they also enhance mental health of dwellers by purchasing things. 
 In conclusion, town planners ought to consider developing both parks, sports facilities and shopping centers to built a thorough developing strategy for a new town in the long term.

prompt: Writing Ielts Task 2:The mass media have an adverse effect on moral standards.
essay:

It is reckoned that the mass media have a devastating impact on moral principles. I am a strong advocate of this point of view, and this essay includes some reasons to support my stand. 
 For a start, children's morals are inclined to be injuriously affected by the media. Not only cannot they discern a huge amount of information, but they also have more spare time to access that. If they usually watch videos containing degrading language without being censored, they may consider them to be normal in real life. For example, my brother often spends his free time on nonsense videos in which the editors use improper language, which can negatively affect his diction when communicating with others. 
 Another notion worth mentioning is that the media also acts as a catalyst for deteriorating moral philosophy. Some people regard social sites as a place not for sharing, but for blaming or using hostile comments towards a person who they even have no knowledge of. Without a multi-faceted view, electronic media's users are easily willing to insult others based on yellow journalism. For instance, there are a host of attention-grabbing posts involving the break-up between Virus and his girlfriend; however, some groups of people not truly understanding their relationship are ready to comment hurtful or sensitive words to discuss or judge this matter on both sides while it's not their business at all. 
 By contrast, merely a small part of kindnesses are transferred through media outlets including television and newspaper. This raises people's awareness of lending a hand and reminds them of how to conduct themselves. Nevertheless, with a fast pace of life, the busier people are, the less time they spend on watching national broadcasters; instead, keeping up-to-date through online magazines is an optimal alternative. Therefore, we have to suffer from the deleterious effects of the media more than the benefits we can reap from.

Ensuring sentences are straightforward and ideas are expressed clearly will improve the overall quality of the essay. Additionally, reviewing and revising the essay to fix grammatical errors and enhance clarity is essential.

However, the arguments could be made more compelling through clearer and more concise language, ensuring that examples directly support the stated position without unnecessary details.

It is also essential to review work carefully to correct any grammatical errors and ensure the essay directly and effectively addresses the prompt.

prompt: Purchasing the same goods in every part of the world - a good or bad trend?
essay:
Here is my essay: 
 There is increasingly common trend these days that residents can purchase the similar goods anywhere in the world. From my perspective, I firmly believe that this is a beneficial change for people in modern life. 
 It is clearly evident that the global distribution of products is of incredible help in reducing the total prices, which is resulted from the decrease of the total cost of importing goods. In fact, the imported goods are priced based on all the relevant fees that a company is supposed to bear when they import goods from foreign countries, for example, shipping fee, importing tax. One good illustration here is that since Zara opened a new branch in Vietnam, Vietnamese can pay more reasonable amount of money for its clothes, more specifically, it is cheaper than the ordered ones from foreign countries. 
 In addition, providing the same products around the world can mitigate the risk of shipping goods to other nations. First of all, long-distance transportation by several means of transport such as ships, trains, planes often take such a long period of time for the products to get their destinations, which sometimes irritates the buyers if those goods are shipped after the expected dates. It is also possible to say that the products are endangered of being lost or stolen on the way. A fairly good example should be mentioned here is that some travelers by planes claim for package pilfering, leading to missing items in the suitcases which are bought in foreign nations.

prompt: IELTS2: Many goods like food and consumables are being imported by many countries all over the world

However, the overuse of chemical additives has been scientifically proven to pose long-term threats to people's health, and too much preservative intake can lead to many cardiovascular diseases, including stomach aches or food poisoning. Additionally, because of tariff and import duties, the market prices of foreign food are always significantly higher than the native ones, thus making them inaccessible to the poor. 
 Be that as it may, I'm convinced that imported food should not be ignored for certain reasons. First of all, the increasing diversity of food provides consumers with more options of exotic tastes and experiences that local people have not had previously. For example, in today's society, it is effortless for Vietnamese people to savour foreign delicacies such as cherry from Australia or Blue Berries from Europe. Moreover, food exportation has been a major source of income for many countries all over the world, including Vietnam, as the third-world country can export their rare and surplus food to other parts of the world in exchange for foreign money, which can help to boost their economy. Another point that is worth mentioning is that importing food can ensure a country with food stocks, which would help the country to scrap through in case of emergencies such as a tsunami or long-term drought where the agricultural areas have been seriously damaged. 
 In conclusion, I believe that we would gain more than we lose if food is allowed to be imported from different parts of the world.

prompt: Being right or being kind, which is more important to you?

 - Dead Poet Society,1989 - 
 Being right and being kind are equivalently essential to the prosperity of humankind. While being right implies one's sense of righteousness and his awareness of universal laws and morals, being kind reflects his ability to sympathize and harmonize with other individuals. 
 In certain cases, righteousness might prove to be of higher value than kindness and vice versa. Situations that require accuracy such as a calculation in math, a prescription for a disease or an installation of parts in engineering, kindness is of no assistance since an error might render consequences as dire as the student's failing an exam or the patients' death or the collapse of a whole system of machinery. However, when it comes to social interaction, to indoctrinate one's stance is often perceived as a domineering act that might result in dissonance or the partition of the group. The reason for such negative consequences is that each person has his very distinctive, exclusive set of disciplines that might apply only to himself. In most cases, people are so rigid with their disciplines that it is of insurmountable hardship for them to compromise with others. 
 But what if a face-deformed child is in sight? Should a person be straightforward and tell the child that he has a distasteful face or should the person show him sympathy? As kindness made its way around, it shatters hope, trust and love. In certain cases, kindness might be regarded as the nobler state of righteousness for knowing when to act kind is when the person is fully aware of social disciplines yet recognizes when to tolerate circumstances that go against his morals.
