prompt: Online education as a replacement to traditional education. Which is more benefitial for a student?
essay:
As technology advances, education thru internet is embraced by the society. While others believe going to school is still the best way to learn. In my opinion, traditional education has more benefits than online education. 
 E-learning is an online way to study. Instead of going to school, students will be in front of their computers instead of boards. Some people prefer this kind of education because it is more accessible and less hassle to the students and even to educators. Laptops and internet are all they need for this to work. 
 However, there are other people who think that being present in the classrooms and face-to-face to their teachers are more conducive in learning. Traditional education involves personal participation that can help the students be active in school activities. Going to school may help young people to interact with other students that can also give them new learnings and different perspectives that they may not achieve by being online. 
 From my perspective, I believe that sitting in a classroom, listening to the teachers and communicating with other students are better for learning. If a student is present in school, he can raise his hand and ask questions personally whenever he does not understand something. While in e-learning, from my personal experience when I was in college, most videos are recorded, and a professor talked nonstop about his or her specialty. Because of that, I was not able to learn anything but was forced to listen and sit in front of the computer and watch my teacher talk. 
 Therefore, I still stand on my belief that traditional education have more benefits than internet education. Though being online is the easiest way to learn, it still cannot replace the old-fashion way to absorb knowledge and gain new information by being present in a room full of students and infront of the teacher. 
 I think this is a weak essay, but I still want to be graded and reviewed so I would know how to correct my future essays if i encounter with the same prompt.

In moving forward, remember to carefully read and understand the essay prompt to ensure your response fully addresses all components. This approach will not only improve the quality of your essays but also help in developing your critical thinking and analytical skills.

In many cultures the penalty of being banished from the clan as an outcast was akin to a death sentence as an individuals chance of survival was remote.

prompt: Some people think that schools should teach/enroll students according to their academic abilities
essay:
People have differing views concerning the question of whether schools should group students according to their academic abilities or have students with different abilities study together. While some maintain that putting school students with similar abilities in groups and teaching them together is effective, I believe that a balanced approach between streaming and mixed-ability models can be the most effective. 
 There are numerous reasons why proponents of ability-based grouping argue, one of which is allowing teachers to tailor their instruction to the needs of each group. By grouping students of similar abilities together, teachers can provide more targeted and challenging instruction to high-achieving students while also providing additional support and remediation to struggling students. This would therefore help maximize learning outcomes as students receive instruction that is appropriate for their current academic level. Another justification is that grouping by ability can create a sense of healthy competition among students, motivating them to strive for higher achievements. More specifically, in a tracking study, the students were equally competent; they did not feel any lack of confidence, which in turn made them feel comfortable expressing themselves and improving. 
 Notwithstanding some critics' objections, some people support the view that mixed-ability classrooms emphasize the importance of diversity and inclusion. They argue that by having students with different abilities study together, it fosters a cooperative and supportive learning environment. In such classrooms, high-achieving students can serve as role models for their peers, while struggling students can benefit from peer tutoring and collaboration. This approach promotes empathy, social skills, and a sense of community among students. It should also be noted that mixed-ability classrooms prepare students for the real world, where they will inevitably encounter people with different abilities and backgrounds. Multiple-level classrooms are the real-life environments that each student faces after going out into the real world. 
 In sum, while there are sensible reasons to believe that schools should group students into classes depending on their levels of attainment, my view is that a balanced approach can be the most effective. A balanced approach that combines elements of both can provide the best learning outcomes. Should the school adjust instruction to individual needs within a diverse classroom setting, students can benefit from the advantages of both approaches.
feedback:
Your essay on whether schools should group students by academic abilities or have mixed-ability classrooms presents a thoughtful argument. You advocate for a balanced approach, which is a nuanced stance. However, there are areas where you could make your essay more effective and aligned with English proficiency test expectations. 

1. **Response to Topic**: Your essay appropriately addresses the topic, presenting arguments for both ability grouping and mixed-ability classrooms before arguing for a balanced approach. This shows a clear understanding of the task.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, Stylistic Issues**: Your essay is mostly free from spelling and grammar errors, which is excellent. However, be cautious with overly complex vocabulary and sentence structures. Your goal is to convey your ideas as clearly and concisely as possible. Overcomplicated language can make your essay harder to follow.

3. **Author's Point of View**: Your viewpoint is clear throughout the essay. You successfully avoid taking an extreme position by advocating for a compromise between the two models. This nuanced perspective is a strength but ensure you clearly outline the benefits of this approach to make your argument more persuasive.

4. **Arguments and Support**: You provide reasons and examples to support your viewpoint, which strengthens your essay. However, to ensure clarity and cohesiveness, focus on providing one strong justification for each model rather than multiple. This will help you manage your time and word count more effectively, allowing for a balanced discussion without over-explaining. For instance, mention one key benefit of ability grouping and one key advantage of mixed-ability classrooms, then clearly explain how a balanced approach can incorporate these benefits. 

5. **Cohesion and Coherence**: To improve the flow of your essay, use transition sentences that smoothly connect one argument to the next. This not only aids reader comprehension but also demonstrates your ability to organize ideas logically. For example, after discussing the benefits of ability grouping, a transition like, "On the other hand, mixed-ability classrooms offer unique advantages such as..." can effectively bridge your points. 

6. **Be Mindful of the Writing Time Allowance**: Remember, proficiency tests have time limits. Your essay should demonstrate your ability to present well-considered arguments within these constraints. Practice summarizing your points effectively to ensure you can convey your ideas within the allotted time.

By focusing on these areas, you can improve your essay's clarity, coherence, and overall effectiveness. Remember, simplicity and clarity often result in a stronger, more persuasive argument than complexity and verbosity. Keep practicing, and consider these tips in your future essays.

prompt: IELTS writing task 2: Each year, a number of languages fade into extinction
essay:
Some people think that this is not important because life will be easier if there are fewer languages in the world. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this opinion? 
 Each year, a number of languages fade into extinction. Some people believe that it does not matter since it brings ease to life. I strongly disagree. In my opinion, the trend is anything but insignificant considering the protection of cultural heritage and the purpose of communication. 
 A language is not merely about letters, words and pronunciations but about a culture. Its dying out means that the culture vanishes, which can be a tragic loss. For instance, if the Chinese language was wiped out, the accumulated knowledge and history of would be lost. No longer could people gain a glimpse of China's five thousand years of civilization and draw on the treasure trove of art, science and technology to make the world a better place to live. 
 As to communication, language barrier is admittedly a major obstacle. If humans ended up speaking the same language, people from all around the world would lead an easier life as they could communicate with ease. However, communication is meant to exchange different ideas, thoughts, opinions and feelings, while people who speak the same language tend to have similar values and point of views. Fewer languages means that people have more difficulties benefiting from the diversity of thoughts, which is a source of creativity and inspiration. 
 In conclusion, I am in strong disagreement that the disappearance of several languages every year carries little importance because of the apparent convenience the trend brings to life. It makes it almost impossible to carry on the cultures the vanished languages represent. People also find it more difficult to learn from diverse thoughts by communication.
feedback:
Your essay demonstrates a strong stance on the importance of preserving languages and clearly outlines your disagreement with the opinion that the extinction of languages is inconsequential due to the simplicity it might bring to life. Here's a detailed feedback focusing on the aspects you queried:

1. **Relevance to the Topic**: Your essay directly addresses the statement but slightly misses fully restating the prompt's original point about the global easiness fewer languages could supposedly bring. A more explicit mention of the global implications and a balanced restatement of the original query would enhance your introduction.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, and Style**: There are no significant issues with spelling or grammar that detract from the readability of your essay. The style is coherent and mostly clear, though simplifying some of the language and sentences could make your arguments more accessible to all readers.

3. **Author's Point of View**: Your position is unmistakably clear — you strongly disagree with the idea that the loss of languages is unimportant due to the ease it would bring to global communication. This is well-articulated throughout the essay.

4. **Arguments and Support**: You present two main arguments: the loss of culture and the impact on communication. Both arguments are supported with examples or explanations. However, your essay could be strengthened by considering counterarguments. For instance, acknowledging that some aspects of culture may survive through language translations before asserting why this does not equate to preserving the full cultural essence.

### Suggested Improvements:

- **Restate the Original Topic More Precisely**: Clarify in your introduction that the discussion is about whether the global ease of fewer languages justifies their extinction. This would set a stronger foundation for your essay.

- **Balance in Arguments**: While your passion for preserving linguistic diversity is commendable, integrating opposing views or acknowledging the efforts to preserve knowledge and history through translations could make your argument stronger. This demonstrates critical thinking and a deeper understanding of the issue.

- **Narrower Focus**: Your discussion on language as a barrier might seem off-track from the main topic of language extinction. Focusing on how the loss of languages diminishes the diversity of ideas and cultural heritage would maintain a tighter relevance to the topic.

- **Defend Against Counterarguments**: Briefly addressing possible counterarguments, such as the role of language translations in preserving culture, would allow you to fortify your stance. This shows you've considered different sides of the issue and still maintain your viewpoint.

Your essay is insightful and passionate, reflecting a deep appreciation for linguistic and cultural diversity. By fine-tuning the clarity of your argument and addressing the stated suggestions, your essay could become an even stronger and more compelling piece. Keep up the reflective thinking and passionate writing.

prompt: IELTS Task 2_women who do not plan to have careers should be allowed to get post-grad degrees or not
essay:
It cannot be denied that the opportunities to learn the desired subjects have been equal for both women and men in these days, but some critics complaint that attending further education courses should not be allowed for women who have decided not to have careers. However, in my opinion, I am convinced that every woman has the right to do what she believes. 
 To start with, some people claim that permitting women who have no plan to have careers to get a post-grad degree is not an acceptable idea. The first reason for the concern is waste of time and money. Nowadays, the education costs are really high and it takes at least one year to finish a post-grad degree; then what is the reason of spending the precious time and money for a degree which would not be used in their lives. Moreover, it would be the burden to the women and their families as the former have to take care of the families and so the lessons. Another point is that in some culture, many old fashioned people believe that the child raring and household works are only for women as they are considered as second-class citizens, consequently, some women give up their ambition to attend post-grad courses because of the fact that their family members force them to. 
 Nonetheless, it is my contention that respecting one's freedom of choice is the most important for human beings. In other words, one is entitled to be treated equally without discrimination. Each and every mature and sound person has the privilege to decide one's own destiny as in the 21st century, gender equality and human right are the one factor that indicates the value of being a human. In addition, letting women to continue their higher education would be at least a small action to narrow gender inequality because education is for everyone regardless of gender, race and religion. Generally, women who have high education level have high self-esteem and self-confidence so that they can keep abreast with men even they have no careers. Being highly educated wives can help their husbands by giving advises related with the latter's works. 
 To conclude, although it is arguable that whether women who would have no careers should be allowed for post-grad degrees or not, I am of the view that women have the right to choose and plan for their lives. Therefore, acknowledging women as human beings not second-class citizens would be the best for women rather giving judgements about them.
feedback:
The essay displays a strong commitment to the topic by arguing for the right of women to pursue education regardless of their career plans. This commitment is a strength, as it indicates a clear point of view and a passion for the subject. However, there are areas in which the essay could be improved, making the arguments more compelling and the structure more coherent.

1. **Responsiveness to the Topic:** The essay begins with a relevant introduction but could more specifically tie the opinion to the context of education and attending graduate school. To improve, ensure that the thesis statement directly addresses the prompt topic by stating clearly that the right to education, including postgraduate studies, should be upheld for everyone, regardless of their career intentions. This refinements will enhance the precision and directness of the argument.

2. **Clarity and Coherence:** While the essay presents a defined standpoint, there are moments where the connection between ideas can be strengthened. For example, ensure that each paragraph has a clear topic sentence that signals its main idea and relates directly back to the thesis. Additionally, transitions between paragraphs could be smoother, guiding the reader through the argument more effectively.

3. **Grammar, Spelling, and Style Issues:** Although the grammar issues do not significantly detract from the overall argument, attention to detail in spelling, punctuation, and sentence structure could elevate the essay. Reviewing the essay for common errors such as subject-verb agreement, consistent tense usage, and the correct form of words would make the writing more polished and professional.

4. **Argument Development and Support:** The essay benefits from its passionate arguments but would gain from more precise examples and clearer reasoning. Specifically, elaborating on how education empowers women personally and socially could strengthen the case. Moreover, addressing counterarguments more thoroughly will demonstrate a deep understanding of the topic.

5. **Conclusion:** The conclusion of an essay is an opportunity to reinforce the main arguments without introducing new information. To improve, succinctly summarize the key points made in the essay and reaffirm the position stated in the introduction. This will ensure the essay ends on a strong, conclusive note.

In summary, the essay has a compelling theme and demonstrates a clear point of view. By enhancing the specificity of the thesis statement, refining the coherence and flow of the arguments, addressing grammatical and stylistic issues, and concluding effectively, it can become a more powerful and persuasive piece of writing.

prompt: Product variety and supply chain
essay: Over the past decades, there has been a developing trend for companies to increase the product variety offerings with the aim of providing customers with more choices and standing out from competitors. Many cases can be found in diverse industries, such as automotive, computer and telecommunication. Yet launching and maintaining a large product variety incurs some intensive conflicts among the processes of supply chain, e.g.,the conflict between the actual long material procurement lead time and the short delivery lead time customer requirement. If the conflicts could not be well treated, the increasing variety may be detrimental to the long run profits and the competitiveness of firms. The existing studies on the decisions of product variety level may include the tactical and strategic decisions. From the tactical perspective, more efficient and flexible manufacturing technologies have made it easier to produce a large products variety without a substantial increase in costs. However, there are some limitations on the tactical decisions, especially when the demand forecast accuracy is not high enough. For example, for the short life cycle products like computers, the procurement lead time of some components (IC chip, chess) may be as long as the development lead time of products. In these industries, it is difficult to make good decisions on the product variety level with the tactical methods. Some studies suggested that the decisions on the product variety level need to consider the supply chain strategy, which is tightly related to every supply chain stage and firm performance. This study was proposed to examine the product variety level from the strategic perspective. A new configuration on supply chain strategy was proposed with considering the decisions on product variety and its consistency relationships with supply chain process, which were examined based on an empirical study.
feedback:
Your essay delves into the complexities of product variety in different industries and explores how this affects supply chain processes and firm competitiveness. The topic you have chosen is interesting and relevant, given the current trends in global markets. However, to further enhance your essay and make your argument more compelling, consider the following points:

1. **Clarity of Purpose:** It appears the essay serves as an exploration of the impact of product variety on supply chains and firms. Yet, the primary focus—whether it is on the product level, supply chain strategies, or their interrelation—is not distinctly articulated. Clearly stating your main thesis or argument at the beginning would help guide the reader through your analysis and conclusion.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, and Style:** Overall, your essay is well-written. However, attention to minor grammatical errors and punctuation (e.g., missing spaces after commas and before parentheses) can improve readability and professionalism. Additionally, simplifying complex sentences can aid understanding without sacrificing the sophistication of your analysis.

3. **Author's Point of View:** Your stance is somewhat implicit, leaning towards the importance of strategic planning in managing product variety and supply chain efficiency. Make your point of view explicit by stating your position clearly, early in the essay. This guides the reader and sets expectations for the arguments to follow.

4. **Descriptive Arguments:** You've done well to illuminate the conflict between supply chain processes and product variety. However, the essay would benefit from more specific examples or case studies illustrating these conflicts and proposed solutions. Describing the tactical versus strategic decisions around product variety in greater detail could provide a stronger foundation for your argument.

5. **Separation of Topics:** The essay seems to intertwine discussions on product variety, supply chain strategy, and their relationship. For clarity, consider more distinctly separating these subjects initially, then demonstrating their interconnectivity through your analysis. This structure can offer readers a cleaner, more digestible presentation of complex topics.

Enhancing your essay by addressing these points can make your argument more robust and your perspective clearer. Remember, the objective is to guide your readers through your analysis to a well-supported conclusion. Focusing on clarity, structure, and exemplification will significantly improve the coherence and impact of your essay.

prompt: SERIOUS CRIMES SOLVE BY DEATH PENALTY OR OTHER SOLUTIONS. DISCUSS BOTH VIEWS
essay:
The number of serious crimes commitments has been increasing annual. It is considered by many that different solutions are needed to be taken into consideration. I, however, believe capital punishment is the greatest measure to tackle this problem as the more tolerant government's law is, the more serious criminals the society appear. 
 On the one hand, there are various reasons why some believe that different solutions still work efficiently instead of carrying death penalty. Firstly, offenders will gain opportunities to become useful citizens if they are well-informed with moral knowledge through education in prisons. Giving wrongdoers a chance of rehabilitation is a special present for them to make a fresh start. Secondly, instead of introducing death penalty, psychological therapy is another effective solution because almost serious criminals do endure at least a psychological problem, which control their guilty behaviors. Once can be solved if the psychological barriers are overcome and thus, they gradually exhibit their humane behaviors. 
 On the other hand, I would argue that capital punishment has a crucial role to play. If a killer is reintegrated into society, there will be a high possibility that they will commit crimes again. This is mainly because they will have more chances to meet their crews and plan for their next flawless crime commitments. As a result, the society's security is profoundly affected and considerably threatened. Moreover, people have a tendency to be afraid of being died and hence, they endeavor not to commit serious crimes. Therefore, the crime rate will be able to drop in the following years. As a consequence, implementing a policy of zero tolerance like capital punishment is the most powerful measure to punish serious criminals. 
 To conclude, although people think that there are other solutions to solve serious crimes, I personally believe that death penalty can act as a deterrent because of its impacts, which are not only on criminals but also on law-abiding citizens.
feedback:
The essay effectively addresses the given topic by examining the role of capital punishment in reducing serious crime rates. However, it is crucial to improve the essay's response to the topic, address spelling, grammar, and stylistic issues, clarify the author's point of view, and provide more explicit and descriptive arguments to support the author's position.

1. Response to the Topic:
The essay focuses primarily on the author's personal opinion regarding capital punishment and somewhat neglects a balanced exploration of broader public perspectives. To enhance the essay, it's recommendable to include a more balanced discussion that contrasts public opinions with personal insights. This will enrich the essay's depth and provide a comprehensive view of the issue.

2. Spelling, Grammar, and Stylistic Issues:
- The phrase "serious crimes commitments" should be corrected to "commitment to serious crimes" for clarity.
- The sentence beginning with "I, however, believe capital punishment is the greatest measure" could be rephrased for clarity and flow.
- Consider changing "the more tolerant government's law is, the more serious criminals the society appear" to ensure clarity and correctness.
- The term "annual" in the first sentence should be replaced with "annually" for grammatical accuracy.
- Use more transitions to improve the flow between sections and arguments within the essay.

3. Clarity of Author's Point of View:
The author's stance on capital punishment is clear; however, integrating views that consider and directly address counter-arguments would further clarify the stance. Demonstrating an understanding of opposing perspectives and then reinforcing one's argument strengthens the essay's persuasive power.

4. Arguments and Descriptive Support:
- While the essay provides reasons for both sides of the argument, the author's personal opinion could benefit from more detailed evidence and examples to substantiate the claim that capital punishment deters crime.
- The argument that capital punishment acts as a deterrent could be enhanced by citing studies or statistics.
- Exploring the psychological aspects of criminal behavior and rehabilitation more deeply with concrete examples or expert opinions could also strengthen the argument against capital punishment.

In conclusion, by addressing the balance between personal opinions and public perspectives, correcting grammatical and stylistic errors, clarifying the author's point of view, and providing more detailed arguments and evidence, the essay could significantly improve. Ultimately, a more structured, balanced, and evidence-backed approach will make the argument more compelling and persuasive.

prompt: [IELTS WRITING TASK 2] UNPAID COMMUNITY SERVICE - obligation for students to make a better society
essay:
In this day and age, a growing number of individuals believe that unpaid community service ought to be a mandatory sector of institution curricular. From my perspective, I strongly agree with that opinion. This essay will first discuss how scholar are able to contribute to the development of the society, and secondly, addressing the fact that they have capability of acquiring a number of essential accomplishment for their future. 
 Firstly, becoming a volunteer might help undergraduates enhance numerous aspects of an area where they work, such as facility. This is owing to the governments do not ought to pay a considerable cost to repair the infrastructure for their residents if they help, that support may lead to a slight amount of money being saved. The quantity of aged football fields in remote area located in the central part of Vietnam is a great evidence, the villagers could have spent an exorbitant fee to a professional team to mend those football fields, on the contrary a charity group from a prestigious institution program joined in without any payment. 
 Furthermore, a number of soft dexterity which is seldom taught at high schools, consequently take part in an unpaid community service is a suitable way to obtain them. In light of the requirements of various specific work, undergraduate not only broaden their mind, they also have the ability to acknowledge and sharpen their expertise. Take teaching sports for kids as an example, the students have to use communication artistry, time-management dexterity effectively and public speaking ingenuity for a plethora of mischievous kids as well. 
 In conclusion, it is recommended for institution curricular to consider unpaid community service as an obligation sector for their students to make a better society and give them indispensable prowess for their career after school. Only by doing consequently can maintain a dynamic and balance development.
feedback:
This essay does a commendable job addressing the topic of making unpaid community service a mandatory part of school curriculums. The stance that volunteering can significantly contribute to society and personal growth is clear and well-stated. However, there are several areas where the essay could be improved for greater clarity and impact.

1. **Clarity and Development of Arguments**: 
   - The essay presents valuable ideas but sometimes falls short in fully developing these ideas. For example, when discussing the contribution of volunteer work to saving costs in community projects (like the football fields in Vietnam), it's important to also mention the outcomes or continuing effects of such volunteer work. Did the volunteer effort lead to lasting improvements or savings? Expanding on the results of volunteer efforts can make your argument stronger and more persuasive.
   - Try to avoid complex sentence structures or vocabulary that may not be necessary to get your point across. A simpler, more direct way of writing can make your essay easier to understand and your arguments more compelling. 

2. **Grammar, Spelling, and Style**:
   - There are some grammatical errors and awkward phrasings that may distract the reader. For instance, phrases like “governments do not ought to pay” would be clearer as “governments do not have to pay.” Paying attention to verb forms and sentence construction can greatly improve the readability of your essay.
   - Watch out for spelling and stylistic issues that could be easily fixed with proofreading. Consistency in terms like “scholar” (which might be more accurately referred to as “students”) will help maintain clarity.

3. **Effectiveness of Examples**:
   - The use of specific examples, like the football fields in Vietnam, is good practice for supporting your arguments. To strengthen these examples, make sure to describe what impact volunteering had in more detail. Did it foster ongoing community involvement or improve the local area significantly? Offering a clear before-and-after picture can enhance your argument.

4. **Demonstration of Personal and Community Benefits**:
   - The essay touches on the important aspect of gaining “soft dexterity” through volunteering. Clarifying these benefits with simpler language and more specific examples will make the argument stronger. Instead of “soft dexterity,” consider using terms like “skills,” such as communication, time management, and public speaking. This makes your point more accessible to readers. 

In conclusion, your essay successfully argues in favor of making unpaid community service a mandatory part of the curriculum, focusing on both societal and individual benefits. By developing your ideas more fully, simplifying your language, and refining your grammar and style, your essay will become even more effective and engaging. Keep up the good work, and remember that clarity and simplicity often lead to the strongest communication.

prompt: WRITING IELTS TASK 2: oral communication is more effective than written word
essay:
There is an opinion that oral communication is more effective than written word. Personally, I wholeheartedly disagree with this statement and this essay will give some points below. 
 One might argue that verbal language is a more powerful means of communication than written language. This is based on the assumption that spoken language is informal and usually involves body language and facial expressions. Therefore, it can be better understood by people of all ages than written language with often long sentences in complex tenses. Evidence can be seen in the way many young children who have not learnt to read and write yet can easily communicate with their parents, for example, by talking or crying. 
 Despite the benefits outlined above, I believe that written communication plays a more integral roles than oral interaction. Since there are no records, the latter's ability to convey information effectively, though present, is restrained to the time and place that the process of communication takes place. Meanwhile, written language promotes communication across space and time as long as the medium (maybe books, articles, magazines, to name a few) exists. In this sense, written language can serve as solid evidence for future reference in case any confusions or conflicts occur. Besides, human can widen their knowledge through studying historical documents archived in the form of written texts that could otherwise evaporate by word of mouth. 
 In conclusion, it is my view that written interaction is of more significance than verbal language for reasons associated with permanence.
feedback:
The essay does a commendable job of stating an opinion that oral communication might be perceived by some as more effective than written communication, presenting a clear disagreement with this viewpoint. The way the opinion is presented is carefully measured, acknowledging it as an opinion rather than stating it as a fact, which is a strong aspect of this essay. However, the essay could be significantly improved with a few adjustments and considerations.

Firstly, the essay lacks a clear thesis statement. A thesis statement is a concise summary of the main point or claim of the essay. It helps readers understand the stance being taken and the reasons behind this stance. Integrating a clear thesis statement at the end of the introduction would enhance the essay's structure and clarity, giving readers a snapshot of the argument that will be explored in more detail.

In terms of structure and argumentation, the essay would benefit from adopting a more systematic comparison discussion format. Initially presenting evidence that supports the common belief in the effectiveness of oral communication, and subsequently introducing counterarguments showcasing why written communication may be superior, can strengthen the argument. This approach demonstrates an understanding of differing viewpoints before convincingly arguing for the chosen position. Implementing this structure twice, with distinct reasons in separate paragraphs, could provide a well-supported argument that meets higher scoring criteria.

Another area for improvement is the conclusion. The concluding section of the essay should restate the main points in a condensed form while still covering at least two sentences and comprising around 40 words. This improvement would ensure that the conclusion meets necessary requirements, possibly leading to a better score in an examination setting.

While the essay effectively communicates the author's viewpoint and demonstrates an understanding of the topic, refining the response format and argumentative approach as suggested could enhance the coherence and persuasiveness of the argument. These adjustments would not only clarify the author's position further but could also contribute to achieving a higher score. Good job on the efforts made so far; with these modifications, the essay has the potential for greater impact and clarity.

prompt: Write an essay about the negative impacts of social media on teens
essay:
In these days and ages, modernization has divided people's lives into the virtual and actual world. With the constant advancements of social media platforms, it seems indispensable to global netizens, especially the younger generations, to maintain a lifestyle with the existence of such virtual chatting and sharing communities. Apart from the variety of beneficial features that social networks can bring about, there are several adverse influences of these platforms on teenagers that are worth becoming a heated issue to discuss. 
 The first and foremost harmful factor is the worsening mentality of young social media users. Plenty of studies have discovered the link between heavy social media and an increased risk of depression, anxiety, self-harm, and even suicidal thoughts. Rather than choosing the conventional way of interaction, face-to-face, young people tend to express their emotions and perspectives through Facebook, Instagram, Zalo, etc. Continuing to keep this kind of habit, in the long run, will eventually limit the release of dopamine hormone produced when having positive thinking in the human brain, which leads to an imbalance in the mental health of teenagers. In 2019, the death of the gorgeous and multi-talented Korean singer Sulli appalled people all over the world. Having been continuously exposed to negative and judgmental anti-fan comments, she had been diagnosed with over-depression and panic disorder. After a long time struggling with these syndromes, she decided to end her beautiful twenties life by suicide. 
 That is not to mention the multiple social problems that young people may face while approaching social media on a regular basis. Having access to tons of websites and pages on social networks, teenagers are not able to identify the genuine information displayed on these types of virtual communities. Unofficial and unconfirmed pieces of news or advice would take a heavy toll on the life quality of the younger generation, and in some cases, they may have trust issues. Their privacy and personal information safety could also be at stake with a click to suspicious links, or being hacked by cybercriminals. Moreover, social media addiction would lessen students' concentration levels. Instead of fully focusing on studying and completing academic work, their brain could be filled with the desire and temptation coming from the on-screen virtual world. 
 Social media have the potential to add color to people's lives; some even consider it as an escape door to a stressful and busy working and studying routine. However, as is aforementioned, it is undeniable that such kinds of networks have unwanted impacts on teenagers, physically and mentally.
feedback:
This essay does an effective job of addressing the negative effects of social media on teenagers, supporting the argument with various consequences that social media can have on young users' mental health and social lives. The topic is well-chosen, relevant, and thoroughly discussed.

1. **Response to the Topic:** The essay is clearly responsive to the topic, providing a focused examination of the drawbacks of social media. The introduction effectively sets the stage for a discussion on the adverse effects, which are then elaborated upon with specific examples. 

2. **Spelling, Grammar, and Stylistic Issues:** The essay is mostly well-written, but there are slight issues that could be improved for clarity and flow. Consider revising phrases like "In these days and ages," to "In this day and age," for a more standard expression. Pay attention to the coherence of arguments and the transition between paragraphs to enhance readability. 

3. **Point of View:** The essay's point of view is clear; it aims to highlight the negative impacts of social media on teenagers. However, adding personal experiences or viewpoints could provide a more compelling narrative. Discussing personal observations or experiences related to social media’s effects could strengthen the essay's position and make the argument more relatable.

4. **Arguments and Support:** While the essay presents strong arguments supporting the thesis, such as the link between social media use and mental health issues, it would benefit from citing reliable sources. When making scientific claims, such as the effect of social media on dopamine release, it is essential to cite sources to enhance credibility. The example of the Korean singer, Sulli, effectively illustrates the extreme consequences of social media negativity but remember to reference where this information was found. This not only validates the argument but also allows readers to explore the topic further.

5. **Personal Opinion and Experience:** The inclusion of personal experience or a more explicit statement of personal viewpoint could enrich the essay. Although the instructions regarding personal opinion are not specified here, sharing personal insights or how you relate to the topic could make your argument more persuasive and engaging. This approach could offer a unique perspective and underscore the relevance of the issue being discussed.

**Overall Feedback:** This essay demonstrates a strong understanding of the negative implications of social media on teenagers, offering both broad and specific examples to support its claims. To elevate the essay further, focus on refining grammatical details, incorporating credible sources for factual claims, and possibly including personal experiences or viewpoints to create a more compelling argument. Applying these adjustments will not only strengthen the essay's credibility but also enhance its impact on readers.

prompt: [Toefl] Buying a new technological device right away is better than waiting until many people...
essay:
Recently, general awareness about whether it is wiser to buy new technology device right away than waiting until many people have purchased it has aroused heated arguments. People, nevertheless, have conflicting ideas; while some people say that it brings many benefits to buy the device later, others deem otherwise. From my point of view, I am in agreement with former stand and my view can be greatly substantiated by the reasons addressed below. 
 The first reason for my opinion that can be seen by every person is that it is too much expensive to purchase the technological device early. This is because there are few demands to buy the newly launched device in the beginning. According to the one of the most fundamental economic theory, supply and demand curves, price would be high when it comes to low demand given constant supply. In addition, one of the well-known reasearch lab at Seoul National University revealed the relationship between price and period of purchase. In fact, the reasearch team revealed the fact that the earlier clients buy the technology commodities, the more they should pay. 
 Another equally important reason is that new technology device can malfuntion more often than other devices which already has been used by many people. To put it again, new device is not testified by the public as much as other devices which are verified by the public. For instance, Samsung Note 7 was recalled within few days after launching this new product because there were some malfunction cases. As more and more people use this new phone, it is revealed that the product has a severe functional flaw that can even endanger people. Like this case, newly launched device has an enormous risk of malfunction. 
 The third and most noteworthy reason is that clients should invest a lot hours to learn how to use the device. That is to say, what client only can do is to spend lots of time to read whole manual, which is quite boring. Since no one are familiar with using the new device, it is hard to find others who can help you to teach this. In reality, according to the article posted on the Korea Times, many clients have a tendency to prefer to ask their friends or family about how to use the device rather than reading the manual by themselves. 
 To wrap up all statements above, buying a new technological device is not reasonable option in terms of price, malfunction and learning curb. In particular, the high price, risk of malfunction and tedious work to read a manual would hinder clients to buy a newly released product. That is why I agree with the opinion that it is more sagacious to wait until many people have purchased this.
feedback:
Your essay on whether it is wiser to buy new technology device right away or wait provides a thoughtful perspective. However, there are several areas for improvement that would make your argument clearer and more effective. Here are some tailored suggestions to help enhance your essay:

1. **Response to the Topic:**
You did a commendable job of addressing the topic by stating your viewpoint clearly and providing reasons for your position. However, it's important to remain grounded in the discussion and avoid exaggerating the level of debate (such as using phrases like "heated arguments"). Try to keep the tone consistent with the prompt and focus on presenting your arguments in a measured way.

2. **Spelling, Grammar, and Style:**
Overall, your essay is well-written, but there are a few areas where grammar and spelling could be improved for clarity and professionalism. Consider revising phrases that feel awkward or incorrect. Moreover, simplifying your language could make your arguments more accessible to all readers, including those who might not be familiar with more technical terms.

3. **Clarity of Viewpoint:** 
Your point of view is clear throughout the essay, which is great. To further strengthen this, ensure that each argument directly supports your viewpoint without introducing unnecessary complexity. Simplify your explanations where possible.

4. **Arguments and Support:**
You've used examples and economic theory to support your viewpoint, which is a good approach. However, be cautious about referencing very technical concepts or specific research without necessary details, as this might confuse readers who are not familiar with these studies. Also, avoid making claims that require outside verification or detailed study; instead, base your arguments more on common knowledge, personal experience, or easily understood facts. This keeps your essay practical and relatable.

A few more specific suggestions:
- Avoid making generalizations about new technology faults, such as the tendency to malfunction, without providing clear examples or solutions.
- Discussing the learning curve for new devices is a valid point, but consider also mentioning potential benefits of early adoption for balance.
- When mentioning studies or articles, like the one from Seoul National University or the Korea Times, it's better to frame these references in a way that doesn't assume the reader can verify them directly. Focus instead on the more general insight they provide.

Your essay shows a significant amount of effort and thoughtfulness. Focusing on the above areas for improvement will not only make your arguments more convincing but also make your writing clearer and more engaging for your audience. Keep practicing, and you'll continue to see improvement in your skills.

prompt: There's an opinion that the benefits of nuclear technology are more valuable than its disadvantages.
essay:
Many people said that the benefits of nuclear technology are more valuable than its disadvantages. The dangers of nuclear weapons keep the world peace and nuclear power is an alternative resource which is bet than other power sources that we are using. Personally, I strongly disagree with this statement due to the harm it causes. 
 First of all, we cannot deny that nuclear technology plays an important role in our lives. If we compare it to fossil fuel, we can see that nuclear power is cheaper, quicker, cleaner and one prominent thing that it is unlimited. It can solve the problem that we are running out of non-renewable natural resources. Furthermore, if nuclear weapons did not exist, world war 3 could happen anytime. prompt: Accept a bad situation, or work hard to improve such situations
essay:

 DISCUSS BOTH THESE VIEWS AND GIVE YOUR OWN OPINION. 
 In this day and age, in terms of how to overcome an unexpected trouble, people are always wondering about whether we should admit the loss or we should put more effort in brainstorming how to tackle it. For me, I am leaning towards the latter manner. 
 On the one hand, there are certain justifiable rationales that make this tendency appealing to the followers. First of all, this manner seems to be the most ideal way when we are on our beams-end and can not come up even a half measure. If we are in such a dilemma, there is nothing to do except for giving up and learn valuable lessons from the failure. On the contrary, if we still insist on involving in the difficulty, we may just confine to the loss and can not be able to move on. For example, Bill Gates ,before being one of the most wealthiest and successful people in the world , was loath to admit the fall of Traf-O-Data and many other failures. 
 However, it would not be a sensible choice to give up when you are still capable of solving the situation. How can we make progress and move on the career ladder when we just accept the failure so easily? As long as we can still come up with initiative, we have to brainstorm and try our best to make our way to success or at least overcome the mishap. It is only when the situation is out of control that we need to give up. Hence, if we ,in the worst case , surrender, we will be likely to obtain more priceless lessons and will not ascribe the loss to our laziness. As an illustration, Nguyen Ngoc Ky ,a handicapped infant, whose desire was to have a normal life like his friend was so enormous that he practiced writing with his feet industriously and as a result, not only manage to write, he is now a teacher who is well-known for his beautiful handwriting. 
 In conclusion, I argue that if you can not go further, you may surrender and draw a leson from that . Otherwises, do your best to tackle the issue.
feedback:

Also, consider simplifying complex sentences to make your argument more clear and straightforward. Addressing these issues will make your essay more polished and easier to follow.

3. **Clarity of Point of View**: Your point of view is clear—you believe it is better to try and improve bad situations. However, clarity could be further enhanced by distinctly discussing the opposing view as well, which would provide a balanced comparison before stating your personal opinion. 

4. **Arguments and Descriptions**: You have presented arguments that support your viewpoint well, using examples like Bill Gates and Nguyen Ngoc Ky. These are compelling and add credibility to your argument. To strengthen your essay, similarly detailed arguments and examples could be used to explore why some people might choose to accept bad situations. This balance will not only fulfill the prompt's requirement but also demonstrate an ability to critically analyze and argue different viewpoints.

By addressing the comparative discussion requirement of the prompt, correcting minor spelling and grammar issues, and ensuring a balanced representation of both viewpoints, your essay will better meet the expectations of an English proficiency test. prompt: Are libraries necessary? IELTS 2: OPINION ESSAY

Topic: Students today can easily access information online, so libraries are no longer necessary. Do you agree or disagree? 
 With the advent of technology, students in the contemporary world can easily access any information on various online platforms, leading to many advocates assume that there are no longer reasonable excuses to visit traditional libraries. In my opinion, I completely disagree with this assertion because some information is not available online and it might not be authentic. 
 Despite plenty of sources of information that can be found on the Internet, there is some information that can solely looked up in the library. The library usually contains ancient books that have existed for a long period and those books are written by authentic authors; hence, it is impossible to find those types of books online. For example, university libraries can provide students with documents from alumni or from their professors, which sometimes cannot be seen on any online platform. In addition, there are some cases in which online information is only capable of giving Internet users basic information, which means that if we want to learn more about it, we need to go to the library to access a huge source of its information. 
 Another point to make is that online information is not always qualified. It is difficult to identify the original version due to online piracy, which can make students confused when they search for the information they want. Additionally, since there is a lot of information, choosing which information is true and which one is false can cause a real struggle. For instance, some students use false information they found randomly on the Internet for their presentation and get a low score as a result. 
 In conclusion, online information cannot be an optimal substitute for traditional libraries because not all information can be searched on the Internet and that information might be false.

prompt: Some have a strong preference for studying alone while others tend to go for learning in a group

 There is no denial that studying alone involves some vital benefits. To begin with, unaccompanied learning helps students concentrate better. For instance, when they study difficult subjects such as maths or physics, they demand for a quiet and peaceful environment without interruption. Learning alone can provide that, so that pupils can not be disturbed whilst doing their assignment and can understand the knowledge more exceptionally. In the second place, learners are likely to be forced to think more when they study on their own. Since there is no one nearby they can ask, they have to brainstorm more. Therefore, this enables the ability of dealing with problems to improve. Finally, studying alone makes students think independently and develop their own opinion. As learners can not receive suggestions from others, no one could have an effect on their point of view. As a result, students may create their thoughts and not become a parrot. 
 However, I do not deny that studying in a group is another good way of acquiring knowledge. One primary reason is that working in a group can help students have more motivation when learning. In particular, when it comes to a difficult problem that one person can not clarify single-handedly, then cooperating with other people may be greatly conducive. Nevertheless, I am convinced that the benefits of studying alone are dominant. 
 To conclude, whether we study alone or in a group, it depends on our habits and awareness. I believe each student may have each way of learning that is suitable for them. 
 302 words.

3. **Clarity of the Author's Point of View**: The viewpoint is clear; however, it would benefit from a more structured presentation. Introducing each paragraph with a topic sentence can help the reader understand the main point more quickly.

4. **Arguments and Descriptions**: The arguments presented are relevant but require more detail and support. Including statistics or factual evidence can significantly bolster an argument. Moreover, exploring the psychological effects on children beyond spending habits and laziness, like issues of self-esteem or unrealistic expectations, could offer a more comprehensive view.

**Additional Suggestions**:

- Academic writing should be formal. Words and phrases used in everyday conversation might not be suitable for an essay. Replace informal language with more precise academic vocabulary.
- Be mindful of the essay’s structure. Organizing content into well-developed paragraphs, each with a clear idea, makes the argument more persuasive and easier to follow.
- Finally, revisiting grammar and punctuation rules will be highly beneficial. Correct usage is essential for clear communication and presenting a professional academic voice.

Focusing on these areas for improvement will not only address the current essay's shortcomings but also enhance writing skills for future assignments. Aim for clear, direct, and formal expression of ideas, supported by evidence and presented in a well-organized format.

prompt: Punishing murderers with death penalty vs life in prison - IELTS Task 2
essay:
Some people said that it is great to throw the killers into the jail than give the death law. Personally, I support the idea that the killers must spend their life in prison, however, I would also argue that death penalty is the best punishment for the killers. 
 There are several reasons why I believe that murderers must life in jail. Firstly, some murderers are still in underage between 13 and 17 years old. Lots of consideration is conducted by the legal institution to get the fair punishment for them. In this case, sending into the prison with predetermined time will be more suitable for underage murderers rather than death penalty. This will be more acceptable for the murder's relatives as well. 
 In addition, the killers still have hopes and dreams which can be realized after the prison penalty is ended. They can arrange their future plans and pursue their dreams for the next chapter of life. Therefore, the death penalty will destroy their future goals at the same time. 
 By contrast, it is true that let the killers still alive will be a threat for society. To illustrate, some news reported that the former killers commit a murder case after they are released from prison. It will be endangered for the human's life if the death punishment is not applied. Besides, the death penalty will eliminate the individual's desire to become a criminal. The number of crimes can be increased as long as the death law still be implemented for the murderers. 
 To conclude, while send to the jail is a good decision, I agree that death penalty can be considered as the punishment for the killers.
feedback:
The essay presents a position on the issue of whether murderers should receive the death penalty or life imprisonment. While attempting to address the topic, the structure and clarity of the argument need significant improvement to meet the requirements of a proficient English essay. 1. **Response to the Topic**: The essay attempts to address the question but lacks a clear stance on the extent of agreement or disagreement with the statement provided in the prompt. 3. **Point of View Clarity**: The essay's point of view appears to be conflicted, suggesting both life imprisonment and the death penalty as suitable punishments. This mixed stance detracts from the clarity of the essay’s argument. To improve, decide on a clear position and support that consistently throughout the essay. It will make the essay more persuasive and easier to follow.

4. **Arguments and Support**: The arguments provided are a good starting point but lack depth and are sometimes contradictory. For example, arguing that murderers have hopes and dreams that will be destroyed by the death penalty conflicts with the later assertion that the death penalty is necessary due to the threat these individuals pose to society. To strengthen the essay, choose arguments that consistently support the chosen stance and explore these in more depth, using evidence or examples to back up each point.

Additionally, it’s essential to move beyond a template response and engage directly with the specifics of the prompt. Focusing on the task's demands, such as discussing the "extent" of your agreement or disagreement, will help align the essay more closely with the expected response format. Avoiding a one-size-fits-all approach and tailoring the essay to the specific question will also showcase your ability to think critically and respond flexibly to different types of prompts.

Remember, practicing writing with clear stances, detailed support for your arguments, and careful attention to language and grammar will significantly improve your essays.

prompt: Essay about the contrast between current generation and my parents generation - IELTS
essay:
English is the common language spoken in the US, but do all people from different ages speak the same language? What this means is does differently in generation creates a new language? Yes, it does. People of my generation and those of my parents have different beliefs, values, languages and life goals. 
 One of the major differences between the two generations is the life goals and definition of success. Current generation defines life goals as having a successful career. They believe it is more important to be successful at work than thinking about the family. They even don't consider having a family unless making a big advancement in their career. On the other hand, old generation goals focus more on the family. They always see family as number one priority in their life. For example, my father was always keen to build a strong family connection between us by giving most of his time to spend it with us. Therefore, basically current and old generation are really different in their life goals. 
 Another difference between the two generations of people is their language. The current generation is more exposed to various cultures with different languages. These young people learned new vocabulary and expressions that were not in the time of old generation. With the existence of the internet and satellites, every day the young generation introduce new vocabulary to the old language. However, old generation didn't have this exposure to the outside world. They used their language without introducing new expressions or words. They didn't have the current varieties of communication like internet and satellite. The current and old generation can't, sometimes, understand each other even if they speak the same language. 
 Current and old generation are also different in life values. For example, current generation cares more about collecting precious stuff. They are more materialistic than the old generation. These young people always dream about having an expensive car, branded watch and up to date clothes. On the other hand, old generation's values were more into authenticity. They didn't consider possessing expensive stuff is essential for them. These old people care more about real person values. Current and old generation have a complete difference in definition of life values. 
 To summarize, at some point all people are similar; however, the difference in generation create a difference in several aspects. People need to study these differences and to take the benefits from both generations.
feedback:
The essay presents a strong understanding of the topic by discussing differences between generations in terms of goals, language, and values. However, improvements can be made to enhance its structure, clarity, and conformity to essay writing standards for English proficiency tests like the IELTS.

Firstly, it's crucial to directly address the essay prompt in the introduction without deviating through the use of rhetorical questions. The initial questions posed risk leading the discussion away from the prompt's focus. In future essays, avoid using questions that may cause deviation from the topic. Instead, clearly restate the provided discussion in your understanding, directly addressing the prompt.

The opening statement needs to be clearer and more direct in presenting the topic. Developing a concise introduction that outlines the key points to be discussed can help in setting a stronger foundation for the essay. 

Regarding the conclusion, it should summarize the main points without introducing new information. The use of run-on sentences through semicolons and excessive commas should be avoided. Aim for a concluding paragraph that recaps the discussion succinctly, consolidating your analysis without extending beyond the established arguments.

The essay structure can also be enhanced by following the recommended format for Task 2 essays, which includes an introduction, three body paragraphs, and a concluding statement. This format not only meets the word count criteria but also ensures a coherent presentation of ideas. Each paragraph should contain 3-5 sentences to clearly express ideas, avoiding overly complex or run-on sentences that might hinder comprehension and impact grading.

Additionally, attention to spelling, grammar, and stylistic choices will further improve the essay. Minor errors in these areas can detract from the overall clarity and professionalism of the writing. Practicing clear and correct sentence structures will benefit both the readability of your essay and your scores.

Lastly, the point of view is generally clear, identifying differences between current and older generations. However, providing specific, descriptive arguments with examples will strengthen the position. While the essay mentions differences in beliefs, a deeper exploration with clear examples could provide more persuasive and compelling support for your viewpoint.

In summary, focus on a direct and clear introduction, adhere to the structured format of the essay, avoid new information in the conclusion, and enhance clarity through attention to grammar and sentence structure. With these adjustments, the quality and effectiveness of future essays are likely to improve significantly.

prompt: Write a letter to your friend, in your letter ask your friend to send you one of the photographs
essay:

 Hope all is well. Here, I need a big favor from you and hope you can help me out. 
 I was in the midst of backing up all recent photos to my laptop and strangely some photos went missing during the data transferring process. While I've managed to retrieve some photos, there was one that went completely missing and could not be found. That photo had both of us in it and it was taken during our trip to Japan last summer! Do you remember which one? It was the one where we took together after we've successfully completed our first full marathon. It's so meaningful as it captured such a memorable event for both of us. It would be a shame if I could not have it back. 
 I wonder if you could send me a copy of the photograph? I would like to print it out and frame it. I'm sure it will be a perfect decoration for my new house.

 Best, 
 Jamie
feedback:

The term "recent" usually refers to a more immediate past, usually a few days to a month old. Therefore, mentioning an event from last summer doesn't quite fit the requirement of discussing a recent trip. This misunderstanding mildly impacts how well the essay responds to the given topic.

2. **Language and Expression:** Your letter is mostly clear and easy to understand, which is great! However, there is a phrase that could be clearer. It's always good to review idiomatic expressions to make sure they're being used correctly.

3. **Grammar, Spelling, and Style:** Overall, your writing is solid, but always remember to review your letter for any potential spelling or grammar mistakes. Also, maintain consistency in your writing style. For example, using contractions like "I've" and "we've" makes your letter sound informal and friendly, which is suitable for writing to a friend. Just be sure this is consistent throughout your letter.

4. **Clarity and Support:** You did well in describing the significance of the photo and why it's meaningful to you. To improve your writing, consider these points:
